sentences.zh: ◎南蠻上南詔南詔，或曰鶴拓，曰龍尾，曰苴咩，曰陽劍，本哀牢夷後，烏蠻別種也。

translations.literal: [Southern Barbarians — Upper] Nanzhao: also called Hetuo, Longwei, Jumie, or Yangjian; originally descendants of the Ailao Yi, a separate branch of the Wuman.
translations.idiomatic: [Southern Barbarians — Upper] Nanzhao—also known as Hetuo, Longwei, Jumie, or Yangjian—was descended from the Ailao Yi, a distinct branch of the Wuman people.

sentences.zh: 夷語王為「詔」。

translations.literal: In the Yi language, "zhao" means king.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yi tongue, zhao means "king."

sentences.zh: 其先渠帥有六，自號「六詔」，曰蒙秀詔、越析詔、浪穹詔、邆睒詔、施浪詔、蒙舍詔。

translations.literal: Earlier their chieftains numbered six and styled themselves the "Six Zhao": Mengxiu Zhao, Yuexi Zhao, Langqiong Zhao, Dianshan Zhao, Shilang Zhao, and Mengshe Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier their chieftains numbered six and styled themselves the "Six Zhao": Mengxiu Zhao, Yuexi Zhao, Langqiong Zhao, Dianshan Zhao, Shilang Zhao, and Mengshe Zhao.

sentences.zh: 兵埒，不能相君，蜀諸葛亮討定之。

translations.literal: Their forces were equal; none could rule the others. Zhuge Liang of Shu subdued and settled them.
translations.idiomatic: Their armies were evenly matched and none could dominate the rest, until Zhuge Liang of Shu pacified them.

sentences.zh: 蒙舍詔在諸部南，故稱南詔。

translations.literal: Mengshe Zhao lay south of the other tribes, hence the name Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Mengshe Zhao stood south of the other tribes—hence the name Nanzhao, "Southern Zhao."

sentences.zh: 居永昌、姚州之間，鐵橋之南，東距爨，東南屬交趾，西摩伽陀，西北與吐蕃接，南女王，西南驃，北抵益州，東北際黔、巫。

translations.literal: They dwelt between Yongchang and Yaozhou, south of the Iron Bridge; east they bordered Cuan; southeast they belonged to Jiaozhi; west to Magadha; northwest they adjoined Tibet; south to the Queen Country; southwest to Pyu; north to Yizhou; northeast to Qian and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Their territory lay between Yongchang and Yaozhou, south of the Iron Bridge—bordering Cuan to the east, Jiaozhi to the southeast, Magadha to the west, and Tibet to the northwest; the Queen Country lay south, Pyu southwest, Yizhou north, and Qian and Wu to the northeast.

sentences.zh: 王都羊苴咩城，別都曰善闡府。

translations.literal: The royal capital was Yangjumie City; the secondary capital was called Shanchan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The king's seat was Yangjumie City; a secondary capital stood at Shanchan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 王坐東向，其臣有所陳，以狀言而不稱臣。

translations.literal: The king sat facing east; when his ministers made representations, they spoke in memorial form without calling themselves "subject."
translations.idiomatic: The king sat facing east. Ministers who wished to speak did so in memorial form, without styling themselves subjects.

sentences.zh: 王自稱曰元，猶朕也；

translations.literal: The king styled himself Yuan, equivalent to "I";
translations.idiomatic: The king called himself Yuan—the equivalent of the imperial "I."

sentences.zh: 謂其下曰昶，猶卿、爾也。

translations.literal: he addressed his subordinates as Chang, equivalent to "you" or "sir."
translations.idiomatic: He addressed subordinates as Chang—the equivalent of "you" or "sir."

sentences.zh: 官曰坦綽、曰布燮、曰久贊，謂之清平官，所以決國事輕重，猶唐宰相也；

translations.literal: Offices were called Tanzhuo, Buxie, and Jiuzan—termed Qingping Officials, who decided the weight of state affairs, like Tang chancellors;
translations.idiomatic: The chief offices were Tanzhuo, Buxie, and Jiuzan—known as Qingping Officials, who weighed the great affairs of state much like Tang chancellors;

sentences.zh: 曰酋望、曰正酋望、曰員外酋望、曰大軍將、曰員外，猶試官也。

translations.literal: there were Qiuvang, Zhengqiuvang, Yuanwaiqiuvang, Dajunjiang, and Yuanwai—like probationary officials.
translations.idiomatic: below them stood Qiuvang, Zhengqiuvang, Yuanwaiqiuvang, Dajunjiang, and Yuanwai—roughly the equivalent of probationary appointments.

sentences.zh: 幕爽主兵，琮爽主戶籍，慈爽主禮，罰爽主刑，勸爽主官人，厥爽主工作，萬爽主財用，引爽主客，禾爽主商賈，皆清平官、酋望、大軍將兼之。

translations.literal: Mushuang oversaw military affairs; Congshuang oversaw household registers; Cishuang oversaw ritual; Fashuang oversaw punishments; Quanshuang oversaw appointments; Juesshuang oversaw labor; Wanshuang oversaw finances; Yinshuang oversaw guests; Heshuang oversaw merchants—all held concurrently by Qingping Officials, Qiuvang, and Dajunjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Mushuang handled military affairs, Congshuang household registers, Cishuang ritual, Fashuang punishments, Quanshuang appointments, Juesshuang labor, Wanshuang finances, Yinshuang guests, and Heshuang commerce—all posts held concurrently by Qingping Officials, Qiuvang, and Dajunjiang.

sentences.zh: 爽，猶言省也。

translations.literal: Shuang means "department."
translations.idiomatic: Shuang means "department" or "ministry."

sentences.zh: 督爽，總三省也。

translations.literal: Dushuang oversaw all three departments.
translations.idiomatic: The Dushuang supervised all three departments.

sentences.zh: 乞托主馬，祿托主牛，巨托主倉廩，亦清平官、酋望、大軍將兼之。

translations.literal: Qituo oversaw horses; Lituo oversaw cattle; Jutuo oversaw granaries—also held concurrently by Qingping Officials, Qiuvang, and Dajunjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Qituo managed horses, Lituo cattle, and Jutuo granaries—again posts held concurrently by Qingping Officials, Qiuvang, and Dajunjiang.

sentences.zh: 曰爽酋、曰彌勤、曰勤齊，掌賦稅。

translations.literal: There were Shuangqiu, Miqin, and Qinqi, who managed taxes and levies.
translations.idiomatic: Shuangqiu, Miqin, and Qinqi managed taxation and levies.

sentences.zh: 曰兵獳司，掌機密。

translations.literal: There was the Bingnusi, which handled secrets.
translations.idiomatic: The Bingnusi handled confidential matters.

sentences.zh: 大府主將曰演習，副曰演覽；

translations.literal: In a great prefecture the commander-in-chief was called Yanxi, his deputy Yanlan;
translations.idiomatic: In a great prefecture the commander was called Yanxi and his deputy Yanlan;

sentences.zh: 中府主將曰繕裔，副曰繕覽；

translations.literal: in a middle prefecture the commander was called Shanyi, his deputy Shanlan;
translations.idiomatic: in a middle prefecture the commander was Shanyi and the deputy Shanlan;

sentences.zh: 下府主將曰淡酋，副曰淡覽；

translations.literal: in a lower prefecture the commander was called Danqiu, his deputy Danlan;
translations.idiomatic: in a lower prefecture the commander was Danqiu and the deputy Danlan;

sentences.zh: 小府主將曰幕撝，副曰幕覽。

translations.literal: in a small prefecture the commander was called Mohui, his deputy Molan.
translations.idiomatic: in a small prefecture the commander was Mohui and the deputy Molan.

sentences.zh: 府有陀酋，若管記；

translations.literal: Each prefecture had a Tuoqiu, like a registrar;
translations.idiomatic: Each prefecture had a Tuoqiu, comparable to a registrar;

sentences.zh: 有陀西，若判官。

translations.literal: and a Tuoxi, like an assistant magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: and a Tuoxi, comparable to an assistant magistrate.

sentences.zh: 大抵如此。

translations.literal: The system was broadly like this.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking, the system worked this way.

sentences.zh: 凡調發，下文書聚邑，必占其期。

translations.literal: Whenever mobilization was ordered, written documents were sent to the settlements, and a deadline was always fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever troops were mobilized, written orders went out to the settlements with a fixed deadline.

sentences.zh: 百家有總佐一，千家有治人官一，萬家有都督一。

translations.literal: Every hundred households had one Zongzuo; every thousand households one Zhiren Official; every ten thousand households one Dudu.
translations.idiomatic: Every hundred households had a Zongzuo; every thousand a Zhiren Official; every ten thousand a Dudu.

sentences.zh: 凡田五畝曰雙。

translations.literal: Five mu of fields made one shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Five mu of farmland constituted one shuang.

sentences.zh: 上官授田四十雙，上戶三十雙，以是而差。

translations.literal: Senior officials received forty shuang of fields; upper households thirty shuang, and so on by gradation.
translations.idiomatic: Senior officials received forty shuang of land, upper households thirty, and so on down the scale.

sentences.zh: 壯者皆為戰卒，有馬為騎軍。

translations.literal: Able-bodied men all became fighting soldiers; those with horses served in the cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: All able-bodied men became fighting soldiers; those with horses joined the cavalry.

sentences.zh: 人歲給韋衫褲。

translations.literal: Each person received a yearly allotment of leather shirts and trousers.
translations.idiomatic: Each man received an annual issue of leather shirt and trousers.

sentences.zh: 以邑落遠近分四軍，以旗幟別四方，面一將統千人，四軍置一將。

translations.literal: By the distance of settlements they were divided into four armies; by banners they were distinguished in the four directions—one general commanded a thousand men, and one general was placed over each of the four armies.
translations.idiomatic: Settlements were grouped into four armies by distance; banners marked the four directions. One general commanded a thousand men, and one general stood over each army.

sentences.zh: 凡敵入境，以所入面將禦之。

translations.literal: When enemies entered the borders, the general of the direction entered was to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: When enemies crossed the border, the general of the direction attacked was responsible for meeting them.

sentences.zh: 王親兵曰朱弩佉苴。

translations.literal: The king's personal guard was called Zhunujuqie.
translations.idiomatic: The king's personal guard was called the Zhunujuqie.

sentences.zh: 佉苴，韋帶也。

translations.literal: Juqie means a leather belt.
translations.idiomatic: Juqie meant a leather belt.

sentences.zh: 擇鄉兵為四軍羅苴子，戴朱鞮鍪，負犀革銅盾而跣，走險如飛。

translations.literal: Selected village soldiers formed the four armies' Luojuzi, wearing red lacquered helmets, bearing rhinoceros-hide copper shields, and fighting barefoot over difficult ground as if flying.
translations.idiomatic: Village soldiers chosen for the four armies formed the Luojuzi—men in red-lacquered helmets and rhinoceros-hide copper shields who fought barefoot over broken ground as if they flew.

sentences.zh: 百人置羅苴子統一人。

translations.literal: For every hundred men one Luojuzi commander was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Every hundred men had one Luojuzi commander.

sentences.zh: 望苴蠻者，在蘭蒼江西。

translations.literal: The Wangju Yi lived west of the Lancang River.
translations.idiomatic: The Wangju Yi lived west of the Lancang River.

sentences.zh: 男女勇捷，不鞍而騎，善用矛劍，短甲蔽胸腹，鞮鍪皆插貓牛尾，馳突若神。

translations.literal: Men and women were brave and agile; they rode without saddles and were skilled with spears and swords; short armor covered chest and belly; their lacquered helmets were topped with cat and ox tails; they charged like spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Their men and women were fierce and agile, riding without saddles and wielding spear and sword with skill. Short armor covered chest and belly; lacquered helmets bristled with cat and ox tails; in a charge they seemed possessed.

sentences.zh: 凡兵出，以望苴子前驅。

translations.literal: Whenever troops marched out, Wangjuzi went ahead as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the army marched, Wangjuzi led the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 以清平子弟為羽儀。

translations.literal: Sons of Qingping Officials served as ceremonial guard.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of Qingping Officials formed the ceremonial guard.

sentences.zh: 王左右有羽儀長八人，清平官見王不得佩劍，唯羽儀長佩之為親信。

translations.literal: Eight ceremonial guard captains stood at the king's side; Qingping Officials could not wear swords when appearing before the king—only the guard captains could, as his trusted intimates.
translations.idiomatic: Eight guard captains stood at the king's side. Qingping Officials appearing before the king could not wear swords—only these captains could, as his personal confidants.

sentences.zh: 有六曹長，曹長有功補大軍將。

translations.literal: There were six Caozhang; Caozhang who performed meritorious service were promoted to Dajunjiang.
translations.idiomatic: There were six Caozhang; those who distinguished themselves were promoted to Dajunjiang.

sentences.zh: 大軍將十二，與清平官等列，日議事王所，出治軍壁稱節度，次補清平官。

translations.literal: Twelve Dajunjiang ranked with Qingping Officials; daily they deliberated at the king's court, and when sent out to manage garrison walls they were styled jiedushi; next in line for promotion to Qingping Official.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve Dajunjiang ranked with Qingping Officials, meeting daily at court to deliberate. Sent out to command garrisons they were styled jiedushi, and stood next in line for promotion to Qingping Official.

sentences.zh: 有內算官，代王裁處；

translations.literal: There was an inner accountant who decided matters on the king's behalf;
translations.idiomatic: An inner accountant decided affairs on the king's behalf;

sentences.zh: 外算官，記王所處分，以付六曹。

translations.literal: an outer accountant recorded the king's decisions and transmitted them to the six Caos.
translations.idiomatic: an outer accountant recorded the king's decisions and passed them to the six Caos.

sentences.zh: 外則有六節度，曰：弄棟、永昌、銀生、劍川、柘東、麗水。

translations.literal: Externally there were six military commissions: Nongdong, Yongchang, Yinsheng, Jianchuan, Zhedong, and Lishui.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the capital stood six military commissions: Nongdong, Yongchang, Yinsheng, Jianchuan, Zhedong, and Lishui.

sentences.zh: 有二都督：會川、通海。

translations.literal: There were two dudu: Huichuan and Tonghai.
translations.idiomatic: Two dudu territories existed: Huichuan and Tonghai.

sentences.zh: 有十瞼，夷語瞼若州，曰：雲南瞼、白厓瞼亦曰勃弄瞼、品淡瞼、邆川瞼、蒙舍瞼、大厘瞼亦曰史瞼、苴咩瞼亦曰陽瞼、蒙秦瞼、矣和瞼、趙川瞼。

translations.literal: There were ten lian—in the Yi tongue lian was like a prefecture: Yunnan Lian, Baiya Lian (also called Bonong Lian), Pindan Lian, Dichuan Lian, Mengshe Lian, Dali Lian (also called Shi Lian), Jumie Lian (also called Yang Lian), Mengqin Lian, Yihe Lian, and Zhaochuan Lian.
translations.idiomatic: There were ten lian—in Yi usage lian meant something like a prefecture: Yunnan, Baiya (also Bonong), Pindan, Dichuan, Mengshe, Dali (also Shi), Jumie (also Yang), Mengqin, Yihe, and Zhaochuan.

sentences.zh: 祁鮮山之西多瘴，地平，草冬不枯。

translations.literal: West of Qixian Mountain miasma was abundant; the land was level and grass did not wither in winter.
translations.idiomatic: West of Qixian Mountain miasma hung heavy, but the land was level and grass stayed green through winter.

sentences.zh: 自曲靖州至滇池，人水耕，食蠶以柘，蠶生閱二旬而繭，織錦縑精致。

translations.literal: From Qujing Prefecture to Lake Dian, people plowed with water and raised silkworms on mulberry; the worms produced cocoons in twenty days, and the woven brocades and fine silks were exquisite.
translations.idiomatic: From Qujing to Lake Dian the people irrigated their fields and raised silkworms on mulberry. Cocoons formed in twenty days, and the brocades and fine silks woven from them were exquisite.

sentences.zh: 大和、祁鮮而西，人不蠶，剖波羅樹實，狀若絮，紐縷而幅之。

translations.literal: West of Dahe and Qixian, people did not raise silkworms; they split the fruit of the pineapple tree, which was like cotton fluff, and spun and wove it into cloth.
translations.idiomatic: West of Dahe and Qixian people did not raise silkworms. They split the fruit of the pineapple tree—its fibers like cotton—and spun and wove it into cloth.

sentences.zh: 覽瞼井產鹽最鮮白，惟王得食，取足輒滅竈。

translations.literal: The salt from Lanlian Well was the whitest and finest; only the king might eat it, and once he had taken enough the brine pans were extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Salt from Lanlian Well was the whitest and finest. Only the king might use it; once he had taken his share the pans were shut down.

sentences.zh: 昆明城諸井皆產鹽，不征，群蠻食之。

translations.literal: All wells around Kunming City produced salt, untaxed; the tribal peoples ate it.
translations.idiomatic: Every well around Kunming City yielded salt, untaxed, for the tribes to consume.

sentences.zh: 永昌之西，野桑生石上，其林上屈兩向而下植，取以為弓，不筋漆而利，名曰瞑弓。

translations.literal: West of Yongchang, wild mulberry grew on stone; the grove bent in two directions downward to take root; taken for bows, they needed no sinew or lacquer yet were sharp—called "sleeping bows."
translations.idiomatic: West of Yongchang wild mulberry grew on stone, its branches bending down to root again. Shaped into bows without sinew or lacquer, they were nonetheless keen—called "sleeping bows."

sentences.zh: 長川諸山，往往有金，或披沙得之。

translations.literal: In the long valleys and many mountains gold was often found, sometimes obtained by panning sand.
translations.idiomatic: Gold was often found in the long valleys and mountain ranges, sometimes gathered by panning river sand.

sentences.zh: 麗水多金麩。

translations.literal: Lishui had abundant gold dust.
translations.idiomatic: Lishui abounded in gold dust.

sentences.zh: 越睒之西，多薦草，產善馬，世稱越睒駿。

translations.literal: West of Yueshan, good pasture grass grew in profusion and fine horses were bred; the age called them Yueshan steeds.
translations.idiomatic: West of Yueshan rich pasture produced fine horses renowned as Yueshan steeds.

sentences.zh: 始生若羔，歲中紐莎縻之，飲以米潘，七年可禦，日馳數百里。

translations.literal: At birth they were like lambs; midyear they were bound with hemp rope and fed rice gruel; at seven years they could be ridden and galloped several hundred li in a day.
translations.idiomatic: At birth they were lamb-sized; midway through the year they were hobbled with hemp rope and fed rice gruel. At seven they could be ridden and cover several hundred li in a day.

sentences.zh: 王出，建八旗，紫若青，白斿；

translations.literal: When the king went out, eight banners were raised—purple, indigo, and white streamers;
translations.idiomatic: When the king went abroad he raised eight banners—purple, indigo, and white streamers;

sentences.zh: 雉翣二；

translations.literal: two pheasant-tail fans;
translations.idiomatic: two pheasant-tail fans;

sentences.zh: 有旄鉞，紫囊之；

translations.literal: there were yak-tail axes wrapped in purple bags;
translations.idiomatic: yak-tail axes wrapped in purple bags;

sentences.zh: 翠蓋。

translations.literal: and an emerald canopy.
translations.idiomatic: and an emerald canopy.

sentences.zh: 王母曰信麼，亦曰九麼。

translations.literal: The queen mother was called Xinmo, also Jiumo.
translations.idiomatic: The queen mother was called Xinmo, also known as Jiumo.

sentences.zh: 妃曰進武。

translations.literal: The consort was called Jinwu.
translations.idiomatic: The principal consort was called Jinwu.

sentences.zh: 信麼出，亦建八旗，絳斿。

translations.literal: When Xinmo went out, she too raised eight banners with crimson streamers.
translations.idiomatic: When Xinmo went abroad she likewise raised eight banners with crimson streamers.

sentences.zh: 自曹長以降，系金佉苴。

translations.literal: From Caozhang downward, all wore golden juqie belts.
translations.idiomatic: From Caozhang downward, officials wore golden juqie belts.

sentences.zh: 尚絳紫。

translations.literal: Crimson and purple were favored.
translations.idiomatic: Crimson and purple were the favored colors.

sentences.zh: 有功加錦，又有功加金波羅。

translations.literal: For merit one added brocade; for further merit one added jinboluo.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious service earned brocade; greater merit earned jinboluo.

sentences.zh: 金波羅，虎皮也。

translations.literal: Jinboluo was tiger skin.
translations.idiomatic: Jinboluo meant tiger skin.

sentences.zh: 功小者，衿背不袖，次止於衿。

translations.literal: Lesser merit meant garments without sleeves on the back, or stopping at the collar.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser honors brought sleeveless backs, or decoration limited to the collar.

sentences.zh: 婦人不粉黛，以蘇澤發。

translations.literal: Women did not use powder or rouge; they dressed their hair with suze.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore no powder or rouge; they dressed their hair with suze.

sentences.zh: 貴者綾錦裙襦，上施錦一幅。

translations.literal: The noble wore brocade skirts and jackets with a panel of brocade draped above.
translations.idiomatic: Noblewomen wore brocade skirts and jackets with a brocade panel draped across the chest.

sentences.zh: 以兩股辮為鬟髻，耳綴珠貝、瑟瑟、虎魄。

translations.literal: They braided two locks into a topknot and hung pearls, shells, sese stones, and amber from their ears.
translations.idiomatic: They braided two locks into a topknot and hung pearls, shells, sese stones, and amber from their ears.

sentences.zh: 女、嫠婦與人亂，不禁，婚夕私相送。

translations.literal: Unmarried women and widows might consort freely with men without prohibition; on the wedding night they privately saw men off.
translations.idiomatic: Unmarried women and widows might take lovers freely; on the eve of marriage they privately saw men off.

sentences.zh: 已嫁有奸者，皆抵死。

translations.literal: If a married woman committed adultery, both were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Adultery by a married woman meant death for both parties.

sentences.zh: 俗以寅為正，四時大抵與中國小差。

translations.literal: They took the yin day as the start of the year; the four seasons differed only slightly from China.
translations.idiomatic: They reckoned the yin day as New Year's Day; their seasons differed only slightly from those of China.

sentences.zh: 膾魚寸，以胡瓜、椒、和之，號鵝闕。

translations.literal: Fish was sliced fine and mixed with cucumber, pepper, and seasonings—called Eque.
translations.idiomatic: Fish sliced fine and mixed with cucumber, pepper, and spices made a dish called Eque.

sentences.zh: 吹瓢笙，笙四管。

translations.literal: They played the gourd sheng; the sheng had four pipes.
translations.idiomatic: They played the gourd sheng, a four-pipe instrument.

sentences.zh: 酒至客前，以笙推盞勸釂。

translations.literal: When wine was set before a guest, the sheng was used to push the cup and urge drinking.
translations.idiomatic: When wine was placed before a guest, the sheng was used to push the cup forward and urge another round.

sentences.zh: 以繒帛及貝市易。

translations.literal: They traded with silk and shells.
translations.idiomatic: Trade was conducted in silk and cowrie shells.

sentences.zh: 貝者大若指，十六枚為一覓。

translations.literal: Shells were about finger-sized; sixteen made one mi.
translations.idiomatic: Cowries were about finger-sized; sixteen made one mi.

sentences.zh: 師行，人賫糧鬥五升，以二千五百人為一營。

translations.literal: On campaign each man carried five sheng of grain; twenty-five hundred men formed one camp.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign each soldier carried five sheng of grain; twenty-five hundred men formed one camp.

sentences.zh: 其法，前傷者養治，後傷者斬。

translations.literal: By their law, those wounded in front were cared for; those wounded in the rear were executed.
translations.idiomatic: By their law, wounds taken in the van were treated; wounds taken in the rear meant execution.

sentences.zh: 犁田以一牛三夫，前挽、中壓、後驅。

translations.literal: Plowing used one ox and three men—one pulling in front, one pressing in the middle, one driving from behind.
translations.idiomatic: Plowing required one ox and three men—one pulling ahead, one pressing in the middle, one driving from behind.

sentences.zh: 然專於農，無貴賤皆耕。

translations.literal: Yet they devoted themselves to farming; noble and common alike all plowed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they were devoted to farming; high and low alike worked the fields.

sentences.zh: 不繇役，人歲輸米二斗。

translations.literal: There was no corvée labor; each person paid two dou of rice per year.
translations.idiomatic: There was no corvée; each person paid two dou of rice annually.

sentences.zh: 一藝者給田，二收乃稅。

translations.literal: Those with a craft received fields; tax was levied only after two harvests.
translations.idiomatic: Craftsmen received land grants; tax was collected only after two harvests.

sentences.zh: 王蒙氏，父子以名相屬。

translations.literal: The royal house was the Meng clan; father and son linked their names in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The royal house was the Meng clan, father and son linking their names in succession.

sentences.zh: 自舍尨以來，有譜次可考。

translations.literal: From Shemang onward the genealogy can be traced.
translations.idiomatic: From Shemang onward the genealogy can be verified.

sentences.zh: 舍尨生獨邏，亦曰細奴邏，高宗時遣使者入朝，賜錦袍。

translations.literal: Shemang begot Duluo, also called Xinuluo; in the Gaozong era he sent envoys to court and was granted a brocade robe.
translations.idiomatic: Shemang begot Duluo, also called Xinuluo, who in Gaozong's reign sent envoys to court and received a brocade robe.

sentences.zh: 細奴邏生邏盛炎，邏盛炎生炎閣。

translations.literal: Xinuluo begot Luoshengyan; Luoshengyan begot Yanyan.
translations.idiomatic: Xinuluo begot Luoshengyan, and Luoshengyan begot Yanyan.

sentences.zh: 武後時，盛炎身入朝，妻方娠，生盛邏皮，喜曰：「我又有子，雖死唐地足矣。」

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time Shengyan came to court in person; his wife was pregnant and bore Shengluopi. He rejoiced: "I have another son; though I die in Tang territory, it is enough."
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu, Shengyan came to court in person. His wife was pregnant and bore Shengluopi. He rejoiced: "I have another son—even if I die on Tang soil, I am content."

sentences.zh: 炎閣立，死開元時。

translations.literal: Yanyan succeeded and died in the Kaiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyan succeeded and died during the Kaiyuan reign.

sentences.zh: 弟盛邏皮立，生皮邏閣，授特進，封臺登郡王。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shengluopi succeeded, begot Piluoge, was granted Special Grand Master, and enfeoffed as Prince of Taideng.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shengluopi took the throne, begot Piluoge, was granted Special Grand Master, and enfeoffed as Prince of Taideng.

sentences.zh: 炎閣未有子時，以閣羅鳳為嗣，及生子，還其宗，而名承合，遂不改。

translations.literal: When Yanyan had no son, he took Geluofeng as heir; when a son was born he restored Geluofeng to his own clan with the name Chenghé, and the arrangement was not changed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanyan had no son he adopted Geluofeng as heir; after a son was born he returned Geluofeng to his own clan under the name Chenghé, and the arrangement stood unchanged.

sentences.zh: 開元末，皮邏閣逐河蠻，取大和城，又襲大厘城守之，因城龍口，夷語山陂陀為「和」，故謂「大和」，以處閣羅鳳。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyuan, Piluoge drove out the River Man, took Dahe City, seized and held Dali City, and fortified Longkou. In the Yi language, a mountain slope was called "he," so it was called "Dahe"; there he placed Geluofeng.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Kaiyuan, Piluoge drove out the River Man, took Dahe City, seized and held Dali City, and fortified Longkou. In the Yi language, a mountain slope was called "he," so it was called "Dahe"; there he placed Geluofeng.

sentences.zh: 天子詔賜皮邏閣名歸義。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven decreed that Piluoge be granted the name Guiyi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor decreed that Piluoge be granted the name Guiyi.

sentences.zh: 當是時，五詔微，歸義獨強，乃厚以利啖劍南節度使王昱，求合六詔為一。

translations.literal: At that time the Five Zhao were weak while Guiyi alone was strong; he lavishly bribed Jiannan Military Commissioner Wang Yu to seek union of the Six Zhao into one.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Five Zhao had waned while Guiyi alone grew strong. He lavishly bribed Jiannan Military Commissioner Wang Yu to petition for uniting the Six Zhao under one rule.

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 歸義已並群蠻，遂破吐蕃，浸驕大。

translations.literal: Guyi had already united all the tribal peoples, then defeated the Tibetans, and gradually grew proud and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Having brought the tribal peoples under his rule, Piluoge went on to defeat the Tibetans—and with each victory his pride swelled.

sentences.zh: 入朝，天子亦為加禮。

translations.literal: When he came to court, the Son of Heaven also treated him with added honor.
translations.idiomatic: When he visited the capital, the emperor received him with special distinction.

sentences.zh: 又以破渳蠻功，馳遣中人冊為雲南王，賜錦袍、金鈿帶七事。

translations.literal: Also, on account of the merit of defeating the Meng tribes, [the court] urgently dispatched a eunuch to invest him as King of Yunnan, granting a brocade robe and the seven items of a gold-inlaid belt.
translations.idiomatic: For his victory over the Meng tribes, the court quickly sent an imperial envoy to enfoff him as King of Yunnan, bestowing a brocade robe and the full regalia of a gold-studded belt.

sentences.zh: 於是徙治大和城。

translations.literal: Thereupon he moved his seat of government to Dali City.
translations.idiomatic: He accordingly relocated his capital to Dali.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，遣閣羅鳳子鳳迦異入宿衛，拜鴻臚卿，恩賜良異。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianbao reign, [Piluoge] sent Geluofeng's son Fengjiayi to serve in the palace guard, appointing him Director of the Court of State Ceremonial, with excellent and special favors.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao era, Piluoge sent Geluofeng's son Fengjiayi to serve as a hostage at court, where he was appointed Director of the Court of State Ceremonial and lavished with exceptional honors.

sentences.zh: 七載，歸義死，閣羅鳳立，襲王，以其子鳳迦異為陽瓜州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Guyi died; Geluofeng succeeded him, inherited the kingship, and appointed his son Fengjiayi as prefect of Yangguazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tianbao, Piluoge died and Geluofeng took the throne, installing his son Fengjiayi as prefect of Yangguazhou.

sentences.zh: 初，安寧城有五鹽井，人得煮鬻自給。

translations.literal: Initially, Anning City had five salt wells; the people could boil [salt] and sell it to support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Anning had five salt wells whose brine the local people boiled and sold to support themselves.

sentences.zh: 玄宗詔特進何履光以兵定南詔境，取安寧城及井，復立馬援銅柱，乃還。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong ordered Senior Adviser He Luguang to lead troops to pacify the Nanzhao border, seize Anning City and its wells, re-erect Ma Yuan's bronze column, and then return.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong dispatched He Luguang at the rank of Special Grand Master with an army to secure Nanzhao's territory, take Anning and its salt wells, restore Ma Yuan's bronze pillar, and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 鮮于仲通領劍南節度使，卞忿少方略。

translations.literal: Xianyu Zhongtong held the post of military governor of Jiannan; he was rash, angry, and lacked strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Zhongtong, military governor of Jiannan, was impulsive, quick to anger, and short on strategic sense.

sentences.zh: 故事，南詔嘗與妻子謁都督，過雲南，太守張虔陀私之，多所求丐，閣羅鳳不應。

translations.literal: By precedent, Nanzhao would visit the regional commander with his wife and children; passing through Yunnan, Prefect Zhang Qiantuo made advances toward her and made many demands; Geluofeng did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: By custom Nanzhao rulers brought their wives and children when paying respects to the regional commander; en route through Yunnan, Prefect Zhang Qiantuo propositioned the queen and piled on extortionate demands—which Geluofeng refused.

sentences.zh: 虔陀數詬靳之，陰表其罪。

translations.literal: Qiantuo repeatedly insulted and mocked him, and secretly memorialized the throne listing his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qiantuo repeatedly abused and belittled him while secretly denouncing him to the court.

sentences.zh: 由是忿怨，反，發兵攻虔陀，殺之，取姚州及小夷州凡三十二。

translations.literal: Because of this resentment and anger, he rebelled, raised troops to attack Qiantuo, killed him, and seized Yaozhou and thirty-two small Yi prefectures in all.
translations.idiomatic: Stung by outrage, Geluofeng rebelled, marched on Zhang Qiantuo, killed him, and captured Yaozhou along with thirty-two smaller frontier prefectures.

sentences.zh: 明年，仲通自將出戎、巂州，分二道進次曲州、靖州。

translations.literal: The next year, Zhongtong personally led troops out from Rong and Xi prefectures, dividing into two routes and advancing to encamp at Quzhou and Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhongtong personally took the field from Rong and Xi, splitting his forces along two routes toward Qu and Jing.

sentences.zh: 閣羅鳳遣使者謝罪，願還所虜，得自新，且城姚州；

translations.literal: Geluofeng sent envoys to apologize, expressing willingness to return captives, obtain renewal, and even fortify Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Geluofeng sent envoys to plead guilty, offering to release captives, make amends, and even garrison Yaozhou for the Tang.

sentences.zh: 如不聽，則歸命吐蕃，恐雲南非唐有。

translations.literal: If [the court] did not listen, then he would submit to the Tibetans, fearing Yunnan might no longer belong to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: If the court refused, he warned, he would throw in his lot with Tibet—and Yunnan might be lost to the Tang forever.

sentences.zh: 仲通怒，囚使者，進薄白厓城，大敗引還。

translations.literal: Zhongtong grew angry, imprisoned the envoys, advanced to press against White Cliff City, suffered a great defeat, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongtong flew into a rage, threw the envoys in chains, pushed on toward White Cliff City, was routed, and retreated in disarray.

sentences.zh: 閣羅鳳斂戰胔，築京觀，遂北臣吐蕃，吐蕃以為弟。

translations.literal: Geluofeng gathered the corpses from battle, built a victory mound of skulls, then submitted northward to the Tibetans; the Tibetans treated him as a younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Geluofeng collected the dead from the battlefield, erected a grisly victory tumulus, then went north to swear fealty to Tibet, who accepted him as a younger brother.

sentences.zh: 夷謂弟「鐘」，故稱「贊普鐘」，給金印，號「東帝」。

translations.literal: The Yi called younger brother "Zhong," so he was called "Zhong of the Tsenpo," given a gold seal, and titled "Eastern Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: In Yi usage "younger brother" was zhong; he was styled Zhong of the Tsenpo, granted a golden seal, and hailed as Emperor of the East.

sentences.zh: 揭碑國門，明不得已而叛，嘗曰：「我上世世奉中國，累封賞，後嗣容歸之。

translations.literal: He erected a stele at the state gate explaining that rebellion was unavoidable, once saying: "My forebears for generations served China, received repeated enfeoffments and rewards; may later generations be allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: At the national gate he raised a stele declaring that rebellion had been forced upon him, writing: "For generations my ancestors served China and were richly rewarded; let our descendants someday return.

sentences.zh: 若唐使者至，可指碑澡祓吾罪也。」

translations.literal: If a Tang envoy should arrive, one may point to this stele to wash away and absolve my crime."
translations.idiomatic: Should Tang envoys come, point them to this stele—it will cleanse me of the stain of treason."

sentences.zh: 會楊國忠以劍南節度當國，乃調天下兵凡十萬，使侍御史李宓討之，輦餉者尚不在。

translations.literal: Just then Yang Guozhong held Jiannan military governorship while dominating state affairs; he mobilized a hundred thousand troops from across the realm, dispatching Palace Censor Li Mi to campaign against [Nanzhao]; those who carted supplies are not yet counted.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Yang Guozhong, who controlled the empire while holding Jiannan, scraped together a hundred thousand men under Palace Censor Li Mi to punish Nanzhao—the supply train alone swelled that number further.

sentences.zh: 涉海而疫死相踵於道，宓敗於大和城，死者十八。

translations.literal: Crossing seas, those who died of plague followed one after another on the road; Mi was defeated at Dali City; the dead were eight-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Troops sickened and died in waves along the march; Li Mi was crushed before Dali—eight out of ten never came home.

sentences.zh: 亦會安祿山反，閣羅鳳因之取巂州會同軍，據清溪關，以破越析，梟於贈，西而降尋傳、驃諸國。

translations.literal: It also happened that An Lushan rebelled; Geluofeng took advantage to seize Xizhou's Huitong Army, hold Qingxi Pass, defeat Yuexi, behead him at Zeng, and westward subdue the Xunchuan and Piao states.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rose in rebellion, Geluofeng seized the moment: he took the Huitong garrison at Xizhou, seized Qingxi Pass, crushed Yuexi and displayed his head at Zeng, then marched west to bring the Xunchuan and Pyu peoples to heel.

sentences.zh: 尋傳蠻者，俗無絲纊，跣履榛棘不苦也。

translations.literal: The Xunchuan tribes, by custom, had no silk or hemp cloth; they went barefoot through brambles and thorns without finding it bitter.
translations.idiomatic: The Xunchuan people wore no silk or hemp; they walked barefoot through thorn and bramble as though it were nothing.

sentences.zh: 射豪豬，生食其肉。

translations.literal: They shot giant forest hogs and ate the meat raw.
translations.idiomatic: They hunted giant forest hogs and ate the flesh raw.

sentences.zh: 戰，以竹籠頭如兜鍪。

translations.literal: In battle, they used bamboo cage-helmets like iron caps.
translations.idiomatic: In war they wore bamboo cage-helmets shaped like iron caps.

sentences.zh: 其西有裸蠻，亦曰野蠻，漫散山中，無君長，作檻舍以居。

translations.literal: To their west were the naked tribes, also called the wild tribes; they wandered scattered in the mountains, had no chieftains, and built cage dwellings to live in.
translations.idiomatic: West of them lived the Naked Tribes—also called the Wild Tribes—scattered through the mountains without rulers, dwelling in cage-like huts.

sentences.zh: 男少女多，無田農，以木皮蔽形，婦或十或五共養一男子。

translations.literal: Men were few and women many; they did no field agriculture; they covered their bodies with tree bark; ten or five women together supported one man.
translations.idiomatic: Men were scarce and women plentiful; they tilled no fields, clothed themselves in bark, and as many as five or ten women might share one husband.

sentences.zh: 廣德初，鳳迦異築柘東城，諸葛亮石刻故在，文曰：「碑即仆，蠻為漢奴。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Guangde reign, Fengjiayi built Tuodong City; Zhuge Liang's stone inscription was still there, reading: "When this stele falls, the tribes become slaves of Han."
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangde, Fengjiayi built Tuodong City, where an inscription attributed to Zhuge Liang still stood: "When this stele topples, the tribes shall be slaves of Han."

sentences.zh: 夷畏誓，常以石搘捂。

translations.literal: The tribes feared this oath and always propped up the stone [with supports].
translations.idiomatic: The tribes feared the curse and always braced the stone against falling.

sentences.zh: 大歷十四年，閣羅鳳卒，以鳳迦異前死，立其孫異牟尋以嗣。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Dali, Geluofeng died; since Fengjiayi had died earlier, his grandson Yimouxun was installed to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of the Dali era, Geluofeng died; Fengjiayi having predeceased him, the throne passed to his grandson Yimouxun.

sentences.zh: 異牟尋有智數，善撫眾，略知書。

translations.literal: Yimouxun had wisdom and resourcefulness, was skilled at winning over the people, and had some knowledge of writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun was shrewd and capable, knew how to hold his people together, and was modestly literate.

sentences.zh: 母李，獨錦蠻女也。

translations.literal: His mother was surnamed Li, a woman of the Dujin tribe.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Li, came from the Dujin tribe.

sentences.zh: 獨錦蠻亦烏蠻種，在秦藏川南。

translations.literal: The Dujin tribe was also of the Wuman stock, located south of Qinzang River.
translations.idiomatic: The Dujin were another branch of the Wuman, living south of the Qinzang River.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，命其長為蹄州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era, [the court] appointed their chief as prefect of Tizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao the court made their chieftain prefect of Tizhou.

sentences.zh: 世與南詔婚聘。

translations.literal: For generations they exchanged marriage alliances with Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: For generations they had intermarried with Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 異牟尋立，悉眾二十萬入寇，與吐蕃並力。

translations.literal: When Yimouxun succeeded, he mobilized all his forces—two hundred thousand men—to raid, joining strength with the Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his accession Yimouxun mustered two hundred thousand men for invasion, fighting alongside Tibet.

sentences.zh: 一趨茂州，逾文川，擾灌口；

translations.literal: One [force] pressed toward Maozhou, crossed Wenchuan, and harassed Guankou.
translations.idiomatic: One column drove on Maozhou, crossed Wenchuan, and ravaged Guankou.

sentences.zh: 一趨扶、文，掠方維、白壩；

translations.literal: One pressed toward Fu and Wen, plundering Fangwei and Baiba.
translations.idiomatic: Another struck toward Fu and Wen, looting Fangwei and Baiba.

sentences.zh: 一侵黎、雅，叩邛郲關。

translations.literal: One invaded Li and Ya, assaulting Qiongxi Pass.
translations.idiomatic: A third invaded Li and Ya, battering at Qiongxi Pass.

sentences.zh: 令其下曰：「為我取蜀為東府，工伎悉送邏娑城，歲賦一縑。」

translations.literal: He ordered his subordinates: "Take Shu for me as the eastern capital; send all craftsmen to Luosuo City; pay one bolt of silk in annual tribute."
translations.idiomatic: He told his commanders: "Make Shu our eastern capital; send every skilled artisan to Luosuo City; and pay one bolt of silk each year in tribute."

sentences.zh: 於是進陷城聚，人率走山。

translations.literal: Thereupon they advanced and captured walled settlements; the people mostly fled into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: They swept through towns and forts while the populace fled en masse into the hills.

sentences.zh: 德宗發禁衛及幽州軍以援東川，與山南兵合，大敗異牟尋眾，斬首六千級，禽生捕傷甚眾，顛踣厓峭且十萬。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong dispatched the palace guard and Youzhou troops to aid Dongchuan; joining with Shannan forces, they greatly defeated Yimouxun's army, beheading six thousand, capturing many alive and wounded; those who tumbled from steep cliffs numbered nearly a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong sent the imperial guard and Youzhou armies to relieve Dongchuan; combined with Shannan troops they shattered Yimouxun's host—six thousand heads taken, countless prisoners—and nearly a hundred thousand more perished on the cliffs.

sentences.zh: 異牟尋懼，更徙苴咩城，築袤十五里，吐蕃封為日東王。

translations.literal: Yimouxun grew afraid and moved again to Yangjumie City, building [walls] fifteen li in circumference; the Tibetans enfoffed him as King of the Eastern Sun.
translations.idiomatic: Frightened, Yimouxun relocated to Yangjumie City and ringed it with fifteen li of walls; Tibet crowned him King of the Eastern Sun.

sentences.zh: 然吐蕃責賦重數，悉奪其險立營候，歲索兵助防，異牟尋稍苦之。

translations.literal: Yet the Tibetans imposed heavy and frequent levies, seized all their strategic points to establish garrison posts, and each year demanded troops to help defend; Yimouxun gradually found this burdensome.
translations.idiomatic: But Tibet taxed them relentlessly, seized every defensible pass for garrisons, and every year demanded troops for joint defense—until Yimouxun could bear it no longer.

sentences.zh: 故西瀘令鄭回者，唐官也，往巂州破，為所虜。

translations.literal: There was one Zheng Hui, formerly a magistrate of Xilu, a Tang official; when Xizhou fell he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Among the captives was Zheng Hui, once magistrate of Xilu—a Tang official taken when Xizhou fell.

sentences.zh: 閣羅鳳重其惇儒，號「蠻利」，俾教子弟，得棰搒，故國中無不憚。

translations.literal: Geluofeng valued his honest learning, called him "Barbarian Profit," had him teach the young, and [Zheng] could use the whip and cudgel; therefore within the state none did not fear [him].
translations.idiomatic: Geluofeng respected his integrity and erudition, styled him "Barbarian Profit," and set him to instruct the young—with the lash and rod at his disposal, so that none in the kingdom dared defy him.

sentences.zh: 後以為清平官。

translations.literal: Later he was made a Qingping official.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed a Qingping minister.

sentences.zh: 說異牟尋曰：「中國有禮義，少求責，非若吐蕃惏刻無極也。

translations.literal: He said to Yimouxun: "China has ritual and righteousness, makes few demands, and is not like the Tibetans, who are insatiably greedy and harsh without limit.
translations.idiomatic: He told Yimouxun: "The Middle Kingdom observes ritual and right conduct and asks little in return—not like Tibet, insatiable and merciless without end.

sentences.zh: 今棄之復歸唐，無遠戍勞，利莫大此。」

translations.literal: Now to abandon them and return to Tang—without distant garrison labor—the benefit would be greatest."
translations.idiomatic: To cast Tibet aside and come back to Tang, free of distant frontier burdens—that would be the greatest gain of all."

sentences.zh: 異牟尋善之，稍謀內附，然未敢發。

translations.literal: Yimouxun approved of this, gradually plotted inward submission, but did not yet dare to act.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun liked the idea and quietly plotted defection, but did not yet dare move.

sentences.zh: 亦會節度使韋臯撫諸蠻有威惠，諸蠻頗得異牟尋語，白於臯，時貞元四年也。

translations.literal: It also happened that Military Governor Wei Gao pacified the various tribes with both authority and kindness; the tribes largely obtained Yimouxun's words and reported them to Gao—this was in the fourth year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wei Gao, military governor of the region, ruled the tribes with a blend of force and grace; word of Yimouxun's intentions reached him through tribal intermediaries—in the fourth year of Zhenyuan.

sentences.zh: 臯乃遣諜者遺書，吐蕃疑之，因責大臣子為質，異牟尋愈怨。

translations.literal: Gao then sent spies bearing letters; the Tibetans grew suspicious and therefore demanded the sons of great ministers as hostages; Yimouxun's resentment deepened.
translations.idiomatic: Gao sent secret envoys with letters; Tibet grew suspicious and demanded hostages from his chief ministers' sons—and Yimouxun's resentment only deepened.

sentences.zh: 後五年，乃決策遣使者三人異道同趣成都，遺臯帛書曰：

translations.literal: Five years later, he finally decided to send three envoys by different routes together toward Chengdu, presenting Gao with a letter written on silk:
translations.idiomatic: Five years on he resolved to act, dispatching three envoys by separate routes to Chengdu with a letter on silk for Gao:

sentences.zh: 異牟尋世為唐臣，曩緣張虔陀誌在吞侮，中使者至，不為澄雪，舉部惶窘，得生異計。

translations.literal: Yimouxun for generations has been a subject of Tang; formerly because Prefect Zhang Qiantuo's intent was to swallow and insult [us], when the Middle Kingdom's envoys arrived they did not clear our name; the whole tribe was fearful and distressed, and [we] survived only by a desperate stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun's house has served Tang for generations; once Prefect Zhang Qiantuo sought to humiliate and devour us, and when Tang envoys came they did not vindicate us—our people were left terrified and cornered, and we survived only by desperate expedient.

sentences.zh: 鮮于仲通比年舉兵，故自新無繇。

translations.literal: Xianyu Zhongtong for successive years raised troops; therefore there was no way to renew [allegiance].
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Zhongtong campaigned year after year, so we had no path back to grace.

sentences.zh: 代祖棄背，吐蕃欺孤背約。

translations.literal: Generation after generation our ancestors were abandoned and betrayed; the Tibetans deceived the isolated and broke their covenant.
translations.idiomatic: Generation upon generation our forebears were cast off and betrayed; Tibet tricked us in our isolation and broke faith.

sentences.zh: 神川都督論訥舌使浪人利羅式眩惑部姓，發兵無時，今十二年。

translations.literal: The Shenchuan regional commander Lun Nashe sent the Lang clansman Liluoshi to bewitch the tribal clans and mobilize troops without fixed times—for twelve years now.
translations.idiomatic: For twelve years now the Shenchuan commander Lun Nashe has sent the Lang tribesman Liluoshi to beguile our clans and call up troops at whim.

sentences.zh: 此一忍也。

translations.literal: This is the first thing endured.
translations.idiomatic: That was the first indignity.

sentences.zh: 天禍蕃廷，降釁蕭墻，太子弟兄流竄，近臣橫汙，皆尚結贊陰計，以行屠害，平日功臣，無一二在。

translations.literal: Heaven brought calamity on the Tibetan court: rebellion arose within the palace walls; the crown prince and his brothers were exiled; close ministers were slaughtered—all through Shang Jiezan's secret plots, carrying out massacre; of the meritorious officials of ordinary days, not one or two remain.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven itself turned on the Tibetan court: rebellion erupted at the palace gates; the crown prince and his brothers were driven into exile; loyal ministers were butchered—all by Shang Jiezan's hidden designs. Of the great men who once served the throne, scarcely one or two survive.

sentences.zh: 訥舌等皆冊封王；

translations.literal: Nashe and the others were all invested as kings.
translations.idiomatic: Nashe and his ilk were all enfoffed as kings.

sentences.zh: 小國奏請，不令上達。

translations.literal: Petitions from small states were not allowed to reach the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Petitions from lesser kingdoms were never permitted to reach the Tibetan throne.

sentences.zh: 此二忍也。

translations.literal: This is the second thing endured.
translations.idiomatic: That was the second indignity.

sentences.zh: 又遣訥舌逼城於鄙，弊邑不堪。

translations.literal: Also, [they] sent Nashe to press the city at our borders; our poor towns could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: They also sent Nashe to menace our border towns until our settlements could endure no more.

sentences.zh: 利羅式私取重賞，部落皆驚。

translations.literal: Liluoshi privately took heavy rewards; all the tribes were alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Liluoshi took hefty bribes on the side, and every tribe trembled.

sentences.zh: 此三忍也。

translations.literal: This is the third thing endured.
translations.idiomatic: That was the third indignity.

sentences.zh: 又利羅式罵使者曰：「滅子之將，非我其誰？

translations.literal: Also Liluoshi cursed the envoy, saying: "The general who destroys your son—if not I, then who?
translations.idiomatic: Liluoshi even reviled our envoy: "The man who will destroy your son—if not me, then who?

sentences.zh: 子所富當為我有。」

translations.literal: The wealth you possess ought to become mine."
translations.idiomatic: Everything you own should be mine."

sentences.zh: 此四忍也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth thing endured.
translations.idiomatic: That was the fourth indignity.

sentences.zh: 今吐蕃委利羅式甲士六十侍衛，因知懷惡不謬。

translations.literal: Now Tibet has entrusted Liluoshi with sixty armored men as guards; thus we know their malicious intent is not mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: Now Tibet has given Liluoshi sixty armored guards—proof enough that their malice is real.

sentences.zh: 此一難忍也。

translations.literal: This is the first thing hard to endure.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first thing beyond bearing.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃陰毒野心，輒懷搏噬。

translations.literal: The Tibetans are secretly poisonous in heart and wild in ambition; they constantly harbor thoughts of seizing and devouring.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet is venomous at heart and ravenous by nature, always hungering to seize and consume.

sentences.zh: 有如俞生，實汙辱先人，辜負部落。

translations.literal: There are men like Yu Sheng who truly defile and disgrace their ancestors and betray their tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Yu Sheng truly dishonor their forebears and betray their people.

sentences.zh: 此二難忍也。

translations.literal: This is the second thing hard to endure.
translations.idiomatic: That is the second thing beyond bearing.

sentences.zh: 往退渾王為吐蕃所害，孤遺受欺；

translations.literal: Formerly the Tuyuhun king was killed by the Tibetans; the orphaned and bereaved were deceived.
translations.idiomatic: Once the king of Tuyuhun was murdered by Tibet; the orphaned and bereft were duped.

sentences.zh: 西山女王，見奪其位；

translations.literal: The queen of the Western Mountains had her position seized.
translations.idiomatic: The queen of the Western Mountains was robbed of her throne.

sentences.zh: 拓拔首領，並蒙誅刈；

translations.literal: The Tuoba chieftains were all put to the sword.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba chieftains were slaughtered to the last.

sentences.zh: 仆固誌忠，身亦喪亡。

translations.literal: Pugu Zhizhong also lost his life.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Zhizhong, too, met his death.

sentences.zh: 每虜一朝亦被此禍。

translations.literal: Every tribe that submitted to the Tibetans likewise suffered this calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Every people who bowed to Tibet suffered the same fate.

sentences.zh: 此三難忍也。

translations.literal: This is the third thing hard to endure.
translations.idiomatic: That is the third thing beyond bearing.

sentences.zh: 往朝廷降使招撫，情心無二，詔函信節，皆送蕃廷。

translations.literal: Formerly when the court sent envoys to summon and pacify, our hearts were without duplicity; imperial edicts, letters, and credentials were all delivered to the Tibetan court.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang sent envoys to win us back, our loyalty was undivided—yet every edict, letter, and credential was handed straight to Lhasa.

sentences.zh: 雖知中夏至仁，業為蕃臣，吞聲無訴。

translations.literal: Although we knew the Middle Kingdom reached utmost benevolence, [we] had already become subjects of Tibet and swallowed our voices without appeal.
translations.idiomatic: We knew Tang's mercy was boundless, but we were already Tibet's vassals and could only swallow our grief in silence.

sentences.zh: 此四難忍也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth thing hard to endure.
translations.idiomatic: That is the fourth thing beyond bearing.

sentences.zh: 曾祖有寵先帝，後嗣率蒙襲王，人知禮樂，本唐風化。

translations.literal: Our ancestors enjoyed favor from the former emperor; later generations have all inherited enfeoffment as kings; our people know ritual and music—the original wind and transformation of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Our forebears were cherished by the late emperor; every successor has inherited a royal seal; our people know ritual and music—it is Tang's civilization in our bones.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃詐紿百情，懷惡相戚。

translations.literal: The Tibetans deceive with a hundred schemes and harbor malice that feeds on itself.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet deceives with endless stratagems, malice breeding malice.

sentences.zh: 異牟尋願竭誠日新，歸款天子。

translations.literal: Yimouxun wishes to exhaust his sincerity day by day in renewal and return in allegiance to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun pledges to renew his loyalty day by day and submit once more to the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 請加戍劍南、西山、涇原等州，安西鎮守，揚兵四臨，委回鶻諸國，所在侵掠，使吐蕃勢分力散，不能為強，此西南隅不煩天兵，可以立功雲。

translations.literal: We request increased garrisons in Jiannan, the Western Mountains, Jingyuan, and other prefectures, and garrisons in Anxi, displaying troops on four sides, entrusting the Uyghurs and other states to raid wherever they can, so that Tibetan power is divided and strength scattered and cannot become strong; thus in this southwestern corner the Son of Heaven need not trouble imperial troops, and merit may be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that Tang strengthen garrisons in Jiannan, the Western Mountains, Jingyuan, and Anxi, show force on every frontier, and unleash the Uyghurs and other allies to raid wherever they can—splitting Tibet's power so it cannot stand whole. Then this corner of the southwest can be won without imperial armies marching south.

sentences.zh: 且贈臯黃金、丹砂。

translations.literal: Moreover he presented Gao with gold and cinnabar.
translations.idiomatic: With the letter he sent Gao gifts of gold and cinnabar.

sentences.zh: 臯護送使者京師，使者奏異牟尋請歸天子，為唐藩輔。

translations.literal: Gao escorted the envoys to the capital; the envoys memorialized that Yimouxun requested to return to the Son of Heaven and serve Tang as a frontier vassal.
translations.idiomatic: Gao escorted the envoys to court, where they reported Yimouxun's wish to renew allegiance and serve Tang as a frontier ally.

sentences.zh: 獻金，示順革；

translations.literal: The gold showed submission and reform.
translations.idiomatic: The gold signified submission and a change of heart.

sentences.zh: 丹，赤心也。

translations.literal: The cinnabar [signified] a red heart.
translations.idiomatic: The cinnabar signified a loyal heart.

sentences.zh: 德宗嘉之，賜以詔書，命臯遣諜往覘。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong commended this, granted an imperial edict, and ordered Gao to send spies to observe.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong was pleased, issued an edict in reply, and ordered Gao to send agents to verify the overture.

sentences.zh: 臯令其屬崔佐時至羊苴咩城。

translations.literal: Gao ordered his subordinate Cui Zuoshi to go to Yangjumie City.
translations.idiomatic: Gao dispatched his officer Cui Zuoshi to Yangjumie City.

sentences.zh: 時吐蕃使者多在，陰戒佐時衣牂柯使者服以入。

translations.literal: At that time many Tibetan envoys were present; [Gao] secretly instructed Zuoshi to wear the dress of a Zangke envoy to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetan envoys were still thick on the ground; Gao secretly told Zuoshi to enter disguised in the garb of a Zangke envoy.

sentences.zh: 佐時曰：「我乃唐使者，安得從小夷服？」

translations.literal: Zuoshi said: "I am a Tang envoy—how can I follow the dress of petty tribes?"
translations.idiomatic: Zuoshi protested: "I am an envoy of Tang—how can I dress like some minor tribe?"

sentences.zh: 異牟尋夜迎之，設位陳燎，佐時即宣天子意。

translations.literal: Yimouxun received him by night, set out seats and kindled torches; Zuoshi immediately proclaimed the Son of Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun welcomed him by night, set out seats and lit beacon fires; Zuoshi at once delivered the emperor's message.

sentences.zh: 異牟尋內畏吐蕃，顧左右失色，流涕再拜受命。

translations.literal: Yimouxun inwardly feared the Tibetans; he looked to left and right and changed color, wept, and bowed twice to accept the command.
translations.idiomatic: Inwardly terrified of Tibet, Yimouxun glanced at his attendants, went pale, wept, and bowed twice to accept the decree.

sentences.zh: 使其子閣勸及清平官與佐時盟點蒼山，載書四：一藏神祠石室，一沈西洱水，一置祖廟，一以進天子。

translations.literal: He had his son Gequan and the Qingping officials join Zuoshi in covenant at Cangshan; four copies of the pact were made: one stored in the stone chamber of the spirit shrine, one sunk in the western Erhai, one placed in the ancestral temple, and one presented to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his son Gequan and the Qingping ministers to swear alliance with Zuoshi on Cangshan; four copies of the pact were made—one sealed in the shrine's stone vault, one sunk in Erhai's western waters, one kept in the ancestral temple, and one sent to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 乃發兵攻吐蕃使者殺之，刻金契以獻，遣曹長南羅、趙迦寬隨佐時入朝。

translations.literal: Thereupon he raised troops, attacked and killed the Tibetan envoys, carved a gold covenant to present, and dispatched Cao Zhang Nanluo and Zhao Jiakuan to follow Zuoshi to court.
translations.idiomatic: Then he mobilized troops, fell upon the Tibetan envoys and killed them, carved a gold covenant as tribute, and sent Cao Zhang Nanluo and Zhao Jiakuan to accompany Zuoshi to the capital.

sentences.zh: 初，吐蕃與回鶻戰，殺傷甚，乃調南詔萬人。

translations.literal: Initially, when Tibet and the Uyghurs fought with heavy casualties on both sides, [Tibet] then mobilized ten thousand men from Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after a bloody war between Tibet and the Uyghurs, Tibet levied ten thousand men from Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 異牟尋欲襲吐蕃，陽示寡弱，以五千人行，許之。

translations.literal: Yimouxun wished to attack Tibet; he feigned weakness and offered only five thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun planned to strike Tibet but feigned weakness, offering only five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 即自將數萬踵後，晝夜行，大破吐蕃於神川，遂斷鐵橋，溺死以萬計，俘其五王。

translations.literal: He himself followed with tens of thousands, marching day and night, and routed the Tibetans at Shenchuan; he then severed the Iron Bridge, drowning tens of thousands, and captured five of their kings.
translations.idiomatic: He himself followed with tens of thousands, marching day and night, and crushed the Tibetans at Shenchuan; he cut the Iron Bridge, drowning tens of thousands and capturing five Tibetan kings.

sentences.zh: 乃遣弟湊羅棟、清平官尹仇寬等二十七人入獻地圖、方物，請復號南詔。

translations.literal: He then sent his younger brother Cuoluodong, Qingping Official Yin Qiukuan, and twenty-seven others to present maps and local products, requesting restoration of the name Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent his brother Cuoluodong, Qingping Official Yin Qiukuan, and twenty-seven others to court with maps and tribute, asking to restore the name Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 帝賜賚有加，拜仇寬左散騎常侍，封高溪郡王。

translations.literal: The emperor granted lavish rewards, appointing Qiukuan Left Regular Attendant of the Palace Guard and enfeoffing him as Prince of Gaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rewarded them generously, appointing Qiukuan Left Regular Attendant of the Palace Guard and enfeoffing him as Prince of Gaoxi.

sentences.zh: 明年夏六月，冊異牟尋為南詔王。

translations.literal: The next summer, in the sixth month, Yimouxun was invested as King of Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: The following summer, in the sixth month, Yimouxun was invested as King of Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 以祠部郎中袁滋持節領使，成都少尹龐頎副之，崔佐時為判官；

translations.literal: Court Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites Yuan Zi was dispatched bearing the imperial insignia as chief envoy, with Chengdu Assistant Governor Pang Qi as deputy and Cui Zuoshi as administrative officer;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zi of the Ministry of Rites was sent bearing the imperial insignia as chief envoy, with Chengdu Assistant Governor Pang Qi as deputy and Cui Zuoshi as administrative officer;

sentences.zh: 俱文珍為宣慰使，劉幽巖為判官。

translations.literal: Ju Wenzhen served as pacification commissioner, with Liu Youyan as administrative officer.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Wenzhen served as pacification commissioner, with Liu Youyan as administrative officer.

sentences.zh: 賜黃金印，文曰「貞元冊南詔印」。

translations.literal: A golden seal was granted, inscribed "Zhenyuan Investiture Seal of Nanzhao."
translations.idiomatic: They were granted a golden seal inscribed "Zhenyuan Investiture Seal of Nanzhao."

sentences.zh: 滋至大和城，異牟尋遣兄蒙細羅勿等以良馬六十迎之，金鍐玉珂，兵振鐸夾路陳。

translations.literal: When Zi reached Dahe City, Yimouxun sent his elder brother Meng Xiluowu and others with sixty fine horses to welcome him—golden bells and jade bridles, soldiers shaking bells lining the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Zi reached Dahe City, Yimouxun sent his brother Meng Xiluowu with sixty fine horses to welcome him—golden bells and jade bridles, with soldiers shaking bells along the route.

sentences.zh: 異牟尋金甲，蒙虎皮，執雙鐸韒。

translations.literal: Yimouxun wore golden armor, a tiger-skin cloak, and held twin iron maces.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun wore golden armor and a tiger-skin cloak, gripping twin iron maces.

sentences.zh: 執矛千人衛，大象十二引於前，騎軍、徒軍以次列。

translations.literal: A thousand spearmen guarded him; twelve elephants led the way, with cavalry and infantry arrayed behind.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand spearmen formed his guard; twelve elephants led the procession, with cavalry and infantry ranked behind.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，授冊，異牟尋率官屬北面立，宣慰使東向，冊使南向，乃讀詔冊。

translations.literal: At dawn the investiture was performed: Yimouxun and his officials stood facing north, the pacification commissioner faced east, the investiture commissioner faced south, and the edict of investiture was read.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn came the investiture: Yimouxun and his officials stood facing north, the pacification commissioner east, the investiture commissioner south, and the edict of investiture was read aloud.

sentences.zh: 相者引異牟尋去位，跽受冊印，稽首再拜；

translations.literal: An usher led Yimouxun from his place; kneeling, he received the seal of investiture and bowed twice;
translations.idiomatic: An usher guided Yimouxun forward; kneeling, he received the investiture seal and bowed twice;

sentences.zh: 又受賜服備物，退曰：「開元、天寶中，曾祖及祖皆蒙冊襲王，自此五十年。

translations.literal: he also received the gifts of robes and objects, then withdrew, saying: "In the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, my great-grandfather and grandfather were both invested as kings; fifty years have passed since then.
translations.idiomatic: He also received robes and gifts, then withdrew and said: "In the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras my great-grandfather and grandfather were both invested as kings—fifty years have passed since then.

sentences.zh: 貞元皇帝洗痕錄功，復賜爵命，子子孫孫永為唐臣。」

translations.literal: The Zhenyuan Emperor has washed away our stain and recorded our merit, restoring our rank and title; our sons and grandsons shall forever be subjects of Tang."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong has washed away our stain and recorded our merit, restoring rank and title—our sons and grandsons shall forever be subjects of Tang."

sentences.zh: 因大會其下，享使者，出銀平脫馬頭盤二，謂滋曰：「此天寶時先君以鴻臚少卿宿衛，皇帝所賜也。」

translations.literal: He then held a great assembly for his subordinates and entertained the envoys, producing two silver repoussé horse-head platters and telling Zi: "These were granted by the emperor when my forefather served as Director of the Court of State Ceremonial in the palace guard during Tianbao."
translations.idiomatic: He then feasted his subordinates and entertained the envoys, bringing out two silver repoussé horse-head platters and telling Zi: "These were granted by the emperor when my forefather served as Director of the Court of State Ceremonial in the palace guard during Tianbao."

sentences.zh: 有笛工、歌女，皆垂白，示滋曰：「此先君歸國時，皇帝賜胡部、龜茲音聲二列，今喪亡略盡，唯二人故在。」

translations.literal: There were flute players and singing girls, all white-haired; he showed them to Zi, saying: "When my forefather returned to allegiance, the emperor granted two troupes of Hu and Kucha music; nearly all have died—only these two remain."
translations.idiomatic: Flute players and singing girls, all white-haired, were presented to Zi: "When my forefather returned to allegiance, the emperor granted two troupes of Hu and Kucha music; nearly all have perished—only these two remain."

sentences.zh: 酒行，異牟尋坐，奉觴滋前，滋受觴曰：「南詔當深思祖考成業，抱忠竭誠，永為西南藩屏，使後嗣有以不絕也。」

translations.literal: As wine was served, Yimouxun seated himself and offered a cup before Zi; Zi received it and said: "Nanzhao should deeply ponder the achievements of its forefathers, hold loyalty and sincerity, and forever serve as the southwestern bulwark, so that posterity may never be cut off."
translations.idiomatic: As wine was served, Yimouxun rose and offered a cup to Zi, who received it and said: "Nanzhao should honor its forefathers' achievements, hold fast to loyalty, and forever serve as the southwestern bulwark, so that posterity may never be cut off."

sentences.zh: 異牟尋拜曰：「敢不承使者所命。」

translations.literal: Yimouxun bowed and said: "How dare I not accept the envoy's command."
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun bowed and said: "How could I fail to obey the envoy's command?"

sentences.zh: 滋還，復遣清平官尹輔酋等七人謝天子，獻鐸鞘、浪劍、郁刃、生金、瑟瑟、牛黃、虎珀、氎、紡絲、象、犀、越睒統倫馬。

translations.literal: When Zi returned, Yimouxun again sent Qingping Official Yin Fuqiu and seven others to thank the Son of Heaven, presenting duoshe, langjian, yuren, raw gold, sese stones, ox bezoar, amber, woolen cloth, spun silk, elephants, rhinoceros horn, and Yueshan thoroughbred horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Zi departed, Yimouxun sent Qingping Official Yin Fuqiu and seven others to thank the emperor, presenting duoshe, langjian, yuren blades, raw gold, sese stones, ox bezoar, amber, woolens, spun silk, elephants, rhinoceros horn, and Yueshan thoroughbreds.

sentences.zh: 鐸鞘者，狀如殘刃，有孔傍達，出麗水，飾以金，所擊無不洞，夷人尤寶，月以血祭之。

translations.literal: Duoshe resembled a broken blade with holes along the side; it came from Lishui and was decorated with gold; nothing it struck failed to be pierced—the Yi especially treasured it and each month offered blood sacrifice to it.
translations.idiomatic: Duoshe resembled a broken blade with holes along the edge, mined from Lishui and decorated with gold; nothing it struck escaped pierced—the Yi especially treasured it and offered it monthly blood sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 郁刃，鑄時以毒藥並治，取迎躍如星者，凡十年乃成，淬以馬血，以金犀飾鐔首，傷人即死。

translations.literal: Yuren was cast with poison mixed into the smelting; only metal showing starlike flecks was chosen; ten years were required to complete one; it was quenched in horse blood and the guard decorated with gold and rhinoceros horn—wounds from it meant death.
translations.idiomatic: Yuren was cast with poison in the alloy; only metal showing starlike flecks was chosen; ten years were needed to finish one blade, quenched in horse blood with gold and rhinoceros horn on the guard—a wound from it meant death.

sentences.zh: 浪人所鑄，故亦名浪劍，王所佩者，傳七世矣。

translations.literal: The Lang people cast it, hence also called langjian; the one the king wore had been handed down seven generations.
translations.idiomatic: The Lang people cast it, hence the name langjian; the blade the king wore had passed through seven generations.

sentences.zh: 異牟尋攻吐蕃，復取昆明城以食鹽池。

translations.literal: Yimouxun attacked Tibet and recaptured Kunming City to control the salt ponds.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun attacked Tibet and recaptured Kunming City to control the salt ponds.

sentences.zh: 又破施蠻、順蠻，並虜其王，置白厓城；

translations.literal: He also defeated the Shi Man and Shun Man, capturing both their kings and establishing Baiya City;
translations.idiomatic: He also defeated the Shi Man and Shun Man, capturing both kings and establishing Baiya City;

sentences.zh: 因定磨些蠻，隸昆山西爨故地；

translations.literal: then he settled the Mosuo Man and placed them under the old Cuan territory west of Kunming;
translations.idiomatic: then he settled the Mosuo Man in the old Cuan territory west of Kunming;

sentences.zh: 破茫蠻，掠弄棟蠻、漢裳蠻，以實雲南東北。

translations.literal: he defeated the Mang Man and plundered the Nongdong Man and Han Shang Man to populate northeastern Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: he defeated the Mang Man and plundered the Nongdong and Han Shang Man to populate northeastern Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 施蠻者，在鐵橋西北，居大施睒、斂尋睒。

translations.literal: The Shi Man lived northwest of the Iron Bridge, dwelling at Dashan and Lianxun.
translations.idiomatic: The Shi Man lived northwest of the Iron Bridge, at Dashan and Lianxun.

sentences.zh: 男子衣繒布；

translations.literal: Men wore silk cloth;
translations.idiomatic: Men wore silk cloth;

sentences.zh: 女分發直額，為一髻垂後，跣而衣皮。

translations.literal: women parted their hair straight across the forehead, gathered it in one topknot hanging behind, went barefoot, and wore leather.
translations.idiomatic: women parted their hair straight across the forehead, gathered it in one topknot at the back, went barefoot, and wore leather.

sentences.zh: 順蠻本與施蠻雜居劍、共諸川。

translations.literal: The Shun Man originally lived mixed with the Shi Man along the Jian and Gong rivers.
translations.idiomatic: The Shun Man originally lived mixed with the Shi Man along the Jian and Gong rivers.

sentences.zh: 咩羅皮、鐸羅望既失邆川、浪穹，奪劍、共地，由是徙鐵橋，在劍睒西北四百里，號劍羌。

translations.literal: After Mieluopi and Tluowang lost Dichuan and Langqiong and seized Jian and Gong territory, they moved to the Iron Bridge, four hundred li northwest of Jianshan, and styled themselves Jian Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: After Mieluopi and Tluowang lost Dichuan and Langqiong and seized Jian and Gong territory, they moved to the Iron Bridge, four hundred li northwest of Jianshan, and styled themselves the Jian Qiang.

sentences.zh: 磨蠻、些蠻與施、順二蠻皆烏蠻種，居鐵橋、大婆、小婆、三探覽、昆池等川。

translations.literal: The Mo Man, Suo Man, Shi Man, and Shun Man were all Wuman stock, dwelling along the Iron Bridge, Dapo, Xiaopo, Santanlan, and Kun Lake.
translations.idiomatic: The Mo, Suo, Shi, and Shun Man were all Wuman stock, dwelling along the Iron Bridge, Dapo, Xiaopo, Santanlan, and Kun Lake.

sentences.zh: 土多牛羊，俗不澤，男女衣皮，俗好飲酒歌舞。

translations.literal: The land had many cattle and sheep; they did not bathe; men and women wore leather; they loved drinking, singing, and dancing.
translations.idiomatic: Their land abounded in cattle and sheep; they did not bathe; men and women wore leather; they loved wine, song, and dance.

sentences.zh: 茫蠻本關南種，茫，其君號也，或呼茫詔。

translations.literal: The Mang Man were originally a Guannan people; Mang was their ruler's title, or they were called Mang Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: The Mang Man were originally a Guannan people; mang was their ruler's title, or they were called Mang Zhao.

sentences.zh: 永昌之南有茫天連、茫吐薅、大睒、茫昌、茫鲊、茫施，大抵皆其種。

translations.literal: South of Yongchang were Mang Tianlian, Mang Tuxao, Dashan, Mangchang, Mangzha, and Mangshi—mostly their kind.
translations.idiomatic: South of Yongchang lay Mang Tianlian, Mang Tuxao, Dashan, Mangchang, Mangzha, and Mangshi—mostly their kind.

sentences.zh: 樓居，無城郭。

translations.literal: They lived in elevated houses without walled cities.
translations.idiomatic: They lived in elevated houses without walled cities.

sentences.zh: 或漆齒，或金齒。

translations.literal: Some lacquered their teeth; some gilded them.
translations.idiomatic: Some lacquered their teeth; others gilded them.

sentences.zh: 衣青布短褲，露骭，以繒布繚腰，出其餘垂後為飾。

translations.literal: They wore blue cloth short trousers, exposing the shins, wrapped silk cloth around the waist, and let the remainder hang behind as ornament.
translations.idiomatic: They wore blue cloth short trousers with bare shins, wrapped silk around the waist, and let the ends hang behind as ornament.

sentences.zh: 婦人披五色娑羅籠。

translations.literal: Women draped themselves in five-colored sura cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Women draped themselves in five-colored sura cloth.

sentences.zh: 象才如牛，養以耕。

translations.literal: Elephants were only as large as cattle and were kept for plowing.
translations.idiomatic: Their elephants were only cattle-sized and were kept for plowing.

sentences.zh: 弄棟蠻，白蠻種也。

translations.literal: The Nongdong Man were a Bai Man people.
translations.idiomatic: The Nongdong Man were a branch of the Bai Man.

sentences.zh: 其部本居弄棟縣鄙地，昔為褒州，有首領為刺史，誤殺其參軍，挈族北走。

translations.literal: Their tribe originally lived in the outskirts of Nongdong County, once Baozhou; their chieftain served as prefect, mistakenly killed his assistant administrator, and fled north with his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Their tribe originally lived in the outskirts of Nongdong County, once Baozhou; their chieftain served as prefect, mistakenly killed his assistant administrator, and fled north with his clan.

sentences.zh: 後散居磨些江側，故劍、共諸川亦有之。

translations.literal: Later they scattered along the Mosuo River, so the Jian and Gong rivers also had them.
translations.idiomatic: Later they scattered along the Mosuo River, so the Jian and Gong valleys also held them.

sentences.zh: 漢裳蠻，本漢人部種，在鐵橋。

translations.literal: The Han Shang Man were originally a Han people tribe, living at the Iron Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The Han Shang Man were originally a Han people tribe living at the Iron Bridge.

sentences.zh: 惟以朝霞纏頭，餘尚同漢服。

translations.literal: Only their heads were wrapped in dawn-colored cloth; otherwise their dress resembled Han clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Only their heads were wrapped in dawn-colored cloth; otherwise they dressed like Han Chinese.

sentences.zh: 十五年，異牟尋謀擊吐蕃，以邆川、寧北等城當寇路，乃峭山深塹修戰備，帝許出兵助力。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Yimouxun planned to attack Tibet; since Dichuan, Ningbei, and other cities lay on the enemy route, he steepened mountains and dug deep trenches to prepare defenses; the emperor approved sending troops to assist.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Yimouxun planned to attack Tibet; since Dichuan, Ningbei, and other cities lay on the enemy route, he fortified mountains and dug deep trenches; the emperor approved sending troops to assist.

sentences.zh: 又請以大臣子弟質於臯，臯辭。

translations.literal: He also requested that sons of great ministers be sent as hostages to Gao; Gao declined.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to send sons of great ministers as hostages to Gao; Gao declined.

sentences.zh: 固請，乃盡舍成都，鹹遣就學。

translations.literal: When he insisted, Gao vacated all of Chengdu and sent them to study there.
translations.idiomatic: When he insisted, Gao cleared all of Chengdu and sent them there to study.

sentences.zh: 且言：「昆明、巂州與吐蕃接，不先加兵，為虜所脅，反為我患。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Kunming and Xizhou border Tibet; if we do not strike first, they will be coerced by the enemy and become a threat to us."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Kunming and Xizhou border Tibet; unless we strike first, the enemy will coerce them and they will become a threat to us."

sentences.zh: 請臯圖之。

translations.literal: He asked Gao to plan for this.
translations.idiomatic: He asked Gao to draw up a plan.

sentences.zh: 時唐兵比歲屯京西、朔方，大峙糧，欲南北並攻取故地。

translations.literal: At that time Tang troops had been stationed in Jingxi and Shuofang for successive years, stockpiling grain, intending to attack north and south simultaneously to recover lost territory.
translations.idiomatic: Tang troops had been stationed in Jingxi and Shuofang for years, stockpiling grain, intending to attack north and south simultaneously to recover lost territory.

sentences.zh: 然南方轉餉稽期，兵不悉集。

translations.literal: Yet southern supply transport was delayed and troops did not fully assemble.
translations.idiomatic: Yet southern supply lines lagged and troops did not fully assemble.

sentences.zh: 是夏，虜麥不熟，疫癘仍興，贊普死，新君立。

translations.literal: That summer the enemy's wheat did not ripen, pestilence continued, the tsenpo died, and a new ruler succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: That summer the enemy's wheat failed, pestilence raged, the tsenpo died, and a new ruler succeeded.

sentences.zh: 臯揣虜未敢動，乃勸異牟尋：「緩舉萬全，愈於速而無功。

translations.literal: Gao judged that the enemy would not dare move and therefore advised Yimouxun: "To act slowly with full assurance is better than acting quickly without success.
translations.idiomatic: Gao judged the enemy would not dare move and advised Yimouxun: "Slow action with full assurance beats haste without success.

sentences.zh: 今境上兵十倍往歲，且行營皆在巂州，扼西瀘吐蕃路，昆明、弄棟可以無虞。」

translations.literal: Now frontier troops are ten times those of former years, and encampments are all at Xizhou, blocking the Tibetan route across the Western Lu; Kunming and Nongdong can be secure."
translations.idiomatic: Frontier troops now outnumber those of former years tenfold, and encampments at Xizhou block the Tibetan route across the Western Lu—Kunming and Nongdong can be secure."

sentences.zh: 異牟尋請期它年。

translations.literal: Yimouxun requested a date in another year.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun asked to postpone until another year.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃大臣以歲在辰，兵宜出，謀襲南詔，閱眾治道，將以十月圍巂州。

translations.literal: Tibetan ministers, because the year was chen, held that troops should march; they plotted to raid Nanzhao, reviewed troops and repaired roads, intending to besiege Xizhou in the tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetan ministers, because the year was chen, held that troops should march; they plotted to raid Nanzhao, reviewed troops and repaired roads, intending to besiege Xizhou in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 軍屯昆明凡八萬，皆命一歲糧。

translations.literal: Eighty thousand troops were stationed at Kunming, all ordered to carry one year's grain.
translations.idiomatic: Eighty thousand troops were stationed at Kunming, each ordered to carry one year's grain.

sentences.zh: 贊普以舅攘鄀羅為都統，遣尚乞力、欺徐濫鑠屯西貢川。

translations.literal: The tsenpo appointed his maternal uncle Rangnuo as commander-in-chief and sent Shang Qili and Qixu Lanyue to garrison Xigongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: The tsenpo appointed his maternal uncle Rangnuo commander-in-chief and sent Shang Qili and Qixu Lanyue to garrison Xigongchuan.

sentences.zh: 異牟尋與臯相聞，臯命部將武免率弩士三千赴之，亢榮朝以萬人屯黎州，韋良金以二萬五千人屯巂州，約南詔有急，皆進軍，過俄準添城者，南詔供饋。

translations.literal: Yimouxun communicated with Gao; Gao ordered his subordinate Wu Mian to lead three thousand crossbowmen to join him; Kang Rongchao stationed ten thousand at Lizhou; Wei Liangjin stationed twenty-five thousand at Xizhou; if Nanzhao was in peril they were all to advance, and Nanzhao would supply provisions beyond Ezhun Tian City.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun communicated with Gao; Gao ordered Wu Mian with three thousand crossbowmen to join him; Kang Rongchao stationed ten thousand at Lizhou; Wei Liangjin twenty-five thousand at Xizhou—with orders that if Nanzhao was in peril all were to advance, and Nanzhao would supply provisions beyond Ezhun Tian City.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃引眾五萬自曩貢川分二軍攻雲南，一軍自諾濟城攻巂州。
