translations.literal: Tibet led fifty thousand men from Nanggongchuan in two armies to attack Yunnan; one army from Nuojicheng attacked Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet led fifty thousand men from Nanggongchuan in two armies against Yunnan; one army from Nuojicheng struck Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 異牟尋畏東蠻、磨些難測，懼為吐蕃鄉導，欲先擊之。

translations.literal: Yimouxun feared the Eastern Man and Mosuo were unpredictable and might guide the Tibetans, and wished to strike them first.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun feared the Eastern Man and Mosuo were unpredictable and might guide the Tibetans, and wished to strike them first.

sentences.zh: 臯報：「巂州實往來道，捍蔽數州，虜百計窺之，故嚴兵以守，屯壁相望，糧械處處有之，東蠻庸敢懷貳乎？」

translations.literal: Gao replied: "Xizhou is the thoroughfare and shields several prefectures; the enemy watches it with a hundred schemes, so we garrison it heavily with camps facing one another and supplies stored everywhere—would the Eastern Man dare harbor disloyalty?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao replied: "Xizhou is the main thoroughfare shielding several prefectures; the enemy watches it with a hundred schemes, so we garrison it heavily with camps facing one another and supplies stored everywhere—would the Eastern Man dare turn traitor?"

sentences.zh: 異牟尋乃檄東、磨些諸蠻內糧城中，不者悉燒之。

translations.literal: Yimouxun then ordered the Eastern and Mosuo tribes to bring grain into the cities or have it all burned.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun then ordered the Eastern and Mosuo tribes to bring grain into the cities or burn it all.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃颙城將楊萬波約降，事泄，吐蕃以兵五千守，臯將擊破之。

translations.literal: Yang Wanbo, Tibetan garrison commander of Yongcheng, plotted to surrender; when the plot was exposed, Tibet sent five thousand troops to hold it; Gao's generals broke through and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wanbo, Tibetan garrison commander of Yongcheng, plotted to surrender; when exposed, Tibet sent five thousand troops to hold the city; Gao's generals broke through and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 萬波與籠官拔颙城以來，徙其人二千於宿川。

translations.literal: Wanbo and the tribal official Ba seized Yongcheng and came over; two thousand of their people were relocated to Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wanbo and the tribal official Ba seized Yongcheng and defected; two thousand of their people were relocated to Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 臯將扶忠義又取末恭城，俘系牛羊千計。

translations.literal: Gao's general Fu Zhongyi also took Mogong City, capturing livestock by the thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Gao's general Fu Zhongyi also took Mogong City, capturing livestock by the thousand.

sentences.zh: 贊普大將既煎讓律以兵距十貢川一舍而屯，國師馬定德率種落出降。

translations.literal: The Tibetan great general Jijian Ranglü stationed one stage from Shigongchuan; the state preceptor Ma Dingde led his tribes in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan great general Jijian Ranglü encamped one stage from Shigongchuan; the state preceptor Ma Dingde led his tribes in surrender.

sentences.zh: 西貢節度監軍野多輸煎者，贊普乞立贊養子，當從先贊普殉，亦詣忠義降。

translations.literal: The Xigong military supervisor Yeduojian, the tsenpo Qilizan's adopted son who should have followed the former tsenpo in death, also came to Zhongyi to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Xigong military supervisor Yeduojian—the tsenpo Qilizan's adopted son who should have followed the former tsenpo to the grave—also came to Zhongyi to surrender.

sentences.zh: 於是虜氣衰，軍不振。

translations.literal: Thereupon enemy morale waned and the army lost its vigor.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy morale collapsed and the army lost its vigor.

sentences.zh: 欺徐濫鑠至鐵橋，南詔毒其水，人多死，乃徙納川，壁而待。

translations.literal: Qixu Lanyue reached the Iron Bridge; Nanzhao poisoned the water and many died; they then moved to Nachuan, fortifying and waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Qixu Lanyue reached the Iron Bridge; Nanzhao poisoned the water and many died; they then withdrew to Nachuan, fortifying and waiting.

sentences.zh: 是年，虜霜雪早，兵無功還，期以明年。

translations.literal: That year frost and snow came early; the army achieved nothing and withdrew, fixing a date for the next year.
translations.idiomatic: That year frost and snow came early; the army achieved nothing and withdrew, fixing a date for the next year.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃苦唐、詔掎角，亦不敢圖南詔。

translations.literal: Tibet, harried by Tang and Nanzhao acting in concert, also did not dare plot against Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Harried by Tang and Nanzhao acting in concert, Tibet also did not dare move against Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 臯令免按兵巂州，節級鎮守，雖南詔境亦所在屯戍。

translations.literal: Gao ordered Mian to hold troops at Xizhou with graded garrisons; even within Nanzhao territory garrisons were stationed everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Gao ordered Mian to hold troops at Xizhou with graded garrisons; even within Nanzhao territory garrisons were posted everywhere.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃懲野戰數北，乃屯三瀘水，遣論妄熱誘瀕瀘諸蠻，復城悉攝。

translations.literal: Tibet, chastened by repeated defeats in field battles, then garrisoned the Three Lu Rivers and sent Lun Wangre to entice the tribes along the Lu, rebuilding the fortress of Xishe.
translations.idiomatic: Chastened by repeated field defeats, Tibet garrisoned the Three Lu Rivers and sent Lun Wangre to entice tribes along the Lu, rebuilding the fortress of Xishe.

sentences.zh: 悉攝，吐蕃險要也。

translations.literal: Xishe was a Tibetan strongpoint.
translations.idiomatic: Xishe was a Tibetan strongpoint.

sentences.zh: 蠻酋潛導南詔與臯部將杜毗羅狙擊。

translations.literal: Tribal chiefs secretly guided Nanzhao and Gao's subordinate Du Piluo in an ambush.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal chiefs secretly guided Nanzhao and Gao's subordinate Du Piluo in an ambush.

sentences.zh: 十七年春，夜絕瀘破虜屯，斬五百級。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventeenth year, they crossed the Lu by night and broke the enemy camp, beheading five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventeenth year they crossed the Lu by night and broke the enemy camp, beheading five hundred.

sentences.zh: 虜保鹿危山，毗羅伏以待，又戰，虜大奔。

translations.literal: The enemy held Luwei Mountain; Piluo lay in wait and fought again; the enemy fled in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy held Luwei Mountain; Piluo lay in wait and fought again; the enemy fled in disorder.

sentences.zh: 於時，康、黑衣大食等兵及吐蕃大酋皆降，獲甲二萬首。

translations.literal: At that time troops of Kang, the Black-robed Abbasids, and other Tibetan great chiefs all surrendered; twenty thousand sets of armor were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Troops of Kang, the Black-robed Abbasids, and other Tibetan great chiefs all surrendered; twenty thousand sets of armor were captured.

sentences.zh: 又合鬼主破虜於瀘西。

translations.literal: They also joined the Gui Zhu in defeating the enemy west of the Lu.
translations.idiomatic: They also joined the Gui Zhu in defeating the enemy west of the Lu.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃君長共計，不得巂州，患未艾，常為兩頭蠻挾唐為輕重，謂南詔也。

translations.literal: Tibetan chieftains jointly calculated that without taking Xizhou their troubles would not end, for they were constantly held in balance by the two-headed barbarians siding with Tang—meaning Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetan chieftains jointly calculated that without taking Xizhou their troubles would not end—they were constantly held in balance by the two-headed barbarians siding with Tang, meaning Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 會虜薦饑，方葬贊普，調斂煩。

translations.literal: It happened that the enemy suffered famine; they were burying the tsenpo and levies were oppressive.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy suffered famine; they were burying the tsenpo and levies were oppressive.

sentences.zh: 至是，大料兵，率三戶出一卒，虜法為大調集。

translations.literal: At this time they mustered troops on a great scale, drafting one soldier from every three households—by Tibetan law a great mobilization.
translations.idiomatic: They mustered troops on a great scale, drafting one soldier from every three households—by Tibetan law a great mobilization.

sentences.zh: 又聞唐兵三萬入南詔，乃大懼，兵戍納川、故洪、諾濟、臘、聿賫五城，欲悉師出西山、劍山，收巂州以絕南詔。

translations.literal: Hearing also that thirty thousand Tang troops had entered Nanzhao, they were greatly afraid; troops garrisoned Nachuan, Guhong, Nuoji, La, and Yubing, intending to march in full force from Xishan and Jianshan to recover Xizhou and cut off Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that thirty thousand Tang troops had entered Nanzhao, they were greatly afraid; troops garrisoned Nachuan, Guhong, Nuoji, La, and Yubing, intending to march in full force from Xishan and Jianshan to recover Xizhou and cut off Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 臯即上言：「京右諸屯宜明斥候，蚤斂田，邠、隴焚萊，可困虜入。」

translations.literal: Gao immediately memorialized: "The garrisons of Jingyou should post clear scouts, harvest fields early; burn the fallow in Bin and Long to trap the enemy's advance."
translations.idiomatic: Gao immediately memorialized: "Jingyou garrisons should post clear scouts and harvest fields early; burn the fallow in Bin and Long to trap the enemy's advance."

sentences.zh: 臯遣將邢毗以兵萬人屯南、北路，趙昱萬人戍黎、雅州。

translations.literal: Gao sent General Xing Pi with ten thousand troops to garrison the southern and northern routes, and Zhao Yu with ten thousand to garrison Li and Ya prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Gao sent General Xing Pi with ten thousand troops to garrison the southern and northern routes, and Zhao Yu with ten thousand to garrison Li and Ya.

sentences.zh: 異牟尋謂臯曰：「虜聲取巂州，實窺雲南，請武免督軍進羊苴咩。

translations.literal: Yimouxun told Gao: "The enemy claims to take Xizhou but truly eyes Yunnan; please have Wu Mian lead troops to Yangjumie.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun told Gao: "The enemy claims to take Xizhou but truly eyes Yunnan; please have Wu Mian lead troops to Yangjumie.

sentences.zh: 若虜不出者，請以來年二月深入。」

translations.literal: If the enemy does not come out, please launch a deep strike in the second month of next year."
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy does not come out, please launch a deep strike in the second month of next year."

sentences.zh: 時虜兵三萬攻鹽州，帝以虜多詐，疑繼以大軍，詔臯深鈔賊鄙，分虜勢。

translations.literal: At that time thirty thousand enemy troops attacked Yanzhou; the emperor, because the enemy was much given to deception, suspected a larger army would follow and ordered Gao to raid deep into enemy territory to divide their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty thousand enemy troops attacked Yanzhou; the emperor, knowing the enemy's deceit, suspected a larger army would follow and ordered Gao to raid deep into enemy territory to divide their strength.

sentences.zh: 臯表：「賊精鎧多置南屯，今向鹽、夏非全軍，欲掠河曲党項畜產耳」。

translations.literal: Gao memorialized: "The enemy's finest armor is mostly in the southern garrisons; the move toward Yan and Xia is not the full army—they wish only to plunder the livestock of the Tangut along the river bend."
translations.idiomatic: Gao memorialized: "The enemy's finest armor is mostly in the southern garrisons; the move toward Yan and Xia is not the full army—they wish only to plunder Tangut livestock along the river bend."

sentences.zh: 俄聞虜破麟州，臯督諸將分道出，或自西山，或由平夷，或下隴陀和、石門，或徑神川、納川，與南詔會。

translations.literal: Soon word came that the enemy had taken Linzhou; Gao directed his generals to march by separate routes—some from Xishan, some from Pingyi, some down Longtuohe and Shimen, some directly through Shenchuan and Nachuan—to join Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that the enemy had taken Linzhou; Gao directed his generals to march by separate routes—some from Xishan, some from Pingyi, some down Longtuohe and Shimen, some directly through Shenchuan and Nachuan—to join Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 是時，回鶻、太原、邠寧、涇原軍獵其北，劍南東川、山南兵震其東，鳳翔軍當其西；

translations.literal: At that time Uyghur, Taiyuan, Binning, and Jingyuan armies hunted them from the north; Dongchuan and Shannan troops threatened them from the east; Fengxiang troops blocked them from the west;
translations.idiomatic: Uyghur, Taiyuan, Binning, and Jingyuan armies hunted them from the north; Dongchuan and Shannan troops threatened them from the east; Fengxiang troops blocked them from the west;

sentences.zh: 蜀、南詔深入，克城七，焚堡百五十所，斬首萬級，獲鎧械十五萬。

translations.literal: Shu and Nanzhao advanced deep, capturing seven cities, burning a hundred fifty fortresses, beheading ten thousand, and seizing a hundred fifty thousand sets of armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Shu and Nanzhao advanced deep, capturing seven cities, burning a hundred fifty fortresses, beheading ten thousand, and seizing a hundred fifty thousand sets of armor and weapons.

sentences.zh: 圍昆明、維州不能克，乃班師。

translations.literal: They besieged Kunming and Weizhou but could not take them and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They besieged Kunming and Weizhou but could not take them and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 振武、靈武兵破虜二萬，涇原、鳳翔軍敗虜原州。

translations.literal: Zhenwu and Lingwu troops defeated twenty thousand of the enemy; Jingyuan and Fengxiang troops defeated the enemy at Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenwu and Lingwu troops defeated twenty thousand of the enemy; Jingyuan and Fengxiang troops defeated the enemy at Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 惟南詔攻其腹心，俘獲最多。

translations.literal: Only Nanzhao struck at the enemy's heartland and captured the most.
translations.idiomatic: Only Nanzhao struck at the enemy's heartland and took the most captives.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中人尹偕尉異牟尋。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched the palace eunuch Yin Kai to comfort Yimouxun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched the palace eunuch Yin Kai to comfort Yimouxun.

sentences.zh: 而吐蕃盛屯昆明、神川、納川自守。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Tibet heavily garrisoned Kunming, Shenchuan, and Nachuan in self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Tibet heavily garrisoned Kunming, Shenchuan, and Nachuan in self-defense.

sentences.zh: 異牟尋比年獻方物，天子禮之。

translations.literal: Yi Mouxun in successive years presented tribute goods, and the Son of Heaven treated him with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year Yi Mouxun sent tribute, and the emperor received him with full court honors.

sentences.zh: ◎南蠻中南詔 續元和三年，異牟尋死，詔太常卿武少儀持節吊祭。

translations.literal: [Southern Barbarians — Nanzhao] Continued: In the third year of Yuanhe, Yi Mouxun died. An edict appointed Grand Master of Ceremonies Wu Shaoyi to bear the imperial insignia and perform mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: [Southern Barbarians — Nanzhao] Continued: In the third year of Yuanhe, Yi Mouxun died. The throne ordered Grand Master of Ceremonies Wu Shaoyi to go bearing the imperial insignia and conduct the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 子尋閣勸立，或謂夢湊，自稱「驃信」，夷語君也。

translations.literal: His son Xungequan took the throne; some called him Mengcou. He styled himself "Piaoxin," which in the barbarian language meant ruler.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xungequan took the throne; some called him Mengcou. He styled himself "Piaoxin," which in the barbarian language meant ruler.

sentences.zh: 改賜元和印章。

translations.literal: He was again granted the Yuanhe seal.
translations.idiomatic: The court issued him a new seal bearing the Yuanhe reign name.

sentences.zh: 明年死，子勸龍晟立，淫肆不道，上下怨疾。

translations.literal: The next year he died. His son Quanlongsheng succeeded, licentious and lawless; above and below alike resented and hated him.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year. His son Quanlongsheng came to the throne—a man given to debauchery and outrage, hated by high and low alike.

sentences.zh: 十一年，為弄棟節度王嵯巔所殺，立其弟勸利。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was killed by Wang Cuodian, commissioner of the Nongdong garrison, who installed his younger brother Quanli.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, Wang Cuodian, military commissioner of Nongdong, had him killed and set his younger brother Quanli on the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔少府少監李銑為冊立吊祭使。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Vice Director of the Palace Workshops Li Xian as commissioner for investiture and mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: The throne appointed Vice Director of the Palace Workshops Li Xian commissioner to invest the new king and perform the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 勸利德嵯巔，賜氏蒙，封「大容」，蠻謂兄為「容」。

translations.literal: Quanli owed his position to Cuodian; the court granted him the surname Meng and enfeoffed him as "Darong," for the barbarians called an elder brother "rong."
translations.idiomatic: Quanli owed his position to Cuodian; the court granted him the surname Meng and enfeoffed him as "Darong," for the barbarians called an elder brother "rong."

sentences.zh: 長慶三年，始賜印。

translations.literal: In the third year of Changqing, he was first granted an imperial seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Changqing he received an imperial seal for the first time.

sentences.zh: 是歲死，弟豐祐立。

translations.literal: That year he died; his younger brother Fengyou succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died that same year, and his younger brother Fengyou took the throne.

sentences.zh: 豐祐趫敢，善用其下，慕中國，不肯連父名。

translations.literal: Fengyou was bold and daring, skilled in commanding his subordinates; he admired China and refused to link his name with his father's.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyou was fierce and capable, commanding his followers with skill. He admired the Tang and would not carry his father's name in his own.

sentences.zh: 穆宗使京兆少尹韋審規持節臨冊。

translations.literal: During Muzong's reign, Assistant Chief Administrator of the Capital Wei Shengui was sent bearing the insignia to invest him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Muzong, Assistant Chief Administrator of the Capital Wei Shengui was dispatched with the imperial insignia to invest him.

sentences.zh: 豐祐遣洪成酋、趙龍些、楊定奇入謝天子。

translations.literal: Fengyou sent the chieftains Hong Cheng, Zhao Longxie, and Yang Dingqi to the court to thank the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyou sent the chieftains Hong Cheng, Zhao Longxie, and Yang Dingqi to the capital to offer thanks to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 於是，西川節度使杜元穎治無狀，障候弛沓相蒙，時大和三年也。

translations.literal: At this time the military commissioner of Xichuan, Du Yuanying, governed wretchedly; frontier watchposts were slack and deceptions piled one upon another. It was the third year of Dahe.
translations.idiomatic: By then Du Yuanying, military commissioner of Xichuan, was governing wretchedly—frontier posts neglected, deceptions layered upon deceptions. It was the third year of Dahe.

sentences.zh: 嵯巔乃悉眾掩邛、戎、巂三州，陷之。

translations.literal: Cuodian then mustered his entire force and struck at the three prefectures of Qiong, Rong, and Xi, capturing them.
translations.idiomatic: Cuodian then gathered his full army, fell upon the three prefectures of Qiong, Rong, and Xi, and took them.

sentences.zh: 入成都，止西郛十日，慰賚居人，市不擾肆。

translations.literal: Entering Chengdu, he halted in the western suburbs for ten days, comforting and rewarding the inhabitants; the markets were undisturbed.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Chengdu and camped in the western suburbs for ten days, comforting the people and distributing gifts; not a shop was disturbed.

sentences.zh: 將還，乃掠子女、工技數萬引而南，人懼自殺者不勝計。

translations.literal: When about to withdraw, he carried off tens of thousands of women, children, and skilled craftsmen and marched south. So many people feared for their lives and killed themselves that the count could not be reckoned.
translations.idiomatic: When he prepared to withdraw, he seized tens of thousands of women, children, and craftsmen and marched them south. Terror drove so many to take their own lives that no one could count the dead.

sentences.zh: 救兵逐，嵯巔身自殿，至大度河，謂華人曰：「此吾南境，爾去國，當哭。」

translations.literal: Relief troops pursued. Cuodian personally commanded the rearguard. Reaching the Dadu River, he said to the Chinese: "This is our southern border. You are leaving your country—you should weep."
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing relief troops pressed close. Cuodian himself commanded the rearguard. At the Dadu River he told the captives: "This is our southern frontier. You are leaving your homeland—you should weep."

sentences.zh: 眾號慟，赴水死者十三。

translations.literal: The crowd wailed in grief; thirteen threw themselves into the river and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: The people broke into wailing lament; thirteen threw themselves into the river and drowned.

sentences.zh: 南詔自是工文織，與中國埒。

translations.literal: From this Nanzhao became skilled in woven brocades, rivaling China.
translations.idiomatic: From that time Nanzhao mastered brocade weaving, matching the workmanship of the Tang.

sentences.zh: 明年，上表請罪。

translations.literal: The next year they submitted a memorial asking forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they sent a memorial begging pardon.

sentences.zh: 比年使者來朝，開成、會昌間再至。

translations.literal: In successive years envoys came to court; during the Kaicheng and Huichang reigns they came twice more.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys continued to arrive at court year after year; during the Kaicheng and Huichang reigns they came twice again.

sentences.zh: 大中時，李琢為安南經略使，苛墨自私，以鬥鹽易一牛。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong era, Li Zhuo served as military commissioner of Annam, harsh and grasping for his own profit, trading a measure of salt for one ox.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dazhong era Li Zhuo served as military commissioner of Annam—harsh, greedy, and trading a cup of salt for a single ox.

sentences.zh: 夷人不堪，結南詔將段酋遷陷安南都護府，號「白衣沒命軍」。

translations.literal: The Yi people could not endure it. They joined with Nanzhao general Duan Qiuchuan and captured the Protectorate of Annam, calling themselves the "White-Clad Death-Defying Army."
translations.idiomatic: The Yi people could not endure it. They joined with Nanzhao general Duan Qiuchuan and captured the Protectorate of Annam, calling themselves the "White-Clad Death-Defying Army."

sentences.zh: 南詔發朱弩佉苴三千助守。

translations.literal: Nanzhao sent three thousand Zhu-nu-ji troops to help hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao dispatched three thousand Zhu-nu-ji troops to help garrison the city.

sentences.zh: 然朝貢猶歲至，從者多。

translations.literal: Yet tribute missions still came every year, and their retinues were large.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, tribute missions still arrived each year, often with large retinues.

sentences.zh: 杜悰自西川入朝，表無多內蠻傔，豐祐怒，即慢言索質子。

translations.literal: When Du Cong came to court from Xichuan, he reported that there were not many inner barbarian attendants. Fengyou grew angry and spoke insolently, demanding hostages.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Cong came to court from Xichuan and reported that there were too few inner-barbarian attendants on the mission, Fengyou flew into a rage and spoke insolently, demanding hostages.

sentences.zh: 會宣宗崩，使者告哀。

translations.literal: Just then Emperor Xuanzong died, and the envoys came to announce the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment Emperor Xuanzong died, and Nanzhao's envoys came to announce the mourning.

sentences.zh: 是時，豐祐亦死，坦綽酋龍立，恚朝廷不吊恤；

translations.literal: At that time Fengyou also died. Tanchuo Qiulong succeeded, enraged that the court had not sent condolences.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyou died about the same time. Tanchuo Qiulong took the throne, furious that the court had sent no condolences.

sentences.zh: 又詔書乃賜故王，以草具進使者而遣。

translations.literal: Moreover the edict had been addressed to the late king; it was drafted on rough paper and given to the envoys to carry back.
translations.idiomatic: Worse, the edict had been addressed to the dead king, written on coarse paper and handed to the envoys to carry home.

sentences.zh: 遂僭稱皇帝，建元建極，自號大禮國。

translations.literal: He then presumptuously styled himself emperor, established the era name Jianji, and called his state the Great Li Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: He then declared himself emperor, adopted the era name Jianji, and styled his realm the Great Li Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 懿宗以其名近玄宗嫌諱，絕朝貢。

translations.literal: Emperor Yizong, because the name was close to the taboo on Emperor Xuanzong's personal name, cut off tribute and court visits.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yizong, finding the name too close to the taboo on Emperor Xuanzong's personal name, severed tribute and diplomatic contact.

sentences.zh: 乃陷播州。

translations.literal: They then captured Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao then seized Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 安南都護李鄠屯武州，咸通元年，為蠻所攻，棄州走。

translations.literal: The Protector of Annam, Li E, garrisoned Wuzhou. In the first year of Xiantong, the barbarians attacked; he abandoned the prefecture and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Li E, Protector of Annam, held Wuzhou. In the first year of Xiantong the barbarians attacked; he abandoned the prefecture and fled.

sentences.zh: 天子斥鄠，以王寬代之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven dismissed Li E and replaced him with Wang Kuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed Li E and appointed Wang Kuan in his place.

sentences.zh: 明年，攻邕管，經略使李弘源兵少不能拒，奔巒州。

translations.literal: The next year they attacked Yong and Guan. Military Commissioner Li Hongyuan had too few troops to resist and fled to Luanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they struck Yong and Guan. Military Commissioner Li Hongyuan had too few men to hold them and fled to Luanzhou.

sentences.zh: 南詔亦引去。

translations.literal: Nanzhao also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao then withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 詔殿中監段文楚為經略使，數改條約，眾不悅，以胡懷玉代之。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Palace Supervisor Duan Wenchu military commissioner; he repeatedly revised treaties, and the people were displeased. Hu Huaiyu replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne appointed Palace Supervisor Duan Wenchu military commissioner, but he kept revising the treaties until the people grew resentful, and Hu Huaiyu replaced him.

sentences.zh: 南詔知邊人困甚，剽掠無有，不入寇。

translations.literal: Nanzhao knew the frontier people were utterly exhausted and plundered whatever they could find, but did not launch a full invasion.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao saw how broken the frontier people were and plundered whatever remained, but did not push deeper with a full invasion.

sentences.zh: 杜悰當國，為帝謀，遣使者吊祭示恩信，並詔驃信以名嫌，冊命未可舉，必易名乃得封。

translations.literal: Du Cong held power at court and counseled the emperor to send envoys to perform mourning rites and show grace and good faith, and also to instruct the Piaoxin that because of the taboo on the name, investiture could not yet be performed—he must change his name before receiving a title.
translations.idiomatic: Du Cong, then chief minister, advised the emperor to send envoys with mourning rites to show grace and good faith, and to tell the Piaoxin that because of the taboo on his name no investiture could be granted until he changed it.

sentences.zh: 帝乃命左司郎中孟穆持節往，會南詔陷巂州，穆不行。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Left Department Director Meng Mu to go bearing the insignia, but just then Nanzhao captured Xizhou and Mu did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Left Department Director Meng Mu to go with the imperial insignia, but Nanzhao seized Xizhou before he could depart, and Mu never went.

sentences.zh: 安南桃林人者，居林西原，七綰洞首領李由獨主之，歲歲戍邊。

translations.literal: The people of Taolin in Annam lived on the Linxi plain; the chieftain of the Seven-Cord Caves, Li Youdu, ruled them, and every year they garrisoned the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In Annam the Taolin people lived on the Linxi plain under Li Youdu, chieftain of the Seven-Cord Caves, who sent them to garrison the frontier every year.

sentences.zh: 李琢之在安南也，奏罷防冬兵六千人，謂由獨可當一隊，遏蠻之入。

translations.literal: When Li Zhuo was in Annam, he memorialized to abolish the six thousand winter-garrison troops, saying Youdu alone could hold one unit and block barbarian incursions.
translations.idiomatic: While Li Zhuo held Annam, he petitioned to disband six thousand winter-garrison troops, claiming Youdu alone could hold the line and stop barbarian entry.

sentences.zh: 蠻酋以女妻由獨子，七綰洞舉附蠻，王寬不能制。

translations.literal: A barbarian chieftain gave his daughter in marriage to Youdu's son; the Seven-Cord Caves all went over to the barbarians, and Wang Kuan could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: A barbarian chieftain married his daughter to Youdu's son; the Seven-Cord Caves all sided with the barbarians, and Wang Kuan could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 三年，以湖南觀察使蔡襲代之，發諸道兵二萬屯守，南詔怛畏不敢出。

translations.literal: In the third year, Hunan Observation Commissioner Cai Xi replaced him, mustering twenty thousand troops from various circuits to garrison the frontier. Nanzhao, always fearful, did not venture out.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Hunan Observation Commissioner Cai Xi replaced him, raising twenty thousand men from the various circuits to hold the frontier. Nanzhao, ever wary, did not venture out.

sentences.zh: 會詔左庶子蔡京經制嶺南，忌襲功，有所欲，沮壞之，乃言：「南方自無虞，武夫幸功，多聚兵耗饋運，請還戍兵惜財用。」

translations.literal: Just then Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent Cai Jing was ordered to oversee Lingnan. Jealous of Cai Xi's achievements and coveting something for himself, he obstructed and undermined him, saying: "The south has no threat on its own; martial men seek merit by amassing troops and wasting supply transport. Request the return of garrison troops to conserve resources."
translations.idiomatic: About then Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent Cai Jing was put in charge of Lingnan. Jealous of Cai Xi's success and hungry for glory of his own, he undermined him, arguing: "The south faces no real threat; soldiers manufacture merit by hoarding troops and wasting supply lines. Send the garrisons home and save the treasury."

sentences.zh: 襲執不可，願留五千兵，累表不報。

translations.literal: Cai Xi held firm that it could not be done and asked to keep five thousand troops; he submitted repeated memorials but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xi refused, pleading to keep five thousand men; he memorialized again and again, but the court never answered.

sentences.zh: 即極陳南詔伺隙久，有十必死狀。

translations.literal: He then set forth in the strongest terms that Nanzhao had long watched for an opening and that ten sure signs of disaster were at hand.
translations.idiomatic: He then laid out in the strongest terms how long Nanzhao had been watching for an opening, citing ten sure signs of disaster.

sentences.zh: 朝廷昏肆，不省也。

translations.literal: The court was muddled and reckless and paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: The court was muddled and heedless and ignored him.

sentences.zh: 京還奏，得意甚，復詔為宣慰安撫使。

translations.literal: When Jing returned and reported, greatly pleased with himself, he was again appointed Pacification and Reassurance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing returned and reported, swollen with pride, he was again named Pacification and Reassurance Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 即建析廣州為嶺南東道，邕州為西道，以龔、象、藤、巖為隸州。

translations.literal: He then proposed dividing Guangzhou into the Eastern Circuit of Lingnan and Yongzhou into the Western Circuit, with Gong, Xiang, Teng, and Yan made subordinate prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed splitting Guangzhou into the Eastern Circuit of Lingnan and Yongzhou into the Western Circuit, with Gong, Xiang, Teng, and Yan placed under them.

sentences.zh: 乃拜京西道節度使。

translations.literal: He was then appointed military commissioner of the Western Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made military commissioner of the Western Circuit.

sentences.zh: 京褊忮貪克，峻條令，為炮熏刳斮法，下愁毒，為軍中所逐，走藤州，矯制作攻討使印，召鄉兵比道軍攻邕州，不克，眾潰，貶死崖州。

translations.literal: Jing was narrow-minded, jealous, and greedy; he enforced harsh regulations and devised methods of roasting, smoking, flaying, and dismemberment. Resentment and suffering ran deep below; the army drove him out. He fled to Tengzhou, forged a seal for a punitive commissioner, and summoned local militia and troops from neighboring circuits to attack Yongzhou, but failed. The force collapsed, and he was demoted and died at Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was petty, jealous, and rapacious. He tightened the laws and devised punishments of roasting, smoking, flaying, and dismemberment until hatred poisoned the ranks. The army drove him out. He fled to Tengzhou, forged a punitive commissioner's seal, and called up local militia and neighboring troops to attack Yongzhou, but failed. His force collapsed, and he was demoted to die at Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 以桂管觀察使鄭愚代節度。

translations.literal: Guiguan Observation Commissioner Zheng Yu replaced him as military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Guiguan Observation Commissioner Zheng Yu replaced him as military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 南詔攻交州，進略安南，襲請救，發湖、荊、桂兵五千屯邕州。

translations.literal: Nanzhao attacked Jiaozhou and pressed toward Annam. Cai Xi requested relief, and five thousand troops from Hunan, Jing, and Gui were sent to garrison Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao attacked Jiaozhou and pressed toward Annam. Cai Xi called for help, and five thousand troops from Hunan, Jing, and Gui were sent to garrison Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 嶺南韋宙奏：「南詔必襲邕管，不先防近而圖遠，恐搗虛絕糧道，且深入。」

translations.literal: Wei Zhou of Lingnan submitted: "Nanzhao is certain to strike Yong and Guan. If we do not first defend what is near while planning for what is far, we fear they will strike at an empty center, cut off supply lines, and penetrate deeply."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhou of Lingnan warned: "Nanzhao will surely hit Yong and Guan. If we chase distant objectives before securing what is near, they will strike our empty center, sever our supply lines, and drive deep."

sentences.zh: 乃詔襲按軍海門，詔鄭愚分兵禦之。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered Cai Xi to inspect the army at Haimen, and ordered Zheng Yu to divide troops to meet the threat.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Cai Xi to inspect the army at Haimen and Zheng Yu to divide his forces to meet the threat.

sentences.zh: 襲請濟師，以山南東道兵千人赴之。

translations.literal: Cai Xi requested reinforcements, and one thousand troops from the eastern circuit of Shannan were sent to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xi asked for reinforcements, and a thousand men from the eastern circuit of Shannan were dispatched to join him.

sentences.zh: 南詔酋將楊思僭、麻光高以兵六千薄城而屯。

translations.literal: The Nanzhao generals Yang Sijian and Ma Guanggao encamped with six thousand men close against the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao's generals Yang Sijian and Ma Guanggao brought six thousand men and camped hard against the walls.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，攻益急，襲錄異牟尋盟言系矢上射入其營，不答。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year the attack grew fiercer. Cai Xi copied the oath of Yi Mouxun's alliance, tied it to an arrow, and shot it into the enemy camp; there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year the assault intensified. Cai Xi copied the oath of Yi Mouxun's old alliance, tied it to an arrow, and shot it into the enemy camp. No answer came.

sentences.zh: 俄而城陷，襲闔宗死者七十人，幕府樊綽取襲印走度江。

translations.literal: Before long the city fell. Seventy members of Cai Xi's clan died; staff officer Fan Chuo seized the seal and fled across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the city fell. Seventy of Cai Xi's clan perished; his aide Fan Chuo seized the seal and fled across the river.

sentences.zh: 荊南兵入東郛苦戰，斬南詔二千級。

translations.literal: Jingnan troops entered the eastern suburbs and fought bitterly, beheading two thousand Nanzhao soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Jingnan troops entered the eastern suburbs and fought bitterly, taking two thousand Nanzhao heads.

sentences.zh: 是夜，蠻遂屠城。

translations.literal: That night the barbarians slaughtered the entire city.
translations.idiomatic: That night the barbarians put the whole city to the sword.

sentences.zh: 有詔諸軍保嶺南，更以秦州經略使高駢為安南都護。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all armies to hold Lingnan. Gao Pian, military commissioner of Qinzhou, was reassigned as Protector of Annam.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered every army to hold Lingnan. Gao Pian, military commissioner of Qinzhou, was reassigned Protector of Annam.

sentences.zh: 帝見輸發頻，罷遊幸，不奏樂，宰相杜悰以為非是，止之。

translations.literal: Seeing frequent supply levies, the emperor stopped pleasure outings and suspended music. Chief Minister Du Cong thought this wrong and had it halted.
translations.idiomatic: As supply levies mounted, the emperor gave up pleasure outings and stopped court music. Chief Minister Du Cong thought this excessive and put a stop to it.

sentences.zh: 南詔稍逼邕州，鄭愚自陳非將帥才，願更擇人。

translations.literal: Nanzhao pressed closer to Yongzhou. Zheng Yu declared himself no general and asked that another be chosen.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao pressed closer to Yongzhou. Zheng Yu confessed he was no commander and asked that someone else be chosen.

sentences.zh: 會康承訓自義成來朝，乃授嶺南西道節度使，發荊、襄、洪、鄂兵萬人從之。

translations.literal: Just then Kang Chengxun came to court from Yicheng and was appointed military commissioner of the Western Circuit of Lingnan; ten thousand troops from Jing, Xiang, Hong, and E followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Chengxun then came to court from Yicheng and was made military commissioner of the Western Circuit of Lingnan, with ten thousand men from Jing, Xiang, Hong, and E following him.

sentences.zh: 承訓辭兵寡，乃大興諸道兵五萬往。

translations.literal: Chengxun declined on the grounds that his force was too small; then a great levy was raised of fifty thousand troops from all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun protested that his force was too small; then a great levy raised fifty thousand men from every circuit.

sentences.zh: 六月，置行交州於海門，進為都護府，調山東兵萬人益戍，以容管經略使張茵鎮之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month a provisional Jiaozhou was established at Haimen and advanced to a protectorate; ten thousand Shandong troops were added to the garrison, with Rongguan Military Commissioner Zhang Yin commanding them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month a provisional Jiaozhou was set up at Haimen and raised to a protectorate; ten thousand Shandong troops were added to the garrison under Rongguan Military Commissioner Zhang Yin.

sentences.zh: 因命經略安南，茵逗留不敢進。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to oversee Annam, but Yin lingered and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to recover Annam, but Yin lingered and would not advance.

sentences.zh: 安南之陷，將吏遺人多客伏溪洞，詔所在招還救恤之，免安南賦入二年。

translations.literal: When Annam fell, many officers, clerks, and refugees hid in stream valleys and cave settlements. An edict ordered local authorities to summon them back, give relief, and exempt Annam from taxes for two years.
translations.idiomatic: After Annam fell, many officers, clerks, and refugees hid in stream valleys and cave settlements. An edict ordered local authorities to summon them back, give relief, and exempt Annam from taxes for two years.

sentences.zh: 韋宙請分兵屯容、藤披蠻勢。

translations.literal: Wei Zhou requested dividing troops to garrison Rong and Teng and break the barbarian momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhou asked to split forces to garrison Rong and Teng and break the barbarian advance.

sentences.zh: 五年，南詔回掠巂州以搖西南。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Nanzhao turned back to raid Xizhou and shake the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Nanzhao swung back to raid Xizhou and unsettle the southwest.

sentences.zh: 西川節度使蕭鄴率屬蠻鬼主邀南詔大度河，敗之。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner of Xichuan Xiao Ye led the affiliated barbarian Ghost Lords to intercept Nanzhao at the Dadu River and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Xichuan Military Commissioner Xiao Ye led allied barbarian Ghost Lords to intercept Nanzhao at the Dadu River and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 明年，復來攻。

translations.literal: The next year they came again to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they attacked again.

sentences.zh: 會刺史喻士珍貪獪，陰掠兩林東蠻口縛賣之，以易蠻金，故開門降。

translations.literal: Just then Prefect Yu Shizhen was greedy and cunning; he secretly seized people of the Eastern Barbarians of the Two Forests, bound them, and sold them to obtain barbarian gold. For this reason he opened the gates and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Yu Shizhen was greedy and cunning; he secretly seized people of the Eastern Barbarians of the Two Forests, bound them, and sold them for barbarian gold. That is why he opened the gates and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 南詔盡殺戍卒，而士珍遂臣於蠻。

translations.literal: Nanzhao killed all the garrison troops, and Shizhen then submitted to the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao slaughtered the garrison to the last man, and Shizhen then submitted to them.

sentences.zh: 安南久屯，兩河銳士死瘴毒者十七，宰相楊收議罷北軍，以江西為鎮南軍，募強弩二萬建節度，且地便近，易調發。

translations.literal: Annam had been garrisoned for a long time; seven-tenths of the crack troops from the two river circuits had died of miasma. Chief Minister Yang Shou proposed abolishing the northern army, making Jiangxi the Zhennan Army, recruiting twenty thousand strong crossbowmen and establishing a military commission—nearby territory, easy to mobilize.
translations.idiomatic: Annam had been garrisoned for years; seven-tenths of the crack troops from the two river circuits had died of miasma. Chief Minister Yang Shou proposed abolishing the northern army, making Jiangxi the Zhennan Army, recruiting twenty thousand strong crossbowmen under a new commission—closer ground, easier to mobilize.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 夏侯孜亦以張茵懦，不足事，悉以兵授高駢。

translations.literal: Xiahou Zi also judged Zhang Yin too timid for the task and transferred all troops to Gao Pian.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Zi likewise judged Zhang Yin too timid for the work and turned all the troops over to Gao Pian.

sentences.zh: 駢以選士五千度江，敗林邑兵於邕州，擊南詔龍州屯，蠻酋燒貲畜走。

translations.literal: Pian crossed the river with five thousand picked troops, defeated the Linyi army at Yongzhou, and struck the Nanzhao encampment at Longzhou; the barbarian chieftains burned their stores and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Pian crossed the river with five thousand picked troops, routed the Linyi army at Yongzhou, and struck Nanzhao's camp at Longzhou; the barbarian chiefs burned their stores and fled.

sentences.zh: 酋龍遣楊緝思助酋遷共守安南，以範胒些為安南都統，趙諾眉為扶邪都統。

translations.literal: Qiulong sent Yang Jisi to help Qiuchuan hold Annam jointly, appointing Fan Pixie commander of Annam and Zhao Nuomei commander of Fuxie.
translations.idiomatic: Qiulong sent Yang Jisi to help Qiuchuan hold Annam, appointing Fan Pixie commander of Annam and Zhao Nuomei commander of Fuxie.

sentences.zh: 七年六月，駢次交州，戰數勝，士酣鬥，斬其將張詮。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the seventh year Pian reached Jiaozhou. After several victories the troops fought with drunken ardor and beheaded the general Zhang Quan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the seventh year Pian reached Jiaozhou. After several victories his men fought with drunken ardor and took the general Zhang Quan.

sentences.zh: 李溠龍舉眾萬人降，拔波風三壁。

translations.literal: Li Polong brought ten thousand men in surrender; three walled camps at Bofeng were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Li Polong surrendered with ten thousand men; three walled camps at Bofeng were taken.

sentences.zh: 緝思出戰，敗，還走城。

translations.literal: Jisi came out to fight, was defeated, and fled back to the city.
translations.idiomatic: Jisi came out to fight, was beaten, and fled back to the city.

sentences.zh: 士乘之，超堞入，斬酋遷、脆些、諾眉，上首三萬級，安南平。

translations.literal: The troops pressed the attack, scaled the walls, and entered. They beheaded Qiuchuan, Cuixie, and Nuomei; thirty thousand heads were presented. Annam was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Pian's men pressed the attack, scaled the walls, and broke in. They beheaded Qiuchuan, Cuixie, and Nuomei; thirty thousand heads were presented. Annam was pacified.

sentences.zh: 初，酋龍遣清平官董成等十九人詣成都，節度使李福將廷見之，成辭曰：「皇帝奉天命改正朔，請以敵國禮見。」

translations.literal: Initially Qiulong had sent the Qingpingguan Dong Cheng and eighteen others to Chengdu. Military Commissioner Li Fu was about to receive them in court audience. Cheng declined, saying: "The Emperor has received Heaven's mandate and changed the calendar. We ask to be received with the rites due a sovereign state."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Qiulong had sent the Qingpingguan Dong Cheng and eighteen others to Chengdu. Military Commissioner Li Fu was about to receive them in full court audience. Cheng refused, saying: "Our emperor has received Heaven's mandate and changed the calendar. We ask to be received with the rites due a sovereign power."

sentences.zh: 福不許。

translations.literal: Fu refused.
translations.idiomatic: Fu refused.

sentences.zh: 導譯五返，日旰士倦，議不決。

translations.literal: The interpreters went back and forth five times; by evening the men were weary and no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: Interpreters shuttled back and forth five times; by evening the men were exhausted and still no agreement had been reached.

sentences.zh: 福怒，命武士捽辱之，械系於館。

translations.literal: Fu grew angry and ordered warriors to seize and humiliate them, shackling them in the guest house.
translations.idiomatic: Fu flew into a rage and ordered soldiers to seize and humiliate them, shackling them in the guest house.

sentences.zh: 俄而劉潼代福節度，即挺其系，表縱還。

translations.literal: Before long Liu Tong replaced Fu as military commissioner; he immediately had their bonds cut and memorialized to release them and send them back.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Liu Tong replaced Fu as military commissioner; he immediately had their bonds cut and memorialized to release them and send them home.

sentences.zh: 有詔召成等至京師，見別殿，賜物良厚，慰遣還國。

translations.literal: An edict summoned Cheng and the others to the capital; they were received in a separate hall, given rich gifts, comforted, and sent back to their country.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned Cheng and the others to the capital; they were received in a separate hall, given lavish gifts, comforted, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 明年，酋龍使楊酋慶等來謝釋囚。

translations.literal: The next year Qiulong sent Yang Youqing and others to thank the court for releasing the prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Qiulong sent Yang Youqing and others to thank the court for freeing the prisoners.

sentences.zh: 初，李師望建言：「成都經總蠻事，曠日不能決，請析邛、蜀、嘉、眉、黎、雅、巂七州為定邊軍，建節度制機事，近且速。」

translations.literal: Initially Li Shiwang had proposed: "Chengdu oversees all barbarian affairs and cannot resolve them for days on end. Request dividing the seven prefectures of Qiong, Shu, Jia, Mei, Li, Ya, and Xi into the Dingbian Army, establishing a military commission to control affairs—near and fast."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Shiwang had argued: "Chengdu oversees all barbarian affairs and takes days to settle anything. Split the seven prefectures of Qiong, Shu, Jia, Mei, Li, Ya, and Xi into the Dingbian Army under a new commission—closer to the frontier and faster to act."

sentences.zh: 天子謂然，即詔師望為節度使，治邛州。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven thought it right and immediately appointed Shiwang military commissioner, with his seat at Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and at once made Shiwang military commissioner, with his seat at Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 邛距成都才五舍，巂州最南，去邛乃千里，緩急首尾不相副，而師望利專制，諱不言。

translations.literal: Qiong was only five stages from Chengdu, while Xi, the southernmost prefecture, was a thousand li from Qiong—urgent and rear ends could not support each other. Yet Shiwang coveted sole command and said nothing of this.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong lay only five stages from Chengdu, while Xi—the southernmost prefecture—was a thousand li from Qiong, so front and rear could not support each other in crisis. Shiwang wanted sole command and said nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 裒積無厭，私賄以百萬計。

translations.literal: He amassed wealth without limit; private bribes ran into the millions.
translations.idiomatic: He hoarded wealth without limit; private bribes ran into the millions.

sentences.zh: 又欲激蠻怒，幸有功，乃殺酋慶等。

translations.literal: He also wished to provoke the barbarians to anger, hoping for merit, and so killed Youqing and the others.
translations.idiomatic: He also hoped to goad the barbarians into war and win glory, and so he killed Youqing and the others.

sentences.zh: 既而戍士怒，將醢師望以逞，會召還，以竇滂代之。

translations.literal: Before long the garrison troops grew furious and were about to mince Shiwang to vent their rage, but just then he was recalled and Dou Bang replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the garrison troops were ready to mince Shiwang alive in their fury, but he was recalled just then and Dou Bang replaced him.

sentences.zh: 滂沓冒尤不法，誅責苛纖甚師望。

translations.literal: Bang was reckless and lawless beyond measure; his punishments and exactions were even harsher and finer-grained than Shiwang's.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Bang was even more reckless and corrupt; his punishments and exactions were finer and crueler than Shiwang's.

sentences.zh: 時蠻役未興，而定邊已困。

translations.literal: At that time the barbarian corvée had not yet been imposed, yet Dingbian was already exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian levy had not yet been imposed, yet Dingbian was already exhausted.

sentences.zh: 酋龍怨殺其使，十年，乃入寇。

translations.literal: Qiulong resented the killing of his envoys; ten years later he invaded.
translations.idiomatic: Qiulong resented the killing of his envoys; ten years on he invaded.

sentences.zh: 以軍綴青溪關，密引眾伐木開道，徑雪皮，盛夏，卒凍死者二千人。

translations.literal: He feigned an attack on Qingxi Pass while secretly leading troops to cut timber and open a road through Xuepi; in midsummer two thousand soldiers died of cold.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned an attack on Qingxi Pass while secretly cutting timber to open a road through Xuepi; in midsummer two thousand soldiers died of cold.

sentences.zh: 出沐源，窺嘉州，破屬蠻，遂次沐源。

translations.literal: Emerging at Muyuan, he spied on Jiazhou, defeated the subordinate tribes, and then encamped at Muyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Emerging at Muyuan, he spied on Jiazhou, defeated the subordinate tribes, and encamped at Muyuan.

sentences.zh: 滂遣兗海兵五百往戰，一軍覆。

translations.literal: Pang sent five hundred Yanhai troops to fight; the entire force was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Pang sent five hundred Yanhai troops to fight; the entire force was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 酋龍乃身自將，督眾五萬侵巂州，攻青溪關。

translations.literal: Qiulong then personally commanded, leading fifty thousand men to invade Xizhou and attack Qingxi Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Qiulong then personally commanded fifty thousand men against Xizhou and Qingxi Pass.

sentences.zh: 屯將杜再榮絕大度河走，諸屯皆退保北涯。

translations.literal: Garrison commander Du Zairong fled across the Dadu River; all garrisons withdrew to hold the north bank.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison commander Du Zairong fled across the Dadu River; all garrisons withdrew to the north bank.

sentences.zh: 蠻攻黎州，詭服漢衣，濟江襲犍為，破之。

translations.literal: The barbarians attacked Lizhou, disguised in Han clothing, crossed the river and raided Qianwei, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians attacked Lizhou in Han disguise, crossed the river to raid Qianwei, and took it.

sentences.zh: 裴回陵、榮間，焚廬舍，掠糧畜。

translations.literal: They ranged between Ling and Rong, burning dwellings and plundering grain and livestock.
translations.idiomatic: They ranged between Ling and Rong, burning dwellings and plundering grain and livestock.

sentences.zh: 薄嘉州，刺史楊忞與南詔夾江而軍，士攢射，蠻不得進，陰自上遊濟，背擊王師，殺忠武將顏慶師，忞走，嘉州陷。

translations.literal: Pressing on Jiazhou, Prefect Yang Min and Nanzhao faced each other across the river; concentrated volleys kept the barbarians from advancing, but they secretly crossed upstream and struck the imperial army from behind, killing Loyalty-and-Fortitude General Yan Qingshi; Min fled and Jiazhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing on Jiazhou, Prefect Yang Min faced Nanzhao across the river; concentrated volleys held them back, but they secretly crossed upstream and struck from behind, killing Loyalty-and-Fortitude General Yan Qingshi; Min fled and Jiazhou fell.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，攻杜再榮，滂自勒兵戰。

translations.literal: The next year, in the first month, they attacked Du Zairong; Pang personally led troops to fight.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the first month, they attacked Du Zairong; Pang personally led troops to fight.

sentences.zh: 酋龍遣使者十輩請和，滂信之，語未半，蠻桴爭岸，噪而進。

translations.literal: Qiulong sent ten envoys to sue for peace; Pang believed them, but before the talks were half finished the barbarians beat drums along the shore and charged with shouts.
translations.idiomatic: Qiulong sent ten envoys to sue for peace; Pang believed them, but before talks were half finished the barbarians beat drums along the shore and charged with shouts.

sentences.zh: 滂不知所為，將自殺，武寧將苗全緒止之，殊死戰，蠻稍卻，滂乃遁，全緒殿而行。

translations.literal: Pang did not know what to do and was about to kill himself; Wuning General Miao Quanxu stopped him; fighting desperately, the barbarians slightly withdrew; Pang then fled while Quanxu covered the retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Pang did not know what to do and was about to kill himself; Wuning General Miao Quanxu stopped him; fighting desperately they drove the barbarians back slightly; Pang fled while Quanxu covered the retreat.

sentences.zh: 黎州陷，人走匿山谷，蠻掠金帛不勝負。

translations.literal: Lizhou fell; people fled into the mountains; the barbarians plundered gold and silk beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhou fell; people fled into the mountains; the barbarians plundered gold and silk beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 入自邛崍關，圍雅州，遂擊邛州。

translations.literal: Entering through Qionglai Pass, they besieged Yazhou and then struck Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Entering through Qionglai Pass, they besieged Yazhou and then struck Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 是冬，滂棄州，壁導江，儲貲峙械皆亡矣。

translations.literal: That winter Pang abandoned the prefecture, fortifying at Daojiang; stored provisions and weapons were all lost.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Pang abandoned the prefecture and fortified at Daojiang; stored provisions and weapons were all lost.

sentences.zh: 酋龍進攻成都，次眉州，坦綽杜元忠日夜教酋龍取全蜀。

translations.literal: Qiulong advanced on Chengdu, halting at Meizhou; Tanzhuo Du Yuanzhong day and night urged Qiulong to take all of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Qiulong advanced on Chengdu, halting at Meizhou; Tanzhuo Du Yuanzhong day and night urged him to take all of Shu.

sentences.zh: 於是西川節度使廬耽遣其副王偃、中人張思廣約和，蠻強之使南面拜，然卒不見酋龍而還。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xichuan Military Governor Lu Dan sent his deputy Wang Yan and the palace eunuch Zhang Siguang to negotiate peace; the barbarians forced them to bow facing south, yet in the end they did not see Qiulong and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xichuan Military Governor Lu Dan sent his deputy Wang Yan and the palace eunuch Zhang Siguang to negotiate peace; the barbarians forced them to bow facing south, yet they never saw Qiulong and returned.

sentences.zh: 蠻次新津，耽復遣副譚奉祀好言申約，蠻留之。

translations.literal: The barbarians encamped at Xinjin; Dan again sent Deputy Tan Fengsi with conciliatory words to renew the agreement; the barbarians detained him.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians encamped at Xinjin; Dan again sent Deputy Tan Fengsi with conciliatory words; the barbarians detained him.

sentences.zh: 耽畏援軍未集，即飛請天子降大使通好，以紓其深入。

translations.literal: Dan, fearing relief troops had not yet assembled, urgently petitioned the Son of Heaven to dispatch a great envoy to negotiate peace and ease the enemy's deep advance.
translations.idiomatic: Dan, fearing relief had not assembled, urgently petitioned the emperor to dispatch a great envoy to negotiate peace and ease the enemy's deep advance.

sentences.zh: 懿宗馳遣太仆卿支詳為和蠻使。

translations.literal: Emperor Yizong hastily dispatched Grand Master of the Imperial Stud Zhi Xiang as envoy to pacify the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yizong hastily dispatched Grand Master of the Imperial Stud Zhi Xiang as envoy to pacify the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 蠻本無謀，不能乘機會鼓行亟驅，但蚍結蠅營，忸鹵剽小利，處處留屯，故蜀孺老得扶攜悉入成都。

translations.literal: The barbarians originally had no strategy; they could not seize the moment to march swiftly and drive forward, but only swarmed like ants and flies, snatching petty gains, leaving garrisons everywhere—so the old and young of Shu were able to be escorted into Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians had no strategy; they could not seize the moment to march swiftly but only swarmed like ants, snatching petty gains and leaving garrisons everywhere—so the old and young of Shu were escorted into Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 阇裏皆滿，戶所占地不得過一床，雨則冒箕盎自庇。

translations.literal: Every lane was full; each household's space did not exceed one bed; when it rained they sheltered under baskets and bowls.
translations.idiomatic: Every lane was packed; each household had no more space than one bed; when it rained they sheltered under baskets and bowls.

sentences.zh: 城中井為竭，則共飲摩訶池，至爭捽溺死者，或沙取滴飲之。

translations.literal: When city wells ran dry, all drank from Lake Mohe; people fought over it and some drowned; others scooped sand and drank the drips.
translations.idiomatic: When city wells ran dry, all drank from Lake Mohe; people fought and some drowned; others scooped sand and drank the drips.

sentences.zh: 死不能具棺，即共坎瘞。

translations.literal: When the dead could not be given coffins, they were buried together in common pits.
translations.idiomatic: When the dead could not be given coffins, they were buried together in common pits.

sentences.zh: 故瀘州刺史楊慶復為耽治攻具、藺石，置牢城兵，八將主之，樹笓格，夜列炬照城，守具雄新。

translations.literal: Former Luzhou Prefect Yang Qingfu prepared siege equipment and catapult stones for Dan, established fortress troops under eight generals, erected palisades, and at night lined torches along the wall—the defenses were formidable and new.
translations.idiomatic: Former Luzhou Prefect Yang Qingfu prepared siege equipment and catapult stones for Dan, established fortress troops under eight generals, erected palisades, and at night lined torches along the wall—the defenses were formidable.

sentences.zh: 又選悍士三千，號「突將」，為長刀、巨撾斧，分左右番休，日隸於軍，士心侈欲鬥。

translations.literal: He also selected three thousand fierce soldiers, called them "Assault Troops," armed them with long knives and great maul-axes, divided them into left and right shifts, and attached them daily to the army; the soldiers' spirits grew extravagant and they longed to fight.
translations.idiomatic: He also selected three thousand fierce soldiers, called them "Assault Troops," armed them with long knives and great maul-axes, divided them into left and right shifts, and attached them daily to the army; the soldiers' spirits grew extravagant and they longed to fight.

sentences.zh: 而酋龍自雙流徐行，內欲報董成之辱，因紿耽請上介至軍議事。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Qiulong advanced slowly from Shuangliu, inwardly wishing to avenge Dong Cheng's humiliation, and deceived Dan by requesting a senior envoy come to the army to discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Qiulong advanced slowly from Shuangliu, inwardly wishing to avenge Dong Cheng's humiliation, and deceived Dan by requesting a senior envoy to discuss affairs at his camp.

sentences.zh: 耽遣節度副使柳槃往見杜元忠議和，元忠妄言：「帝見耽，請具車蓋葆翣。」

translations.literal: Dan sent Deputy Military Governor Liu Pan to see Du Yuanzhong and discuss peace; Yuanzhong falsely said: "When the emperor sees Dan, please prepare carriage canopies and pheasant-tail fans."
translations.idiomatic: Dan sent Deputy Military Governor Liu Pan to see Du Yuanzhong; Yuanzhong falsely said: "When the emperor sees Dan, please prepare carriage canopies and pheasant-tail fans."

sentences.zh: 槃未能決，還。

translations.literal: Pan could not decide and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Pan could not decide and returned.

sentences.zh: 蠻以三百騎負幄幕來，大言曰：「供帳隋蜀王聽事，為驃信行在。」

translations.literal: The barbarians came with three hundred cavalry bearing tents and pavilions, loudly declaring: "Prepare the hall of the Sui Prince of Shu as the piaoxin's traveling palace."
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred cavalry came bearing tents, loudly declaring: "Prepare the hall of the Sui Prince of Shu as the piaoxin's traveling palace."

sentences.zh: 耽不許，乃馳去。

translations.literal: Dan refused; they then galloped away.
translations.idiomatic: Dan refused; they galloped away.

sentences.zh: 蠻稍前，傅外郛。

translations.literal: The barbarians advanced slightly and pressed against the outer suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians advanced and pressed against the outer suburbs.

sentences.zh: 於是遊弈使王晝督援兵三千屯毗橋；

translations.literal: Thereupon Patrol Commissioner Wang Zhou supervised three thousand relief troops garrisoned at Piqiao;
translations.idiomatic: Patrol Commissioner Wang Zhou supervised three thousand relief troops at Piqiao;

sentences.zh: 竇滂亦以其軍自導江來，將與大軍掎角，然戰不甚力，小不勝即保廣漢。

translations.literal: Dou Pang also came from Daojiang with his army, intending to join the main force in pincer attack, yet he did not fight vigorously; after a small defeat he withdrew to Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Pang also came from Daojiang with his army to join the main force in pincer attack, yet fought halfheartedly; after a small defeat he withdrew to Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 自以失定邊，覬成都陷，得薄其罪。

translations.literal: He himself, having lost Dingbian, hoped Chengdu would fall so his guilt might be lightened.
translations.idiomatic: Having lost Dingbian, he hoped Chengdu would fall so his guilt might be lightened.

sentences.zh: 會有詔斥徙，軍遂無功。

translations.literal: An edict then arrived rebuking and transferring him; the army achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: An edict arrived rebuking and transferring him; the army achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 耽部將李自孝者，與刺史喻士珍善。

translations.literal: Among Dan's subordinate generals was Li Zixiao, who was friendly with Prefect Yu Shizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Among Dan's subordinate generals was Li Zixiao, friendly with Prefect Yu Shizhen.

sentences.zh: 士珍臣蠻，自孝陰與賊通，乃說耽城下蒔葦稻，瀦水頹城，舉府不之覺。

translations.literal: Shizhen had submitted to the barbarians; Zixiao secretly communicated with the enemy and persuaded Dan to plant reeds and rice below the walls, damming water to undermine the city—the entire prefecture did not notice.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen had submitted to the barbarians; Zixiao secretly communicated with the enemy and persuaded Dan to plant reeds and rice below the walls, damming water to undermine the city—no one in the prefecture noticed.

sentences.zh: 蠻攻城，自孝守陴，樹麾以自表。

translations.literal: When the barbarians attacked, Zixiao defended the battlements and raised a banner to signal himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the barbarians attacked, Zixiao defended the battlements and raised a banner to signal himself.

sentences.zh: 麾所指，蠻輒攻之，為下所覺，耽殺自孝以徇。

translations.literal: Wherever the banner pointed, the barbarians attacked; this was discovered by those below; Dan executed Zixiao as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever the banner pointed, the barbarians attacked; subordinates discovered the treachery and Dan executed Zixiao as a warning.

sentences.zh: 城左有民樓肆，蠻俯射城中，耽募勇士燒之，器械俱盡。

translations.literal: To the left of the city were civilian buildings and shops from which the barbarians shot down into the city; Dan recruited brave men to burn them; all equipment was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Civilian buildings to the left of the city let the barbarians shoot down into the walls; Dan recruited brave men to burn them; all equipment was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 二月，蠻以雲梁、鵝車四面攻，士叫呼，鵝車未至，陴者以巨索鉤系，投膏炬，車焚，箱間蠻卒盡死。

translations.literal: In the second month the barbarians attacked from four sides with cloud bridges and goose carts; soldiers shouted; before the goose carts arrived, defenders on the battlements hooked them with great ropes, threw grease torches, and the carts burned; barbarian soldiers in the compartments all died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the barbarians attacked from four sides with cloud bridges and goose carts; before the goose carts arrived, defenders hooked them with great ropes, threw grease torches, and the carts burned; barbarian soldiers in the compartments all died.

sentences.zh: 耽遣李璹、張察率突將戰城下，俘斬二千級。

translations.literal: Dan sent Li Jun and Zhang Cha leading Assault Troops to fight below the wall, capturing and beheading two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Dan sent Li Jun and Zhang Cha with Assault Troops to fight below the wall, capturing and beheading two thousand.

sentences.zh: 蠻徹民鄣落為蓬籠如車{厶大}，下設枕木，推而前，不及城丈，匿蠻其內以穴墉。

translations.literal: The barbarians pulled down civilian stockades to make covered wagons like chariots, with rollers beneath, pushing them forward; they did not reach within a zhang of the wall; barbarians hid inside to tunnel under the ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians pulled down civilian stockades to make covered wagons on rollers, pushing them forward; they did not reach within a zhang of the wall; barbarians hid inside to tunnel under the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 楊忞以貯糞沈潑蠻，蠻不能處；

translations.literal: Yang Min poured stored night soil to drench the barbarians; they could not endure it;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Min poured stored night soil to drench the barbarians; they could not endure it;

sentences.zh: 註以鐵液，蓬籠皆火。

translations.literal: molten iron was poured in and the covered wagons all caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: molten iron was poured in and the covered wagons all caught fire.

sentences.zh: 然南詔負眾，益治器械，斧兵晝夜有聲，將擊錦樓，眾失色。

translations.literal: Yet Nanzhao, relying on superior numbers, further prepared equipment; the sound of axes day and night—they were about to strike the brocade tower and the crowd turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Nanzhao, relying on superior numbers, further prepared equipment; the sound of axes day and night—they were about to strike the brocade tower and the crowd turned pale.

sentences.zh: 耽遣將出，三面苦戰，蠻引卻。

translations.literal: Dan sent generals out to fight bitterly on three sides; the barbarians withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Dan sent generals out to fight bitterly on three sides; the barbarians withdrew.

sentences.zh: 蠻利夜晦，輒薄城，聞呼嘯，眾齊奮。

translations.literal: The barbarians favored dark nights and pressed close to the wall; at the sound of shouts the crowd rallied together.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians favored dark nights and pressed close to the wall; at the sound of shouts the crowd rallied.

sentences.zh: 城上施鐵籠千炬，賊來不得隱，屯夫終夜哄，蠻不能侵。

translations.literal: A thousand iron-caged torches were set on the wall; when enemies came they could not hide; laborers shouted all night and the barbarians could not penetrate.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand iron-caged torches blazed on the wall; enemies could not hide; laborers shouted all night and the barbarians could not penetrate.

sentences.zh: 支詳遣諜與約好，且謂耽毋多殺以速蠻和。

translations.literal: Zhi Xiang sent spies to arrange peace and told Dan not to kill too many lest peace with the barbarians be hastened.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Xiang sent spies to arrange peace and told Dan not to kill too many lest peace with the barbarians be hastened.

sentences.zh: 是時，傳言救師至，城中合噪開門，士爭出迎軍，南詔搏戰不解。

translations.literal: At that time rumor spread that relief troops had arrived; the city erupted in shouts and opened the gates; soldiers rushed out to welcome the army; Nanzhao fought without breaking off.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor spread that relief had arrived; the city erupted in shouts and opened the gates; soldiers rushed out to welcome the army; Nanzhao fought without breaking off.

sentences.zh: 日入，判官程克裕以北門兵二千乘之，蠻乃走。

translations.literal: At sunset Administrative Officer Cheng Keyu led two thousand troops from the north gate to strike them; the barbarians then fled.
translations.idiomatic: At sunset Administrative Officer Cheng Keyu led two thousand troops from the north gate to strike them; the barbarians fled.

sentences.zh: 耽猶遺之書，謝不得已交兵，且請和。

translations.literal: Dan still sent them a letter, apologizing that battle had been unavoidable and requesting peace.
translations.idiomatic: Dan still sent a letter apologizing that battle had been unavoidable and requesting peace.

sentences.zh: 士脫鎧迎支詳，詳陳所賫，植二旗，署曰「賜雲南幣物」。

translations.literal: Soldiers doffed armor to welcome Zhi Xiang; Xiang displayed what he had brought and erected two banners inscribed "Gifts Bestowed upon Yunnan."
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers doffed armor to welcome Zhi Xiang, who displayed his gifts and erected two banners inscribed "Gifts Bestowed upon Yunnan."

sentences.zh: 謂蠻使者曰：「天子詔雲南和解，而兵薄成都，奈何？

translations.literal: He told the barbarian envoys: "The Son of Heaven decreed reconciliation with Yunnan—yet your army presses Chengdu. What is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: He told the barbarian envoys: "The emperor decreed reconciliation with Yunnan—yet your army presses Chengdu. What is to be done?

sentences.zh: 請退舍撤警以修好。」

translations.literal: Please withdraw your camp, lift the alarm, and renew friendship."
translations.idiomatic: Please withdraw, lift the alarm, and renew friendship."

sentences.zh: 或勸詳：「蠻多詐，毋入死地。」

translations.literal: Some advised Xiang: "The barbarians are much given to deception; do not enter deadly ground."
translations.idiomatic: Some advised Xiang: "The barbarians are much given to deception; do not enter deadly ground."

sentences.zh: 詳不行。

translations.literal: Xiang would not go.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang would not go.

sentences.zh: 蠻復圍成都，夜穿西北隅，犁旦乃覺，即頹茭火於壖，蠻皆死穴中。

translations.literal: The barbarians again besieged Chengdu, tunneling through the northwest corner at night; it was discovered only at dawn; straw was piled in the ditch and set afire; barbarians in the tunnels all died.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians again besieged Chengdu, tunneling through the northwest corner at night; discovered only at dawn; straw was piled in the ditch and set afire; barbarians in the tunnels all died.

sentences.zh: 以鐵縆曳雲朋仆之，燎作，少選盡，益固守。

translations.literal: Iron chains dragged down the cloud bridges and burned them; in a short while all were consumed; the defenses were strengthened further.
translations.idiomatic: Iron chains dragged down the cloud bridges and burned them; in a short while all were consumed; the defenses were strengthened further.

sentences.zh: 是時，帝遣東川節度使顏慶復為大度河制置、劍南應接使，兵次新都，博野將曾元裕敗蠻兵，斬二千級。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor dispatched Dongchuan Military Governor Yan Qingfu as Dadu River Commissioner and Jiannan Relief Commissioner; troops halted at Xindu; Boye General Zeng Yuanyu defeated the barbarian army and beheaded two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Dongchuan Military Governor Yan Qingfu as Dadu River Commissioner and Jiannan Relief Commissioner; troops halted at Xindu; Boye General Zeng Yuanyu defeated the barbarians and beheaded two thousand.

sentences.zh: 南詔騎數萬晨壓官軍以騁，大將宋威以忠武兵戰，斬首五千，獲馬四百尾。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands of Nanzhao cavalry pressed the imperial army at dawn; Great General Song Wei fought with Loyalty-and-Fortitude troops, beheading five thousand and capturing four hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of Nanzhao cavalry pressed the imperial army at dawn; Great General Song Wei fought with Loyalty-and-Fortitude troops, beheading five thousand and capturing four hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 南詔退屯星宿山，威進戍沱江。

translations.literal: Nanzhao withdrew to garrison Xingsu Mountain; Wei advanced to hold Tuojiang.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao withdrew to Xingsu Mountain; Wei advanced to hold Tuojiang.

sentences.zh: 酋龍遣酋望至支詳所請和，詳曰：「今列城固守，北軍望功，歸語而主，審自度。」

translations.literal: Qiulong sent a qiuvang to Zhi Xiang's camp to sue for peace; Xiang said: "Now the cities stand firm in defense and northern troops await merit—tell your lord to judge for himself."
translations.idiomatic: Qiulong sent a qiuvang to Zhi Xiang's camp to sue for peace; Xiang said: "Cities stand firm and northern troops await merit—tell your lord to judge for himself."

sentences.zh: 耽遣銳將趣蠻壁燒攻具，殺二千人，為南詔所躡，卻而潰。

translations.literal: Dan sent sharp generals to rush the barbarian camp and burn siege equipment, killing two thousand; pursued by Nanzhao, they withdrew in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Dan sent sharp generators to rush the barbarian camp and burn siege equipment, killing two thousand; pursued by Nanzhao, they withdrew in rout.

sentences.zh: 蠻聞鳳翔、山南軍且來，乃迎戰毗橋，不勝，趨沱江，為伏士所擊，又敗。

translations.literal: Hearing that Fengxiang and Shannan armies were coming, the barbarians met them in battle at Piqiao, were defeated, hurried toward Tuojiang, and were struck by ambushers and defeated again.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Fengxiang and Shannan armies were coming, the barbarians met them at Piqiao, were defeated, hurried toward Tuojiang, and were struck by ambushers again.

sentences.zh: 城中出突將，夜火蠻營，酋龍、坦綽身督戰。

translations.literal: Assault Troops sallied from the city and burned the barbarian camp at night; Qiulong and Tanzhuo personally directed the battle.
translations.idiomatic: Assault Troops sallied from the city and burned the barbarian camp at night; Qiulong and Tanzhuo personally directed the battle.

sentences.zh: 後三日，王師奪升遷梁，蠻大敗，夜燒亭傳，乘火所向，雨矢射王師。

translations.literal: Three days later the imperial army seized Shenqianliang; the barbarians suffered a great defeat; at night they burned pavilions and posts; riding the flames wherever they went, rainlike arrows struck the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later the imperial army seized Shenqianliang; the barbarians suffered a great defeat; at night they burned pavilions and posts; riding the flames, rainlike arrows struck the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 威疏軍行，向矢所發叢射之。

translations.literal: Wei spread out his army's formation and volleyed toward the source of the arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Wei spread his formation and volleyed toward the source of the arrows.

sentences.zh: 兩軍不能決，各解去。

translations.literal: Neither army could prevail; each withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Neither army could prevail; each withdrew.

sentences.zh: 酋龍知不敵，夜徹營南奔，至雙流，江無梁，計窮，將赴水死，或止之曰：「今北軍與成都兵合，若來追，我無類矣。

translations.literal: Qiulong knew he could not prevail; at night he broke camp and fled south to Shuangliu; there was no bridge across the river; at his wit's end he was about to throw himself into the water; someone stopped him: "Now northern troops and Chengdu forces are united—if they pursue, we are finished.
translations.idiomatic: Qiulong knew he could not prevail; at night he broke camp and fled south to Shuangliu; with no bridge across the river he was about to drown himself; someone stopped him: "Northern troops and Chengdu forces are united—if they pursue, we are finished.

sentences.zh: 不如偽和以紓急；

translations.literal: Better to feign peace to ease the crisis;
translations.idiomatic: Better to feign peace to ease the crisis;

sentences.zh: 不然，死未晚。」

translations.literal: otherwise death is not yet too late."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise death is not yet too late."

sentences.zh: 乃來請。

translations.literal: He then came to sue for peace.
translations.idiomatic: He then came to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 三日梁成而濟，即斷梁，按隊緩驅。

translations.literal: Three days later the bridge was completed and they crossed; then the bridge was cut; ranks were formed and they withdrew slowly.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later the bridge was completed and they crossed; then the bridge was cut; ranks were formed and they withdrew slowly.

sentences.zh: 黎州刺史嚴師本收散卒保邛州，酋龍懼，圍二日去。

translations.literal: Lizhou Prefect Yan Shiben gathered scattered troops to hold Qiongzhou; Qiulong feared this and after besieging two days departed.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhou Prefect Yan Shiben gathered scattered troops to hold Qiongzhou; Qiulong feared this and after two days' siege departed.

sentences.zh: 蠻俘華民，必劓耳鼻已，縱之，既而居人刻木為耳鼻者什八。

translations.literal: When barbarians captured Han people they always cut off nose and ears before releasing them; afterward eight or nine of ten townspeople wore wooden noses and ears.
translations.idiomatic: When barbarians captured Han people they cut off nose and ears before releasing them; afterward eight or nine of ten townspeople wore wooden noses and ears.

sentences.zh: 慶復之來，眾以其弟慶師死於蠻，必甘心。

translations.literal: When Qingfu came, the crowd thought that because his brother Qingshi had died at barbarian hands he would surely be implacable.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingfu came, the crowd thought that because his brother Qingshi had died at barbarian hands he would surely be implacable.

sentences.zh: 及成都不破，以己功輕，乃按軍廣溪，縱殘寇，人人切齒。

translations.literal: When Chengdu was not taken, he considered his own merit slight; he therefore held his army at Guangxi and let the remnant enemy go—everyone gnashed their teeth.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengdu was not taken, he considered his own merit slight; he held his army at Guangxi and let the remnant enemy go—everyone gnashed their teeth.

sentences.zh: 初，成都無隍塹，乃教耽浚隍，廣三丈，作戰棚於埤，列左右屯營，營別五區。

translations.literal: Initially Chengdu had no moat; Dan was taught to dig a moat thirty zhang wide and build fighting sheds on the ramparts, with left and right garrison camps divided into five sections.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Chengdu had no moat; Dan was taught to dig a moat thirty zhang wide and build fighting sheds on the ramparts, with left and right garrison camps in five sections.

sentences.zh: 區卒五十，蒔皂莢夾壕，後三年合拱。

translations.literal: Fifty soldiers per section planted black locust between the trenches; three years later they formed an arch.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty soldiers per section planted black locust between the trenches; three years later they formed an arch.

sentences.zh: 又為大旝連弩。

translations.literal: Large banner-linked crossbows were also made.
translations.idiomatic: Large banner-linked crossbows were also made.

sentences.zh: 自是南詔憚之。

translations.literal: From this Nanzhao feared them.
translations.idiomatic: From this Nanzhao feared them.

sentences.zh: 酋龍年少嗜殺戮，親戚異己者皆斬，兵出無寧歲，諸國更讎忿，屢覆眾，國耗虛。

translations.literal: Qiulong was young and addicted to killing; kinsmen and those who differed from him were all executed; whenever troops marched out there was no year of peace; the various states nursed mutual hatred; armies were repeatedly destroyed and the state grew hollow.
translations.idiomatic: Qiulong was young and addicted to killing; kinsmen and dissenters were all executed; whenever troops marched there was no year of peace; neighboring states nursed mutual hatred; armies were repeatedly destroyed and the state grew hollow.

sentences.zh: 蜀之役，男子十五以下悉發，婦耕以餉軍。

translations.literal: In the Shu campaign, all males fifteen and under were mobilized; women plowed to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shu campaign all males fifteen and under were mobilized; women plowed to supply the army.

sentences.zh: 十四年，坦綽復寇蜀，縆舟大度河以濟，為刺史黃景復擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Tanzhuo again raided Shu, roping boats to cross the Dadu River; Prefect Huang Jingfu repulsed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Tanzhuo again raided Shu, roping boats to cross the Dadu River; Prefect Huang Jingfu repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 眾循河而南，夜桴上流兵，夾攻瀕水諸屯，景復敗，走還黎州。

translations.literal: The crowd followed the river south; at night they poled upstream troops and attacked jointly the garrisons along the water; Jingfu was defeated and fled back to Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd followed the river south; at night they poled upstream troops and jointly attacked garrisons along the water; Jingfu was defeated and fled to Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 蠻躡追，為景復所敗。

translations.literal: The barbarians pursued closely and were defeated by Jingfu.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians pursued closely and were defeated by Jingfu.
