sentences.zh: 會蠻踵來，還攻大度河，仆旗息鼓，請曰：「坦綽欲上書天子白冤事。」

translations.literal: When barbarians came in succession they again attacked the Dadu River, lowered banners and silenced drums, requesting: "Tanzhuo wishes to send a memorial to the Son of Heaven to explain grievances."
translations.idiomatic: When barbarians came in succession they again attacked the Dadu River, lowered banners and silenced drums, saying: "Tanzhuo wishes to send a memorial to the emperor to explain grievances."

sentences.zh: 戍兵信之，不戰。

translations.literal: Garrison soldiers believed them and did not fight.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison soldiers believed them and did not fight.

sentences.zh: 橋成而濟，黎州陷。

translations.literal: The bridge was completed and they crossed; Lizhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: The bridge was completed and they crossed; Lizhou fell.

sentences.zh: 遂攻雅州，擊定邊軍，卒潰入邛州。

translations.literal: They then attacked Yazhou, struck the Dingbian army, and the soldiers broke and fled into Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: They then attacked Yazhou, struck the Dingbian army, and soldiers broke and fled into Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 成都大震，人亡入玉壘關，士乘城。

translations.literal: Chengdu was greatly shaken; people fled into Yulei Pass; soldiers manned the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu was greatly shaken; people fled into Yulei Pass; soldiers manned the walls.

sentences.zh: 坦綽遣使者王保城等四十人賫驃信書遺節度使牛叢，欲假道入朝，請憩蜀王故殿。

translations.literal: Tanzhuo sent envoys Wang Baocheng and forty others bearing the piaoxin's letter to Military Governor Niu Cong, requesting passage to court and rest in the former hall of the Prince of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhuo sent envoys Wang Baocheng and forty others bearing the piaoxin's letter to Military Governor Niu Cong, requesting passage to court and rest in the former hall of the Prince of Shu.

sentences.zh: 叢欲許之，楊慶諫曰：「蠻無信，彼禮屈辭甘，詐我也。

translations.literal: Cong wished to agree; Yang Qing remonstrated: "The barbarians are faithless; their humble ritual and sweet words are deception.
translations.idiomatic: Cong wished to agree; Yang Qing remonstrated: "The barbarians are faithless; their humble ritual and sweet words are deception.

sentences.zh: 請斬其使，留二人還書。」

translations.literal: Please execute their envoys and keep two to carry back a reply."
translations.idiomatic: Execute their envoys and keep two to carry back a reply."

sentences.zh: 叢因責之曰：「詔王之祖，六詔最小夷也。

translations.literal: Cong therefore rebuked them: "The edict says your king's ancestor was the smallest Yi among the Six Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Cong rebuked them: "The edict says your king's ancestor was the smallest Yi among the Six Zhao.

sentences.zh: 天子錄其勤，合六詔為一，俾附庸成都，名之以國，許子弟入太學，使習華風，今乃自絕王命。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven recorded his merit, united the Six Zhao into one, made him a vassal attached to Chengdu, named him with a state title, permitted sons and younger brothers to enter the Imperial College to learn Chinese ways—yet now you have cut yourselves off from the royal command.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor recorded his merit, united the Six Zhao into one, made him a vassal attached to Chengdu, named him with a state title, permitted sons and younger brothers to enter the Imperial College to learn Chinese ways—yet now you have cut yourselves off from the royal command.

sentences.zh: 且雀蛇犬馬，猶能報德，王乃不如蟲鳥乎？

translations.literal: Moreover sparrows, snakes, dogs, and horses can still repay kindness—are you not even the equal of insects and birds?
translations.idiomatic: Sparrows, snakes, dogs, and horses can still repay kindness—are you not even the equal of insects and birds?

sentences.zh: 比成都以武備未修，故令爾突我疆埸。

translations.literal: Recently, because Chengdu's defenses were not yet repaired, you were allowed to burst into our borders.
translations.idiomatic: Because Chengdu's defenses were not yet repaired, you were allowed to burst into our borders.

sentences.zh: 然毗橋、沱江之敗，積胔附城，不四年復來。

translations.literal: Yet at Piqiao and Tuojiang you were defeated; corpses piled against the walls—and in less than four years you came again.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at Piqiao and Tuojiang you were crushed; corpses piled against the walls—and in less than four years you came again.

sentences.zh: 今吾有十萬眾，舍其半未用。

translations.literal: Now I have a hundred thousand troops and have not yet used half.
translations.idiomatic: Now I have a hundred thousand troops and have not yet used half.

sentences.zh: 以千人為軍。

translations.literal: A thousand men form one army.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand men form one army.

sentences.zh: 十軍為部，驍將主之。

translations.literal: Ten armies form a division, commanded by a fierce general.
translations.idiomatic: Ten armies form a division under a fierce general.

sentences.zh: 凡部有強弩二百，镈斧輔之；

translations.literal: Each division has two hundred strong crossbows, supported by broad-axes;
translations.idiomatic: Each division has two hundred strong crossbows supported by broad-axes;

sentences.zh: 勁弓二百，越銀刀輔之；

translations.literal: two hundred powerful bows, supported by Yue silver blades;
translations.idiomatic: two hundred powerful bows supported by Yue silver blades;

sentences.zh: 長戈二百，掇刀輔之；

translations.literal: two hundred long halberds, supported by hooking knives;
translations.idiomatic: two hundred long halberds supported by hooking knives;

sentences.zh: 短矛二百，連錘輔之。

translations.literal: two hundred short spears, supported by linked maces.
translations.idiomatic: two hundred short spears supported by linked maces.

sentences.zh: 又軍四面，面有鐵騎五百。

translations.literal: Each army also has iron cavalry on four sides—five hundred on each face.
translations.idiomatic: Each army also has iron cavalry on four sides—five hundred on each face.

sentences.zh: 悉收芻薪、米粟、牛馬、犬豕，清野待爾。

translations.literal: All fodder, grain, cattle, horses, dogs, and pigs have been gathered; the countryside cleared to await you.
translations.idiomatic: All fodder, grain, cattle, horses, dogs, and pigs have been gathered; the countryside cleared to await you.

sentences.zh: 吾又能以旁騎略爾樵采。

translations.literal: I can also use flanking cavalry to cut off your foraging.
translations.idiomatic: I can also use flanking cavalry to cut off your foraging.

sentences.zh: 我日出以一部與爾戰，部別二番，日中而代；

translations.literal: Each day I send one division to fight you; each division rotates in two watches, replaced at midday;
translations.idiomatic: Each day I send one division to fight you; each division rotates in two watches, replaced at midday;

sentences.zh: 日昃一部至，以夜屯，月明則戰，黑則休，夜半而代。

translations.literal: at sunset another division arrives to garrison by night; when the moon is bright we fight, when dark we rest, replaced at midnight.
translations.idiomatic: at sunset another division arrives to garrison by night; when the moon is bright we fight, when dark we rest, replaced at midnight.

sentences.zh: 凡我兵五日一殺敵，爾乃晝夜戰，不十日，懵且死矣。

translations.literal: My troops kill enemies once every five days; you fight day and night—in less than ten days you will be dazed and dead.
translations.idiomatic: My troops kill enemies once every five days; you fight day and night—in less than ten days you will be dazed and dead.

sentences.zh: 州縣繕甲厲兵，掎角相從，皆蠻之深讎，雖女子能齽齘薄賊，況強夫烈士哉！

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties repair armor and sharpen weapons, acting in concert from both flanks—all are the barbarians' deep enemies; even women can gnash teeth and revile the bandits—how much more strong men and heroes!
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties repair armor and sharpen weapons, acting in concert—all are the barbarians' deep enemies; even women can gnash teeth at the bandits—how much more strong men and heroes!

sentences.zh: 爾祖嘗奴事西蕃，為爾仇家，今顧臣之，何恩讎之戾邪？

translations.literal: Your ancestor once served Tibet as a slave—your family's enemy—yet now you submit to them; what perversity of gratitude and vengeance is this?
translations.idiomatic: Your ancestor once served Tibet as a slave—your family's enemy—yet now you submit to them; what perversity of gratitude and vengeance is this?

sentences.zh: 蜀王故殿，先世之寶宮，非邊夷所宜舍，神怒人憤，驃信且死！」

translations.literal: The former hall of the Prince of Shu is a treasure palace of former generations—not a place frontier barbarians should occupy; gods will rage and men will resent— the piaoxin is about to die!"
translations.idiomatic: The former hall of the Prince of Shu is a treasure palace of former generations—not a place for frontier barbarians; gods will rage and men will resent—the piaoxin is about to die!"

sentences.zh: 叢猶火郊民室廬觀閣，嚴兵為固守計。

translations.literal: Cong still burned suburban dwellings, pavilions, and towers, and deployed troops for a plan of stout defense.
translations.idiomatic: Cong still burned suburban dwellings and deployed troops for stout defense.

sentences.zh: 坦綽至新津而還，回寇黔中，經略使秦匡謀懼，奔荊南。

translations.literal: Tanzhuo reached Xinjin and returned, then raided Qianzhong; Military Commissioner Qin Kuangmou fled in fear to Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhuo reached Xinjin and returned, then raided Qianzhong; Military Commissioner Qin Kuangmou fled in fear to Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 會僖宗立，遣金吾將軍韓重持節往使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong succeeded, he dispatched Golden Guard General Han Chong bearing the imperial insignia as envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong succeeded, he dispatched Golden Guard General Han Chong bearing the imperial insignia as envoy.

sentences.zh: 俄攻黎州，景復擊走之。

translations.literal: Soon they attacked Lizhou; Jingfu repulsed them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they attacked Lizhou; Jingfu repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 乾符元年，劫略巂、雅間，破黎州，入邛崍關，掠成都，成都閉三日，蠻乃去。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianfu they plundered between Xie and Ya, took Lizhou, entered Qionglai Pass, and raided Chengdu; Chengdu closed its gates for three days before the barbarians withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianfu they plundered between Xie and Ya, took Lizhou, entered Qionglai Pass, and raided Chengdu; Chengdu closed its gates for three days before the barbarians withdrew.

sentences.zh: 詔徙天平軍高駢領西川節度使，乃奏：「蠻小醜，勢易制。

translations.literal: An edict transferred Gao Pian of the Tianping Army to serve as Xichuan Military Governor; he memorialized: "The barbarians are petty bandits and easily controlled.
translations.idiomatic: An edict transferred Gao Pian of the Tianping Army to Xichuan Military Governor; he memorialized: "The barbarians are petty bandits and easily controlled.

sentences.zh: 而蜀道險，館餉窮覂。

translations.literal: Yet the Shu road is perilous and supply posts are exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Shu road is perilous and supply posts exhausted.

sentences.zh: 今左神策所發長武、河東兵多，用度繁廣。

translations.literal: Now the Left Shence Army's Changwu and Hedong troops are numerous and expenses are heavy.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Shence Army's Changwu and Hedong troops are numerous and expenses heavy.

sentences.zh: 且彼皆扼制羌戎，不可以弛備。」

translations.literal: Moreover they all restrain the Qiang and Rong and cannot relax defenses."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover they all restrain the Qiang and Rong and cannot relax defenses."

sentences.zh: 詔乃罷長武等兵。

translations.literal: An edict then dismissed the Changwu and other troops.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then dismissed the Changwu and other troops.

sentences.zh: 駢至不淹月，閱精騎五千，逐蠻至大度河，奪鎧馬，執酋長五十斬之，收邛崍關，復取黎州，南詔遁還。

translations.literal: Within less than a month of Pian's arrival he reviewed five thousand elite cavalry, pursued the barbarians to the Dadu River, seized armor and horses, captured and beheaded fifty chieftains, recovered Qionglai Pass, retook Lizhou, and Nanzhao fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month of Pian's arrival he reviewed five thousand elite cavalry, pursued the barbarians to the Dadu River, seized armor and horses, beheaded fifty chieftains, recovered Qionglai Pass and Lizhou, and Nanzhao fled.

sentences.zh: 駢召景復責大度河之敗，斬以徇。

translations.literal: Pian summoned Jingfu and rebuked him for the Dadu River defeat, executing him as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Pian summoned Jingfu, rebuked him for the Dadu River defeat, and executed him as a warning.

sentences.zh: 戍望星、清溪等關。

translations.literal: Garrisons were established at Wangxing, Qingxi, and other passes.
translations.idiomatic: Garrisons were established at Wangxing, Qingxi, and other passes.

sentences.zh: 南詔懼，遣使者詣駢結好，而踵出兵寇邊，駢斬其使。

translations.literal: Nanzhao feared this and sent envoys to Pian to renew friendship, yet repeatedly sent troops to raid the border; Pian executed their envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao feared this and sent envoys to renew friendship, yet repeatedly raided the border; Pian executed their envoys.

sentences.zh: 初，安南經略判官杜驤為蠻所俘，其妻，宗室女也，故酋龍使奉書丐和。

translations.literal: Initially Annan Military Commissioner Assistant Du Xiang was captured by the barbarians; his wife was a clanswoman of the imperial house, so Qiulong had a letter sent begging peace.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Annan Assistant Du Xiang was captured; his wife was an imperial clanswoman, so Qiulong sent a letter begging peace.

sentences.zh: 駢答曰：「我且將百萬眾至龍尾城問爾罪。」

translations.literal: Pian replied: "I shall soon bring a million troops to Longwei City to inquire after your crimes."
translations.idiomatic: Pian replied: "I shall soon bring a million troops to Longwei City to answer for your crimes."

sentences.zh: 酋龍大震。

translations.literal: Qiulong was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Qiulong was greatly shaken.

sentences.zh: 自南詔叛，天子數遣使至其境，酋龍不肯拜，使者遂絕。

translations.literal: Since Nanzhao rebelled, the Son of Heaven repeatedly sent envoys to their borders; Qiulong refused to bow and envoys ceased going.
translations.idiomatic: Since Nanzhao rebelled, the emperor repeatedly sent envoys; Qiulong refused to bow and envoys ceased going.

sentences.zh: 駢以其俗尚浮屠法，故遣浮屠景仙攝使往，酋龍與其下迎謁且拜，乃定盟而還。

translations.literal: Pian, because their custom honored Buddhist law, therefore sent the monk Jing Xian as acting envoy; Qiulong and his subordinates came out to receive and bow to him, and alliance was settled before their return.
translations.idiomatic: Pian, knowing they honored Buddhism, sent the monk Jing Xian as acting envoy; Qiulong and his subordinates came out to receive and bow to him, and alliance was settled.

sentences.zh: 遣清平官酋望趙宗政、質子三十入朝乞盟，請為兄弟若舅甥。

translations.literal: He sent Qingping Official Qiuvang Zhao Zongzheng and thirty hostages to court to beg alliance, requesting to be brothers or uncle and nephew.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Qingping Official Qiuvang Zhao Zongzheng and thirty hostages to court to beg alliance, requesting brotherhood or uncle-nephew ties.

sentences.zh: 詔拜景仙鴻臚卿、檢校左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Jing Xian Director of the Court of State Ceremonial and Acting Left Regular Attendant of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Jing Xian Director of the Court of State Ceremonial and Acting Left Regular Attendant of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 駢結吐蕃尚延心、嗢末魯耨月等為間，築戎州馬湖、沐源川、大度河三城，列屯拒險，料壯卒為平夷軍，南詔氣奪。

translations.literal: Pian allied with Tibet's Shang Yanxin, Wamo Lunuyue, and others as intermediaries, built three fortresses at Rongzhou's Mahu, Muyuanchuan, and Dadu River, posted garrisons at strategic points, selected strong soldiers for the Pingyi Army—Nanzhao's spirit was broken.
translations.idiomatic: Pian allied with Tibet's Shang Yanxin and Wamo Lunuyue, built three fortresses at Mahu, Muyuanchuan, and the Dadu River, posted garrisons at strategic points, and formed the Pingyi Army—Nanzhao's spirit was broken.

sentences.zh: 酋龍恚，發疽死，偽謚景莊皇帝。

translations.literal: Qiulong, enraged, developed a carbuncle and died; posthumously styled Emperor Jingzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Qiulong, enraged, developed a carbuncle and died; posthumously styled Emperor Jingzhuang.

sentences.zh: 子法嗣，改元貞明、承智、大同，自號大封人。

translations.literal: His son Fa succeeded, changing reign titles to Zhenming, Chengzhi, and Datong, styling himself "Great Feng Person."
translations.idiomatic: His son Fa succeeded, changing reign titles to Zhenming, Chengzhi, and Datong, styling himself Great Feng Person.

sentences.zh: 法年少，好畋獵酣逸，衣絳紫錦罽，鏤金帶。

translations.literal: Fa was young, fond of hunting and dissipation, wearing crimson purple brocade and fur, with inlaid gold belts.
translations.idiomatic: Fa was young, fond of hunting and dissipation, wearing crimson purple brocade and fur with inlaid gold belts.

sentences.zh: 國事顓決大臣。

translations.literal: State affairs were entirely decided by great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: State affairs were entirely decided by great ministers.

sentences.zh: 乾符四年，遣陀西段羌寶詣邕州節度使辛讜請修好，詔使者答報。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qianfu he sent Tuoxi Duan Qiangbao to Yongzhou Military Governor Xin Dan to request renewed friendship; an edict ordered envoys to reply.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qianfu he sent Tuoxi Duan Qiangbao to Yongzhou Military Governor Xin Dan to request renewed friendship; an edict ordered envoys to reply.

sentences.zh: 未幾，寇西川，駢奏請與和親，右諫議大夫柳韜、吏部侍郎崔淡醜其事，上言：「遠蠻畔逆，乃因浮屠誘致，入議和親，垂笑後世。

translations.literal: Before long they raided Xichuan; Pian memorialized requesting marriage alliance; Right Remonstrance Officer Liu Tao and Vice Minister of Personnel Cui Dan denounced the affair, memorializing: "Distant barbarians rebel—yet through Buddhist monks they were enticed to propose marriage alliance, bringing ridicule on posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they raided Xichuan; Pian memorialized requesting marriage alliance; Right Remonstrance Officer Liu Tao and Vice Minister Cui Dan denounced it: "Distant barbarians rebel—yet Buddhist monks enticed them to propose marriage, bringing ridicule on posterity.

sentences.zh: 駢職上將，謀乘謬，不可從。」

translations.literal: Pian holds the rank of supreme general yet plots to exploit error—this cannot be followed."
translations.idiomatic: Pian holds supreme command yet plots to exploit error—this cannot be followed."

sentences.zh: 遂寢。

translations.literal: The proposal was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 蠻使者再入朝議和親，而駢徙荊南，持前請不置。

translations.literal: Barbarian envoys again came to court to discuss marriage alliance, but Pian was transferred to Jingnan and his earlier request was not pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian envoys again came to discuss marriage alliance, but Pian was transferred to Jingnan and his earlier request lapsed.

sentences.zh: 宰相鄭畋、廬攜爭不決，皆賜罷。

translations.literal: Chancellors Zheng Tian and Lu Xie disputed without resolution; both were dismissed with honors.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors Zheng Tian and Lu Xie disputed without resolution; both were dismissed with honors.

sentences.zh: 辛讜遣幕府徐雲虔攝使者往覘。

translations.literal: Xin Dan dispatched staff member Xu Yunqian as acting envoy to observe them.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Dan dispatched staff member Xu Yunqian as acting envoy to observe them.

sentences.zh: 到善闡府，見騎數十，曳長矛，擁絳服少年，朱繒約發。

translations.literal: Arriving at Shanchan Prefecture, he saw several dozen horsemen dragging long spears, escorting crimson-clad youths with red silk binding their hair.
translations.idiomatic: At Shanchan Prefecture he saw dozens of horsemen dragging long spears, escorting crimson-clad youths with red silk binding their hair.

sentences.zh: 典客伽陀酋孫慶曰：「此驃信也。」

translations.literal: Protocol Officer Qiatuoqiu Sun Qing said: "This is the piaoxin."
translations.idiomatic: Protocol Officer Qiatuoqiu Sun Qing said: "This is the piaoxin."

sentences.zh: 問天子起居，下馬揖客，取使者佩刀視之，自解左右鈕以示。

translations.literal: He inquired after the Son of Heaven's health, dismounted to bow to the guest, took the envoy's belt knife to examine it, and unfastened his own left clasp to show him.
translations.idiomatic: He inquired after the emperor's health, dismounted to bow, examined the envoy's belt knife, and unfastened his own left clasp to show him.

sentences.zh: 乃除地剚三丈版，命左右馳射。

translations.literal: He then cleared ground and planted a three-zhang board, ordering his attendants to gallop and shoot.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared ground and planted a three-zhang board, ordering attendants to gallop and shoot.

sentences.zh: 每一人射，法駷馬逐以為樂，數十發止。

translations.literal: For each man's shot, Fa galloped in pursuit for amusement, stopping after several dozen shots.
translations.idiomatic: For each shot Fa galloped in pursuit for amusement, stopping after several dozen rounds.

sentences.zh: 引客就幄，侲子捧瓶盂，四女子侍樂飲，夜乃罷。

translations.literal: He led the guest to a pavilion; boys held bottles and cups; four women attended with music and drink; only at night did it end.
translations.idiomatic: He led the guest to a pavilion where boys held bottles and four women attended with music and drink; only at night did it end.

sentences.zh: 又遣問客《春秋》大義，送使者還。

translations.literal: He also sent to ask the guest about the great meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, then sent the envoy back.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked about the great meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, then sent the envoy back.

sentences.zh: 是時，駢徙節鎮海，劾淡等沮議，帝蒙弱不能曉，下詔尉解。

translations.literal: At that time Pian was transferred to Zhenhai; he impeached Cui Dan and others for obstructing the discussion; the emperor was weak and did not understand; an edict was issued to comfort and reconcile.
translations.idiomatic: Pian was transferred to Zhenhai and impeached Cui Dan for obstructing the discussion; the weak emperor did not understand; an edict comforted and reconciled.

sentences.zh: 西川節度使崔安潛上言：「蠻蓄鳥獸心，不識禮義，安可以賤隸尚貴主，失國家大體？

translations.literal: Xichuan Military Governor Cui Anqian memorialized: "The barbarians harbor the hearts of birds and beasts and know neither ritual nor righteousness—how can a lowly slave be matched with a noble princess, violating the great principle of the state?
translations.idiomatic: Xichuan Military Governor Cui Anqian memorialized: "The barbarians harbor the hearts of birds and beasts and know neither ritual nor righteousness—how can a lowly slave be matched with a noble princess, violating the state's great principle?

sentences.zh: 淡等議可用。

translations.literal: Cui Dan and others' proposal may be used.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Dan's proposal should stand.

sentences.zh: 臣請募義征子，率十戶一保，願發山東銳兵六千戍諸州，比五年，蠻可為奴。」

translations.literal: I request to recruit volunteers for punitive campaigns, ten households forming one bao; I wish to dispatch six thousand sharp troops from Shandong to garrison the prefectures—in five years the barbarians can be made slaves."
translations.idiomatic: I request volunteers for punitive campaigns, ten households per bao; dispatch six thousand sharp troops from Shandong to garrison the prefectures—in five years the barbarians can be enslaved."

sentences.zh: 久之，帝手詔問安潛和親事，答曰：「雲南姚州譬一縣，中國何資於彼而遣重使，加厚禮？

translations.literal: After a long time, the emperor personally issued an edict asking Anqian about the marriage alliance. He replied, "Yunnan and Yaozhou are like a single county; what benefit would China gain from them that it should send a weighty envoy and add generous rites?
translations.idiomatic: After a long time, the emperor personally issued an edict asking Anqian about the marriage alliance. He replied, "Yunnan and Yaozhou are like a single county; what benefit would China gain from them that it should send a weighty envoy and add generous rites?

sentences.zh: 彼且妄謂朝廷畏怯無能為，脫有它請，陛下何以待之？

translations.literal: They will falsely say that the court is fearful and powerless; if they make some other request, how will Your Majesty deal with it?
translations.idiomatic: They will falsely say that the court is fearful and powerless; if they make some other request, how will Your Majesty deal with it?

sentences.zh: 且天宗近屬，不可下小蠻夷。

translations.literal: A close relative of the imperial clan cannot be lowered to petty barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: A close relative of the imperial clan cannot be lowered to petty barbarians.

sentences.zh: 臣比移書，不言舅甥，黜所僭也。

translations.literal: In my recent letter I did not speak of uncle and nephew, rejecting what they arrogated to themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In my recent letter I did not speak of uncle and nephew, rejecting what they arrogated to themselves.

sentences.zh: 有如蠻使者不復至，當遣諜人伺其隙，可以得誌。」

translations.literal: If the barbarian envoys do not come again, spies should be sent to watch for openings; then our purpose may be achieved."
translations.idiomatic: If the barbarian envoys do not come again, spies should be sent to watch for openings; then our purpose may be achieved."

sentences.zh: 南詔知蜀強，故襲安南，陷之，都護曾袞奔邕府，戍兵潰。

translations.literal: Nanzhao knew Shu was strong and therefore raided Annan and took it; Protector-General Zeng Gun fled to Yong Prefecture and garrison troops collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao knew Shu was strong and therefore raided Annan and took it; Protector-General Zeng Gun fled to Yong Prefecture and garrison troops collapsed.

sentences.zh: 會西川節度使陳敬瑄申和親議，時廬攜復輔政，與豆廬彖皆厚駢，乃譎說帝曰：「陛下初即位，遣韓重使南詔，將官屬留蜀期年，費不貲，蠻不肯迎。

translations.literal: When Xichuan Military Governor Chen Jingxuan proposed marriage alliance, Lu Xie again assisted in government together with Dou Lu Tuan, both favoring Pian; they therefore deceived the emperor, saying: "When Your Majesty first succeeded, Han Chong was sent to Nanzhao; officials were left in Shu for a year at immeasurable expense, yet the barbarians would not receive them.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Jingxuan proposed marriage alliance, Lu Xie again assisted government with Dou Lu Tuan, both favoring Pian; they deceived the emperor: "When Your Majesty first succeeded, Han Chong was sent to Nanzhao; officials were left in Shu a year at immeasurable expense, yet the barbarians would not receive them.

sentences.zh: 及駢節度西川，招嗢末，繕甲訓兵，蠻夷震動，遣趙宗政入獻，見天子，附驃信再拜；

translations.literal: When Pian governed Xichuan he recruited Wamo, repaired armor and trained troops; the barbarians were shaken and sent Zhao Zongzheng to present tribute; seeing the Son of Heaven, he attached to the piaoxin and bowed twice;
translations.idiomatic: When Pian governed Xichuan he recruited Wamo, repaired armor and trained troops; the barbarians were shaken and sent Zhao Zongzheng to court; seeing the emperor, he attached to the piaoxin and bowed twice;

sentences.zh: 雲虔之使，驃信答拜。

translations.literal: when Yunqian was envoy, the piaoxin returned the bow.
translations.idiomatic: when Yunqian was envoy, the piaoxin returned the bow.

sentences.zh: 其於禮不為少。

translations.literal: In ritual this was not slight.
translations.idiomatic: In ritual this was not slight.

sentences.zh: 宣宗皇帝收三州七關，平江、嶺以南，至大中十四年，內庫貲積如山，戶部延資充滿，故宰相敏中領西川，庫錢至三百萬緡，諸道亦然。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong recovered three prefectures and seven passes; south of the Yangzi and Ling ranges, until the fourteenth year of Dazhong, the inner treasury accumulated like mountains and the Household Ministry's reserves overflowed—therefore Chancellor Minzhong held Xichuan with three million strings in the treasury, and other circuits likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong recovered three prefectures and seven passes; south of the Yangzi and Ling, until Dazhong's fourteenth year the inner treasury accumulated like mountains and Household Ministry reserves overflowed—Chancellor Minzhong held Xichuan with three million strings, other circuits likewise.

sentences.zh: 咸通以來，蠻始叛命，再入安南、邕管，一破黔州，四盜西川，遂圍廬耽，召兵東方，戍海門，天下騷動，十有五年，賦輸不內京師者過半，中藏空虛，士死瘴癘，燎骨傳灰，人不念家，亡命為盜，可為痛心！

translations.literal: Since Xian Tong the barbarians began to rebel; twice they entered Annan and Yongguan, once broke Qinzhou, four times raided Xichuan, besieged Lu Dan, called troops from the east, garrisoned Haimen—the realm was shaken for fifteen years; more than half of tax tribute did not reach the capital; the inner storehouses were empty; soldiers died of miasma; bones were burned and ashes passed on; men forgot their homes; fugitives became bandits—it is heartbreaking!
translations.idiomatic: Since Xian Tong the barbarians rebelled; twice they entered Annan and Yongguan, once broke Qinzhou, four times raided Xichuan, besieged Lu Dan, called troops from the east, garrisoned Haimen—the realm shook fifteen years; half of tax tribute never reached the capital; storehouses emptied; soldiers died of miasma; bones burned and ashes passed on; men forgot home; fugitives became bandits—it is heartbreaking!

sentences.zh: 前年留宗政等，南方無虞，及遣還，彼猶冀望。

translations.literal: The year before, Zongzheng and others were detained and the south was untroubled; when they were sent back, the barbarians still hoped.
translations.idiomatic: The year before, Zongzheng and others were detained and the south was untroubled; when sent back, the barbarians still hoped.

sentences.zh: 蒙法立三年，比兵不出要防，其蓄力以間我虞。

translations.literal: Meng Fa had reigned three years; troops had not marched to key defenses—they were storing strength to watch for our weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Fa had reigned three years without marching to key defenses—storing strength to watch for our weakness.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷府庫匱，甲兵少，牛叢有北兵七萬，首尾奔沖不能救，況安南客戍單寡，涉冬寇禍可虞。

translations.literal: Now the court treasury is depleted and armor few; Niu Cong has seventy thousand northern troops who cannot save both ends; moreover Annan's guest garrisons are thin and solitary—winter raids are to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Now the treasury is depleted and armor few; Niu Cong's seventy thousand northern troops cannot save both ends; Annan's guest garrisons are thin—winter raids are to be feared.

sentences.zh: 誠命使者臨報，縱未稱臣，且伐其謀，外以縻服蠻夷，內得蜀休息也。」

translations.literal: Truly if envoys are sent to report, even if they do not styled themselves subjects, their plots may be broken; outwardly barbarians may be restrained, inwardly Shu may rest."
translations.idiomatic: If envoys are sent to report, even if they do not call themselves subjects, their plots may be broken; outwardly barbarians restrained, inwardly Shu may rest."

sentences.zh: 帝謂然，乃以宗室女為安化長公主許婚。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed and therefore gave an imperial clanswoman as Princess Anhua in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and gave an imperial clanswoman as Princess Anhua in marriage.

sentences.zh: 拜嗣曹王龜年宗正少卿，為雲南使，大理司直徐雲虔副之；

translations.literal: He appointed Prince of Si Cao Guinian as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, Yunnan envoy, with Dali Court Direct Xu Yunqian as deputy;
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Prince of Si Cao Guinian as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan and Yunnan envoy, with Dali Court Direct Xu Yunqian as deputy;

sentences.zh: 內常侍劉光裕為雲南內使，霍承錫副之。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Liu Guangyu as Yunnan inner envoy, with Huo Chengsi as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Liu Guangyu as Yunnan inner envoy, with Huo Chengsi as deputy.

sentences.zh: 及還，具言驃信誠款，以為敬瑄功，故進檢校司空，賜一子官。

translations.literal: Upon return they fully reported the piaoxin's sincere devotion; this was credited to Jingxuan's merit; he was therefore promoted Acting Minister of Works and one son was granted office.
translations.idiomatic: Upon return they reported the piaoxin's sincere devotion; credited to Jingxuan's merit, he was promoted Acting Minister of Works and one son granted office.

sentences.zh: 法遣宰相趙隆眉、楊奇混、段義宗朝行在，迎公主。

translations.literal: Fa sent chancellors Zhao Longmei, Yang Qihun, and Duan Yizong to the imperial camp to welcome the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Fa sent chancellors Zhao Longmei, Yang Qihun, and Duan Yizong to the imperial camp to welcome the princess.

sentences.zh: 高駢自揚州上言：「三人者，南詔心腹也，宜止而鴆之，蠻可圖也。」

translations.literal: Gao Pian from Yangzhou memorialized: "These three are Nanzhao's trusted intimates—they should be detained and poisoned; the barbarians can then be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian from Yangzhou memorialized: "These three are Nanzhao's trusted intimates—detain and poison them; the barbarians can then be taken."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed this.

sentences.zh: 隆眉等皆死，自是謀臣盡矣，蠻益衰。

translations.literal: Longmei and the others all died; from this strategists were exhausted and the barbarians declined further.
translations.idiomatic: Longmei and the others all died; from this strategists were exhausted and the barbarians declined further.

sentences.zh: 中和元年，復遣使者來迎主，獻珍怪氈罽百床，帝以方議公主車服為解。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhonghe they again sent envoys to welcome the princess, presenting a hundred beds of rare felt and rugs; the emperor used discussion of the princess's carriage and robes as pretext to decline.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhonghe they again sent envoys to welcome the princess with a hundred beds of rare felt and rugs; the emperor used discussion of carriage and robes as pretext to decline.

sentences.zh: 後二年，又遣布燮楊奇肱來迎，詔檢校國子祭酒張譙為禮會五禮使，徐雲虔副之，宗正少卿嗣虢王約為婚使。

translations.literal: Two years later they again sent Buxie Yang Qixiong to welcome her; an edict appointed Acting Director of the Imperial Academy Zhang Qiao as Commissioner of the Five Rites Assembly, with Xu Yunqian as deputy, and Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan Prince of Si Guo as marriage envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later they sent Buxie Yang Qixiong to welcome her; an edict appointed Acting Director Zhang Qiao as Commissioner of the Five Rites Assembly with Xu Yunqian as deputy, and Vice Director Prince of Si Guo as marriage envoy.

sentences.zh: 未行，而黃巢平，帝東還，乃歸其使。

translations.literal: Before they departed, Huang Chao was pacified and the emperor returned east; the envoys were sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Before they departed, Huang Chao was pacified and the emperor returned east; the envoys were sent back.

sentences.zh: 法死，偽謚聖明文武皇帝。

translations.literal: Fa died; posthumously styled Emperor Shengming Wenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Fa died; posthumously styled Emperor Shengming Wenwu.

sentences.zh: 子舜化立，建元中興。

translations.literal: His son Shunhua succeeded, establishing the reign title Zhongxing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shunhua succeeded, establishing the reign title Zhongxing.

sentences.zh: 遣使款黎州修好，昭宗不答。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to Lizhou with friendly overtures; Emperor Zhaozong did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to Lizhou with friendly overtures; Emperor Zhaozong did not reply.

sentences.zh: 後中國亂，不復通。

translations.literal: Later China fell into chaos and communication ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Later China fell into chaos and communication ceased.

sentences.zh: 八詔先是，有時傍、矣川羅識二族，通號「八詔」。

translations.literal: Before the Eight Zhao, there were the two clans Shibang and Yichuan Luoshi, jointly styled the "Eight Zhao."
translations.idiomatic: Before the Eight Zhao, there were the two clans Shibang and Yichuan Luoshi, jointly styled the "Eight Zhao."

sentences.zh: 時傍母，歸義女也。

translations.literal: Shibang's mother was Guiyi's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Shibang's mother was Guiyi's daughter.

sentences.zh: 其女復妻閣羅鳳。

translations.literal: Her daughter in turn married Geluofeng.
translations.idiomatic: Her daughter in turn married Geluofeng.

sentences.zh: 初，咩羅皮之敗，時傍入居厓川州，誘上浪千餘，勢稍張，為閣羅所猜，徙置白厓城。

translations.literal: Initially, after Mieluopi's defeat, Shibang entered and dwelt in Yachuan Prefecture, enticing more than a thousand Shanglang and gradually growing stronger; Geluo suspected him and moved him to Baiya City.
translations.idiomatic: After Mieluopi's defeat, Shibang entered Yachuan Prefecture, enticing more than a thousand Shanglang and growing stronger; Geluo suspected him and moved him to Baiya City.

sentences.zh: 後與矣川羅識詣神川都督求自立為詔，謀泄被殺。

translations.literal: Later he and Yichuan Luoshi went to the Shenchuan military commissioner requesting to establish themselves as zhao; the plot was exposed and they were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Yichuan Luoshi went to the Shenchuan military commissioner requesting to establish themselves as zhao; the plot was exposed and they were executed.

sentences.zh: 矣川羅識奔神川，都督送之羅些城。

translations.literal: Yichuan Luoshi fled to Shenchuan; the military commissioner sent him to Luoxie City.
translations.idiomatic: Yichuan Luoshi fled to Shenchuan; the military commissioner sent him to Luoxie City.

sentences.zh: 蒙巂詔，最大。

translations.literal: Mengxie Zhao was the largest.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxie Zhao was the largest.

sentences.zh: 其王巂輔首死，無子，弟佉陽照立。

translations.literal: Its king Xiefushou died without a son; his younger brother Qiyangzhao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Its king Xiefushou died without a son; his younger brother Qiyangzhao succeeded.

sentences.zh: 佉陽照死，子照原立，喪明，子原羅質南詔。

translations.literal: Qiyangzhao died; his son Zhaoyuan succeeded; blind, his son Yuanluo became king of Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyangzhao died; his son Zhaoyuan succeeded; blind, his son Yuanluo became king of Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 歸義欲並國，故歸其子原羅，眾果立之。

translations.literal: Guiyi wished to annex the state and therefore returned his son Yuanluo; the crowd indeed enthroned him.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyi wished to annex the state and returned his son Yuanluo; the crowd indeed enthroned him.

sentences.zh: 居數月，使人殺照原，逐原羅，遂有其地。

translations.literal: Within several months he sent men to kill Zhaoyuan, drive out Yuanluo, and thus possessed the land.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he sent men to kill Zhaoyuan, drive out Yuanluo, and seized the land.

sentences.zh: 越析詔，或謂磨些詔，居故越析州，西距曩蔥山一日行。

translations.literal: Yuexi Zhao, also called Mosuo Zhao, dwelt in former Yuexi Prefecture, one day's journey west of Nangcong Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Yuexi Zhao, also called Mosuo Zhao, dwelt in former Yuexi Prefecture, one day's journey west of Nangcong Mountain.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，有豪酋張尋求烝其王波沖妻，因殺波沖。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era the powerful chieftain Zhang Xunqiu violated the wife of King Bochong and therefore killed Bochong.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenyuan era the powerful chieftain Zhang Xunqiu violated King Bochong's wife and killed him.

sentences.zh: 劍南節度使召尋求至姚州，殺之。

translations.literal: The Jiannan Military Commissioner summoned Xunqiu to Yaozhou and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiannan Military Commissioner summoned Xunqiu to Yaozhou and executed him.

sentences.zh: 部落無長，以地歸南詔。

translations.literal: The tribe had no leader and ceded the land to Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: The tribe had no leader and ceded the land to Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 波沖兄了於贈持王所寶鐸鞘東北度瀘，邑於龍佉河，才百里，號雙舍。

translations.literal: Bochong's elder brother Yuzeng took the king's treasured duoshe and crossed the Lu northeast, settling at Longqiahe—only a hundred li—and styled themselves Shuangshe.
translations.idiomatic: Bochong's elder brother Yuzeng took the king's treasured duoshe and crossed the Lu northeast, settling at Longqiahe—only a hundred li—and styled themselves Shuangshe.

sentences.zh: 使部酋楊墮居河東北。

translations.literal: He had tribal chieftain Yang Duo dwell northeast of the river.
translations.idiomatic: He had tribal chieftain Yang Duo dwell northeast of the river.

sentences.zh: 歸義樹壁侵於贈，不克。

translations.literal: Guiyi built walls and invaded Yuzeng but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyi built walls and invaded Yuzeng but could not overcome him.

sentences.zh: 閣羅鳳自請往擊楊墮，破之，於贈投瀘死。

translations.literal: Geluofeng volunteered to go attack Yang Duo, defeated him; Yuzeng threw himself into the Lu and died.
translations.idiomatic: Geluofeng volunteered to attack Yang Duo, defeated him; Yuzeng threw himself into the Lu and died.

sentences.zh: 得鐸鞘，故王出軍必雙執之。

translations.literal: The duoshe was obtained; hence when the king marched he always held two of them.
translations.idiomatic: The duoshe was obtained; hence when the king marched he always held two of them.

sentences.zh: 浪穹詔，其王豐時死，子羅鐸立。

translations.literal: Langqiong Zhao: its king Fengshi died; his son Luoduo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Langqiong Zhao: its king Fengshi died; his son Luoduo succeeded.

sentences.zh: 羅鐸死，子鐸羅望立，為浪穹州刺史，與南詔戰，不勝，挈其部保劍川，更稱劍浪。

translations.literal: Luoduo died; his son Tluowang succeeded as prefect of Langqiong; he fought Nanzhao without victory, led his tribe to hold Jianchuan, and restyled themselves Jianlang.
translations.idiomatic: Luoduo died; his son Tluowang succeeded as prefect of Langqiong; he fought Nanzhao without victory, led his tribe to hold Jianchuan, and restyled themselves Jianlang.

sentences.zh: 死，子望偏立。

translations.literal: He died; his son Wangpian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Wangpian succeeded.

sentences.zh: 望偏死，子偏羅矣立。

translations.literal: Wangpian died; his son Pianluoyi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Wangpian died; his son Pianluoyi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 偏羅矣死，子羅君立。

translations.literal: Pianluoyi died; his son Luojun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Pianluoyi died; his son Luojun succeeded.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，南詔擊破劍川，虜羅君，徙永昌。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era Nanzhao broke Jianchuan, captured Luojun, and relocated him to Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenyuan era Nanzhao broke Jianchuan, captured Luojun, and relocated him to Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 凡浪穹，邆睒、施浪，謂之浪人，亦稱「三浪」。

translations.literal: Langqiong, Dianshan, and Shilang together were called Lang people and were also styled the "Three Lang."
translations.idiomatic: Langqiong, Dianshan, and Shilang together were called Lang people and were also styled the "Three Lang."

sentences.zh: 邆睒詔，其王豐咩，初據邆睒，為御史李知古所殺。

translations.literal: Dianshan Zhao: its king Fengmie initially held Dianshan and was killed by Censor Li Zhigu.
translations.idiomatic: Dianshan Zhao: its king Fengmie initially held Dianshan and was killed by Censor Li Zhigu.

sentences.zh: 子咩羅皮自為邆川州刺史，治大厘城，歸義襲敗之，復入邆睒，與浪穹、施浪合拒歸義。

translations.literal: His son Mieluopi styled himself prefect of Dichuan, governing Dali City; Guiyi raided and defeated him; he re-entered Dianshan and joined Langqiong and Shilang to resist Guiyi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mieluopi styled himself prefect of Dichuan, governing Dali City; Guiyi raided and defeated him; he re-entered Dianshan and joined Langqiong and Shilang to resist Guiyi.

sentences.zh: 既戰，大敗，歸義奪邆睒，咩羅皮走保野共川。

translations.literal: After battle they suffered a great defeat; Guiyi seized Dianshan; Mieluopi fled to hold Yegongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: After battle they suffered a great defeat; Guiyi seized Dianshan; Mieluopi fled to hold Yegongchuan.

sentences.zh: 死，子皮羅鄧立。

translations.literal: He died; his son Piluodeng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Piluodeng succeeded.

sentences.zh: 皮羅鄧死，子鄧羅顛立。

translations.literal: Piluodeng died; his son Dengluodian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Piluodeng died; his son Dengluodian succeeded.

sentences.zh: 鄧羅顛死，子顛文托立。

translations.literal: Dengluodian died; his son Dianwentuo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Dengluodian died; his son Dianwentuo succeeded.

sentences.zh: 南詔破劍川，虜之。

translations.literal: Nanzhao broke Jianchuan and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao broke Jianchuan and captured him.

sentences.zh: 徙永昌。

translations.literal: He was relocated to Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was relocated to Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 施浪詔，其王施望欠居矣苴和城。

translations.literal: Shilang Zhao: its king Shiwangqian dwelt at Yijuhe City.
translations.idiomatic: Shilang Zhao: its king Shiwangqian dwelt at Yijuhe City.

sentences.zh: 有施各皮者，亦八詔之裔，據石和城。

translations.literal: There was Shigebo, also a descendant of the Eight Zhao, who held Shihe City.
translations.idiomatic: There was Shigebo, also a descendant of the Eight Zhao, who held Shihe City.

sentences.zh: 閣羅鳳攻虜之，而施望欠孤立，故與咩羅皮合攻歸義，不勝。

translations.literal: Geluofeng attacked and captured him; Shiwangqian stood alone and therefore joined Mieluopi to attack Guiyi without victory.
translations.idiomatic: Geluofeng attacked and captured him; Shiwangqian stood alone and joined Mieluopi to attack Guiyi without victory.

sentences.zh: 歸義以兵脅降其部，施望欠以族走永昌，獻其女遺南詔丐和，歸義許之，度蘭江死。

translations.literal: Guiyi threatened and subdued his tribe; Shiwangqian fled to Yongchang with his clan, offered his daughter to Nanzhao to beg peace; Guiyi agreed; crossing the Lan River he died.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyi threatened and subdued his tribe; Shiwangqian fled to Yongchang with his clan, offered his daughter to Nanzhao to beg peace; Guiyi agreed; crossing the Lan River he died.

sentences.zh: 弟望千走吐蕃，吐蕃立為詔，納之劍川，眾數萬。

translations.literal: His younger brother Wangqian fled to Tibet; Tibet enthroned him as zhao and settled him in Jianchuan—tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Wangqian fled to Tibet; Tibet enthroned him as zhao and settled him in Jianchuan—tens of thousands strong.

sentences.zh: 望千死，子千旁羅顛立。

translations.literal: Wangqian died; his son Qianpangluodian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Wangqian died; his son Qianpangluodian succeeded.

sentences.zh: 南詔破劍川，千旁羅顛走瀘北。

translations.literal: Nanzhao broke Jianchuan; Qianpangluodian fled north of the Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao broke Jianchuan; Qianpangluodian fled north of the Lu.

sentences.zh: 三浪悉滅，唯千旁羅顛及矣川羅識子孫在吐蕃。

translations.literal: The Three Lang were all destroyed; only Qianpangluodian and Yichuan Luoshi's descendants remained in Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Lang were all destroyed; only Qianpangluodian and Yichuan Luoshi's descendants remained in Tibet.

sentences.zh: 小論贊曰：

translations.literal: Minor Commentary says:
translations.idiomatic: Minor Commentary says:

sentences.zh: 唐之治不能過兩漢，而地廣於三代，勞民費財，禍所繇生。

translations.literal: Tang governance could not surpass the Two Han, yet its territory was broader than the Three Dynasties; exhausting the people and wasting wealth—calamity arose from this.
translations.idiomatic: Tang governance could not surpass the Two Han, yet its territory was broader than the Three Dynasties; exhausting the people and wasting wealth—calamity arose from this.

sentences.zh: 晉獻公殺嫡，賊二公子，號為暗君。

translations.literal: Duke Xian of Jin killed the legitimate heir and wronged two princes—styled a dark ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xian of Jin killed the legitimate heir and wronged two princes—styled a dark ruler.

sentences.zh: 明皇一日殺三庶人，昏蔽甚矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming in one day killed three common-born sons—how deeply benighted!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming in one day killed three common-born sons—how deeply benighted!

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 父子不相信，而遠治閣羅鳳之罪，士死十萬，當時冤之。

translations.literal: Father and son did not trust each other, yet they blamed Geluofeng from afar—a hundred thousand soldiers died; at the time it was deemed unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son did not trust each other, yet they blamed Geluofeng from afar—a hundred thousand soldiers died; at the time it was deemed unjust.

sentences.zh: 懿宗任相不明，藩鎮屢畔，南詔內侮，屯戍思亂，龐勛乘之，倡戈橫行。

translations.literal: Emperor Yizong employed chancellors without clarity; frontier commands repeatedly rebelled; Nanzhao raided inward; garrison troops thought of mutiny; Pang Xun seized the moment and raised weapons to march unchecked.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yizong employed chancellors without clarity; frontier commands repeatedly rebelled; Nanzhao raided inward; garrison troops thought of mutiny; Pang Xun seized the moment and raised weapons to march unchecked.

sentences.zh: 雖兇渠殲夷，兵連不解，唐遂以亡。

translations.literal: Though the chief rebels were destroyed, warfare did not cease; Tang thus perished.
translations.idiomatic: Though the chief rebels were destroyed, warfare did not cease; Tang thus perished.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「喪牛於易。」

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "Losing cattle at Yi."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "Losing cattle at Yi."

sentences.zh: 有國者知戒西北之虞，而不知患生於無備。

translations.literal: Those who hold a state know to guard against trouble in the northwest yet do not know disaster arises from lack of preparation.
translations.idiomatic: Those who hold a state know to guard the northwest yet do not know disaster arises from lack of preparation.

sentences.zh: 漢亡於董卓，而兵兆於冀州；

translations.literal: Han perished through Dong Zhuo, yet the omen of armies arose in Jizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Han perished through Dong Zhuo, yet the omen of armies arose in Jizhou;

sentences.zh: 唐亡於黃巢，而禍基於桂林。

translations.literal: Tang perished through Huang Chao, yet the foundation of calamity lay in Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: Tang perished through Huang Chao, yet the foundation of calamity lay in Guilin.

sentences.zh: 《易》之意深矣！

translations.literal: The meaning of the Changes runs deep!
translations.idiomatic: The meaning of the Changes runs deep!

sentences.zh: ◎南蠻下環王 （林邑）環王，本林邑也，一曰占不勞，亦曰占婆。

translations.literal: [Southern Barbarians — Lower] Huanwang (Lin-yi): Huanwang was originally Lin-yi, also called Zhanbulao, also called Zhanpo.
translations.idiomatic: [Southern Barbarians — Lower] Huanwang (Lin-yi): Huanwang was originally Lin-yi, also called Zhanbulao or Zhanpo.

sentences.zh: 直交州南，海行三千里。

translations.literal: Directly south of Jiaozhou, three thousand li by sea.
translations.idiomatic: Directly south of Jiaozhou, three thousand li by sea.

sentences.zh: 地東西三百里而贏，南北千里。

translations.literal: The land was three hundred li east to west and narrow, a thousand li north to south.
translations.idiomatic: The land ran three hundred li east to west and narrow, a thousand li north to south.

sentences.zh: 西距真臘霧溫山，南抵奔浪陀州。

translations.literal: West it bordered Chenla's Wuwenshan; south it reached Benlangtuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: West it bordered Chenla's Wuwenshan; south it reached Benlangtuozhou.

sentences.zh: 其南大浦，有五銅柱，山形若倚蓋，西重巖，東涯海，漢馬援所植也。

translations.literal: On its southern great estuary were five bronze pillars; the mountains shaped like leaning canopies; west heavy cliffs, east bound by sea—planted by Han Ma Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: On its southern great estuary stood five bronze pillars; mountains shaped like leaning canopies; west heavy cliffs, east bound by sea—planted by Han Ma Yuan.

sentences.zh: 又有西屠夷，蓋援還，留不去者，才十戶。

translations.literal: There were also Xitu Yi; when Yuan returned, those who remained numbered only ten households.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Xitu Yi; when Yuan returned, those who remained numbered only ten households.

sentences.zh: 隋末孳衍至三百，皆姓馬，俗以其寓，故號「馬留人」，與林邑分唐南境。

translations.literal: By the end of Sui they had multiplied to three hundred, all surnamed Ma; because of where they lodged, custom called them the "Ma Liu people," and together with Linyi they divided Tang's southern border.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Sui they had multiplied to three hundred, all surnamed Ma; because of where they lodged, custom called them the "Ma Liu people," and together with Linyi they divided Tang's southern border.

sentences.zh: 其地冬溫，多霧雨，產虎魄、猩猩獸、結遼鳥。

translations.literal: The land was warm in winter with much fog and rain; it produced amber, orangutans, and jieliao birds.
translations.idiomatic: The land was warm in winter with much fog and rain; it produced amber, orangutans, and jieliao birds.

sentences.zh: 以二月為歲首，稻歲再熟，取檳榔沈為酒，椰葉為席。

translations.literal: They took the second month as New Year; rice ripened twice yearly; betel nut was steeped to make wine; coconut leaves served as mats.
translations.idiomatic: They took the second month as New Year; rice ripened twice yearly; betel nut was steeped for wine; coconut leaves served as mats.

sentences.zh: 俗兇悍，果戰鬥，以麝塗身，日再塗再澡，拜謁則合爪頓顙。

translations.literal: Custom was fierce and bold, fond of battle; musk was smeared on the body, applied twice daily with two baths; in audience they joined palms and bowed the forehead.
translations.idiomatic: Custom was fierce and bold, fond of battle; musk was smeared on the body twice daily with two baths; in audience they joined palms and bowed the forehead.

sentences.zh: 有文字，喜浮屠道，冶金銀像，大或十圍。

translations.literal: They had writing and favored Buddhist law; they cast metal and silver images, some ten arm-spans around.
translations.idiomatic: They had writing and favored Buddhism; they cast metal and silver images, some ten arm-spans around.

sentences.zh: 呼王為陽蒲逋，王妻為陀陽阿熊，太子為阿長逋，宰相為婆漫地。

translations.literal: They called the king Yangpupu, the queen Tuoyangaxiong, the crown prince Achangpu, and the chancellor Pomanidi.
translations.idiomatic: They called the king Yangpupu, the queen Tuoyangaxiong, the crown prince Achangpu, and the chancellor Pomanidi.

sentences.zh: 王所居曰占城，別居曰齊國、曰蓬皮勢。

translations.literal: Where the king dwelt was called Zhancheng; secondary seats were called Qiguo and Pengpishi.
translations.idiomatic: Where the king dwelt was called Zhancheng; secondary seats were Qiguo and Pengpishi.

sentences.zh: 王衣白氎，古貝斜絡臂，飾金琲為纓，鬈髮，戴金華冠如章甫。

translations.literal: The king wore white woolen cloth, ancient shell arm-wrappings, gold beads as tassels, coiled hair, and a golden flower crown like a zhangfu.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore white woolen cloth, ancient shell arm-wrappings, gold bead tassels, coiled hair, and a golden flower crown like a zhangfu.

sentences.zh: 妻服朝霞，古貝短裙，冠纓如王。

translations.literal: The consort wore dawn-colored cloth, ancient shell short skirts, and tassels like the king.
translations.idiomatic: The consort wore dawn-colored cloth, ancient shell short skirts, and tassels like the king.

sentences.zh: 王衛兵五千，戰乘象，藤為鎧，竹為弓矢，率象千、馬四百，分前後。

translations.literal: The king's guard numbered five thousand; in battle they rode elephants; rattan served as armor, bamboo as bow and arrow; a thousand elephants and four hundred horses were divided front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: The king's guard numbered five thousand; in battle they rode elephants with rattan armor and bamboo bows; a thousand elephants and four hundred horses divided front and rear.

sentences.zh: 不設刑，有罪者使象踐之；

translations.literal: No punishments were established; the guilty were made to be trampled by elephants;
translations.idiomatic: No punishments were established; the guilty were trampled by elephants;

sentences.zh: 或送不勞山，畀自死。

translations.literal: or sent to Bulao Mountain to die by themselves.
translations.idiomatic: or sent to Bulao Mountain to die by themselves.

sentences.zh: 隋仁壽中，遣將軍劉芳伐之，其王範梵誌挺走，以其地為三郡，置守令。

translations.literal: In Renshou of Sui, General Liu Fang was dispatched to attack; King Fanfanzhi fled; the land was made three commanderies with prefects and magistrates appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui Renshou, General Liu Fang attacked; King Fanfanzhi fled; the land was made three commanderies with prefects and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 道阻不得通，梵誌裒遺眾，別建國邑。

translations.literal: The road was blocked and could not be traversed; Fanfanzhi gathered the remnant people and separately established a state and settlement.
translations.idiomatic: The road was blocked; Fanfanzhi gathered remnant people and separately established a state.

sentences.zh: 武德中，再遣使獻方物，高祖為設九部樂饗之。

translations.literal: In Wude they twice sent envoys presenting local products; Gaozu set up the Nine Departments of Music to entertain them.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude they twice sent envoys with local products; Gaozu set up the Nine Departments of Music to entertain them.

sentences.zh: 貞觀時，王頭黎獻馴象、镠鎖、五色帶、朝霞布、火珠，與婆利、羅剎二國使者偕來。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan, King Touli presented tame elephants, liusuo, five-colored belts, dawn-colored cloth, and fire pearls, coming together with envoys from Poli and Luosha.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan, King Touli presented tame elephants, liusuo, five-colored belts, dawn cloth, and fire pearls, coming with envoys from Poli and Luosha.

sentences.zh: 林邑其言不恭，群臣請問罪。

translations.literal: Lin-yi's words were disrespectful; ministers requested punishment be inquired.
translations.idiomatic: Lin-yi's words were disrespectful; ministers requested punishment.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「昔苻堅欲吞晉，眾百萬，一戰而亡。

translations.literal: Taizong said: "Formerly Fu Jian wished to swallow Jin with a million men and was destroyed in one battle.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said: "Formerly Fu Jian wished to swallow Jin with a million men and was destroyed in one battle.

sentences.zh: 隋取高麗，歲調發，人與為怨，乃死匹夫手。

translations.literal: Sui took Goguryeo with yearly mobilizations until men resented it and the emperor died at a commoner's hand.
translations.idiomatic: Sui took Goguryeo with yearly mobilizations until men resented it and the emperor died at a commoner's hand.

sentences.zh: 朕敢妄議發兵邪？」

translations.literal: How dare I rashly discuss dispatching troops?"
translations.idiomatic: How dare I rashly dispatch troops?"

sentences.zh: 赦不問。

translations.literal: They were pardoned without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: They were pardoned without inquiry.

sentences.zh: 又獻五色鸚鵡、白鸚鵡，數訴寒，有詔還之。

translations.literal: They again presented five-colored parrots and white parrots, repeatedly complaining of cold; an edict ordered them returned.
translations.idiomatic: They again presented five-colored and white parrots, repeatedly complaining of cold; an edict ordered them returned.

sentences.zh: 頭黎死，子鎮龍立，獻通天犀、雜寶。

translations.literal: Touli died; his son Zhenlong succeeded and presented tongtian rhinoceros and miscellaneous treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Touli died; his son Zhenlong succeeded and presented tongtian rhinoceros and miscellaneous treasures.

sentences.zh: 十九年，摩訶慢多伽獨弒鎮龍，滅其宗，範姓絕。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Mohamanduojia alone murdered Zhenlong and destroyed his clan; the Fan surname was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Mohamanduojia alone murdered Zhenlong and destroyed his clan; the Fan surname was cut off.

sentences.zh: 國人立頭黎婿婆羅門為王，大臣共廢之，更立頭黎女為王。

translations.literal: The people enthroned Touli's son-in-law, a Brahmin, as king; great ministers jointly deposed him and again enthroned Touli's daughter as king.
translations.idiomatic: The people enthroned Touli's Brahmin son-in-law; great ministers deposed him and enthroned Touli's daughter.

sentences.zh: 諸葛地者，頭黎之姑子，父得罪，奔真臘。

translations.literal: Zhugedi was Touli's nephew by marriage; his father offended and fled to Chenla.
translations.idiomatic: Zhugedi was Touli's nephew by marriage; his father offended and fled to Chenla.

sentences.zh: 女之王不能定國，大臣共迎諸葛地為王，妻以女。

translations.literal: The woman could not stabilize the state as queen; great ministers jointly welcomed Zhugedi as king and gave him the daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The woman could not stabilize the state; great ministers welcomed Zhugedi as king and gave him the daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 永徽至天寶，凡三入獻。

translations.literal: From Yonghui to Tianbao they presented tribute three times.
translations.idiomatic: From Yonghui to Tianbao they presented tribute three times.

sentences.zh: 至德後，更號環王。

translations.literal: After Zhide they changed the name to Huanwang.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhide they changed the name to Huanwang.

sentences.zh: 元和初不朝獻，安南都護張舟執其偽、愛州都統，斬三萬級，虜王子五十九，獲戰象、舠、鎧。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe they did not come to court; Annan Protector Zhang Zhou captured their false Ai Prefecture commander, beheaded thirty thousand, captured fifty-nine princes, and seized war elephants, boats, and armor.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuanhe's beginning they did not come to court; Annan Protector Zhang Zhou captured their false Ai Prefecture commander, beheaded thirty thousand, captured fifty-nine princes, and seized war elephants, boats, and armor.

sentences.zh: 婆利婆利者，直環王東南，自交州泛海，歷赤土、丹丹諸國乃至。

translations.literal: Poli: directly southeast of Huanwang; from Jiaozhou by sea, passing Chitu, Dandan, and other states to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Poli: directly southeast of Huanwang; from Jiaozhou by sea, passing Chitu, Dandan, and other states.

sentences.zh: 地大洲，多馬，亦號馬禮。

translations.literal: The land was a great continent with many horses; also called Mali.
translations.idiomatic: The land was a great continent with many horses; also called Mali.

sentences.zh: 袤長數千里。

translations.literal: Length and breadth several thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: It stretched several thousand li in length and breadth.

sentences.zh: 多火珠，大者如雞卵，圓白，照數尺，日中以艾藉珠，輒火出。

translations.literal: Many fire pearls; large ones like hen's eggs, round and white, illuminating several chi; at midday moxa placed beneath the pearl would produce fire.
translations.idiomatic: Many fire pearls; large ones like hen's eggs, round and white, illuminating several chi; at midday moxa beneath a pearl would burst into flame.

sentences.zh: 產玳瑁、文螺；

translations.literal: It produced tortoiseshell and patterned conches;
translations.idiomatic: It produced tortoiseshell and patterned conches;

sentences.zh: 石坩，初取柔可治，既鏤刻即堅。

translations.literal: stone gan—initially taken soft and workable, once carved becoming hard.
translations.idiomatic: stone gan—initially soft and workable, once carved becoming hard.

sentences.zh: 有舍利鳥，通人言。

translations.literal: There were sheli birds that understood human speech.
translations.idiomatic: There were sheli birds that understood human speech.

sentences.zh: 俗黑身，朱發而拳，鷹爪獸牙，穿耳傅珰，以古貝橫一幅繚於腰。

translations.literal: Custom: black bodies, red curled hair, eagle claws and beast teeth, pierced ears with pendants, ancient shell draped horizontally one panel around the waist.
translations.idiomatic: Custom: black bodies, red curled hair, eagle claws and beast teeth, pierced ears with pendants, ancient shell draped one panel around the waist.

sentences.zh: 古貝，草也，緝其花為布，粗曰貝，精曰氎。

translations.literal: Ancient shell was a plant; its flowers woven into cloth—coarse called bei, fine called zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient shell was a plant; its flowers woven into cloth—coarse called bei, fine called zhan.

sentences.zh: 俗以夜為市，自掩其面。

translations.literal: Custom took night as market time; faces were covered by themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They traded by night, each covering the face.

sentences.zh: 王姓剎利邪伽，名護路那婆，世居位。

translations.literal: The king's surname was Kshatriya; his name Hulunapo; the family had held the throne for generations.
translations.idiomatic: The king's surname was Kshatriya; his name Hulunapo; the family had held the throne for generations.

sentences.zh: 繚班絲貝，綴珠為飾。

translations.literal: Wrapped in patterned silk shell, adorned with pearls.
translations.idiomatic: Wrapped in patterned silk shell, adorned with pearls.

sentences.zh: 坐金榻，左右持白拂、孔雀翣。

translations.literal: He sat on a golden couch; attendants at left and right held white whisks and peacock-tail fans.
translations.idiomatic: He sat on a golden couch; attendants at left and right held white whisks and peacock-tail fans.

sentences.zh: 出以象駕車，羽蓋珠箔，鳴金、擊鼓、吹蠡為樂。

translations.literal: When going out he rode in an elephant-drawn carriage with feather canopy and pearl curtains; gold was struck, drums beaten, and conch blown for music.
translations.idiomatic: Going abroad he rode in an elephant-drawn carriage with feather canopy and pearl curtains; gold was struck, drums beaten, and conch blown for music.

sentences.zh: 羅剎其東即羅剎也，與婆利同俗。

translations.literal: Luosha: to its east was Luosha, sharing Poli's customs.
translations.idiomatic: Luosha lay to the east, sharing Poli's customs.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝遣常駿使赤土，遂通中國。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang of Sui dispatched Chang Jun as envoy to Chitu, thus opening contact with China.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang dispatched Chang Jun as envoy to Chitu, opening contact with China.

sentences.zh: 婆羅赤土西南入海，得婆羅。

translations.literal: Southwest of Poli by sea one reached Poluo.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest of Poli by sea one reached Poluo.

sentences.zh: 總章二年，其王旃達缽遣使者與環王使者偕朝。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zongzhang its king Chandabuo sent envoys to court together with Huanwang's envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In Zongzhang's second year its king Chandabuo sent envoys to court with Huanwang's envoys.

sentences.zh: 殊柰環王南有殊柰者，泛交趾海三月乃至，與婆羅同俗。

translations.literal: Shunai: south of Huanwang was Shunai; three months by sea from Jiaozhi to arrive, sharing Poli's customs.
translations.idiomatic: Shunai lay south of Huanwang; three months by sea from Jiaozhi, sharing Poli's customs.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年，使者上方物。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan envoys presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan's second year envoys presented local products.

sentences.zh: 九年，甘棠使者入朝，國居海南。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Gantang envoys came to court; the state lay south of the sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Gantang envoys came to court; the state lay south of the sea.

sentences.zh: 十二年，僧高、武令、迦乍、鳩密四國使者朝貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year envoys from Senggao, Wuling, Jiazhai, and Jiumi presented tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year envoys from Senggao, Wuling, Jiazhai, and Jiumi presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 僧高直水真臘西北，與環王同俗。

translations.literal: Senggao lay directly northwest of Chenla, sharing Huanwang's customs.
translations.idiomatic: Senggao lay northwest of Chenla, sharing Huanwang's customs.

sentences.zh: 其後鳩密王屍利鳩摩又與富那王屍利提婆跋摩等遣使來貢。

translations.literal: Later King Jimijumo of Jiumi together with King Jimotipomo of Funna and others sent envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Later King Jimijumo of Jiumi together with King Jimotipomo of Funna sent envoys to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 僧高等國，永徽後為真臘所並。

translations.literal: Senggao and other states after Yonghui were annexed by Chenla.
translations.idiomatic: Senggao and other states after Yonghui were annexed by Chenla.

sentences.zh: 盤盤盤盤，在南海曲，北距環王，限少海，與狼牙脩接，自交州海行四十日乃至。

translations.literal: Shepan: Shepan lay in a bend of the southern sea, north bordering Huanwang, bounded by the Lesser Sea, adjoining Langyaxiu; forty days by sea from Jiaozhou to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Shepan lay in a bend of the southern sea, north bordering Huanwang, bounded by the Lesser Sea, adjoining Langyaxiu—forty days by sea from Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 王曰楊粟翨。

translations.literal: The king was called Yanglishe.
translations.idiomatic: The king was called Yanglishe.

sentences.zh: 其民瀕水居，比木為柵，石為矢鏃。

translations.literal: The people dwelt along the water, building palisades of wood; stone served as arrowheads.
translations.idiomatic: The people dwelt along the water in wooden palisades; stone served as arrowheads.

sentences.zh: 王坐金龍大榻，諸大人見王，交手抱肩以跽。

translations.literal: The king sat on a great golden dragon couch; great men seeing the king joined hands, embraced shoulders, and knelt.
translations.idiomatic: The king sat on a great golden dragon couch; great men seeing him joined hands, embraced shoulders, and knelt.

sentences.zh: 其臣曰勃郎索濫，曰昆侖帝也，曰昆侖勃和，曰昆侖勃諦索甘，亦曰古龍。

translations.literal: His ministers were called Bolangsolan, Kunlundi, Kunlunbohe, Kunlunbodisogan—also called Gulong.
translations.idiomatic: His ministers were Bolangsolan, Kunlundi, Kunlunbohe, Kunlunbodisogan—also called Gulong.

sentences.zh: 古龍者，昆侖聲近耳。

translations.literal: Gulong—the sound approximates Kunlun.
translations.idiomatic: Gulong—the sound approximates Kunlun.

sentences.zh: 在外曰那延，猶中國刺史也。

translations.literal: Externally there was Nayyan, like a Chinese prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Externally there was Nayyan, like a Chinese prefect.

sentences.zh: 有佛、道士祠，僧食肉，不飲酒，道士謂為貪，不食酒肉。

translations.literal: There were Buddhist and Daoist temples; monks ate meat and did not drink wine; Daoists were called "greedy" and ate neither wine nor meat.
translations.idiomatic: There were Buddhist and Daoist temples; monks ate meat and did not drink wine; Daoists ate neither wine nor meat.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，再遣使朝。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan they twice sent envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan they twice sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 哥羅其東南有哥羅，一曰個羅，亦曰哥羅富沙羅。

translations.literal: Southeast of Shepan was Gela, also called Gela or Gelafushaluo.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast of Shepan was Gela, also called Gela or Gelafushaluo.

sentences.zh: 王姓矢利波羅，名米失缽羅。

translations.literal: The king's surname was Shilipoluo; his name Mishiboluo.
translations.idiomatic: The king's surname was Shilipoluo; his name Mishiboluo.

sentences.zh: 累石為城，樓闕宮室茨以草。

translations.literal: Piled stone formed the city; towers, pavilions, and palace rooms were thatched with grass.
translations.idiomatic: Piled stone formed the city; towers and palace rooms were thatched with grass.

sentences.zh: 州二十四。

translations.literal: Twenty-four prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four prefectures.

sentences.zh: 其兵有弓矢槊殳，以孔雀羽飾纛。

translations.literal: Their weapons included bow, arrow, spear, and shu; peacock feathers adorned banners.
translations.idiomatic: Their weapons included bow, arrow, spear, and shu; peacock feathers adorned banners.

sentences.zh: 每戰，以百象為一隊，一象百人，鞍若檻，四人執弓槊在中。

translations.literal: In battle a hundred elephants formed one company; one elephant carried a hundred men; the saddle like a cage; four men wielding bow and spear in the center.
translations.idiomatic: In battle a hundred elephants formed one company; one elephant carried a hundred men in saddle-cages; four men wielding bow and spear in the center.

sentences.zh: 賦率輸銀二銖。

translations.literal: Tax rate: two zhu of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Tax rate: two zhu of silver.

sentences.zh: 無絲纻，惟古貝。

translations.literal: No silk or hemp—only ancient shell cloth.
translations.idiomatic: No silk or hemp—only ancient shell cloth.

sentences.zh: 畜多牛少馬。

translations.literal: Livestock: many cattle, few horses.
translations.idiomatic: Livestock: many cattle, few horses.

sentences.zh: 非有官不束發。

translations.literal: Unless holding office, hair was not bound.
translations.idiomatic: Unless holding office, hair was not bound.

sentences.zh: 凡嫁娶，納檳榔為禮，多至二百盤。

translations.literal: In marriage betrothal, betel nut was presented as gift—up to two hundred trays.
translations.idiomatic: In marriage, betel nut was presented as gift—up to two hundred trays.

sentences.zh: 婦已嫁，從夫姓。

translations.literal: Once married, women took the husband's surname.
translations.idiomatic: Once married, women took the husband's surname.

sentences.zh: 樂有琵琶、橫笛、銅鈸、鐵鼓、蠡。

translations.literal: Music included pipa, transverse flute, bronze cymbals, iron drum, and conch.
translations.idiomatic: Music included pipa, transverse flute, bronze cymbals, iron drum, and conch.

sentences.zh: 死者焚之，取燼貯金罌沈之海。

translations.literal: The dead were cremated; ashes were stored in golden urns and sunk in the sea.
translations.idiomatic: The dead were cremated; ashes were stored in golden urns and sunk in the sea.

sentences.zh: 拘蔞蜜東南有拘蔞蜜，海行一月至。

translations.literal: Southeast of Gela was Juloumi; one month by sea to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast of Gela was Juloumi; one month by sea.

sentences.zh: 南距婆利，行十日至。

translations.literal: South ten days' journey to Poli.
translations.idiomatic: South ten days' journey to Poli.

sentences.zh: 東距不述，行五日至。

translations.literal: East five days' journey to Bushu.
translations.idiomatic: East five days' journey to Bushu.

sentences.zh: 西北距文單，行六日至。

translations.literal: Northwest six days' journey to Wendan.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest six days' journey to Wendan.

sentences.zh: 與赤土、墮和羅同俗。

translations.literal: Sharing Chitu's and Duohailuo's customs.
translations.idiomatic: Sharing Chitu's and Duohailuo's customs.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，獻五色鸚鵡。

translations.literal: In Yonghui they presented five-colored parrots.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui they presented five-colored parrots.

sentences.zh: 扶南扶南，在日南之南七千里，地卑窪，與環王同俗，有城郭宮室。

translations.literal: Funan: Funan lay seven thousand li south of Rinan; the land was low and marshy, sharing Huanwang's customs; there were walled cities and palace rooms.
translations.idiomatic: Funan lay seven thousand li south of Rinan; low and marshy, sharing Huanwang's customs; walled cities and palaces stood there.

sentences.zh: 王姓古龍。

translations.literal: The king's surname was Gulong.
translations.idiomatic: The king's surname was Gulong.

sentences.zh: 居重觀，柵城，楉葉以覆屋。

translations.literal: He dwelt in a multi-storied pavilion, palisade city, nipa leaves covering the roof.
translations.idiomatic: He dwelt in a multi-storied pavilion in a palisade city, nipa leaves covering the roof.

sentences.zh: 王出乘象。

translations.literal: When the king went out he rode an elephant.
translations.idiomatic: When the king went out he rode an elephant.

sentences.zh: 其人黑身、鬈髮，倮行，俗不為寇盜。

translations.literal: The people had black bodies and coiled hair, went naked, and by custom did not rob or steal.
translations.idiomatic: The people had black bodies and coiled hair, went naked, and by custom did not rob or steal.

sentences.zh: 田一歲種，三歲獲。

translations.literal: Fields were sown once yearly and harvested thrice.
translations.idiomatic: Fields were sown once yearly and harvested thrice.

sentences.zh: 國出剛金，狀類紫石英，生水底石上，人沒水取之，可以刻玉，扣以羖角，乃泮。

translations.literal: The state produced gang steel, resembling purple quartz, on stones at the river bottom; men dove to take it; it could carve jade; struck with ram's horn it melted.
translations.idiomatic: The state produced gang steel resembling purple quartz on riverbed stones; divers took it; it could carve jade; struck with ram's horn it melted.

sentences.zh: 人喜鬥雞及豬。

translations.literal: People loved cockfighting and pigs.
translations.idiomatic: People loved cockfighting and pigs.

sentences.zh: 以金、珠、香為稅。

translations.literal: Gold, pearls, and incense served as tax.
translations.idiomatic: Gold, pearls, and incense served as tax.

sentences.zh: 治特牧城，俄為真臘所並，益南徙那弗那城。

translations.literal: The capital was Temucheng; soon annexed by Chenla, they moved further south to Nafuna City.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was Temucheng; soon annexed by Chenla, they moved further south to Nafuna City.

sentences.zh: 武德、貞觀時，再入朝，又獻白頭人二。

translations.literal: In Wude and Zhenguan they twice came to court and also presented two white-headed men.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude and Zhenguan they twice came to court and presented two white-headed men.

sentences.zh: 白頭白頭者，直扶南西，人皆素首，膚理如脂。

translations.literal: Baitou: Baitou lay directly west of Funan; all had white heads; skin smooth as grease.
translations.idiomatic: Baitou lay directly west of Funan; all had white heads; skin smooth as grease.

sentences.zh: 居山穴，四面峭絕，人莫得至。

translations.literal: They dwelt in mountain caves on all sides steep and inaccessible; none could reach them.
translations.idiomatic: They dwelt in mountain caves on all sides steep and inaccessible.

sentences.zh: 與參半國接。

translations.literal: They bordered Canban Country.
translations.idiomatic: They bordered Canban Country.

sentences.zh: 真臘真臘，一曰吉蔑，本扶南屬國。

translations.literal: Chenla: Chenla, also called Jimie, was originally a Funan vassal state.
translations.idiomatic: Chenla, also called Jimie, was originally a Funan vassal state.

sentences.zh: 去京師二萬七百里。

translations.literal: Twenty-seven thousand li from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-seven thousand li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 東距車渠，西屬驃，南瀕海，北與道明接，東北抵州。

translations.literal: East bordering Chequ, west belonging to Pyu, south facing the sea, north adjoining Daoming, northeast reaching prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: East bordering Chequ, west to Pyu, south facing the sea, north adjoining Daoming.

sentences.zh: 其王剎利伊金那，貞觀初並扶南有其地。

translations.literal: Its king was Kshatriya Ijinnuo; at the beginning of Zhenguan he annexed Funan and possessed its land.
translations.idiomatic: Its king was Kshatriya Ijinnuo; at Zhenguan's beginning he annexed Funan and possessed its land.

sentences.zh: 戶皆東向，坐上東。

translations.literal: All households faced east; when seated one faced east.
translations.idiomatic: All households faced east; when seated one faced east.

sentences.zh: 客至，屑檳榔、龍腦、香蛤以進。

translations.literal: When guests arrived, shredded betel nut, borneol, and fragrant clams were presented.
translations.idiomatic: When guests arrived, shredded betel nut, borneol, and fragrant clams were presented.

sentences.zh: 不飲酒，比之淫。

translations.literal: They did not drink wine—compared to debauchery.
translations.idiomatic: They did not drink wine—it was compared to debauchery.

sentences.zh: 與妻飲房中，避尊屬。

translations.literal: They drank with wives in inner chambers, avoiding elders.
translations.idiomatic: They drank with wives in inner chambers, avoiding elders.

sentences.zh: 有戰象五千，良者飼以肉。

translations.literal: There were five thousand war elephants; the best were fed meat.
translations.idiomatic: There were five thousand war elephants; the best were fed meat.

sentences.zh: 世與參半、驃通好，與環王乾陀洹數相攻。

translations.literal: For generations they maintained friendship with Canban and Pyu; with Huanwang and Gandhara they repeatedly fought.
translations.idiomatic: For generations they maintained friendship with Canban and Pyu; with Huanwang and Gandhara they repeatedly fought.

sentences.zh: 自武德至聖歷，凡四來朝。

translations.literal: From Wude to Shengli they came to court four times.
translations.idiomatic: From Wude to Shengli they came to court four times.

sentences.zh: 神龍後分為二半：北多山阜，號陸真臘半；

translations.literal: After Shenlong it split in two: the north had many hills and mounds, styled Land Chenla;
translations.idiomatic: After Shenlong it split in two: the north had many hills, styled Land Chenla;

sentences.zh: 南際海，饒陂澤，號水真臘半。

translations.literal: the south bordered the sea, rich in marshes, styled Water Chenla.
translations.idiomatic: the south bordered the sea, rich in marshes, styled Water Chenla.

sentences.zh: 水真臘，地八百里，王居婆羅提拔城。

translations.literal: Water Chenla: eight hundred li of land; the king dwelt at Poluotiba City.
translations.idiomatic: Water Chenla: eight hundred li; the king dwelt at Poluotiba City.

sentences.zh: 陸真臘或曰文單，曰婆鏤，地七百里，王號「屈」。

translations.literal: Land Chenla, also called Wendan and Polou, covered seven hundred li; its king was styled "Qu."
translations.idiomatic: Land Chenla, also called Wendan and Polou, covered seven hundred li; its king was styled "Qu."

sentences.zh: 開元、天寶時，王子率其屬二十六來朝，拜果毅都尉。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan and Tianbao a prince led twenty-six of his followers to court and was appointed Guoyi Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan and Tianbao a prince led twenty-six followers to court and was appointed Guoyi Commander.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，副王婆彌及妻來朝，獻馴象十一；

translations.literal: In Dali the vice-king Pomi and his wife came to court, presenting eleven tame elephants;
translations.idiomatic: In Dali vice-king Pomi and his wife came to court, presenting eleven tame elephants;

sentences.zh: 擢婆彌試殿中監，賜名賓漢。

translations.literal: Pomi was promoted Trial Director of the Palace Administration and granted the name Binhan.
translations.idiomatic: Pomi was promoted Trial Director of the Palace Administration and granted the name Binhan.

sentences.zh: 是時，德宗初即位，珍禽奇獸悉縱之，蠻夷所獻馴象畜苑中，元會充廷者凡三十二，悉放荊山之陽。

translations.literal: At that time Dezong had just succeeded; rare birds and beasts were all released; tame elephants presented by barbarians kept in the park, thirty-two filling the court at New Year's, were all released on the southern slopes of Jingshan.
