translations.idiomatic: Dezong had just succeeded; rare birds and beasts were released; tame elephants from barbarian tribute, thirty-two filling the court at New Year's, were released on Jingshan's southern slopes.

sentences.zh: 及元和中，水真臘亦遣使入貢。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era Water Chenla also sent envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe Water Chenla also sent envoys to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 參半文單西北屬國曰參半，武德八年使者來。

translations.literal: Canban: northwest of Wendan was the vassal state Canban; in the eighth year of Wude envoys came.
translations.idiomatic: Canban, northwest of Wendan, was a vassal state; in Wude's eighth year envoys came.

sentences.zh: 道明道明者，亦屬國，無衣服，見衣服者共笑之。

translations.literal: Daoming: also a vassal state; without clothing—seeing clothes they laughed together.
translations.idiomatic: Daoming was also a vassal state; without clothing—seeing clothes they laughed together.

sentences.zh: 無鹽鐵，以竹弩射鳥獸自給。

translations.literal: Without salt or iron; bamboo crossbows shot birds and beasts for subsistence.
translations.idiomatic: Without salt or iron; bamboo crossbows shot birds and beasts for subsistence.

sentences.zh: 訶陵訶陵，亦曰社婆，曰阇婆，在南海中。

translations.literal: Heling: Heling, also called Shepo or Shepo, lay in the southern sea.
translations.idiomatic: Heling, also Shepo or Shepo, lay in the southern sea.

sentences.zh: 東距婆利，西墮婆登，南瀕海，北真臘。

translations.literal: East bordering Poli, west Duobodeng, south facing the sea, north Chenla.
translations.idiomatic: East bordering Poli, west Duobodeng, south facing the sea, north Chenla.

sentences.zh: 木為城，雖大屋亦覆以栟櫚。

translations.literal: Wood formed the city; even great houses were covered with areca palm.
translations.idiomatic: Wood formed the city; even great houses were covered with areca palm.

sentences.zh: 象牙為床若席。

translations.literal: Ivory served as bed or mat.
translations.idiomatic: Ivory served as bed or mat.

sentences.zh: 出玳瑁、黃白金、犀、象，國最富。

translations.literal: It produced tortoiseshell, yellow gold, white gold, rhinoceros horn, and elephants—the richest state.
translations.idiomatic: It produced tortoiseshell, yellow and white gold, rhinoceros horn, and elephants—the richest state.

sentences.zh: 有穴自湧鹽。

translations.literal: There were caves from which salt sprang forth.
translations.idiomatic: Caves sprang forth salt.

sentences.zh: 以柳花、椰子為酒，飲之輒醉，宿昔壞。

translations.literal: Willow flowers and coconut made wine; drinking it one became drunk; overnight it spoiled.
translations.idiomatic: Willow flowers and coconut made wine; one drink brought drunkenness; overnight it spoiled.

sentences.zh: 有文字，知星歷。

translations.literal: They had writing and knew astronomy and calendrics.
translations.idiomatic: They had writing and knew astronomy and calendrics.

sentences.zh: 食無匕筋。

translations.literal: They ate without spoon or chopsticks.
translations.idiomatic: They ate without spoon or chopsticks.

sentences.zh: 有毒女，與接輒苦瘡，人死屍不腐。

translations.literal: There were poison women; contact brought painful sores; corpses of the dead did not decay.
translations.idiomatic: There were poison women; contact brought painful sores; corpses did not decay.

sentences.zh: 王居阇婆城。

translations.literal: The king dwelt at Shepo City.
translations.idiomatic: The king dwelt at Shepo City.

sentences.zh: 其祖吉延東遷於婆露伽斯城，旁小國二十八，莫不臣服。

translations.literal: His ancestor Jiyan moved east to Poluojiasi City; twenty-eight small neighboring states all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Jiyan moved east to Poluojiasi City; twenty-eight small neighboring states all submitted.

sentences.zh: 其官有三十二大夫，而大坐敢兄為最貴。

translations.literal: Offices numbered thirty-two grandees; the Great Seat Ganxiong was most honored.
translations.idiomatic: Offices numbered thirty-two grandees; the Great Seat Ganxiong was most honored.

sentences.zh: 山上有郎卑野州，王常登以望海。

translations.literal: On the mountain was Langbei Wild Prefecture; the king often ascended to view the sea.
translations.idiomatic: On the mountain was Langbei Wild Prefecture; the king often ascended to view the sea.

sentences.zh: 夏至立八尺表，景在表南二尺四寸。

translations.literal: At the summer solstice an eight-chi gnomon was set; the shadow lay two chi four cun south of the gnomon.
translations.idiomatic: At the summer solstice an eight-chi gnomon was set; the shadow lay two chi four cun south of it.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，與墮和羅、墮婆登皆遣使者入貢，太宗以璽詔優答。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan, together with Duohailuo and Duobodeng, they sent envoys to present tribute; Taizong replied with imperial seal edicts of favor.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan, with Duohailuo and Duobodeng, they sent envoys; Taizong replied with imperial seal edicts of favor.

sentences.zh: 墮和羅丐良馬，帝與之。

translations.literal: Duohailuo begged fine horses; the emperor granted them.
translations.idiomatic: Duohailuo begged fine horses; the emperor granted them.

sentences.zh: 至上元間，國人推女子為王，號「悉莫」，威令整肅，道不舉遺。

translations.literal: By the Shangyuan era, the people enthroned a woman as ruler, styled "Simo"; her commands were strict, and lost things were not picked up on the road.
translations.idiomatic: By the Shangyuan era, the people enthroned a woman as ruler, styled "Simo"; her commands were strict, and lost things were not picked up on the road.

sentences.zh: 大食君聞之，賫金一囊置其郊，行者輒避，如是三年。

translations.literal: The Abbasid lord heard of this and placed a bag of gold in the suburbs; travelers all avoided it—for three years thus.
translations.idiomatic: The Abbasid lord heard and placed a bag of gold in the suburbs; travelers avoided it—for three years.

sentences.zh: 太子過，以足躪金，悉莫怒，將斬之，群臣固請。

translations.literal: The crown prince passed and trampled the gold with his foot; Simo grew angry and was about to execute him; ministers firmly pleaded.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince passed and trampled the gold; Simo grew angry and was about to execute him; ministers firmly pleaded.

sentences.zh: 悉莫曰：「而罪實本於足，可斷趾。」

translations.literal: Simo said: "Your crime truly originates in the foot—the toes may be cut off."
translations.idiomatic: Simo said: "Your crime truly originates in the foot—the toes may be cut off."

sentences.zh: 群臣復為請，乃斬指以徇。

translations.literal: Ministers again pleaded; fingers were cut off as warning.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers again pleaded; fingers were cut off as warning.

sentences.zh: 大食聞而畏之，不敢加兵。

translations.literal: The Abbasids heard and feared her, not daring to send troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Abbasids heard and feared her, not daring to send troops.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，訶陵使者三至。

translations.literal: In the Dali era Heling envoys came three times.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali era Heling envoys came three times.

sentences.zh: 元和八年，獻僧只奴四、五色鸚鵡、頻伽鳥等。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanhe they presented four sangzhi slaves, five-colored parrots, pinjia birds, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe's eighth year they presented four sangzhi slaves, five-colored parrots, pinjia birds, and others.

sentences.zh: 憲宗拜內四門府左果毅。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong appointed them Guoyi of the Inner Four Gates Office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong appointed them Guoyi of the Inner Four Gates Office.

sentences.zh: 使者讓其弟，帝嘉美，並官之。

translations.literal: The envoy yielded precedence to his younger brother; the emperor praised this and enfeoffed both.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy yielded precedence to his younger brother; the emperor praised this and enfeoffed both.

sentences.zh: 訖大和，再朝貢。

translations.literal: Until Dahe they came to court twice with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Until Dahe they came to court twice with tribute.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，遣使獻女樂。

translations.literal: In Xian Tong they sent envoys presenting female musicians.
translations.idiomatic: In Xian Tong they sent envoys presenting female musicians.

sentences.zh: 墮和羅墮和羅，亦曰獨和羅，南距盤盤，北迦羅舍弗，西屬海，東真臘。

translations.literal: Duohailuo: Duohailuo, also called Duohailuo, south bordering Shepan, north Kalaoshefu, west belonging to the sea, east Chenla.
translations.idiomatic: Duohailuo, also Duohailuo, south of Shepan, north of Kalaoshefu, west to the sea, east to Chenla.

sentences.zh: 自廣州行五月乃至。

translations.literal: Five months' journey from Guangzhou to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Five months' journey from Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 國多美犀，世謂墮和羅犀。

translations.literal: The state had many fine rhinoceros; the age called them Duohailuo rhinoceros.
translations.idiomatic: The state had many fine rhinoceros renowned as Duohailuo rhinoceros.

sentences.zh: 有二屬國，曰曇陵、陀洹。

translations.literal: Two vassal states: Tanling and Tuohuan.
translations.idiomatic: Two vassal states: Tanling and Tuohuan.

sentences.zh: 曇陵曇陵在海洲中。

translations.literal: Tanling lay on an island in the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Tanling lay on an island in the sea.

sentences.zh: 陀洹，一曰耨陀洹，在環王西南海中，與墮和羅接，自交州行九十日乃至。

translations.literal: Tuohuan, also called Noutuohuan, southwest of Huanwang in the sea, adjoining Duohailuo; ninety days from Jiaozhou to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Tuohuan, also Noutuohuan, southwest of Huanwang in the sea, adjoining Duohailuo—ninety days from Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 王姓察失利，名婆那，字婆末。

translations.literal: The king's surname was Chalishi; his name Pona, style Pomo.
translations.idiomatic: The king's surname was Chalishi; his name Pona, style Pomo.

sentences.zh: 無蠶桑，有稻、麥、麻、豆。

translations.literal: No silkworms or mulberry; there were rice, wheat, hemp, and beans.
translations.idiomatic: No silkworms or mulberry; rice, wheat, hemp, and beans grew there.

sentences.zh: 畜有白象、牛、羊、豬。

translations.literal: Livestock included white elephants, cattle, sheep, and pigs.
translations.idiomatic: Livestock included white elephants, cattle, sheep, and pigs.

sentences.zh: 俗喜樓居，謂為幹欄。

translations.literal: Custom favored elevated dwellings, called ganlan.
translations.idiomatic: They favored elevated dwellings called ganlan.

sentences.zh: 以白氎、朝霞布為衣。

translations.literal: White woolen cloth and dawn-colored cloth served as clothing.
translations.idiomatic: White woolens and dawn-colored cloth served as clothing.

sentences.zh: 親喪，在室不食，燔屍已，則剔發浴於池，然後食。

translations.literal: When kin died, they did not eat indoors; after cremating the corpse they shaved the head and bathed in a pool, then ate.
translations.idiomatic: When kin died they fasted indoors; after cremation they shaved and bathed in a pool, then ate.

sentences.zh: 貞觀時，並遣使者再入朝，又獻婆律膏、白鸚鵡，首有十紅毛，齊於翅。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan they jointly sent envoys twice to court, also presenting balu ointment and white parrots with ten red feathers on the head level with the wings.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan they sent envoys twice, presenting balu ointment and white parrots with ten red head feathers level with the wings.

sentences.zh: 因丐馬、銅鐘，帝與之。

translations.literal: They begged horses and bronze bells; the emperor granted them.
translations.idiomatic: They begged horses and bronze bells; the emperor granted them.

sentences.zh: 墮婆登墮婆登在環王南，行二月乃至。

translations.literal: Duobodeng: Duobodeng lay south of Huanwang; two months' journey to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Duobodeng lay south of Huanwang; two months' journey.

sentences.zh: 東訶陵，西迷黎車，北屬海。

translations.literal: East Heling, west Miliche, north belonging to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: East to Heling, west to Miliche, north to the sea.

sentences.zh: 俗與訶陵同。

translations.literal: Customs resembled Heling.
translations.idiomatic: Customs resembled Heling.

sentences.zh: 種稻，月一熟。

translations.literal: Rice was planted; it ripened once monthly.
translations.idiomatic: Rice ripened once monthly.

sentences.zh: 有文字，以貝多葉寫之。

translations.literal: They had writing, using pattra leaves.
translations.idiomatic: They had writing on pattra leaves.

sentences.zh: 死者實金於口，以釧貫其體，加婆律膏、龍腦眾香，積薪燔之。

translations.literal: When the dead died, gold was placed in the mouth; bracelets pierced the body; balu ointment and borneol and many fragrances were added; firewood was piled and they were cremated.
translations.idiomatic: The dead received gold in the mouth, bracelets through the body, balu ointment and borneol and many fragrances; firewood was piled and they were cremated.

sentences.zh: 投和投和，在真臘南，自廣州西南海行百日乃至。

translations.literal: Touhe: Touhe lay south of Chenla; a hundred days by sea southwest from Guangzhou to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Touhe lay south of Chenla; a hundred days by sea southwest from Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 王姓投和羅，名脯邪迄遙。

translations.literal: The king's surname was Touheluo; his name Puyeqiyao.
translations.idiomatic: The king's surname was Touheluo; his name Puyeqiyao.

sentences.zh: 官有朝請將軍、功曹、主簿、贊理、贊府，分領國事。

translations.literal: Offices included Court-Requesting General, Merit Officer, Chief Clerk, Assistant Administrator, and Assistant Prefect, dividing state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Offices included Court-Requesting General, Merit Officer, Chief Clerk, and assistants dividing state affairs.

sentences.zh: 分州、郡、縣三等。

translations.literal: Prefectures, commanderies, and counties were divided into three grades.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures, commanderies, and counties came in three grades.

sentences.zh: 州有參軍，郡有金威將軍，縣有城、有局，長官得選僚屬自助。

translations.literal: Prefectures had military aides; commanderies had Golden Might Generals; counties had walls and bureaus; chief officials could select staff to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures had military aides; commanderies Golden Might Generals; counties walls and bureaus; chiefs could select staff.

sentences.zh: 民居率樓閣，畫壁。

translations.literal: People mostly lived in towers and pavilions with painted walls.
translations.idiomatic: People mostly lived in towers with painted walls.

sentences.zh: 王宿衛百人，衣朝霞，耳金鈈，金綖被頸，寶飾革履。

translations.literal: The king's guard numbered a hundred; dawn-colored clothing, gold ear ornaments, gold thread around the neck, precious ornaments and leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: The king's guard numbered a hundred in dawn cloth, gold ear ornaments, gold thread at the neck, precious ornaments and leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 頻盜者死，次穿耳及頰而劗其發，盜鑄者截手。

translations.literal: Repeated thieves were executed; lesser offenders had ears and cheeks pierced and hair shaved; counterfeiters had hands cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated thieves were executed; lesser offenders had ears and cheeks pierced and hair shaved; counterfeiters lost their hands.

sentences.zh: 無賦稅，民以地多少自輸。

translations.literal: No taxes or levies; people paid according to land held.
translations.idiomatic: No fixed taxes; people paid according to land held.

sentences.zh: 王以農商自業。

translations.literal: The king engaged in farming and commerce himself.
translations.idiomatic: The king farmed and traded himself.

sentences.zh: 銀作錢，類榆莢。

translations.literal: Silver made coin resembling elm pods.
translations.idiomatic: Silver coin resembled elm pods.

sentences.zh: 民乘象及馬，無鞍靮，繩穿頰禦之。

translations.literal: People rode elephants and horses without saddle or bridle; rope through the cheek controlled them.
translations.idiomatic: People rode elephants and horses without saddle; rope through the cheek controlled them.

sentences.zh: 親喪，斷發為孝，焚屍斂灰於罌，沈之水。

translations.literal: When kin died, hair was cut in mourning; corpses were cremated and ashes stored in urns sunk in water.
translations.idiomatic: When kin died hair was cut in mourning; corpses were cremated and ashes sunk in urns.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，遣使以黃金函內表，並獻方物。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan envoys came with a memorial in a golden casket and presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan envoys came with a memorial in a golden casket and local products.

sentences.zh: 瞻博瞻博，或曰瞻婆。

translations.literal: Zhanbo: Zhanbo, or Zhanpo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanbo, or Zhanpo.

sentences.zh: 北距兢伽河。

translations.literal: North bordering the Jinga River.
translations.idiomatic: North bordered the Jinga River.

sentences.zh: 多野象群行。

translations.literal: Many wild elephants moved in herds.
translations.idiomatic: Wild elephants moved in herds.

sentences.zh: 顯慶中，與婆岸、千支弗、舍跋若、磨臘四國並遣使者入朝。

translations.literal: In Xianqing, together with Po'an, Qianzhifu, Shebamo, and Mola, four states sent envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing, with Po'an, Qianzhifu, Shebamo, and Mola, four states sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 千支千支在西南海中，本南天竺屬國，亦曰半支跋，若唐言五山也，北距多摩萇。

translations.literal: Qianzhi: Qianzhi in the southwest sea was originally a vassal of South India, also called Ban Zhibo—in Tang usage Five Mountains—north bordering Duomochang.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi in the southwest sea was originally a South Indian vassal, also Ban Zhibo—Five Mountains—north bordering Duomochang.

sentences.zh: 哥羅舍分、脩羅分、甘畢又有哥羅舍分、脩羅分、甘畢三國貢方物。

translations.literal: Gelashefen, Xiuluofen, and Ganbi: also Gelashefen, Xiuluofen, and Ganbi presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: Gelashefen, Xiuluofen, and Ganbi also presented local products.

sentences.zh: 甘畢在南海上，東距環王，王名旃陀越摩，有勝兵五千。

translations.literal: Ganbi on the southern sea, east bordering Huanwang; King Chandayuemo had five thousand effective troops.
translations.idiomatic: Ganbi on the southern sea east of Huanwang; King Chandayuemo had five thousand effective troops.

sentences.zh: 哥羅舍分者，在南海南，東墮和羅。

translations.literal: Gelashefen lay on the southern sea, east of Duohailuo.
translations.idiomatic: Gelashefen lay on the southern sea east of Duohailuo.

sentences.zh: 脩羅分者，在海北，東距真臘。

translations.literal: Xiuluofen lay north of the sea, east bordering Chenla.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuluofen lay north of the sea, east of Chenla.

sentences.zh: 其風俗大略相類，有君長，皆柵郛。

translations.literal: Their customs were broadly similar; all had lords; all palisaded suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Customs were broadly similar; all had lords and palisaded suburbs.

sentences.zh: 二國勝兵二萬，甘畢才五千。

translations.literal: The two states had twenty thousand effective troops; Ganbi only five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The two states had twenty thousand effective troops; Ganbi only five thousand.

sentences.zh: 多摩萇又有多摩萇，東距婆鳳，西多隆，南千支弗，北訶陵。

translations.literal: Duomochang: also Duomochang, east bordering Pofeng, west Duolong, south Qianzhifu, north Heling.
translations.idiomatic: Duomochang bordered Pofeng east, Duolong west, Qianzhifu south, Heling north.

sentences.zh: 地東西一月行，南北二十五日行。

translations.literal: The land was one month's journey east to west, twenty-five days north to south.
translations.idiomatic: One month's journey east to west, twenty-five days north to south.

sentences.zh: 其王名骨利，詭雲得大卵，剖之，獲女子，美色，以為妻。

translations.literal: Its king was named Guli; he falsely claimed to have obtained a great egg, split it, and found a woman of beautiful countenance whom he took as wife.
translations.idiomatic: King Guli claimed to have found a great egg, split it, and taken the beautiful woman inside as wife.

sentences.zh: 俗無姓，婚姻不別同姓。

translations.literal: Custom had no surnames; marriage did not distinguish same surname.
translations.idiomatic: There were no surnames; marriage did not distinguish same surname.

sentences.zh: 王坐常東向。

translations.literal: When the king sat he always faced east.
translations.idiomatic: The king always sat facing east.

sentences.zh: 勝兵二萬，有弓刀甲槊，無馬。

translations.literal: Effective troops twenty thousand; they had bow, knife, armor, and spear; no horses.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty thousand effective troops with bow, knife, armor, and spear; no horses.

sentences.zh: 果有波那婆、宅護遮庵摩、石榴。

translations.literal: Fruits included bonaba, zhaohuzhe'anmo, and pomegranate.
translations.idiomatic: Fruits included bonaba, zhaohuzhe'anmo, and pomegranate.

sentences.zh: 其國經薩廬、都訶廬、君那廬、林邑諸國，乃得交州。

translations.literal: The state passed through Salu, Duholu, Junnalu, Lin-yi, and other states to reach Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The route passed Salu, Duholu, Junnalu, Lin-yi, and other states to Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 顯慶中貢方物。

translations.literal: In Xianqing they presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing they presented local products.

sentences.zh: 室利佛逝室利佛逝，一曰屍利佛誓。

translations.literal: Shilifoshi: Shilifoshi, also Shilifoshi.
translations.idiomatic: Shilifoshi, also Shilifoshi.

sentences.zh: 過軍徒弄山二千里，地東西千里，南北四千里而遠。

translations.literal: Beyond Juntunong Mountain two thousand li; the land a thousand li east to west, four thousand li north to south in length.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond Juntunong Mountain two thousand li; a thousand li east to west, four thousand li north to south.

sentences.zh: 有城十四，以二國分總。

translations.literal: Fourteen cities; two states divided overall governance.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen cities; two states divided governance.

sentences.zh: 西曰郎婆露斯。

translations.literal: The west was called Langbolusi.
translations.idiomatic: The west was called Langbolusi.

sentences.zh: 多金、汞砂、龍腦。

translations.literal: Much gold, cinnabar, and borneol.
translations.idiomatic: Much gold, cinnabar, and borneol.

sentences.zh: 夏至立八尺表，影在表南二尺五寸。

translations.literal: At the summer solstice an eight-chi gnomon was set; the shadow lay two chi five cun south of the gnomon.
translations.idiomatic: At the summer solstice an eight-chi gnomon cast a shadow two chi five cun south.

sentences.zh: 國多男子。

translations.literal: The state had many men.
translations.idiomatic: The state had many men.

sentences.zh: 有橐它，豹文而犀角，以乘且耕，名曰它牛豹。

translations.literal: There was tuotuo with leopard markings and rhinoceros horn, used for riding and plowing—called tuoniubao.
translations.idiomatic: There was tuotuo with leopard markings and rhinoceros horn, used for riding and plowing—called tuoniubao.

sentences.zh: 又有獸類野豕，角如山羊，名曰雩，肉味美，以饋膳。

translations.literal: Also a beast like a wild boar with horns like a goat, called yu—flesh delicious, presented for meals.
translations.idiomatic: Also a beast like a wild boar with goat-like horns called yu—delicious flesh for meals.

sentences.zh: 其王號「曷蜜多」。

translations.literal: Its king was styled "Hemiduo."
translations.idiomatic: Its king was styled "Hemiduo."

sentences.zh: 咸亨至開元間，數遣使者朝，表為邊吏侵掠，有詔廣州慰撫。

translations.literal: From Xianheng to Kaiyuan envoys repeatedly came to court, memorializing that frontier officials had raided them; an edict ordered Guangzhou to comfort and pacify.
translations.idiomatic: From Xianheng to Kaiyuan envoys repeatedly came, memorializing frontier raids; an edict ordered Guangzhou to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 又獻侏儒、僧祗女各二及歌舞。

translations.literal: They also presented two dwarfs and two sangzhi women along with song and dance.
translations.idiomatic: They also presented two dwarfs, two sangzhi women, and song and dance.

sentences.zh: 官使者為折沖，以其王為左威衛大將軍，賜紫袍、金細帶。

translations.literal: The envoy was appointed Zhechong; their king was made Left Weiwu Guard General and granted purple robe and gold fine belt.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy was appointed Zhechong; their king made Left Weiwu Guard General with purple robe and gold fine belt.

sentences.zh: 後遣子入獻，詔宴於曲江，宰相會，冊封賓義王，授右金吾衛大將軍，還之。

translations.literal: Later he sent his son to present tribute; an edict feasted them at Qujiang with chancellors attending; he was enfeoffed Prince Binyi, appointed Right Golden Guard General, and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Later he sent his son to court; an edict feasted them at Qujiang; he was enfeoffed Prince Binyi, appointed Right Golden Guard General, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 名蔑名蔑，東接真陀桓，西但遊，南屬海，北波剌。

translations.literal: Mingmie: Mingmie east adjoined Zhentuohuan, west Danyou, south belonging to the sea, north Bola.
translations.idiomatic: Mingmie east of Zhentuohuan, west of Danyou, south to the sea, north to Bola.

sentences.zh: 其地一月行，有州三十。

translations.literal: The land one month's journey; thirty prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: One month's journey across; thirty prefectures.

sentences.zh: 以十二月為歲首。

translations.literal: The twelfth month was taken as New Year.
translations.idiomatic: The twelfth month was New Year.

sentences.zh: 王衣朝霞、氎。

translations.literal: The king wore dawn-colored cloth and woolens.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore dawn cloth and woolens.

sentences.zh: 賦二十取一。

translations.literal: Tax: one part in twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Tax: one part in twenty.

sentences.zh: 交易皆用金準直。

translations.literal: Trade all used gold at standard value.
translations.idiomatic: Trade used gold at standard value.

sentences.zh: 其人短小，兄弟共娶一妻，婦總發為角，辨夫之多少。

translations.literal: The people were short; brothers shared one wife; the wife gathered hair in a horn shape to distinguish how many husbands.
translations.idiomatic: The people were short; brothers shared one wife; the wife's horn-shaped topknot showed how many husbands she had.

sentences.zh: 王號「斯多題」。

translations.literal: The king was styled "Siduoti."
translations.idiomatic: The king was styled "Siduoti."

sentences.zh: 龍朔初，使者來貢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longshuo envoys came with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: At Longshuo's beginning envoys came with tribute.

sentences.zh: 單單單單，在振州東南，多羅磨之西，亦有州縣。

translations.literal: Dandan: Dandan southeast of Zhenzhou, west of Duoluomo; also had prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Dandan southeast of Zhenzhou, west of Duoluomo; also had prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 木多白檀。

translations.literal: Many white sandalwood trees.
translations.idiomatic: White sandalwood abounded.

sentences.zh: 王姓剎利，名屍陵伽，日視事。

translations.literal: The king's surname was Kshatriya; his name Shilingjia; he held audience daily.
translations.idiomatic: The king's surname was Kshatriya; his name Shilingjia; he held audience daily.

sentences.zh: 有八大臣，號八坐。

translations.literal: Eight great ministers styled the Eight Seats.
translations.idiomatic: Eight great ministers styled the Eight Seats.

sentences.zh: 王以香塗身，冠雜寶瓔，近行乘車，遠乘象。

translations.literal: The king smeared fragrance on his body, wore a crown of mixed jewels; for short distances he rode in carriage, for long distances on elephant.
translations.idiomatic: The king smeared fragrance on his body and wore a crown of mixed jewels; short distances by carriage, long by elephant.

sentences.zh: 戰必吹蠡、擊鼓。

translations.literal: In battle conch was blown and drums beaten.
translations.idiomatic: In battle conch was blown and drums beaten.

sentences.zh: 盜無輕重皆死。

translations.literal: Theft regardless of severity meant death.
translations.idiomatic: Theft regardless of severity meant death.

sentences.zh: 乾封、總章時，獻方物。

translations.literal: In Qianfeng and Zongzhang they presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianfeng and Zongzhang they presented local products.

sentences.zh: 羅越羅越者，北距海五千里，西南哥谷羅。

translations.literal: Luoyue: Luoyue five thousand li north of the sea, southwest Gegulu.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyue five thousand li north of the sea, southwest Gegulu.

sentences.zh: 商賈往來所湊集，俗與墮羅缽底同。

translations.literal: Merchants gathered in coming and going; customs resembled Duoluobodi.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants gathered there; customs resembled Duoluobodi.

sentences.zh: 歲乘舶至廣州，州必以聞。

translations.literal: Each year ships reached Guangzhou; the prefecture always reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Each year ships reached Guangzhou; the prefecture always reported it.

sentences.zh: 驃驃，古朱波也，自號突羅朱，阇婆國人曰徒裏拙。

translations.literal: Pyu: Pyu was ancient Zhuobo; it styled itself Tuluozhu; Shepo people called it Tulizhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Pyu was ancient Zhuobo; it styled itself Tuluozhu; Shepo people called it Tulizhuo.

sentences.zh: 在永昌南二千里，去京師萬四千里。

translations.literal: Two thousand li south of Yongchang; fourteen thousand li from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand li south of Yongchang; fourteen thousand li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 東陸真臘，西接東天竺，西南墮和羅，南屬海，北南詔。

translations.literal: East Land Chenla, west East India, southwest Duohailuo, south belonging to the sea, north Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: East Land Chenla, west East India, southwest Duohailuo, south to the sea, north Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 地長三千里，廣五千里，東北袤長，屬羊苴芋城。

translations.literal: The land three thousand li long, five thousand li wide; northeast elongated, belonging to Yangjumie City.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand li long, five thousand li wide; northeast elongated, belonging to Yangjumie City.

sentences.zh: 屬國凡屬國十八：曰迦羅婆提，曰摩禮烏特，曰迦梨迦，曰半地，曰彌臣，曰坤朗，曰偈奴，曰羅聿，曰佛代，曰渠論，曰婆梨，曰偈陀，曰多歸，曰摩曳，餘即舍衛、瞻婆、阇婆也。

translations.literal: Vassal states numbered eighteen: Kalaboti, Moliwute, Kalijia, Bandi, Michén, Kunlang, Jinu, Luoyu, Fodai, Qulun, Poli, Jituo, Duogui, Moyi—the rest being Shewei, Zhanbo, and Shepo.
translations.idiomatic: Vassal states numbered eighteen: Kalaboti, Moliwute, Kalijia, Bandi, Michén, Kunlang, Jinu, Luoyu, Fodai, Qulun, Poli, Jituo, Duogui, Moyi—the rest being Shewei, Zhanbo, and Shepo.

sentences.zh: 鎮城凡鎮城九：曰道林王，曰悉利移，曰三陀，曰彌諾道立，曰突旻，曰帝偈，曰達梨謀，曰乾唐，曰末浦。

translations.literal: Fortress cities numbered nine: Daolinwang, Xiliyi, Santuo, Minuodaoli, Tumin, Dijie, Dalimou, Qiantang, and Mopu.
translations.idiomatic: Fortress cities numbered nine: Daolinwang, Xiliyi, Santuo, Minuodaoli, Tumin, Dijie, Dalimou, Qiantang, and Mopu.

sentences.zh: 部落凡部落二百九十八，以名見者三十二：曰萬公，曰充惹，曰羅君潛，曰彌綽，曰道雙，曰道甕，曰道勿，曰夜半，曰不惡奪，曰莫音，曰伽龍睒，曰阿梨吉，曰阿梨阇，曰阿梨忙，曰達磨，曰求潘，曰僧塔，曰提梨郎，曰望騰，曰擔泊，曰祿烏，曰乏毛，曰僧迦，曰提追，曰阿末邏，曰逝越，曰騰陵，曰歐咩，曰磚羅婆提，曰祿羽，曰陋蠻，曰磨地勃。

translations.literal: Tribes numbered two hundred ninety-eight; thirty-two known by name: Wangong, Chongre, Luojunqian, Michuo, Daoshuang, Daoweng, Daowu, Yebàn, Bueduo, Moyin, Jialongshan, Aliji, Alishe, Alimang, Damo, Qiupan, Sengta, Tililang, Wangteng, Danbo, Luyu, Famo, Sengjia, Tizhui, Amoluo, Shiyue, Tengling, Oumie, Zhuanluoboti, Luyu, Louman, and Modibó.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes numbered two hundred ninety-eight; thirty-two known by name including Wangong, Chongre, Luojunqian, Michuo, and Modibó.

sentences.zh: 王族繇彌臣至坤朗，又有小昆侖部，王名茫悉越，俗與彌臣同。

translations.literal: The royal clan ran from Michén to Kunlang; there was also a Lesser Kunlun tribe; the king was named Mangxiyue; customs resembled Michén.
translations.idiomatic: The royal clan ran from Michén to Kunlang; a Lesser Kunlun tribe had king Mangxiyue; customs resembled Michén.

sentences.zh: 繇坤朗至祿羽，有大昆侖王國，王名思利泊婆難多珊那。

translations.literal: From Kunlang to Luyu was the Great Kunlun kingdom; the king was named Siliboponanduoshanna.
translations.idiomatic: From Kunlang to Luyu was Great Kunlun; the king was Siliboponanduoshanna.

sentences.zh: 川原大於彌臣。

translations.literal: Rivers and plains were larger than Michén.
translations.idiomatic: Rivers and plains exceeded Michén.

sentences.zh: 繇昆侖小王所居，半日行至磨地勃柵，海行五月至佛代國。

translations.literal: From where the Lesser Kunlun king dwelt, half a day's journey reached Modibó stockade; five months by sea to Fodai Country.
translations.idiomatic: Half a day's journey from the Lesser Kunlun king's seat reached Modibó stockade; five months by sea to Fodai.

sentences.zh: 有江，支流三百六十。

translations.literal: There was a river with three hundred sixty tributaries.
translations.idiomatic: A river had three hundred sixty tributaries.

sentences.zh: 其王名思利些彌他。

translations.literal: Its king was named Silixiimita.
translations.idiomatic: Its king was Silixiimita.

sentences.zh: 有川名思利毗離芮。

translations.literal: There was a river named Silipilirui.
translations.idiomatic: A river named Silipilirui flowed there.

sentences.zh: 土多異香。

translations.literal: The soil produced many exotic fragrances.
translations.idiomatic: The soil produced many exotic fragrances.

sentences.zh: 北有市，諸國估舶所湊，越海即阇婆也。

translations.literal: North was a market where merchant ships of all states gathered; crossing the sea one reached Shepo.
translations.idiomatic: North lay a market where merchant ships gathered; crossing the sea one reached Shepo.

sentences.zh: 十五日行，逾二大山，一曰正迷，一曰射鞮，有國，其王名思利摩訶羅阇，俗與佛代同。

translations.literal: Fifteen days' journey, crossing two great mountains—one called Zhenmi, one called Shedi—was a state whose king was named Silimohaluoshe; customs resembled Fodai.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen days' journey over two great mountains—Zhenmi and Shedi—lay a state whose king Silimohaluoshe shared Fodai's customs.

sentences.zh: 經多茸補邏川至阇婆，八日行至婆賄伽廬，國土熱，衢路植椰子、檳榔，仰不見日。

translations.literal: Passing Duorongbuoluochuan to Shepo, eight days to Pohuojialu; the land was hot; coconut and betel lined the roads; the sun could not be seen overhead.
translations.idiomatic: Via Duorongbuoluochuan to Shepo, eight days to Pohuojialu; the land was hot; coconut and betel lined the roads; one could not see the sun overhead.

sentences.zh: 王居以金為甓，廚覆銀瓦，爨香木，堂飾明珠。

translations.literal: Where the king dwelt, tiles were gold; kitchen roofs silver tiles; sandalwood burned for cooking; halls adorned with bright pearls.
translations.idiomatic: The king's dwelling had gold tiles, silver kitchen roofs, sandalwood fires, and halls adorned with bright pearls.

sentences.zh: 有二池，以金為堤，舟楫皆飾金寶。

translations.literal: Two pools with gold embankments; boats all decorated with gold and jewels.
translations.idiomatic: Two pools with gold embankments; boats decorated with gold and jewels.

sentences.zh: 驃王姓困沒長，名摩羅惹。

translations.literal: The Pyu king's surname was Kunmeizhang; his name Moluore.
translations.idiomatic: The Pyu king's surname was Kunmeizhang; his name Moluore.

sentences.zh: 其相名曰摩訶思那。

translations.literal: His chancellor was named Mohesina.
translations.idiomatic: His chancellor was Mohesina.

sentences.zh: 王出，輿以金繩床，遠則乘象。

translations.literal: When the king went out, a golden rope bed served as litter; for distance he rode elephants.
translations.idiomatic: Going abroad the king used a golden rope litter; for distance he rode elephants.

sentences.zh: 嬪史數百人。

translations.literal: Consorts and clerks numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts and clerks numbered several hundred.

sentences.zh: 青甓為圓城，周百六十里，有十二門，四隅作浮圖，民皆居中，鉛錫為瓦，荔支為材。

translations.literal: Blue tiles formed a round city a hundred sixty li in circumference with twelve gates; pagodas at the four corners; people all lived within; lead and tin served as tiles; lychee as timber.
translations.idiomatic: Blue tiles formed a round city a hundred sixty li around with twelve gates; pagodas at the corners; people lived within; lead and tin tiles; lychee timber.

sentences.zh: 俗惡殺。

translations.literal: Custom abhorred killing.
translations.idiomatic: Custom abhorred killing.

sentences.zh: 拜以手抱臂稽顙為恭。

translations.literal: In bowing one joined hands, embraced arms, and bowed the forehead in respect.
translations.idiomatic: Bowings joined hands, embraced arms, and bowed the forehead.

sentences.zh: 明天文，喜佛法。

translations.literal: They understood astronomy and favored Buddhist law.
translations.idiomatic: They understood astronomy and favored Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 有百寺，琉璃為甓，錯以金銀，丹彩紫礦塗地，覆以錦罽，王居亦如之。

translations.literal: A hundred temples with glazed tiles inlaid with gold and silver; cinnabar and purple ore painted the ground; brocade rugs covered roofs; the king's dwelling likewise.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred temples with glazed tiles inlaid with gold and silver; cinnabar and purple ore on the ground; brocade roofs; the king's dwelling likewise.

sentences.zh: 民七歲祝髮止寺，至二十有不達其法，復為民。

translations.literal: At seven sui boys tonsured and entered temples; by twenty if they had not mastered the law they returned to lay life.
translations.idiomatic: At seven boys tonsured and entered temples; by twenty if they had not mastered the law they returned to lay life.

sentences.zh: 衣用白氎、朝霞，以蠶帛傷生不敢衣。

translations.literal: Clothing used white woolens and dawn cloth; silkworm cloth harmed life and they dared not wear it.
translations.idiomatic: Clothing used white woolens and dawn cloth; silkworm cloth harmed life and they dared not wear it.

sentences.zh: 戴金花冠、翠冒，絡以雜珠。

translations.literal: They wore golden flower crowns and emerald caps strung with mixed pearls.
translations.idiomatic: They wore golden flower crowns and emerald caps strung with mixed pearls.

sentences.zh: 王宮設金銀二鐘，寇至，焚香出之，以占吉兇。

translations.literal: The royal palace had gold and silver bells; when enemies came incense was burned and the bells brought out to read fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The palace had gold and silver bells; when enemies came incense was burned and bells brought out to read fortune.

sentences.zh: 有巨白象，高百尺，訟者焚香跽象前，自思是非而退。

translations.literal: There was a great white elephant a hundred chi high; litigants burned incense and knelt before it, reflected on right and wrong, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: A great white elephant stood a hundred chi high; litigants burned incense, knelt before it, reflected on right and wrong, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 有災疫，王亦焚香對象跽，自咎。

translations.literal: When plague came the king also burned incense and knelt before the elephant, blaming himself.
translations.idiomatic: When plague came the king burned incense and knelt before the elephant, blaming himself.

sentences.zh: 無桎梏，有罪者束五竹捶背，重者五、輕三，殺人則死。

translations.literal: No shackles; the guilty were bound with five bamboo rods and beaten on the back—five strokes for serious, three for light; murder meant death.
translations.idiomatic: No shackles; the guilty were beaten with five bamboo rods—five strokes for serious, three for light; murder meant death.

sentences.zh: 土宜菽、粟、稻、梁，蔗大若脛，無麻、麥。

translations.literal: Soil suited beans, millet, rice, and sorghum; sugarcane thick as a shin; no hemp or wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Soil suited beans, millet, rice, and sorghum; sugarcane thick as a shin; no hemp or wheat.

sentences.zh: 以金銀為錢，形如半月，號登伽佗，亦曰足彈陀。

translations.literal: Gold and silver made coin crescent-shaped, called Dengqiata, also Zutantuo.
translations.idiomatic: Gold and silver coin was crescent-shaped, called Dengqiata or Zutantuo.

sentences.zh: 無膏油，以蠟雜香代炷。

translations.literal: No oil or grease; wax mixed with incense substituted for lamp fuel.
translations.idiomatic: No oil; wax mixed with incense substituted for lamp fuel.

sentences.zh: 與諸蠻市，以江豬、白氎、琉璃罌缶相易。

translations.literal: Trading with various barbarians used river pigs, white woolens, and glazed jars.
translations.idiomatic: Trade with barbarians used river pigs, white woolens, and glazed jars.

sentences.zh: 婦人當頂作高髻，飾銀珠琲，衣青娑裙，披羅段；

translations.literal: Women wore high topknots adorned with silver beads and pearls, blue sura skirts, draped silk panels;
translations.idiomatic: Women wore high topknots with silver beads, blue sura skirts, draped silk panels;

sentences.zh: 行持扇，貴家者傍至五六。

translations.literal: walking they held fans; the noble might have five or six attendants.
translations.idiomatic: walking they held fans; nobles might have five or six attendants.

sentences.zh: 近城有沙山不毛，地亦與波斯、婆羅門接，距西舍利城二十日行。

translations.literal: Near the city were barren sand hills; the land also adjoined Persia and Brahmin lands; twenty days' journey west to Xisheli City.
translations.idiomatic: Barren sand hills lay near the city; the land adjoined Persia and Brahmin lands; twenty days west to Xisheli City.

sentences.zh: 西舍利者，中天竺也。

translations.literal: Xisheli was Central India.
translations.idiomatic: Xisheli was Central India.

sentences.zh: 南詔以兵強地接，常羈制之。

translations.literal: Nanzhao, strong in troops with adjoining territory, constantly restrained them.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao, strong and adjoining, constantly restrained them.

sentences.zh: 歸唐貞元中，王雍羌聞南詔歸唐，有內附心，異牟尋遣使楊加明詣劍南西川節度使韋臯請獻夷中歌曲，且令驃國進樂人。

translations.literal: Returning to Tang: in the Zhenyuan era King Yongqiang heard Nanzhao had returned to Tang and had a mind to submit; Yimouxun sent envoy Yang Jiaming to Jiannan West Circuit Military Governor Wei Gao requesting to present Yi songs and ordering Pyu to send musicians.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan King Yongqiang heard Nanzhao had returned to Tang and wished to submit; Yimouxun sent Yang Jiaming to Wei Gao requesting to present Yi songs and ordering Pyu to send musicians.

sentences.zh: 於是臯作《南詔奉聖樂》，用正律黃鐘之均。

translations.literal: Thereupon Gao composed "Nanzhao Presents Sage Music," using the standard pitch of the yellow bell.
translations.idiomatic: Gao composed "Nanzhao Presents Sage Music" in the standard pitch of yellow bell.

sentences.zh: 宮、徵一變，象西南順也；

translations.literal: Gong and zhi altered once, symbolizing the southwest submission;
translations.idiomatic: Gong and zhi altered once, symbolizing southwest submission;

sentences.zh: 角、羽終變，象戎夷革心也。

translations.literal: jue and yu finally altered, symbolizing the barbarians' change of heart.
translations.idiomatic: jue and yu finally altered, symbolizing the barbarians' change of heart.

sentences.zh: 舞六成，工六十四人，贊引二人，序曲二十八疊，舞「南詔奉聖樂」字。

translations.literal: Six dance sections; sixty-four performers; two lead chanters; twenty-eight prelude layers; dancing the characters of "Nanzhao Presents Sage Music."
translations.idiomatic: Six dance sections; sixty-four performers; two lead chanters; twenty-eight prelude layers; dancing the characters of "Nanzhao Presents Sage Music."

sentences.zh: 舞人十六，執羽翟，以四為列。

translations.literal: Sixteen dancers held feather plumes in columns of four.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen dancers held feather plumes in columns of four.

sentences.zh: 舞「南」字，歌《聖主無為化》；

translations.literal: Dancing "Nan," singing "The Sage Lord Rules Without Action";
translations.idiomatic: Dancing Nan, singing "The Sage Lord Rules Without Action";

sentences.zh: 舞「詔」字，歌《南詔朝天樂》；

translations.literal: dancing "Zhao," singing "Nanzhao Faces Heaven in Joy";
translations.idiomatic: dancing Zhao, singing "Nanzhao Faces Heaven in Joy";

sentences.zh: 舞「奉」字，歌《海宇修文化》；

translations.literal: dancing "Feng," singing "Within the Seas Culture Is Cultivated";
translations.idiomatic: dancing Feng, singing "Within the Seas Culture Is Cultivated";

sentences.zh: 舞「聖」字，歌《雨露覃無外》；

translations.literal: dancing "Sheng," singing "Rain and Dew Extend Without Limit";
translations.idiomatic: dancing Sheng, singing "Rain and Dew Extend Without Limit";

sentences.zh: 舞「樂」字，歌《辟土丁零塞》。

translations.literal: dancing "Yue," singing "Opening Land at Dingling Pass."
translations.idiomatic: dancing Yue, singing "Opening Land at Dingling Pass."

sentences.zh: 皆一章三疊而成。

translations.literal: Each song one chapter in three layers.
translations.idiomatic: Each song one chapter in three layers.

sentences.zh: 舞舞者初定，執羽，簫、鼓等奏散序一疊，次奏第二疊，四行，贊引以序入。

translations.literal: When dancers first took position holding plumes, xiao and drums played one prelude layer; then the second layer—four rows—as lead chanters entered in order.
translations.idiomatic: Dancers first took position; xiao and drums played one prelude layer; then the second as lead chanters entered.

sentences.zh: 將終，雷鼓作於四隅，舞者皆拜，金聲作而起，執羽稽首，以象朝覲。

translations.literal: Near the end thunder drums sounded at the four corners; dancers all bowed; golden sounds rose and they stood, holding plumes and bowing forehead—symbolizing audience at court.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end thunder drums at four corners; dancers bowed; golden sounds rose and they stood with plumes, bowing forehead—symbolizing court audience.

sentences.zh: 每拜跪，節以鉦鼓。

translations.literal: Each bow and kneel timed with cymbals and drums.
translations.idiomatic: Each bow and kneel timed with cymbals and drums.

sentences.zh: 次奏拍序一疊，舞者分左右蹈舞，每四拍，揖羽稽首，拍終，舞者拜，復奏一疊，蹈舞抃揖，以合「南」字。

translations.literal: Next, one section of the beat prelude was played. The dancers divided left and right and stepped in dance; every four beats they bowed with plumes and kowtowed. When the beat ended, the dancers bowed, and another section was played, with stepping, dancing, clapping, and bowing to match the character "nan."
translations.idiomatic: Next, one section of the beat prelude was played. The dancers divided left and right and stepped in dance; every four beats they bowed with plumes and kowtowed. When the beat ended, the dancers bowed, and another section was played, with stepping, dancing, clapping, and bowing to match the character "nan."

sentences.zh: 字成遍終，舞者北面跪歌，導以絲竹。

translations.literal: When each character was complete, dancers knelt north singing, led by silk and bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: When each character was complete, dancers knelt north singing, led by silk and bamboo.

sentences.zh: 歌已，俯伏，鉦作，復揖舞。

translations.literal: When song ended they prostrated; cymbals sounded; they bowed and danced again.
translations.idiomatic: When song ended they prostrated; cymbals sounded; they bowed and danced again.

sentences.zh: 餘字皆如之，唯「聖」字詞末皆恭揖，以明奉聖。

translations.literal: The remaining characters all followed this pattern; only at the end of each phrase for the character "sheng" did they bow reverently, to show that they were honoring the sage.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining characters all followed this pattern; only at the end of each phrase for the character "sheng" did they bow reverently, to show that they were honoring the sage.

sentences.zh: 每一字，曲三疊，名為五成。

translations.literal: Each character: three layers of melody, called five completions.
translations.idiomatic: Each character: three melody layers, called five completions.

sentences.zh: 次急奏一疊，四十八人分行罄折，象將臣禦邊也。

translations.literal: Next rapid layer played; forty-eight in rows bowed broken—symbolizing ministers defending the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Next rapid layer; forty-eight in rows bowed broken—symbolizing ministers defending the frontier.

sentences.zh: 字舞畢，舞者十六人為四列，又舞《辟四門》之舞。

translations.literal: When character-dance ended, sixteen dancers in four columns again danced "Opening Four Gates."
translations.idiomatic: When character-dance ended, sixteen in four columns danced "Opening Four Gates."

sentences.zh: 遽舞入遍兩疊，與鼓吹合節，進舞三，退舞三，以象三才、三統。

translations.literal: Quick dance entered through two layers, matching drums and wind; advance three dances, retreat three—symbolizing three talents and three unities.
translations.idiomatic: Quick dance through two layers matching drums; advance three, retreat three—symbolizing three talents and three unities.

sentences.zh: 舞終，皆稽首逡巡。

translations.literal: When dance ended all bowed forehead and withdrew hesitatingly.
translations.idiomatic: When dance ended all bowed and withdrew hesitatingly.

sentences.zh: 又一人舞《億萬壽》之舞，歌《天南滇越俗》四章，歌舞七疊六成而終。

translations.literal: One person danced "Ten Thousand Longevities," singing four chapters of "Southern Yunnan Frontier Custom"; song and dance seven layers, six completions and end.
translations.idiomatic: One danced "Ten Thousand Longevities," singing four chapters of "Southern Yunnan Frontier Custom"; seven layers, six completions and end.

sentences.zh: 七者，火之成數，象天子南面生成之恩。

translations.literal: Seven—the completion number of fire—symbolizes the Son of Heaven facing south generating grace.
translations.idiomatic: Seven—the fire completion number—symbolizes the Son of Heaven facing south generating grace.

sentences.zh: 六者，坤數，象西南向化。

translations.literal: Six—the kun number—symbolizes southwest turning to civilization.
translations.idiomatic: Six—the kun number—symbolizes southwest turning to civilization.

sentences.zh: 樂凡樂三十，工百九十六人，分四部：一、龜茲部，二、大鼓部，三、胡部，四、軍樂部。

translations.literal: Music totaled thirty pieces; one hundred ninety-six workers in four sections: Kucha, Great Drum, Hu, and Military Music.
translations.idiomatic: Music totaled thirty pieces; one hundred ninety-six workers in four sections: Kucha, Great Drum, Hu, and Military Music.

sentences.zh: 龜茲部，有羯鼓、揩鼓、腰鼓、雞婁鼓、短笛、大小觱篥、拍板，皆八；

translations.literal: Kucha section: jie drum, kai drum, waist drum, jilou drum, short flute, large and small bili, clappers—all eight;
translations.idiomatic: Kucha section: jie drum, kai drum, waist drum, jilou drum, short flute, large and small bili, clappers—all eight;

sentences.zh: 長短簫、橫笛、方響、大銅鈸、貝，皆四。

translations.literal: long and short xiao, transverse flute, square sound, large bronze cymbals, shells—all four.
translations.idiomatic: long and short xiao, transverse flute, square sound, large bronze cymbals, shells—all four.

sentences.zh: 凡工八十八人，分四列，屬舞筵四隅，以合節鼓。

translations.literal: Eighty-eight workers in four columns at the four corners of the dance arena matching rhythm drums.
translations.idiomatic: Eighty-eight workers in four columns at dance arena corners matching rhythm drums.

sentences.zh: 大鼓部，以四為列，凡二十四，居龜茲部前。

translations.literal: Great Drum section: columns of four, twenty-four total, before the Kucha section.
translations.idiomatic: Great Drum section: columns of four, twenty-four total, before Kucha.

sentences.zh: 胡部，有箏、大小箜篌、五弦琵琶、笙、橫笛、短笛、拍板，皆八；

translations.literal: Hu section: zheng, large and small konghou, five-string pipa, sheng, transverse flute, short flute, clappers—all eight;
translations.idiomatic: Hu section: zheng, large and small konghou, five-string pipa, sheng, transverse flute, short flute, clappers—all eight;

sentences.zh: 大小觱篥，皆四。

translations.literal: large and small bili—all four.
translations.idiomatic: large and small bili—all four.

sentences.zh: 工七十二人，分四列，屬舞筵之隅，以導歌詠。

translations.literal: Seventy-two workers in four columns at arena corners leading song.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-two workers at arena corners leading song.

sentences.zh: 軍樂部，金饒、金鐸，皆二；

translations.literal: Military Music section: golden nao, golden duo—all two;
translations.idiomatic: Military Music: golden nao, golden duo—all two;

sentences.zh: 鼓、金鉦，皆四。

translations.literal: drums, golden cymbals—all four.
translations.idiomatic: drums, golden cymbals—all four.

sentences.zh: 鉦、鼓，金飾蓋，垂流蘇。

translations.literal: Cymbals and drums had golden covers with hanging tassels.
translations.idiomatic: Cymbals and drums had golden covers with tassels.

sentences.zh: 工十二人，服南詔服，立《壁四門》舞筵四隅，節拜合樂。

translations.literal: Twelve workers in Nanzhao dress stood at the four corners of "Opening Four Gates" dance arena, timing bows to combined music.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve in Nanzhao dress stood at four corners of "Opening Four Gates," timing bows to music.

sentences.zh: 又十六人，畫半臂，執鼓，四人為列。

translations.literal: Also sixteen painted half-sleeves holding drums, four per column.
translations.idiomatic: Also sixteen in painted half-sleeves holding drums, four per column.

sentences.zh: 舞人服南詔衣、絳裙襦、黑頭囊、金佉苴、畫皮靴革，首飾襪額，冠金寶花鬘，襦上復加畫半臂。

translations.literal: Dancers wore Nanzhao robes, crimson skirts and jackets, black head pouches, golden juqie, painted leather boots, sock-forehead ornaments, golden jewel flower crowns, jackets with added painted half-sleeves.
translations.idiomatic: Dancers wore Nanzhao robes, crimson skirts, black head pouches, golden juqie, painted boots, golden jewel crowns, painted half-sleeves.

sentences.zh: 執羽翟舞，俯伏，以象朝拜；

translations.literal: Holding feather plumes they danced, prostrating—symbolizing court bow;
translations.idiomatic: Holding plumes they danced prostrate—symbolizing court bow;

sentences.zh: 裙襦畫鳥獸草木，文以八彩雜華，以象庶物鹹遂；

translations.literal: skirts and jackets painted with birds, beasts, plants, and trees in eight-colored splendor—symbolizing all things flourishing;
translations.idiomatic: skirts painted with birds, beasts, plants in eight colors—symbolizing all things flourishing;

sentences.zh: 羽葆四垂，以象天無不覆；

translations.literal: feather canopies hung on four sides—symbolizing heaven covering all;
translations.idiomatic: feather canopies on four sides—symbolizing heaven covering all;

sentences.zh: 正方布位，以象地無不載；

translations.literal: square cloth positions—symbolizing earth bearing all;
translations.idiomatic: square cloth positions—symbolizing earth bearing all;

sentences.zh: 分四列，以象四氣；

translations.literal: four columns—symbolizing four seasons;
translations.idiomatic: four columns—symbolizing four seasons;

sentences.zh: 舞為五字，以象五行；

translations.literal: five-character dance—symbolizing five phases;
translations.idiomatic: five-character dance—symbolizing five phases;

sentences.zh: 秉羽翟，以象文德；

translations.literal: holding plumes—symbolizing civil virtue;
translations.idiomatic: holding plumes—symbolizing civil virtue;

sentences.zh: 節鼓，以象號令遠布；

translations.literal: rhythm drums—symbolizing orders broadcast afar;
translations.idiomatic: rhythm drums—symbolizing orders broadcast afar;

sentences.zh: 振以鐸，明采詩之義；

translations.literal: shaken with duo—clarifying the meaning of gathering poems;
translations.idiomatic: shaken with duo—clarifying gathering poems;

sentences.zh: 用龜茲等樂，以象遠夷悅服。

translations.literal: using Kucha and other music—symbolizing distant barbarians' joyful submission.
translations.idiomatic: Kucha and other music symbolized distant barbarians' joyful submission.

sentences.zh: 鉦鼓則古者振旅獻捷之樂也。

translations.literal: Cymbals and drums were ancient music for marshaling troops and presenting victory.
translations.idiomatic: Cymbals and drums were ancient music for marshaling troops and presenting victory.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘，君聲，配運為土，明土德常盛。

translations.literal: Yellow bell—the ruler's sound—paired with earth as element, showing earth virtue ever flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow bell—the ruler's sound—paired with earth, showing earth virtue ever flourishing.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘得《乾》初九，自為其宮，則林鐘四律以正聲應之，象大君南面提天統於上，乾道明也。

translations.literal: Yellow bell obtained Qian's initial nine as its own palace; then forest bell's four pitches responded in correct sound—symbolizing the great lord facing south holding heaven's unity above; Qian's way is bright.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow bell as Qian's initial nine; forest bell's four pitches responded—symbolizing the lord facing south holding heaven's unity; Qian's way bright.

sentences.zh: 林鐘得《坤》初六，其位西南，西南感至化於下，坤體順也。

translations.literal: Forest bell obtained Kun's initial six; its position southwest—southwest feeling utmost transformation below; Kun's body is yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Forest bell as Kun's initial six in the southwest—feeling utmost transformation below; Kun yielding.

sentences.zh: 太蔟得《乾》九二，是為人統，天地正而三才通，故次應以太蔟。

translations.literal: Taicu obtained Qian's nine-two as human unity; heaven and earth correct and three talents connect—therefore Taicu responded next.
translations.idiomatic: Taicu as Qian's nine-two human unity; heaven and earth correct, three talents connect—Taicu responded next.

sentences.zh: 三才既通，南呂復以羽聲應之。

translations.literal: Three talents connected; southern pitch again responded with yu sound.
translations.idiomatic: Three talents connected; southern pitch responded with yu.

sentences.zh: 南呂，酉，西方金也；

translations.literal: Southern pitch—you, west, metal of the west;
translations.idiomatic: Southern pitch—you, west, metal of the west;

sentences.zh: 羽，北方水也。

translations.literal: yu—north, water of the north.
translations.idiomatic: yu—north, water of the north.

sentences.zh: 金、水悅而應乎時，以象西戎、北狄悅服。

translations.literal: Metal and water joyful and responding to the season—symbolizing Western Rong and Northern Di's joyful submission.
translations.idiomatic: Metal and water joyful and responding to the season—symbolizing Western Rong and Northern Di's submission.

sentences.zh: 然後姑洗以角音終之。

translations.literal: Then Guxian ended with jue pitch.
translations.idiomatic: Then Guxian ended with jue pitch.

sentences.zh: 姑，故也；

translations.literal: Gu means former;
translations.idiomatic: Gu means former;

sentences.zh: 洗，濯也。

translations.literal: xian means wash.
translations.idiomatic: xian means wash.

sentences.zh: 以象南詔背吐蕃歸化，洗過日新。

translations.literal: Symbolizing Nanzhao turning from Tibet to submit, washing away faults and renewing day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Symbolizing Nanzhao turning from Tibet to submit, washing away faults and renewing day by day.

sentences.zh: 五宮臯以五宮異用，獨唱殊音，復述《五均譜》，分金石之節奏：

translations.literal: Five palace pitches Gao used five palace pitches differently, each singing distinct tones; he also composed "Five Meanings Chart," dividing metal and stone rhythms:
translations.idiomatic: Gao used five palace pitches differently; he also composed "Five Meanings Chart," dividing metal and stone rhythms:

sentences.zh: 一曰黃鐘，宮之宮，軍士歌《奉聖樂》者用之。

translations.literal: First, yellow bell, palace of palace—used by soldiers singing "Present Sage Music."
translations.idiomatic: First, yellow bell, palace of palace—for soldiers singing "Present Sage Music."

sentences.zh: 舞人服南詔衣，秉翟俯伏拜抃，合「南詔奉聖樂」五字，倡詞五，舞人乃易南方朝天之服，絳色，七節襦袖，節有青𥛦排衿，以象鳥翼。

translations.literal: Dancers wore Nanzhao robes, holding plumes prostrating and bowing, combining the five characters of "Nanzhao Presents Sage Music," five chant texts; dancers then changed to southern court-facing dress, crimson, seven-section jacket sleeves with blue feathered lapels symbolizing bird wings.
translations.idiomatic: Dancers wore Nanzhao robes with plumes, combining five characters of "Nanzhao Presents Sage Music"; then changed to crimson southern court dress with blue feathered lapels symbolizing wings.

sentences.zh: 樂用龜茲、胡部，金鉦、鼓、鐃、貝、大鼓。

translations.literal: Music used Kucha, Hu section, golden cymbals, drums, nao, shells, great drums.
translations.idiomatic: Music used Kucha, Hu, golden cymbals, drums, nao, shells, great drums.

sentences.zh: 二曰太蔟，商之宮，女子歌《奉聖樂》者用之。

translations.literal: Second, Taicu, shang's palace—used by women singing "Present Sage Music."
translations.idiomatic: Second, Taicu, shang's palace—for women singing "Present Sage Music."

sentences.zh: 合以管弦。

translations.literal: Combined with wind and strings.
translations.idiomatic: Combined with wind and strings.

sentences.zh: 若奏庭下，則獨舞一曲。

translations.literal: If performed below the hall, one danced alone.
translations.idiomatic: Below the hall, one danced alone.

sentences.zh: 樂用龜茲、鼓、笛各四部，與胡部等合作。

translations.literal: Music used Kucha, drums, flutes four sections each, combined with Hu section.
translations.idiomatic: Music used Kucha, drums, flutes four sections each, with Hu.

sentences.zh: 琵琶、笙、箜篌，皆八；

translations.literal: Pipa, sheng, konghou—all eight;
translations.idiomatic: Pipa, sheng, konghou—all eight;

sentences.zh: 大小觱篥、箏、弦、五弦琵琶、長笛、短笛、方響，各四。

translations.literal: large and small bili, zheng, strings, five-string pipa, long flute, short flute, square sound—each four.
translations.idiomatic: large and small bili, zheng, strings, five-string pipa, long and short flute, square sound—each four.

sentences.zh: 居龜茲部前。

translations.literal: Before the Kucha section.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Kucha section.

sentences.zh: 次貝一人，大鼓十二分左右，餘皆坐奏。

translations.literal: Next one shell player; twelve great drums left and right; the rest all seated.
translations.idiomatic: Next one shell player; twelve great drums left and right; the rest seated.

sentences.zh: 三曰姑洗，角之宮，應古律林鐘為徵宮，女子歌《奉聖樂》者用之。

translations.literal: Third, Guxian, jue's palace, responding to ancient pitch forest bell as zhi palace—used by women singing "Present Sage Music."
translations.idiomatic: Third, Guxian, jue's palace, forest bell as zhi—for women singing "Present Sage Music."

sentences.zh: 舞者六十四人，飾羅彩襦袖，間以八采，曳雲花履，首飾雙鳳、八卦、彩雲、花鬘，執羽為拜抃之節。

translations.literal: Sixty-four dancers wore silk brocade jacket sleeves mixed with eight colors, cloud-flower shoes, headdresses of twin phoenixes, eight trigrams, colored clouds, flower crowns, holding plumes for bowing rhythm.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty-four dancers in silk brocade with eight colors, cloud-flower shoes, twin phoenix and eight trigram crowns, holding plumes for bowing rhythm.

sentences.zh: 以林鐘當地統，象歲功備、萬物成也。

translations.literal: Forest bell as earth unity symbolizing year's work complete and all things fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Forest bell as earth unity symbolizing year's work complete.

sentences.zh: 雙鳳，明律呂之和也。

translations.literal: Twin phoenixes showing pitch harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Twin phoenixes showing pitch harmony.

sentences.zh: 八卦，明還相為用也。

translations.literal: Eight trigrams showing mutual generation.
translations.idiomatic: Eight trigrams showing mutual generation.

sentences.zh: 彩雲，象氣也。

translations.literal: Colored clouds symbolizing qi.
translations.idiomatic: Colored clouds symbolizing qi.

sentences.zh: 花鬘，象冠也。

translations.literal: Flower crown symbolizing cap.
translations.idiomatic: Flower crown symbolizing cap.

sentences.zh: 合「奉聖樂」三字，唱詞三，表天下懷聖也。

translations.literal: Combining "Present Sage Music" three characters, three chant texts, showing all under heaven cherishing the sage.
translations.idiomatic: Combining "Present Sage Music" three characters, three chants, showing all cherishing the sage.

sentences.zh: 小女子字舞，則碧色襦袖，象角音主木；

translations.literal: Small girls' character dance wore blue jacket sleeves symbolizing jue governing wood;
translations.idiomatic: Small girls' character dance wore blue sleeves symbolizing jue governing wood;

sentences.zh: 首飾巽卦，應姑洗之氣；

translations.literal: headdress Xun trigram responding to Guxian's qi;
translations.idiomatic: headdress Xun trigram responding to Guxian's qi;

sentences.zh: 以六人略後，象六合一心也。

translations.literal: six slightly behind symbolizing six directions one heart.
translations.idiomatic: six slightly behind symbolizing six directions one heart.

sentences.zh: 樂用龜茲、胡部，其鉦、、鐃、鐸，皆覆以彩蓋，飾以花趺，上陳錦綺，垂流蘇。

translations.literal: Music used Kucha, Hu; cymbals, nao, duo all covered with colored canopies, flower bases, brocade above, hanging tassels.
translations.idiomatic: Music used Kucha, Hu; cymbals and nao covered with colored canopies, flower bases, brocade, tassels.

sentences.zh: 按《瑞圖》曰：「王者有道，則儀鳳在鼓。」

translations.literal: According to the Omen Chart: "When the king has the Way, the ceremonial phoenix rests on the drum."
translations.idiomatic: According to the Omen Chart: "When the king has the Way, the ceremonial phoenix rests on the drum."

sentences.zh: 故羽葆鼓棲以鳳凰，鉦棲孔雀，鐃、鐸集以翔鷺，鉦、頂足又飾南方鳥獸，明澤及飛走翔伏。

translations.literal: Therefore feather-canopy drums perched phoenixes; cymbals perched peacocks; nao and duo gathered flying egrets; cymbal tops and feet also decorated with southern birds and beasts, showing grace reaching flying, walking, soaring, and crouching.
translations.idiomatic: Feather-canopy drums perched phoenixes; cymbals peacocks; nao and duo egrets; tops decorated with southern birds and beasts, grace reaching all creatures.

sentences.zh: 鉦、、鐃、鐸，皆二人執擊之。

translations.literal: Cymbals, nao, duo—all two men striking.
translations.idiomatic: Cymbals, nao, duo—two men each striking.

sentences.zh: 貝及大鼓工伎之數，與軍士《奉聖樂》同，而加鼓、笛四部。

translations.literal: Shell and great drum worker numbers same as soldiers' "Present Sage Music," plus four sections of drums and flutes.
translations.idiomatic: Shell and great drum numbers matched soldiers' "Present Sage Music," plus four drum and flute sections.

sentences.zh: 四曰林鐘，徵之宮，斂拍單聲，奏《奉聖樂》，丈夫一人獨舞。

translations.literal: Fourth, forest bell, zhi's palace, restrained beat single sound, performing "Present Sage Music"—one man danced alone.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, forest bell, zhi's palace, restrained single beat, "Present Sage Music"—one man danced alone.

sentences.zh: 樂用龜茲，鼓、笛每色四人。

translations.literal: Music used Kucha; drums, flutes four of each color.
translations.idiomatic: Music used Kucha; drums, flutes four each.

sentences.zh: 方響二，置龜茲部前。

translations.literal: Square sound two, before Kucha section.
translations.idiomatic: Square sound two before Kucha.

sentences.zh: 二隅有金鉦，中植金鐸二、貝二、鈴鈸二、大鼓十二分左右。

translations.literal: Two corners golden cymbals; center planted golden duo two, shells two, bell cymbals two, great drums twelve left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Two corners golden cymbals; center golden duo two, shells two, bell cymbals two, great drums twelve.

sentences.zh: 五曰南呂，羽之宮，應古律黃鐘為君之宮。

translations.literal: Fifth, southern pitch, yu's palace, responding to ancient yellow bell as ruler's palace.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, southern pitch, yu's palace, yellow bell as ruler's palace.

sentences.zh: 樂用古黃鐘方響一，大琵琶、五弦琵琶、大箜篌倍，黃鐘觱篥、小觱篥、竽、笙、塤、篪、搊箏、軋箏、黃鐘簫，笛倍。

translations.literal: Music used ancient yellow bell square sound one, great pipa, five-string pipa, great konghou doubled, yellow bell bili, small bili, yu, sheng, xun, chi, plucked zheng, rolled zheng, yellow bell xiao, flutes doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Music used yellow bell square sound, great pipa, five-string pipa, doubled great konghou, yellow bell bili, yu, sheng, xun, chi, zheng, yellow bell xiao, doubled flutes.

sentences.zh: 笛、節鼓、拍板等工皆一人，坐奏之。

translations.literal: Flute, rhythm drum, clappers and other workers each one, seated performance.
translations.idiomatic: Flute, rhythm drum, clappers—each one worker, seated.

sentences.zh: 絲竹緩作，一人獨唱，歌工復通唱軍士《奉聖樂》詞。

translations.literal: Silk and bamboo played slowly; one sang alone; song workers also chanted soldiers' "Present Sage Music" text.
translations.idiomatic: Silk and bamboo slow; one sang alone; song workers also chanted soldiers' "Present Sage Music."

sentences.zh: 器雍羌亦遣弟悉利移城主舒難陀獻其國樂，至成都，韋臯復譜次其聲。

translations.literal: Yongqiang also sent his younger brother Xiliyi city lord Shunantu to present his state's music; reaching Chengdu, Wei Gao again arranged the tones.
translations.idiomatic: Yongqiang sent his brother Xiliyi city lord Shunantu to present Pyu music; at Chengdu Wei Gao arranged the tones.

sentences.zh: 以其舞容、樂器異常，乃圖畫以獻。

translations.literal: Because dance form and instruments were unusual, illustrations were drawn and presented.
translations.idiomatic: Because dance and instruments were unusual, illustrations were drawn and presented.

sentences.zh: 工器二十有二，其音八：金、貝、絲、竹、匏、革、牙、角。

translations.literal: Instruments numbered twenty-two; tones eight: metal, shell, silk, bamboo, gourd, leather, ivory, horn.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-two instruments; eight tones: metal, shell, silk, bamboo, gourd, leather, ivory, horn.

sentences.zh: 金二、貝一、絲七、竹二、匏二、革二、牙一、角二。

translations.literal: Metal two, shell one, silk seven, bamboo two, gourd two, leather two, ivory one, horn two.
translations.idiomatic: Metal two, shell one, silk seven, bamboo two, gourd two, leather two, ivory one, horn two.

sentences.zh: 鈴鈸四，制如龜茲部，周圓三寸，貫以韋，擊磕應節。

translations.literal: Bell cymbals four, shaped like Kucha section, three cun round, strung with leather, struck matching rhythm.
translations.idiomatic: Bell cymbals four, Kucha style, three cun round, leather-strung, struck to rhythm.

sentences.zh: 鐵板二，長三寸五分，博二寸五分，面平，背有柄，系以韋，與鈴鈸皆飾絳紛，以花氎縷為蕊。

translations.literal: Iron plates two, three cun five fen long, two cun five fen wide, flat face, back with handle, leather-strung; with bell cymbals all decorated crimson tassels, flower woolen cores.
translations.idiomatic: Iron plates two, flat with handles; with bell cymbals decorated crimson tassels.

sentences.zh: 螺貝四，大者可受一升，飾絳紛。

translations.literal: Conch shells four, largest holding one sheng, crimson decorated.
translations.idiomatic: Conch shells four, largest holding one sheng, crimson decorated.

sentences.zh: 有鳳首箜篌二：其一長二尺，腹廣七寸，鳳首及項長二尺五寸，面飾虺皮，弦一十有四，項有軫，鳳首外向；

translations.literal: Phoenix-head konghou two: one two chi long, belly seven cun wide, phoenix head and neck two chi five cun, python skin on face, fourteen strings, pegs on neck, phoenix head outward;
translations.idiomatic: Phoenix-head konghou two: one two chi, fourteen strings, phoenix head outward;

sentences.zh: 其一頂有條，軫有鼉首。

translations.literal: one top had bar, pegs with crocodile heads.
translations.idiomatic: one top had bar, pegs with crocodile heads.

sentences.zh: 箏二：其一形如鼉，長四尺，有四足，虛腹，以鼉皮飾背，面及仰肩如琴，廣七寸，腹闊八寸，尾長尺餘，卷上虛中，施關以張九弦，左右一十八柱；

translations.literal: Zheng two: one crocodile-shaped, four chi, four legs, hollow belly, crocodile skin on back, face and shoulders like qin, seven cun wide, eight cun belly, tail over one chi curled hollow with bridges for nine strings, eighteen pillars left and right;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng two: one crocodile-shaped four chi with nine strings and eighteen pillars;

sentences.zh: 其一面飾彩花，傅以虺皮為別。

translations.literal: one face decorated colored flowers, python skin distinguishing.
translations.idiomatic: one face colored flowers, python skin.

sentences.zh: 有龍首琵琶一，如龜茲制，而項長二尺六寸餘，腹廣六寸，二龍相向為首；

translations.literal: Dragon-head pipa one, Kucha style, neck two chi six cun plus, belly six cun wide, two dragons facing as head;
translations.idiomatic: Dragon-head pipa one, Kucha style, two dragons as head;

sentences.zh: 有軫柱各三，弦隨其數，兩軫在項，一在頸，其覆形如師子。

translations.literal: pegs three each side, strings matching number, two pegs on neck one on nape, cover lion-shaped.
translations.idiomatic: pegs three each, strings matching, cover lion-shaped.

sentences.zh: 有雲頭琵琶一，形如前，面飾虺皮，四面有牙釘，以雲為首，軫上有花象品字，三弦，覆手皆飾虺皮，刻捍撥為舞昆侖狀而彩飾之。

translations.literal: Cloud-head pipa one, like former, python skin face, ivory nails four sides, cloud as head, pegs with flower character marks, three strings, all covers python skin, plectrum guard carved dancing Kunlun figure and colored.
translations.idiomatic: Cloud-head pipa one, python skin, cloud head, three strings, plectrum carved dancing Kunlun figure.

sentences.zh: 有大匏琴二，覆以半匏，皆彩畫之，上加銅甌。

translations.literal: Great gourd qin two, half gourd cover, all colored, copper bowl on top.
translations.idiomatic: Great gourd qin two, half gourd cover colored, copper bowl on top.

sentences.zh: 以竹為琴，作虺文橫其上，長三尺餘，頭曲如拱，長二寸，以絳系腹，穿甌及匏本，可受二升。

translations.literal: Bamboo as qin with python pattern across, over three chi, head curved like arch two cun, crimson cord through belly piercing bowl and gourd root, holding two sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Bamboo qin over three chi, crimson cord through belly holding two sheng.

sentences.zh: 大弦應太蔟，次弦應姑洗。

translations.literal: Great string Taicu, next string Guxian.
translations.idiomatic: Great string Taicu, next Guxian.

sentences.zh: 有獨弦匏琴，以班竹為之，不加飾，刻木為虺首；

translations.literal: Single-string gourd qin, spotted bamboo unadorned, carved wood python head;
translations.idiomatic: Single-string gourd qin, spotted bamboo, carved python head;

sentences.zh: 張弦無軫，以弦系頂，有四柱如龜茲琵琶，弦應太蔟。

translations.literal: string without pegs, cord at top, four pillars like Kucha pipa, string Taicu.
translations.idiomatic: string without pegs, four pillars like Kucha pipa, Taicu.

sentences.zh: 有小匏琴二，形如大匏琴，長二尺；

translations.literal: Small gourd qin two, like great gourd qin, two chi long;
translations.idiomatic: Small gourd qin two, two chi;

sentences.zh: 大弦應南呂，次應應鐘。

translations.literal: great string southern pitch, next responding bell.
translations.idiomatic: great string southern pitch, next responding bell.

sentences.zh: 有橫笛二：一長尺餘，取其合律，去節無爪，以蠟實首，上加師子頭，以牙為之，穴六以應黃鐘商，備五音七聲；

translations.literal: Transverse flutes two: one over one chi, matching pitch, nodes removed no claws, wax-filled head plus lion head ivory, six holes for yellow bell shang, five tones seven sounds;
translations.idiomatic: Transverse flutes two: one over one chi, ivory lion head, six holes for yellow bell shang;

sentences.zh: 又一，管唯加象首，律度與荀勖《笛譜》同，又與清商部鐘聲合。

translations.literal: another tube only added elephant head, pitch same as Xun Xu's flute chart and matching Clear Shang section bell sounds.
translations.idiomatic: another elephant head, pitch matching Xun Xu's chart and Clear Shang bells.

sentences.zh: 有兩頭笛二，長二尺八寸，中隔一節，節左右開沖氣穴，兩端皆分洞體為笛量。

translations.literal: Double-end flutes two, two chi eight cun, middle node, holes left and right for breath, both ends divided into flute measure.
translations.idiomatic: Double-end flutes two, two chi eight cun, both ends flute measure.

sentences.zh: 左端應太蔟，管末三穴：一姑洗，二蕤賓，三夷則。

translations.literal: Left end Taicu, tube end three holes: Guxian, Ruibin, Yize.
translations.idiomatic: Left end Taicu, three holes: Guxian, Ruibin, Yize.

sentences.zh: 右端應林鐘，管末三穴：一南呂，二應鐘，三大呂。

translations.literal: Right end forest bell, three holes: southern pitch, responding bell, great pitch.
translations.idiomatic: Right end forest bell, three holes: southern pitch, responding bell, great pitch.

sentences.zh: 下托指一穴，應清太蔟。

translations.literal: Lower finger hole one, clear Taicu.
translations.idiomatic: Lower finger hole clear Taicu.

sentences.zh: 兩洞體七穴，共備黃鐘、林鐘兩均。

translations.literal: Two tube bodies seven holes, together supplying yellow bell and forest bell two mean pitches.
translations.idiomatic: Seven holes total, supplying yellow bell and forest bell mean pitches.

sentences.zh: 有大匏笙二，皆十六管，左右各八，形如鳳翼，大管長四尺八寸五分，餘管參差相次，制如笙管，形亦類鳳翼，竹為簧，穿匏達本。

translations.literal: Great gourd sheng two, sixteen tubes, eight each side phoenix-wing shaped, greatest tube four chi eight cun five fen, others graduated, sheng-tube shaped also phoenix wing, bamboo reeds piercing gourd to root.
translations.idiomatic: Great gourd sheng two, sixteen phoenix-wing tubes, bamboo reeds piercing gourd.

sentences.zh: 上古八音，皆以木漆代之，用金為簧，無匏音，唯驃國得古制。

translations.literal: Ancient eight tones all replaced with lacquered wood; using metal reeds without gourd tone—only Pyu obtained ancient system.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient eight tones replaced with lacquered wood; metal reeds without gourd tone—only Pyu kept ancient system.

sentences.zh: 又有小匏笙二，制如大笙，律應林鐘商。

translations.literal: Also small gourd sheng two, like great sheng, pitch forest bell shang.
translations.idiomatic: Small gourd sheng two, like great, forest bell shang.

sentences.zh: 有三面鼓二，形如酒缸，高二尺，首廣下銳，上博七寸，底博四寸，腹廣不過首，冒以虺皮，束三為一，碧絳約之，下當地則不冒，四面畫驃國工伎執笙鼓以為飾。

translations.literal: Three-faced drums two, wine-jar shaped, two chi high, top wide bottom narrow, top seven cun bottom four cun, belly not exceeding top, python skin, three bound one, green crimson wrapped, bottom unwrapped, four sides painted Pyu artisans with sheng drums as ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Three-faced drums two, jar-shaped two chi, python skin, painted Pyu artisans.

sentences.zh: 有小鼓四，制如腰鼓，長五寸，首廣三寸五分，冒以虺皮，牙釘彩飾，無柄，搖之為樂節，引贊者皆執之。

translations.literal: Small drums four, waist-drum style, five cun long, top three cun five fen wide, python skin, ivory nails colored, no handle, shaken for rhythm; lead chanters all held them.
translations.idiomatic: Small drums four, waist-drum style five cun, shaken for rhythm; lead chanters held them.

sentences.zh: 有牙笙，穿匏達本，漆之，上植二象牙代管，雙簧皆應姑洗。

translations.literal: Ivory sheng, piercing gourd to root lacquered, two ivory tubes planted replacing pipes, double reeds both Guxian.
translations.idiomatic: Ivory sheng piercing lacquered gourd, two ivory tubes, double reeds Guxian.

sentences.zh: 有三角笙，亦穿匏達本，漆之，上植三牛角，一簧應姑洗，餘應南呂，角銳在下，穿匏達本，柄觜皆直。

translations.literal: Triangular sheng, also piercing gourd lacquered, three ox horns planted, one reed Guxian, rest southern pitch, horns sharp below piercing gourd, handle and mouth straight.
translations.idiomatic: Triangular sheng, three ox horns, one reed Guxian, rest southern pitch.

sentences.zh: 有兩角笙，亦穿匏達本，上植二牛角，簧應姑洗，匏以彩飾。

translations.literal: Two-horn sheng, piercing gourd, two ox horns planted, reeds Guxian, gourd colored.
translations.idiomatic: Two-horn sheng, two ox horns, reeds Guxian, colored gourd.

sentences.zh: 曲凡曲名十有二：

translations.literal: Tunes numbered twelve:
translations.idiomatic: Tunes numbered twelve:

sentences.zh: 一曰《佛印》，驃云《沒馱彌》，國人及天竺歌以事王也。

translations.literal: First "Buddha Seal," Pyu "Moduomi," people and Indians sing to serve the king.
translations.idiomatic: First "Buddha Seal," Pyu Moduomi—people and Indians sing to serve the king.

sentences.zh: 二曰《贊娑羅花》，驃云《嚨莽第》，國人以花為衣服，能凈其身也。

translations.literal: Second "Praise Sarasa Flower," Pyu "Longmangdi," people use flowers as clothing to purify the body.
translations.idiomatic: Second "Praise Sarasa Flower," Pyu Longmangdi—flowers as clothing to purify the body.

sentences.zh: 三曰《白鴿》，驃云《都》，美其飛止遂情也。

translations.literal: Third "White Dove," Pyu "Du," praising its flight resting as feelings wish.
translations.idiomatic: Third "White Dove," Pyu Du—praising flight and rest as feelings wish.

sentences.zh: 四曰《白鶴遊》，驃云《蘇謾底哩》，謂翔則摩空，行則徐步也。

translations.literal: Fourth "White Crane Soars," Pyu "Sumandili," meaning soaring rubs heaven, walking steps slowly.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth "White Crane Soars," Pyu Sumandili—soaring rubs heaven, walking steps slowly.

sentences.zh: 五曰《鬥羊勝》，膘云《來乃》。

translations.literal: Fifth "Ram Fight Victory," Pyu "Lainai."
translations.idiomatic: Fifth "Ram Fight Victory," Pyu Lainai.

sentences.zh: 昔有人見二羊鬥海岸，強者則見，弱者入山，時人謂之「來乃」。

translations.literal: Long ago someone saw two rams fighting on the seacoast: the stronger one was visible, while the weaker entered the mountains. People of the time called this "Lainai."
translations.idiomatic: Long ago someone saw two rams fighting on the seacoast: the stronger one was visible, while the weaker entered the mountains. People of the time called this "Lainai."

sentences.zh: 來乃者，勝勢也。

translations.literal: Lainai means victorious force.
translations.idiomatic: Lainai means victorious force.

sentences.zh: 六曰《龍首獨琴》，驃云《彌思彌》，此一弦而五音備，象王一德以畜萬邦也。

translations.literal: Sixth "Dragon Head Single Qin," Pyu "Misimisi," one string yet five tones complete—symbolizing the king's one virtue nourishing all states.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth "Dragon Head Single Qin," Pyu Misimisi—one string, five tones—king's one virtue nourishing all states.

sentences.zh: 七曰《禪定》，驃云《掣覽詩》，謂離俗寂靜也。

translations.literal: Seventh "Meditation," Pyu "Chilianshi," meaning leaving the world in quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh "Meditation," Pyu Chilianshi—leaving the world in quiet.

sentences.zh: 七曲唱舞，皆律應黃鐘商。

translations.literal: Seven tunes sung and danced, all pitch yellow bell shang.
translations.idiomatic: Seven tunes sung and danced in yellow bell shang.

sentences.zh: 八曰《革蔗王》，驃云《遏思略》，謂佛教民如蔗之甘，皆悅其味也。

translations.literal: Eighth "Sugarcane King," Pyu "Esilue," meaning Buddhism teaches people as sugarcane's sweetness—all relish the flavor.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth "Sugarcane King," Pyu Esilue—Buddhism sweet as sugarcane.

sentences.zh: 九曰《孔雀王》，驃云《桃臺》，謂毛采光華也。

translations.literal: Ninth "Peacock King," Pyu "Taotai," meaning feathers shine with glory.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth "Peacock King," Pyu Taotai—feathers shining with glory.

sentences.zh: 十曰《野鵝》，謂飛止必雙，徒侶畢會也。

translations.literal: Tenth "Wild Geese," meaning flight and rest always in pairs, companions all gather.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth "Wild Geese"—flight and rest always in pairs.

sentences.zh: 十一曰《宴樂》，驃云《嚨聰網摩》，謂時康宴會嘉也。

translations.literal: Eleventh "Banquet Music," Pyu "Longcongwangmo," meaning timely peace and joyous assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh "Banquet Music," Pyu Longcongwangmo—timely peace and joyous assembly.

sentences.zh: 十二曰《滌煩》，亦白《笙舞》，驃云《扈那》，謂時滌煩暋，以此適情也。

translations.literal: Twelfth "Wash Cares," also called "Sheng Dance," Pyu "Huna," meaning washing vexation and adjusting feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth "Wash Cares," also "Sheng Dance," Pyu Huna—washing vexation.

sentences.zh: 五曲律應黃鐘兩均：一黃鐘商伊越調，一林鐘商小植調。

translations.literal: Five tunes pitch yellow bell two mean: yellow bell shang Yiyue mode, forest bell shang Xiaozhi mode.
translations.idiomatic: Five tunes in yellow bell two mean: Yiyue and Xiaozhi modes.

sentences.zh: 樂工皆昆侖，衣絳氎，朝霞為蔽膝，謂之裓襔。

translations.literal: Musicians all Kunlun, crimson woolen dress, dawn cloth as apron called jiepan.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians all Kunlun in crimson woolens, dawn cloth apron called jiepan.

sentences.zh: 兩肩加朝霞，絡腋。

translations.literal: Both shoulders added dawn cloth, armpit straps.
translations.idiomatic: Both shoulders dawn cloth, armpit straps.

sentences.zh: 足臂有金寶環釧。

translations.literal: Arms and feet golden jewel rings and bracelets.
translations.idiomatic: Arms and feet golden rings and bracelets.

sentences.zh: 冠金冠，左珥珰，絳貫花鬘，珥雙簪，散以毳。
