translations.literal: Golden crown, left ear pendant, crimson strung flower crown, double hairpins, loose feathers.
translations.idiomatic: Golden crown, left ear pendant, crimson flower crown, double hairpins, loose feathers.

sentences.zh: 初奏樂，有贊者一人先導樂意，其舞容隨曲。

translations.literal: When music first played, one lead chanter guided musical intent; dance form followed the tune.
translations.idiomatic: One lead chanter guided intent; dance followed the tune.

sentences.zh: 用人或二、或六、或四、或八、至十，皆珠冒，拜首稽首以終節。

translations.literal: Performers two, six, four, eight, up to ten—all pearl-capped, bowing forehead to end the section.
translations.idiomatic: Performers two to ten, pearl-capped, bowing forehead to end each section.

sentences.zh: 其樂五譯而至，德宗授舒難陀太仆卿，遣還。

translations.literal: The music passed through five translations to arrive; Dezong appointed Shunantu Grand Master of the Imperial Stud and sent him home.
translations.idiomatic: The music passed through five translations; Dezong appointed Shunantu Grand Master of the Imperial Stud and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 開州刺史唐次述《驃國獻樂頌》以獻。

translations.literal: Kaizhou Prefect Tang Ci composed "Ode on Pyu's Presentation of Music" and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Kaizhou Prefect Tang Ci composed "Ode on Pyu's Presentation of Music" and presented it.

sentences.zh: 大和六年，南詔掠其民三千，徙之柘東。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dahe, Nanzhao plundered three thousand of its people and relocated them to Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: In Dahe's sixth year Nanzhao plundered three thousand Pyu people and relocated them to Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 兩爨蠻兩爨蠻。

translations.literal: The Two Cuan Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The Two Cuan Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 自曲州、靖州西南昆川、曲軛、晉寧、喻獻、安寧距龍和城，通謂之西爨白蠻；

translations.literal: From Quzhou and Jingzhou southwest through Kun River, Qu'e, Jinning, Yuxian, and Anning to Longhe City—all called Western Cuan White Barbarians;
translations.idiomatic: From Quzhou and Jingzhou southwest through Kun River, Qu'e, Jinning, Yuxian, and Anning to Longhe—all called Western Cuan White Barbarians;

sentences.zh: 自彌鹿、升麻二川，南至步頭，謂之東爨烏蠻。

translations.literal: from Milu and Shengma two rivers south to Butou—called Eastern Cuan Wuman.
translations.idiomatic: from Milu and Shengma south to Butou—called Eastern Cuan Wuman.

sentences.zh: 西爨自雲本安邑人，七世祖晉南寧太守，中國亂，遂王蠻中。

translations.literal: Western Cuan originally were Anyi people; a seventh-generation ancestor was Jinning prefect of Jin; when China fell into chaos they became kings among the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Western Cuan were originally Anyi people; a seventh-generation ancestor was Jin prefect of Jinning; when China fell into chaos they became kings among the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝時，南寧州刺史徐文盛召詣荊州，有爨瓚者，據其地，延袤二千餘里。

translations.literal: In Emperor Yuan of Liang's time Nanning Prefect Xu Wensheng summoned them to Jingzhou; Cuan Zan held the land, extending over two thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yuan of Liang, Nanning Prefect Xu Wensheng summoned them to Jingzhou; Cuan Zan held the land, extending over two thousand li.

sentences.zh: 土多駿馬、犀、象、明珠。

translations.literal: The land had many fine horses, rhinoceros, elephants, and bright pearls.
translations.idiomatic: The land had fine horses, rhinoceros, elephants, and bright pearls.

sentences.zh: 既死，子震玩分統其眾。

translations.literal: After his death his sons Zhen and Wan divided command of the masses.
translations.idiomatic: After his death sons Zhen and Wan divided command.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，遣使朝貢，命韋世沖以兵戍之，置恭州、協州、昆州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Sui Kaihuang envoys came with tribute; Wei Shichong was ordered to garrison with troops, establishing Gong, Xie, and Kun prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: At Sui Kaihuang envoys came; Wei Shichong garrisoned troops, establishing Gong, Xie, and Kun prefectures.

sentences.zh: 未幾叛，史萬歲擊之，至西洱河、滇池而還。

translations.literal: Soon they rebelled; Shi Wansui attacked to the Western Er River and Lake Dian and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they rebelled; Shi Wansui attacked to the Western Er River and Lake Dian and returned.

sentences.zh: 震玩懼而入朝，文帝誅之，諸子沒為奴。

translations.literal: Zhenwan feared and came to court; Emperor Wen executed him; sons were enslaved.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenwan feared and came to court; Emperor Wen executed him; sons were enslaved.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，以其子弘達為昆州刺史，奉父喪歸。

translations.literal: When Gaozu succeeded, his son Hongda was made Kunzhou prefect and returned bearing his father's coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu made son Hongda Kunzhou prefect; he returned bearing his father's coffin.

sentences.zh: 而益州刺史段綸遣俞大施至南寧，治共範川，誘諸部皆納款貢方物。

translations.literal: Yizhou Prefect Duan Lun sent Yu Dashi to Nanning, governing Gongfanchuan, inducing all tribes to submit tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou Prefect Duan Lun sent Yu Dashi to Nanning, inducing all tribes to submit tribute.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣將擊西爨，開青蛉、弄棟為縣。

translations.literal: Taizong sent generals against Western Cuan, opening Qingling and Nongdong as counties.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent generals against Western Cuan, opening Qingling and Nongdong as counties.

sentences.zh: 爨蠻之西，有徒莫只蠻、儉望蠻，貞觀二十三年內屬，以其地為傍、望、覽、丘、求五州，隸郎州都督府。

translations.literal: West of Cuan were Tumo and Jianwang barbarians; in Zhenguan twenty-third year they submitted internally, their land made Bang, Wang, Lan, Qiu, and Qiu five prefectures under Langzhou dudu.
translations.idiomatic: West of Cuan were Tumo and Jianwang; in Zhenguan 23 they submitted, land made five prefectures under Langzhou dudu.

sentences.zh: 白水蠻，地與青蛉、弄棟接，亦隸郎州。

translations.literal: White Water barbarians bordered Qingling and Nongdong, also under Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: White Water barbarians bordered Qingling and Nongdong, also under Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 弄棟西有大勃弄、小勃弄二川蠻，其西與黃瓜、葉榆、西洱河接，其眾完富與蜀埒，無酋長，喜相讎怨。

translations.literal: West of Nongdong were Great and Lesser Bonong river tribes; west bordered Huanggua, Yeyu, and Western Er River; their masses were wealthy rivaling Shu; no chieftains; fond of mutual vengeance.
translations.idiomatic: West of Nongdong were Great and Lesser Bonong tribes, wealthy as Shu, without chieftains, fond of vengeance.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，大勃弄楊承顛私署將帥，寇麻州。

translations.literal: At Yonghui's beginning Great Bonong Yang Chengdian privately appointed generals and raided Ma Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At Yonghui's beginning Great Bonong Yang Chengdian raided Ma Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 都督任懷玉招之，不聽。

translations.literal: Protector-General Ren Huaiyu summoned him; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Protector-General Ren Huaiyu summoned him; he refused.

sentences.zh: 高宗以左領軍將軍趙孝祖為郎州道行軍總管，與懷玉討之。

translations.literal: Gaozong made Left Guard General Zhao Xiaozu Langzhou Circuit marching commander with Huaiyu to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong made Zhao Xiaozu Langzhou marching commander with Huaiyu to punish them.

sentences.zh: 至羅仵侯山，其酋禿磨蒲與大鬼主都幹以眾塞菁口，孝祖大破之。

translations.literal: At Luowuhou Mountain chieftain Tumopu and great ghost master Dugan blocked Jingkou with masses; Xiaozu routed them.
translations.idiomatic: At Luowuhou Mountain chieftain Tumopu and ghost master Dugan blocked Jingkou; Xiaozu routed them.

sentences.zh: 夷人尚鬼，謂主祭者為鬼主，每歲戶出一牛或一羊，就其家祭之。

translations.literal: Barbarians honored ghosts; the chief sacrificer was called ghost master; each year one ox or sheep per household sacrificed at his home.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians honored ghosts; chief sacrificer was ghost master; each year one ox or sheep per household sacrificed at his home.

sentences.zh: 送鬼迎鬼必有兵，因以復仇雲。

translations.literal: Sending off ghosts and welcoming ghosts always meant troops—thus revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Ghost ceremonies always meant troops—for revenge.

sentences.zh: 孝祖按軍，多棄城，逐北至周近水。

translations.literal: Xiaozu held the army; many abandoned cities; pursued north to Zhoujin River.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozu held the army; many cities abandoned; pursued north to Zhoujin River.

sentences.zh: 大酋儉彌於、鬼主董樸瀕水為柵，以輕騎逆戰。

translations.literal: Great chieftain Jianmiyu and ghost master Dong Pu built palisades by the water; light cavalry met in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Great chieftain Jianmiyu and ghost master Dong Pu built palisades; light cavalry met battle.

sentences.zh: 孝祖擊斬彌於、禿磨蒲、鬼主十餘級，會大雪，皸凍死者略盡。

translations.literal: Xiaozu struck killing Jianmiyu, Tumopu, and over ten ghost masters; heavy snow came; frostbite deaths nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozu killed Jianmiyu, Tumopu, and over ten ghost masters; heavy snow; frostbite deaths nearly all.

sentences.zh: 孝祖上言：「小勃弄、大勃弄常誘弄棟叛，今因破白水，請遂西討。」

translations.literal: Xiaozu memorialized: "Lesser and Greater Bonong often entice Nongdong to rebel; now breaking White Water, please advance west."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozu memorialized: "Lesser and Greater Bonong entice Nongdong; now breaking White Water, please advance west."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: Edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Edict approved.

sentences.zh: 孝祖軍入，夷人皆走險。

translations.literal: Xiaozu's army entered; barbarians all fled to defiles.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozu's army entered; barbarians fled to defiles.

sentences.zh: 小勃弄酋長歿盛屯白旗城，率萬騎戰，敗，斬之。

translations.literal: Lesser Bonong chieftain Mosheng held White Flag City with ten thousand cavalry; defeated and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser Bonong chieftain Mosheng held White Flag City with ten thousand cavalry; defeated and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 進至大勃弄，楊承顛嬰城守。

translations.literal: Advancing to Greater Bonong, Yang Chengdian defended the city.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to Greater Bonong, Yang Chengdian defended the city.

sentences.zh: 孝祖招之，不從，麾軍進，執承顛。

translations.literal: Xiaozu summoned him; he would not obey; waved the army forward and captured Chengdian.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozu summoned him; he refused; the army captured Chengdian.

sentences.zh: 餘屯大者數萬、小數千，皆破降之，西南夷遂定。

translations.literal: Remaining garrisons large tens of thousands, small thousands—all broken and surrendered; southwest barbarians were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Remaining garrisons—all broken and surrendered; southwest barbarians settled.

sentences.zh: 罷郎州都督，更置戎州都督。

translations.literal: Langzhou dudu was abolished; Rongzhou dudu established.
translations.idiomatic: Langzhou dudu abolished; Rongzhou dudu established.

sentences.zh: 爨弘達既死，以爨歸王為南寧州都督，居石城，襲殺東爨首領蓋聘及子蓋啟，徙共範川。

translations.literal: After Cuan Hongda died, Cuan Guiwang was made Nanning dudu, dwelling at Stone City; he assassinated Eastern Cuan leader Gai Pin and son Gai Qi, relocating to Gongfanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Hongda died, Guiwang was made Nanning dudu at Stone City; he assassinated Eastern Cuan leader Gai Pin and son Gai Qi.

sentences.zh: 有兩爨大鬼主崇道者，與弟日進、日用居安寧城左，聞章仇兼瓊開步頭路，築安寧城，群蠻震騷，共殺築城使者。

translations.literal: Two Cuan great ghost masters Chongdao and brothers Rijin and Riyong dwelt left of Anning City; hearing Zhang Qiu Jianqiong opened Butou road and built Anning City, tribes were shaken and together killed the city-building envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Great ghost masters Chongdao and brothers Rijin and Riyong dwelt near Anning; hearing Butou road opened, tribes killed the city-building envoy.

sentences.zh: 玄宗詔蒙歸義討之。

translations.literal: Xuanzong ordered Meng Guiyi to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong ordered Meng Guiyi to punish them.

sentences.zh: 師次波州，歸王及崇道兄弟千餘人泥首謝罪，赦之。

translations.literal: Army halted at Bo Prefecture; Guiwang and Chongdao brothers over a thousand mud-crowned begging pardon; pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Army halted at Bo; Guiwang and Chongdao over a thousand begged pardon; pardoned.

sentences.zh: 俄而崇道殺日進及歸王。

translations.literal: Soon Chongdao killed Rijin and Guiwang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chongdao killed Rijin and Guiwang.

sentences.zh: 歸王妻阿乇，烏蠻女也，走父部，乞兵相仇，於是諸爨亂。

translations.literal: Guiwang's wife Azhuo, a Wuman woman, fled to her father's tribe begging troops for revenge; all Cuan rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Guiwang's wife Azhuo, a Wuman woman, fled begging troops; all Cuan rebelled.

sentences.zh: 阿乇遣使詣歸義求殺夫者，書聞，詔以其子守隅為南寧州都督，歸義以女妻之，又以一女妻崇道子輔朝。

translations.literal: Azhuo sent envoys to Guiyi seeking her husband's killer; edict heard; ordered son Shouyu Nanning dudu; Guiyi married him a daughter and also a daughter to Chongdao's son Fuchao.
translations.idiomatic: Azhuo sought her husband's killer; son Shouyu made Nanning dudu; Guiyi married him a daughter and Fuchao a daughter.

sentences.zh: 然崇道、守隅相攻討不置，阿乇訴歸義，為興師，營昆川。

translations.literal: Yet Chongdao and Shouyu attacked each other unceasingly; Azhuo appealed to Guiyi who raised troops encamping at Kun River.
translations.idiomatic: Chongdao and Shouyu attacked unceasingly; Azhuo appealed; Guiyi raised troops at Kun River.

sentences.zh: 崇道走黎州，遂虜其族，殺輔朝，收其女，崇道俄亦被殺，諸爨稍離弱。

translations.literal: Chongdao fled to Lizhou; then captured his clan, killed Fuchao, took his daughter; Chongdao soon also killed; all Cuan gradually weakened.
translations.idiomatic: Chongdao fled to Lizhou; Guiyi captured his clan, killed Fuchao; Chongdao soon killed; Cuan gradually weakened.

sentences.zh: 閣羅鳳閣羅鳳立，召守隅並妻歸河睒，不通中國。

translations.literal: When Geluofeng succeeded he summoned Shouyu and wife to Hexian, cutting off China.
translations.idiomatic: When Geluofeng succeeded he summoned Shouyu to Hexian, cutting off China.

sentences.zh: 阿乇自主其部落，歲入朝，恩賞蕃厚。

translations.literal: Azhuo governed her tribe herself, yearly coming to court with generous favor.
translations.idiomatic: Azhuo governed her tribe, yearly at court with generous favor.

sentences.zh: 閣羅鳳遣昆川城使楊牟利以兵脅西爨，徙戶二十餘萬於永昌城。

translations.literal: Geluofeng sent Kun River city envoy Yang Mouli with troops to coerce Western Cuan, relocating over two hundred thousand households to Yongchang City.
translations.idiomatic: Geluofeng sent Yang Mouli to coerce Western Cuan, relocating over two hundred thousand households to Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 東爨以言語不通，多散依林谷，得不徙。

translations.literal: Eastern Cuan, languages not matching, mostly scattered in forests and valleys, escaped relocation.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Cuan, languages not matching, mostly scattered in valleys, escaped relocation.

sentences.zh: 自曲靖州、石城、升麻、昆川南北至龍和，皆殘於兵。

translations.literal: From Qujing, Shicheng, Shengma, Kun River north to south to Longhe—all ravaged by war.
translations.idiomatic: From Qujing to Longhe—all ravaged by war.

sentences.zh: 日進等子孫居永昌城。

translations.literal: Rijin and others' descendants dwelt at Yongchang City.
translations.idiomatic: Rijin and others' descendants dwelt at Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 烏蠻種復振，徙居西爨故地，與峰州為鄰。

translations.literal: Wuman stock revived, relocating to Western Cuan old lands, neighboring Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wuman revived, relocating to Western Cuan lands, neighboring Feng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，置都督府，領羈縻州十八。

translations.literal: In Zhenyuan a dudu office was established governing eighteen jimi prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan a dudu office governed eighteen jimi prefectures.

sentences.zh: 烏蠻烏蠻與南詔世昏姻，其種分七部落：一曰阿芋路，居曲州、靖州故地；

translations.literal: Wuman intermarried with Nanzhao for generations; the kind divided seven tribes: first Ayulu, dwelling Quzhou and Jingzhou old lands;
translations.idiomatic: Wuman intermarried with Nanzhao; seven tribes: Ayulu in Quzhou and Jingzhou old lands;

sentences.zh: 二曰阿猛；

translations.literal: second Ameng;
translations.idiomatic: second Ameng;

sentences.zh: 三曰夔山；

translations.literal: third Kuishan;
translations.idiomatic: third Kuishan;

sentences.zh: 四曰暴蠻；

translations.literal: fourth Baoman;
translations.idiomatic: fourth Baoman;

sentences.zh: 五曰盧鹿蠻，二部落分保竹子嶺；

translations.literal: fifth and sixth Lulu tribes guarding Zhuziling;
translations.idiomatic: fifth and sixth Lulu tribes at Zhuziling;

sentences.zh: 六曰磨彌斂；

translations.literal: seventh Molian;
translations.idiomatic: seventh Molian;

sentences.zh: 七曰勿鄧。

translations.literal: eighth Wudeng.
translations.idiomatic: eighth Wudeng.

sentences.zh: 土多牛馬，無布帛，男子髽髻，女人被發，皆衣牛羊皮。

translations.literal: Land had many cattle and horses, no cloth; men topknotted, women loose-haired, all wore cattle and sheep hide.
translations.idiomatic: Many cattle and horses, no cloth; men topknotted, women loose-haired, cattle and sheep hide.

sentences.zh: 俗尚巫鬼，無拜跪之節。

translations.literal: Custom honored shamans and ghosts; no bowing or kneeling rites.
translations.idiomatic: Custom honored shamans; no bowing or kneeling.

sentences.zh: 其語四譯乃與中國通。

translations.literal: Their speech required four translations to reach China.
translations.idiomatic: Their speech required four translations to reach China.

sentences.zh: 大部落有大鬼主，百家則置小鬼主。

translations.literal: Great tribes had great ghost masters; a hundred households set lesser ghost masters.
translations.idiomatic: Great tribes had great ghost masters; hundred households lesser ghost masters.

sentences.zh: 勿鄧地方千里，有邛部六姓，一姓白蠻也，五姓烏蠻也。

translations.literal: Wudeng territory a thousand li; Qiong tribe six surnames—one White Barbarian, five Wuman.
translations.idiomatic: Wudeng a thousand li; Qiong six surnames—one White, five Wuman.

sentences.zh: 又有初裹五姓，皆烏蠻也，居邛部、臺登之間。

translations.literal: Also Chubao five surnames all Wuman between Qiong and Taideng.
translations.idiomatic: Chubao five surnames all Wuman between Qiong and Taideng.

sentences.zh: 婦人衣黑繒，其長曳地。

translations.literal: Women wore black silk dragging on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore black silk dragging on the ground.

sentences.zh: 又有東欽蠻二姓，皆白蠻也，居北谷。

translations.literal: Also Dongqin two surnames all White Barbarian in North Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Dongqin two surnames all White Barbarian in North Valley.

sentences.zh: 婦人衣白繒，長不過膝。

translations.literal: Women wore white silk not past the knee.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore white silk not past the knee.

sentences.zh: 又有粟蠻二姓、雷蠻三姓、夢蠻三姓，散處黎、巂、戎數州之鄙，皆隸勿鄧。

translations.literal: Also Su two surnames, Lei three, Meng three scattered at Li, Xie, Rong prefecture borders—all under Wudeng.
translations.idiomatic: Su two, Lei three, Meng three scattered at Li, Xie, Rong—all under Wudeng.

sentences.zh: 勿鄧南七十里，有兩林部落，有十低三姓、阿屯三姓、虧望三姓隸焉。

translations.literal: Seventy li south of Wudeng was Lianglin tribe; Shidi three, Atun three, Kuiwang three surnames under it.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy li south was Lianglin; Shidi, Atun, Kuiwang three surnames under it.

sentences.zh: 其南有豐琶部落，阿諾二姓隸焉。

translations.literal: South was Fengpa tribe; Anuo two surnames under it.
translations.idiomatic: South was Fengpa; Anuo two surnames under it.

sentences.zh: 兩林地雖狹，而諸部推為長，號都大鬼主。

translations.literal: Though Lianglin land was narrow, all tribes honored it as elder, styled Chief Great Ghost Master.
translations.idiomatic: Though Lianglin was narrow, tribes honored it as elder—Chief Great Ghost Master.

sentences.zh: 勿鄧、豐琶、兩林皆謂之東蠻，天寶中，皆受封爵。

translations.literal: Wudeng, Fengpa, Lianglin all called Eastern Barbarians; in Tianbao all received ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Wudeng, Fengpa, Lianglin called Eastern Barbarians; in Tianbao all received ranks.

sentences.zh: 及南詔陷巂州，遂羈屬吐蕃。

translations.literal: When Nanzhao took Xie Prefecture they came under Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanzhao took Xie they came under Tibet.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，復通款，以勿鄧大鬼主苴嵩兼邛部團練使，封長川郡公。

translations.literal: In Zhenyuan they renewed contact; Wudeng great ghost master Jusong also Qiong regiment commander, enfeoffed Changchuan Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan contact renewed; Jusong enfeoffed Changchuan Prince.

sentences.zh: 及死，子苴驃離幼，以苴夢沖為大鬼主，數為吐蕃侵獵。

translations.literal: After death son Jubiaoli young; Jumengchong made great ghost master; repeatedly raided by Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: After death son young; Jumengchong made great ghost master; repeatedly raided by Tibet.

sentences.zh: 兩林都大鬼主苴那時遺韋臯書，乞兵攻吐蕃。

translations.literal: Lianglin chief great ghost master Junashi sent Wei Gao letter begging troops against Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Lianglin chief Junashi sent Gao letter begging troops against Tibet.

sentences.zh: 臯遣將劉朝彩出銅山道，吳鳴鶴出清溪關道，鄧英俊出定蕃柵道，進逼臺登城。

translations.literal: Gao sent Liu Chaocai out Tongshan road, Wu Minghe Qingxi Pass road, Deng Yingjun Dingfan stockade road, pressing Taideng City.
translations.idiomatic: Gao sent Liu Chaocai, Wu Minghe, Deng Yingjun pressing Taideng City.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃退壁西貢川，據高為營。

translations.literal: Tibet withdrew to fortify Xigongchuan, holding heights as camp.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet withdrew to Xigongchuan, holding heights.

sentences.zh: 苴那時戰甚力，分兵大破吐蕃青海、臘城二節度軍於北谷，青海大兵馬使乞藏遮遮、臘城兵馬使悉多楊朱、節度論東柴、大將論結突梨等皆戰死，執籠官四十五人，鎧仗一萬，牛馬稱是。

translations.literal: Junashi fought with great force, divided his troops, and at Beigu routed the two Tibetan military commands of Qinghai and Lacheng. Qizang Zhezhe, the Great Army Commissioner of Qinghai; Xiduo Yangzhu, the Army Commissioner of Lacheng; the military commissioner Lun Dongchai; the great general Lun Jietuli; and others all died in battle. He captured forty-five longguan, ten thousand suits of armor and weapons, and an equal number of cattle and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Junashi fought with great force, divided his troops, and at Beigu routed the two Tibetan military commands of Qinghai and Lacheng. Qizang Zhezhe, the Great Army Commissioner of Qinghai; Xiduo Yangzhu, the Army Commissioner of Lacheng; the military commissioner Lun Dongchai; the great general Lun Jietuli; and others all died in battle. He captured forty-five longguan, ten thousand suits of armor and weapons, and an equal number of cattle and horses.

sentences.zh: 進拔於蔥柵。

translations.literal: Advanced taking Yucang stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Advanced taking Yucang stockade.

sentences.zh: 乞藏遮遮，尚結贊子也，以屍還。

translations.literal: Qizangzhezhe was Shang Jiezan's son; corpse returned.
translations.idiomatic: Qizangzhezhe was Shang Jiezan's son; corpse returned.

sentences.zh: 其下曩貢節度蘇論百餘人行哭，使一人立屍左，一人問之曰：「瘡痛乎？」

translations.literal: His subordinate Nanggong commissioner Sulun over a hundred walked weeping; one stood left of corpse, one asked: "Does the wound pain?
translations.idiomatic: Sulun over a hundred walked weeping; one asked the corpse: "Does the wound pain?"

sentences.zh: 曰「然。」

translations.literal: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: "Yes."

sentences.zh: 即傅藥。

translations.literal: Then applied medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Medicine applied.

sentences.zh: 曰「食乎？」

translations.literal: Said "Eat?
translations.idiomatic: "Eat?"

sentences.zh: 曰「然。」

translations.literal: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: "Yes."

sentences.zh: 即進膳。

translations.literal: Then offered meal.
translations.idiomatic: Meal offered.

sentences.zh: 曰「衣乎？」

translations.literal: Said "Clothing?
translations.idiomatic: "Clothing?"

sentences.zh: 曰「然。」

translations.literal: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: "Yes."

sentences.zh: 即命裘。

translations.literal: Then ordered fur.
translations.idiomatic: Fur ordered.

sentences.zh: 又問「歸乎？」

translations.literal: Asked again "Return?
translations.idiomatic: "Return?"

sentences.zh: 曰「然。」

translations.literal: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: "Yes."

sentences.zh: 以馬載屍而去。

translations.literal: Horse carried corpse away.
translations.idiomatic: Horse carried corpse away.

sentences.zh: 詔封苴那時為順政郡王，苴夢沖為懷化郡王，豐琶部落大鬼主驃傍為和義郡王，給印章、袍帶。

translations.literal: Edict enfeoffed Junashi Shunzheng Prince, Jumengchong Huaihua Prince, Fengpa great ghost master Piaobang Heyi Prince, granting seals, robes, belts.
translations.idiomatic: Edict enfeoffed Junashi Shunzheng Prince, Jumengchong Huaihua Prince, Piaobang Heyi Prince.

sentences.zh: 三王皆入朝，宴麟德殿，賞賚加等，歲給其部祿鹽衣彩，黎、巂二州吏就賜之。

translations.literal: Three kings all came to court; feast at Qinde Hall; rewards doubled; yearly salary salt cloth to their tribes; Li and Xie prefecture officials delivered.
translations.idiomatic: Three kings came to court; feast at Qinde Hall; yearly salary salt and cloth delivered.

sentences.zh: 以山阻多為盜侵，亡失所賜，臯令二州為築館，有賜，約酋長自至，授賜而遣之。

translations.literal: Because mountains blocked, bandits often stole gifts; Gao ordered two prefectures build lodges; chiefs came in person for gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits stole gifts; Gao ordered lodges built; chiefs came in person.

sentences.zh: 然苴夢沖內附吐蕃，斷南詔使路，臯遣巂州總管蘇峞以兵三百召夢沖至琵琶川，聲其罪斬之，披其族為六部，以樣棄主之。

translations.literal: Yet Jumengchong submitted internally to Tibet, cutting Nanzhao envoy road; Gao sent Xie commander Su Yan with three hundred troops summoning Mengchong to Pipa River, proclaimed his crime and executed, splitting clan into six parts with Yangqiben chief.
translations.idiomatic: Jumengchong submitted to Tibet; Gao executed him at Pipa River, splitting clan into six parts.

sentences.zh: 及苴驃離長，乃命為大鬼主。

translations.literal: When Jubiaoli grew he was made great ghost master.
translations.idiomatic: When Jubiaoli grew he was made great ghost master.

sentences.zh: 驃傍年少驍敢，數出兵攻吐蕃。

translations.literal: Piaobang young and fierce repeatedly sent troops against Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Piaobang young and fierce repeatedly attacked Tibet.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃間道焚其居室、部落，亡所賜印章。

translations.literal: Tibet by secret route burned their dwellings and tribes; lost granted seals.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet burned their dwellings; lost granted seals.

sentences.zh: 臯為請，復得印。

translations.literal: Gao requested on their behalf; seals recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Gao requested; seals recovered.

sentences.zh: 昆明蠻爨蠻西有昆明蠻，一曰昆彌，以西洱河為境，即葉榆河也。

translations.literal: Kunming Barbarians: west of Cuan was Kunming, also Kunmi, bordering on Western Er River—Yeyu River.
translations.idiomatic: West of Cuan was Kunming, also Kunmi, bordering Western Er River—Yeyu River.

sentences.zh: 距京師九千里。

translations.literal: Nine thousand li from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Nine thousand li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 土濕，宜粳稻。

translations.literal: Soil damp, suited to glutinous rice.
translations.idiomatic: Damp soil suited to glutinous rice.

sentences.zh: 人辮首、左衽，與突厥同。

translations.literal: People braided hair, left-lapelled—same as Turks.
translations.idiomatic: People braided hair, left-lapelled like Turks.

sentences.zh: 隨水草畜牧，夏處高山，冬入深谷。

translations.literal: Following water and grass for pasture; summer in high mountains, winter in deep valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Pastoral; summer in mountains, winter in valleys.

sentences.zh: 尚戰死，惡病亡，勝兵數萬。

translations.literal: Honored death in battle, hated death by illness; effective troops tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Honored death in battle; effective troops tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 武德中，巂州治中吉偉使南寧，因至其國，諭使使朝貢，求內屬，發兵戍守。

translations.literal: In Wude, Xie Prefecture assistant Ji Wei sent to Nanning, reaching their state, persuading envoys to court and submit internally; troops garrisoned.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude Ji Wei reached their state, persuading submission; troops garrisoned.

sentences.zh: 自是歲與牂柯使偕來。

translations.literal: From then yearly with Zangke envoys together.
translations.idiomatic: From then yearly with Zangke envoys.

sentences.zh: 龍朔三年，矩州刺史謝法成招慰比樓等七千戶內附。

translations.literal: Longshuo third year Juzhou Prefect Xie Facheng summoned Bilou and seven thousand households to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo 3 Xie Facheng summoned seven thousand households.

sentences.zh: 總章三年，置祿州、湯望州。

translations.literal: Zongzhang third year established Lu and Tangwang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhang 3 established Lu and Tangwang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 咸亨三年，昆明十四姓率戶二萬內附，析其地為殷州、㧾州、敦州，以安輯之。

translations.literal: Xianheng third year Kunming fourteen surnames led twenty thousand households internally; land split into Yin, Huo, Dun prefectures to pacify.
translations.idiomatic: Xianheng 3 fourteen surnames led twenty thousand households; Yin, Huo, Dun prefectures established.

sentences.zh: 殷州居戎州西北，㧾州居西南，敦州居南，遠不過五百餘里，近三百里。

translations.literal: Yin north of Rong, Huo southwest, Dun south—far not over five hundred li, near three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Yin north of Rong, Huo southwest, Dun south—three to five hundred li.

sentences.zh: 其後又置盤、麻等四十一州，皆以首領為刺史。

translations.literal: Later also established Pan, Ma and forty-one prefectures—all chieftains as prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Later Pan, Ma and forty-one prefectures—chieftains as prefects.

sentences.zh: 昆明東九百里，即牂柯國也。

translations.literal: Nine hundred li east of Kunming was Zangke Country.
translations.idiomatic: Nine hundred li east was Zangke.

sentences.zh: 兵數出，侵地數千里。

translations.literal: Troops repeatedly marched out, seizing land several thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Troops repeatedly seized land thousands of li.

sentences.zh: 元和八年，上表請盡歸牂柯故地。

translations.literal: Yuanhe eighth year memorialized requesting full return of Zangke old lands.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhe 8 requested return of Zangke old lands.

sentences.zh: 開成元年，鬼主阿珮內屬。

translations.literal: Kaicheng first year ghost master Apei submitted internally.
translations.idiomatic: Kaicheng 1 ghost master Apei submitted.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，封其別帥為羅殿王，世襲爵。

translations.literal: Huichang enfeoffed vice-chief as Luodian King, hereditary rank.
translations.idiomatic: Huichang enfeoffed vice-chief Luodian King, hereditary.

sentences.zh: 其後又封別帥為滇王，皆牂柯蠻也。

translations.literal: Later also enfeoffed vice-chief as Dian King—all Zangke barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Later vice-chief enfeoffed Dian King—all Zangke.

sentences.zh: 東距辰州二千四百里，其南千五百里即交州也。

translations.literal: East fifteen hundred li to Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: East fifteen hundred li to Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 無城郭，土熱多霖雨，稻粟再熟。

translations.literal: No walled cities; land hot with much rain; rice twice yearly.
translations.idiomatic: No walls; hot rainy land; rice twice yearly.

sentences.zh: 無徭役，戰乃屯聚。

translations.literal: No corvée; war then gathering.
translations.idiomatic: No corvée; war then gathering.

sentences.zh: 刻木為契，盜者倍三而償，殺人者出牛馬三十。

translations.literal: Carved wood as contract; thieves repay triple; killers pay thirty cattle and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Carved wood contracts; thieves repay triple; killers pay thirty cattle.

sentences.zh: 俗與東謝同。

translations.literal: Custom like Eastern Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Custom like Eastern Xie.

sentences.zh: 首領亦姓謝氏，至龍羽有兵三萬。

translations.literal: Chieftains also surnamed Xie; to Longyu had thirty thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chieftains surnamed Xie; Longyu had thirty thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 武德三年，遣使者朝，以其地為牂州，拜龍羽刺史，封夜郎郡公。

translations.literal: Wude third year envoys came; land made Zang Prefecture; Longyu enfeoffed prefect, Prince of Yelang.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 3 envoys came; Zang Prefecture; Longyu Prince of Yelang.

sentences.zh: 其北百五十里，有別部曰充州蠻，勝兵二萬，亦來朝貢，以地為充州。

translations.literal: North one hundred fifty li another tribe Chongzhou barbarians, twenty thousand effective troops, also tribute; land made Chong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: North one hundred fifty li Chongzhou barbarians, twenty thousand troops; Chong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開元中，牂柯酋長元齊死，孫嘉藝襲官，封其後，乃以趙氏為酋長。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan Yuan Qi died; grandson Jiayi inherited; enfeoffed descendants; then Zhao clan as chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan Yuan Qi died; grandson Jiayi inherited; Zhao chieftains.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，趙君道來朝。

translations.literal: Twenty-fifth year Zhao Jundao came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Year 25 Zhao Jundao came to court.

sentences.zh: 其裔有趙國珍，天寶中戰有功。

translations.literal: Descendant Zhao Guozhen, Tianbao battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: Descendant Zhao Guozhen had Tianbao merit.

sentences.zh: 閣羅鳳叛，宰相楊國忠兼劍南節度使，以國珍有方略，授黔中都督，屢敗南詔，護五溪十餘年，天下方亂，其部獨寧。

translations.literal: When Geluofeng rebelled Chancellor Yang Guozhong also Jiannan jiedushi; Guozhen had strategy; made Qianzhong dudu; repeatedly defeated Nanzhao; guarded Five Streams over ten years; realm in chaos his tribe alone peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: Geluofeng rebelled; Guozhen made Qianzhong dudu; repeatedly defeated Nanzhao; tribe peaceful amid chaos.

sentences.zh: 終工部尚書。

translations.literal: Ended Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Ended Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，官其酋長趙主俗，亦以褒朝貢不絕。

translations.literal: Zhenyuan enfeoffed chieftain Zhao Zhusu; tribute unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyuan enfeoffed Zhao Zhusu; tribute unceasing.

sentences.zh: 至十八年，五遣使朝。

translations.literal: To eighteenth year five envoy missions.
translations.idiomatic: To year 18 five missions.

sentences.zh: 元和二年，詔黔南觀察使常以本道將為押領牂柯、昆明等使，自是數遣使，或朝正月，訖開成不絕。

translations.literal: Yuanhe second year edict Qiannan observation commissioner always local general leading Zangke, Kunming envoys; from then frequent envoys New Year court until Kaicheng unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhe 2 edict observation commissioner led Zangke envoys until Kaicheng.

sentences.zh: 故事：戎夷朝貢，將至都，中官驛勞於郊，既及館，恩禮尤渥。

translations.literal: Precedent: approaching capital, palace eunuchs welcomed at suburbs; at lodge favor especially thick.
translations.idiomatic: Precedent: palace eunuchs welcomed at suburbs; thick favor at lodge.

sentences.zh: 東謝蠻西爨之南，有東謝蠻，居黔州西三百里，南距守宮獠，西連夷子，地方千里。

translations.literal: Eastern Xie: south of Western Cuan; west three hundred li from Qian; south Shougong Liao; west Yizi; territory a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Xie south of Western Cuan; a thousand li territory.

sentences.zh: 宜五谷，為畬田，歲一易之。

translations.literal: Suited five grains; slash-and-burn fields, one year then move.
translations.idiomatic: Five grains; slash-and-burn, one year then move.

sentences.zh: 眾處山，巢居，汲流以飲。

translations.literal: Masses in mountains, nest dwellings; drew streams to drink.
translations.idiomatic: Nest dwellings in mountains; stream water.

sentences.zh: 無賦稅，刻木為契。

translations.literal: No taxes; carved wood contracts.
translations.idiomatic: No taxes; carved wood contracts.

sentences.zh: 見貴人執鞭而拜。

translations.literal: Seeing nobles held whip and bowed.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing nobles held whip and bowed.

sentences.zh: 賞有功者以牛馬、銅鼓。

translations.literal: Rewarding merit with cattle, horses, bronze drums.
translations.idiomatic: Merit rewarded with cattle, horses, bronze drums.

sentences.zh: 犯小罪則杖，大事殺之，盜物者倍償。

translations.literal: Small crimes beaten; great affairs killed; thieves repay double.
translations.idiomatic: Small crimes beaten; great killed; thieves repay double.

sentences.zh: 昏姻以牛酒為聘。

translations.literal: Marriage betrothal cattle and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage betrothal cattle and wine.

sentences.zh: 女婦夫家，夫慚澀避之，旬日乃出。

translations.literal: Wife to husband's home; husband shy avoided; ten days then emerged.
translations.idiomatic: Wife to husband's home; husband shy ten days.

sentences.zh: 會聚，擊銅鼓，吹角。

translations.literal: Gatherings beat bronze drums, blew horns.
translations.idiomatic: Gatherings beat bronze drums and horns.

sentences.zh: 俗椎髻，韜以絳，垂於後。

translations.literal: Custom topknot, red wrapped hanging behind.
translations.idiomatic: Topknot, red wrapped behind.

sentences.zh: 坐必蹲踞，常帶刀劍。

translations.literal: Sitting always squatting; always carried sword.
translations.idiomatic: Always squatting; always sword.

sentences.zh: 男子服衫襖、大口褲，以帶斜馮右肩，以螺殼、虎豹、猿狖、犬羊皮為飾。

translations.literal: Men wore jackets and large trousers, belt slung right shoulder; shells, tiger, ape, dog, sheep skin ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Men jackets and large trousers; shell and fur ornaments.

sentences.zh: 有謝氏，世為酋長，部落尊畏之。

translations.literal: Xie clan generation chieftains; tribes feared them.
translations.idiomatic: Xie clan generation chieftains; tribes feared them.

sentences.zh: 其族不育女，自以姓高不可以嫁人。

translations.literal: Clan did not raise daughters—surname too noble to marry out.
translations.idiomatic: Clan did not raise daughters—surname too noble.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，其酋元深入朝，冠烏熊皮若註旄，以金銀絡額，被毛帔，韋行縢，著履。

translations.literal: Zhenguan third year chieftain Yuanshen came; crown black bear skin like yak tail; gold silver forehead; fur cape; leather leggings; shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan 3 Yuanshen came in bear-skin crown and fur cape.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎顏師古因是上言：「昔周武王時，遠國入朝，太史次為《王會篇》，今蠻夷入朝，如元深冠服不同，可寫為《王會圖》。」

translations.literal: Zhongshu Vice Minister Yan Shigu therefore memorialized, "In the past, when distant states entered court under King Wu of Zhou, the Grand Historian arranged them in the 'Wanghui' chapter. Now barbarians and Yi enter court; since figures such as Yuanshen have different caps and clothing, they may be drawn as a 'Wanghui Chart.'"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu Vice Minister Yan Shigu therefore memorialized, "In the past, when distant states entered court under King Wu of Zhou, the Grand Historian arranged them in the 'Wanghui' chapter. Now barbarians and Yi enter court; since figures such as Yuanshen have different caps and clothing, they may be drawn as a 'Wanghui Chart.'"

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: Edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Edict approved.

sentences.zh: 帝以地為應州，即拜元深刺史，隸黔州都督府。

translations.literal: Emperor made land Ying Prefecture; Yuanshen prefect under Qian dudu.
translations.idiomatic: Land made Ying Prefecture; Yuanshen prefect under Qian.

sentences.zh: 又有南謝首領謝強亦來朝，以其地為莊州，授強刺史。

translations.literal: Also Southern Xie chieftain Xie Qiang came; land Zhuang Prefecture; Qiang prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Xie Xie Qiang came; Zhuang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 建中三年，大酋長檢校蠻州長史、資陽郡公宋鼎與諸謝朝賀，德宗以其國小，不許。

translations.literal: Jianzhong third year great chieftain Song Ding of Man Prefecture came; Dezong because state small did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhong 3 Song Ding came; Dezong refused small state.

sentences.zh: 訴於黔中觀察使王礎，以州接牂柯，願隨牂柯朝賀，礎奏：「牂、蠻二州，戶繁力強，為鄰蕃所憚，請許三年一朝。」

translations.literal: He appealed to Wang Chu, Surveillance Commissioner of Qianzhong. Because the prefecture bordered Zangke, he wished to follow Zangke in presenting court congratulations. Chu memorialized, "Zang and Man prefectures have many households and strong forces and are feared by neighboring foreign peoples; please allow them to come to court once every three years."
translations.idiomatic: He appealed to Wang Chu, Surveillance Commissioner of Qianzhong. Because the prefecture bordered Zangke, he wished to follow Zangke in presenting court congratulations. Chu memorialized, "Zang and Man prefectures have many households and strong forces and are feared by neighboring foreign peoples; please allow them to come to court once every three years."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: Edict followed.
translations.idiomatic: Edict followed.

sentences.zh: 元和中，辰、漵蠻酋張伯靖嫉本道督斂苛刻，聚眾叛，侵播、費二州，黔中經略使崔能、荊南節度使嚴綬、湖南觀察使柳公綽討之，三歲不能定。

translations.literal: Yuanhe Chen, Xu barbarian chief Zhang Bojing hated harsh levies, rebelled raiding Bo, Fei; Cui Neng, Yan Shou, Liu Gongchuo three years could not settle.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhe Bojing rebelled; three years unsettled.

sentences.zh: 伯靖上表請隸荊南，乃降。

translations.literal: Bojing memorialized requesting Jingnan affiliation; then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Bojing requested Jingnan; surrendered.

sentences.zh: 崔能內恨之，更請調荊南、湖南、桂管軍為援，約西原十洞兵皆出，可以成功。

translations.literal: Neng inwardly resentful requested Jingnan, Hunan, Guiguan troops; Xiyuan ten cave soldiers—all could succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Neng requested more troops from three circuits.

sentences.zh: 公卿議者皆以為便。

translations.literal: Ministers all thought convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers approved.

sentences.zh: 宰相李吉甫曰：「伯靖挾怨而叛，壓以大兵而招之，可不戰自定。」

translations.literal: Chancellor Li Jifu said, "Bojing rebelled while nursing resentment. If he is pressed with a great army and then summoned, he can be settled without battle."
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Li Jifu said, "Bojing rebelled while nursing resentment. If he is pressed with a great army and then summoned, he can be settled without battle."

sentences.zh: 乃命能兵毋出，獨詔嚴綬招伯靖率家屬詣江陵降，授右威衛翊府中郎將。

translations.literal: Ordered Neng not march; only edict Yan Shou summon Bojing family to Jiangling surrender; appointed Right Weiwu Yifu General.
translations.idiomatic: Neng held; Yan Shou summoned surrender; Bojing appointed general.

sentences.zh: 西趙蠻東謝南有西趙蠻，東距夷子，西屬昆明，南西洱河也。

translations.literal: Western Zhao: south of Eastern Xie; east Yizi; west Kunming; south Western Er River.
translations.idiomatic: Western Zhao south of Eastern Xie; west Kunming.

sentences.zh: 山穴阻深，莫知道裏。

translations.literal: Mountain caves deep; none knew distance.
translations.idiomatic: Deep mountain caves; distance unknown.

sentences.zh: 南北十八日行，東西二十三日行，戶萬餘，俗與東謝同，趙氏世為酋長。

translations.literal: Eighteen days north-south, twenty-three east-west; over ten thousand households; custom like Eastern Xie; Zhao generation chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen days north-south; ten thousand households; Zhao chieftains.

sentences.zh: 夷子渠帥姓季氏，與西趙皆南蠻別種，勝兵各萬人。

translations.literal: Yizi chieftain surname Ji; with Western Zhao both Southern Barbarian branches; ten thousand effective troops each.
translations.idiomatic: Yizi Ji clan; ten thousand troops each.

sentences.zh: 自古未嘗通中國，黔州豪帥田康諷之，故貞觀中皆遣使入朝。

translations.literal: Never contacted China; Qian Prefecture magnate Tian Kang induced; Zhenguan all sent envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Never contacted China until Tian Kang induced Zhenguan envoys.

sentences.zh: 西趙首領趙酋摩率所部萬餘戶內附，以其地為明州，授酋摩刺史。

translations.literal: Western Zhao chieftain Zhao Qiumo led over ten thousand households internally; land Ming Prefecture; Qiumo prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qiumo ten thousand households; Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 松外蠻松外蠻尚數十百部，大者五六百戶，小者二三百。

translations.literal: Songwai Barbarians: still several tens of hundreds of tribes; large five-six hundred households, small two-three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Songwai: tens of tribes; large five-six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 凡數十姓，趙、楊、李、董為貴族，皆擅山川，不能相君長。

translations.literal: Several tens surnames; Zhao, Yang, Li, Dong noble; all held mountains and rivers; none could rule others.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, Yang, Li, Dong noble; held mountains; no unified rule.

sentences.zh: 有城郭、文字，頗知陰陽歷數。

translations.literal: Had walled cities, writing; knew yin-yang calendrics.
translations.idiomatic: Walled cities, writing; yin-yang calendrics.

sentences.zh: 自夜郎、滇池以西，皆莊之裔。

translations.literal: West of Yelang and Lake Dian all Zhuang descendants.
translations.idiomatic: West of Yelang and Lake Dian Zhuang descendants.

sentences.zh: 有稻、麥、粟、豆、絲、麻、薤、蒜、桃、李。

translations.literal: Had rice, wheat, millet, beans, silk, hemp, scallion, garlic, peach, plum.
translations.idiomatic: Rice, wheat, millet, beans, silk, hemp, produce.

sentences.zh: 以十二月為歲首。

translations.literal: Twelfth month New Year.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month New Year.

sentences.zh: 布幅廣七寸。

translations.literal: Cloth width seven cun.
translations.idiomatic: Cloth seven cun wide.

sentences.zh: 正月蠶生，二月熟。

translations.literal: First month silkworms born; second ripe.
translations.idiomatic: Silkworms first month; second ripe.

sentences.zh: 男子氈革為帔，女衣迤布裙衫，髻盤如髽。

translations.literal: Men felt and leather capes; women cloth skirts; topknot like men's.
translations.idiomatic: Men felt capes; women cloth skirts; topknots.

sentences.zh: 飯用竹筲摶而啖之，烏杯貯羹如雞彜。

translations.literal: Rice in bamboo tubes eaten; owl cups for soup like chicken vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Rice in bamboo tubes; owl cups for soup.

sentences.zh: 徒跣，有舟無車。

translations.literal: Barefoot; boats no carts.
translations.idiomatic: Barefoot; boats not carts.

sentences.zh: 死則坎地，殯舍左，屋之，三年乃葬，以蠡蚌封棺。

translations.literal: Death pit burial; coffin left of house three years then bury; clam shell sealed coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Pit burial; house three years; clam shell coffin.

sentences.zh: 父母喪，斬衰布衣不澡者四五年，近者二三年。

translations.literal: Parent mourning hemp unbathed four-five years; near two-three.
translations.idiomatic: Parent mourning hemp unbathed years.

sentences.zh: 為人所殺者，子以麻括發，墨面，衣不緝。

translations.literal: Murdered—son hemp bound hair, ink face, unhemmed clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Murdered—son ink face, unhemmed clothes.

sentences.zh: 居喪，昏嫁不廢，亦弗避同姓。

translations.literal: Mourning marriage not stopped; no avoiding same surname.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning marriage not stopped.

sentences.zh: 婿不親迎。

translations.literal: Son-in-law did not fetch bride.
translations.idiomatic: Son-in-law did not fetch bride.

sentences.zh: 富室娶妻，納金銀牛羊酒，女所賫亦如之。

translations.literal: Rich marrying gave gold silver cattle wine; bride dowry likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Rich marriage gold silver cattle wine both sides.

sentences.zh: 有罪者，樹一長木，擊鼓集眾其下。

translations.literal: Guilty—long wood planted; drum gathered masses below.
translations.idiomatic: Guilty—long wood; drum gathered masses.

sentences.zh: 強盜殺之，富者貰死，燒屋奪其田；

translations.literal: Robbers killed; rich ransomed death, house burned land seized;
translations.idiomatic: Robbers killed; rich ransomed; house burned;

sentences.zh: 盜者倍九而償贓。

translations.literal: thieves repay ninefold.
translations.idiomatic: thieves repay ninefold.

sentences.zh: 奸淫，則強族輸金銀請和而棄其妻，處女、厘婦不坐。

translations.literal: Adultery—powerful clan paid gold silver reconcile abandoning wife; virgins widows not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Adultery—clan paid reconcile; virgins widows exempt.

sentences.zh: 凡相殺必報，力不能則其部助攻之。

translations.literal: Mutual killing must be avenged; if weak tribe helped attack.
translations.idiomatic: Killing must be avenged; weak tribes helped.

sentences.zh: 祭祀，殺牛馬，親聯畢會，助以牛酒，多至數百人。

translations.literal: Sacrifice killed cattle horses; kin all gathered aiding cattle wine hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice cattle horses; kin hundreds gathered.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，巂州都督劉伯英上疏：「松外諸蠻，率暫附亟叛，請擊之，西洱河天竺道可通也。」

translations.literal: During the Zhenguan reign, Liu Boying, Governor of Xizhou, submitted a memorial: "The various Man beyond Song generally submit briefly and then quickly rebel. Please attack them, and the road from the Xi'er River to India can be opened."
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign, Liu Boying, Governor of Xizhou, submitted a memorial: "The various Man beyond Song generally submit briefly and then quickly rebel. Please attack them, and the road from the Xi'er River to India can be opened."

sentences.zh: 居數歲，太宗以右武候將軍梁建方發蜀十二州兵進討，酋帥雙舍拒戰，敗走，殺獲十餘。

translations.literal: Years later Taizong sent Right Wuwei General Liang Jianfang Sichuan twelve prefecture troops; chieftain Shuangshe resisted; defeated fled; over ten killed captured.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Jianfang twelve prefecture troops; Shuangshe defeated.

sentences.zh: 群蠻震駭，走保山谷。

translations.literal: Tribes terrified fled valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes fled valleys.

sentences.zh: 建方諭降者七十餘部，戶十萬九千，署首領蒙、和為縣令，餘眾感悅。

translations.literal: Jianfang persuaded over seventy tribes surrender; one hundred nine thousand households; chieftains Meng, He county magistrates; masses grateful.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy tribes surrendered; 109,000 households; Meng, He magistrates.

sentences.zh: 西洱河蠻西洱河蠻，亦曰河蠻，道繇郎州走三千里，建方遣奇兵自巂州道千五百里掩之，其帥楊盛大駭，欲遁去，使者好語約降，乃遣首領十人納款軍門，建方振旅還。

translations.literal: Western Er River Barbarians, also River Barbarians: route from Lang Prefecture three thousand li; Jianfang sent elite from Xie three thousand five hundred li to strike; chief Yang Shengdah terrified wished flee; envoy kind words agreed surrender; sent ten chieftains submit at gate; Jianfang withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Western Er River Barbarians: Jianfang struck; Yang Shengdah surrendered; ten chieftains submitted.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，西洱河大首領楊同外、東洱河大首領楊斂、松外首領蒙羽皆入朝，授官袟。

translations.literal: Twenty-second year Western Er great chieftain Yang Tongwai, Eastern Er Yang Lian, Songwai Meng Yu all came; granted seals.
translations.idiomatic: Year 22 Yang Tongwai, Yang Lian, Meng Yu came; granted seals.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年，西洱河大首領楊棟附顯、和蠻大首領王羅祁、郎昆梨盤四州大首領王伽沖率部落四千人歸附，入朝貢方物。

translations.literal: Xianqing first year Western Er Yang Dongfu, He Man Wang Luoqi, Lang Kun Lijian four prefecture chiefs Wang Jiaochong led four thousand tribes submit tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Xianqing 1 four chiefs led four thousand tribes submit.

sentences.zh: 其後茂州西南築安戎城，絕吐蕃通蠻之道。

translations.literal: Later Maozhou southwest built Anrong City cutting Tibet-barbarian road.
translations.idiomatic: Anrong City built cutting Tibet-barbarian road.

sentences.zh: 生羌為吐蕃向導，攻拔之，增兵以守，西洱河諸蠻皆臣吐蕃。

translations.literal: Raw Qiang guided Tibet taking it; increased garrison; Western Er tribes all submitted Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Raw Qiang guided Tibet; Western Er submitted Tibet.

sentences.zh: 開元中，首領始入朝，授刺史。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan chieftains first came; appointed prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan chieftains appointed prefects.

sentences.zh: 會南詔蒙歸義拔大和城，乃北徙，更羈制於浪穹詔。

translations.literal: When Nanzhao Meng Guiyi took Dahe City they moved north, again coming under Langqiong zhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanzhao took Dahe they moved north under Langqiong.

sentences.zh: 浪穹詔已破，又徙雲南柘城。

translations.literal: Langqiong zhao already broken, they again moved to Yunnan Zhe City.
translations.idiomatic: Langqiong broken, they moved to Yunnan Zhe City.

sentences.zh: 黎州黎州，領羈縻奉上等州二十六。

translations.literal: Li Prefecture governed twenty-six jimi Feng, Shang and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Li Prefecture twenty-six jimi prefectures.

sentences.zh: 開元十七年，又領羈縻夏梁、卜貴等州三十一。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan seventeenth year also thirty-one Xia, Liang, Bu and others.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan 17 also thirty-one prefectures.

sentences.zh: 南路有廓清道部落主三人，婆鹽鬼主十人。

translations.literal: South road Kuqing road three tribal lords, ten Poyan ghost masters.
translations.idiomatic: South road three lords, ten ghost masters.

sentences.zh: 又有阿逼蠻分十四部落：一曰大龍池，二曰小龍池，三曰控，四曰苴質，五曰烏披，六曰苴賃，七曰觱篥水，八曰戎列，九曰婆狄，十曰石地，十一曰羅公，十二曰𧧯，十三曰離旻，十四曰裏漢。

translations.literal: Also the Abi Man were divided into fourteen tribes: first Dalongchi, second Xiaolongchi, third Kong, fourth Juzhi, fifth Wupo, sixth Juzhen, seventh Bili River, eighth Ronglie, ninth Bodi, tenth Shidi, eleventh Luogong, twelfth ?, thirteenth Limin, fourteenth Lihan.
translations.idiomatic: The Abi Man comprised fourteen tribes: Dalongchi, Xiaolongchi, Kong, Juzhi, Wupo, Juzhen, Bili River, Ronglie, Bodi, Shidi, Luogong, Limin, Lihan, and one more.

sentences.zh: 三王部落黎、邛二州之東，又有淩蠻。

translations.literal: Three Kings tribe east of Li, Qiong; also Ling barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Three Kings east of Li, Qiong; Ling barbarians.

sentences.zh: 西有三王蠻，蓋莋都夷白馬氏之遺種。

translations.literal: West Three Kings—Zhuodu Yi White Horse clan remnant.
translations.idiomatic: Three Kings Zhuodu Yi White Horse remnant.

sentences.zh: 楊、劉、郝三姓世為長，襲封王，謂之「三王」部落。

translations.literal: The Yang, Liu, and Hao surnames had hereditary chiefs and inherited royal enfeoffment; they were called the "Three Kings" tribes.
translations.idiomatic: The Yang, Liu, and Hao surnames had hereditary chiefs and inherited royal enfeoffment; they were called the "Three Kings" tribes.

sentences.zh: 疊甓而居，號舍。

translations.literal: Stacked tiles dwelling called she.
translations.idiomatic: Stacked tile dwellings called she.

sentences.zh: 歲稟節度府帛三千匹，以诇南詔，而南詔亦密賂之，覘成都虛實。

translations.literal: Yearly three thousand bolts silk from circuit for spying Nanzhao; Nanzhao also bribed observing Chengdu strength.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand bolts yearly spying Nanzhao; Nanzhao bribed back.

sentences.zh: 每節度使至，酋長來謁，節度使多奏威惠所懷，以罔天子也。

translations.literal: Each jiedushi arrival chiefs audience; jiedushi memorialized favor deceiving Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Jiedushi memorialized favor deceiving emperor.

sentences.zh: 前謁必請於都押衙，且聽命，都押衙不令者，輒諷其叛，常倚三王部落求姑息，至唐末益甚。

translations.literal: Prior audience requested chief guard permission; Three Kings often blackmailed for indulgence; late Tang worse.
translations.idiomatic: Three Kings blackmailed for indulgence; late Tang worse.

sentences.zh: 諸蠻雅州西有通吐蕃道三：曰夏陽、曰夔松、曰始陽，皆諸蠻錯居。

translations.literal: Ya Prefecture west three Tibet roads: Xiayang, Kuison, Shiyang—all tribes mixed.
translations.idiomatic: Ya west three Tibet roads; tribes mixed.

sentences.zh: 凡部落四十六：距州三百餘里之外有百坡、當品、嚴城、中川、鉗矣、昌逼、鉗井七部落，四百餘里之外有羅巖、當馬、三井、束鋒、名耶、鉗恭、畫重、羅林、籠羊、林波、林燒、龍逢、索古、敢川、驚川、禍眉、不燭十七部落，五百餘里之外有諾祚、三恭、布嵐、欠馬、論川、讓川、遠南、卑廬、夔龍、曜川、金川、東嘉梁、西嘉梁十三部落，六百餘里之外有椎梅、作重、禍林、金林、邏蓬五部落，皆羈縻州也。

translations.literal: Forty-six tribes in all: beyond three hundred li from the prefecture were seven tribes—Baipo, Dangpin, Yancheng, Zhongchuan, Qianyi, Changbi, and Qianjing; beyond four hundred li were seventeen tribes including Luoyan, Dangma, Sanjing, Shufeng, Mingye, Qiangong, Huazhong, Luolin, Longyang, Linbo, Linshao, Longfeng, Sogu, Ganchuan, Jingchuan, Huomei, and Buzhu; beyond five hundred li were thirteen tribes including Nuozuo, Sangong, Bulan, Qianma, Lunchuan, Rangchuan, Yuannan, Beilu, Kuilong, Yaochuan, Jinchuan, Dongjialiang, and Xijialiang; beyond six hundred li were five tribes—Zhuimei, Zuozhong, Huolin, Jinlin, and Luopeng—all jimi prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-six tribes in all: within three hundred li stood seven; within four hundred li seventeen; within five hundred li thirteen; within six hundred li five—all registered as jimi prefectures.

sentences.zh: 以首領襲刺史。

translations.literal: Chieftains inherited prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Chieftains inherited prefect.

sentences.zh: 六姓蠻巂州新安城傍有六姓蠻：一曰蒙蠻、二曰夷蠻、三曰訛蠻、四曰狼蠻，餘勿鄧及白蠻也。

translations.literal: Six Surname barbarians beside Xin'an City: Meng, Yi, E, Lang; rest Wudeng and White.
translations.idiomatic: Six Surname beside Xin'an: Meng, Yi, E, Lang.

sentences.zh: 戎州管內有馴、騁、浪三州大鬼主董嘉慶，累世內附，以忠謹稱，封歸義郡王。

translations.literal: Rong Prefecture Xun, Cheng, Lang three prefecture great ghost master Dong Jiaqing generations internal, loyal, enfeoffed Guiyi Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jiaqing loyal generations; Guiyi Prince.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，狼蠻亦請內附，補首領浪沙為刺史，然卒不出，劍南西川節度使韋臯檄嘉慶兼押狼蠻。

translations.literal: During the Zhenyuan reign, the Lang barbarians also requested to submit. Their chief Langsha was appointed prefect, but in the end he never came out; Wei Gao, Military Governor of Jiannan Xichuan, sent a directive ordering Jiaqing also to supervise the Lang barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenyuan reign, the Lang barbarians also requested to submit. Their chief Langsha was appointed prefect, but in the end he never came out; Wei Gao, Military Governor of Jiannan Xichuan, sent a directive ordering Jiaqing also to supervise the Lang barbarians.

sentences.zh: 又有魯望等部落，徙居戎州馬鞍山，臯以其遠邊僥，戶給米二斛、鹽五斤。

translations.literal: Also Luwang tribes moved Rong Ma'an Mountain; Gao because remote gave two dou rice five jin salt.
translations.idiomatic: Luwang moved Ma'an; Gao gave rice salt.

sentences.zh: 北又有浪稽蠻、羅哥谷蠻。

translations.literal: North Langji, Luogegu.
translations.idiomatic: North Langji, Luogegu.

sentences.zh: 東有婆秋蠻、烏皮蠻。

translations.literal: East Poqiu, Wupi.
translations.idiomatic: East Poqiu, Wupi.

sentences.zh: 南有離東蠻、鍋銼蠻。

translations.literal: South Lidong, Guosuo.
translations.idiomatic: South Lidong, Guosuo.

sentences.zh: 西有磨些蠻，與南詔、越析相姻婭。

translations.literal: West Mosuo—intermarried Nanzhao, Yuexi.
translations.idiomatic: West Mosuo intermarried Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 自浪稽以下，古滇王、哀牢雜種，其地與吐蕃接。

translations.literal: Below Langji ancient Dian King Ailao mixed; land borders Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Below Langji Dian Ailao mixed; borders Tibet.

sentences.zh: 亦有姐羌，古白馬氐之裔。

translations.literal: Also Jie Qiang ancient White Horse Di remnant.
translations.idiomatic: There were also the Jie Qiang, descendants of the ancient White Horse Di.

sentences.zh: 部落劍山當吐蕃大路，屬石門、柳強三鎮，置戍、守捉，以招討使領五部落：一曰彌羌、二曰鑠羌、三曰胡叢，其餘東欽、磨些也。

translations.literal: Tribes Jianshan on Tibet main road; Shimen, Liuqiang three garrisons; pacification commissioner five tribes: Miqang, Shuogiang, Hucong; rest Dongqin, Mosuo.
translations.idiomatic: The Jianshan tribe lay on the main road to Tibet and belonged to the three garrisons of Shimen and Liuqiang. Garrisons and guard-posts were established there, and a pacification commissioner supervised five tribes: first Mi Qiang, second Shuo Qiang, third Hucong, with Dongqin and Moxie as the remaining two.

sentences.zh: 又有夷望、鼓路、西望、安樂、湯谷、佛蠻、虧野、阿益、阿鶚、蠻、林井、阿異十二鬼主皆隸巂州。

translations.literal: Also Yiwang, Gulu, Xiwang, Anle, Tanggu, Foman, Kuiye, Ayi, A'e twelve ghost masters all under Xie.
translations.idiomatic: There were also twelve ghost-masters, Yiwang, Gulu, Xiwang, Anle, Tanggu, Foman, Kuiye, Ayi (阿益), A'e, Man, Linjing, and Ayi (阿異), all under Xie Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又有奉國、苴伽十一部落，春秋受賞於巂州，然挾吐蕃為輕重。

translations.literal: Also Fengguo, Juga eleven tribes spring rewards Xie; yet leveraged Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven tribes spring rewards; leveraged Tibet.

sentences.zh: 每節度使至，諸部獻馬，酋長衣虎皮，餘皆紅巾束發，錦纈襖、半臂。

translations.literal: Each jiedushi arrival tribes presented horses; chiefs tiger skin; rest red turban topknot brocade jacket half-sleeve.
translations.idiomatic: Jiedushi arrival horses; chiefs tiger skin.

sentences.zh: 既見，請匹錦、鬥酒，折草招父祖魂以歸鄉里。

translations.literal: After audience requested bolt silk cup wine; broke grass summoned ancestors return home.
translations.idiomatic: Requested silk wine; summoned ancestors.

sentences.zh: 及還，裹錦植馬上而去。

translations.literal: Returning wrapped silk on horse.
translations.idiomatic: Returned silk on horse.

sentences.zh: 又有顯養、東魯諸蠻，永徽三年與胡叢皆叛。

translations.literal: Also Xianyang, Donglu rebelled Yonghui third year with Hucong.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyang, Donglu rebelled Yonghui 3.

sentences.zh: 高宗以右驍衛將軍曹繼叔為巂州道行軍總管，戰斜山，拔十餘城，斬首七百，獲馬、犛牛萬五千。

translations.literal: Gaozong Right Xiaowei Cao Jishu Xie marching commander battled Xieshan took over ten cities beheaded seven hundred captured horses yaks fifteen thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jishu took ten cities; 700 heads; 15,000 cattle.

sentences.zh: 永昌蠻姚州境有永昌蠻，居古永昌郡地。

translations.literal: In Yaozhou territory there were Yongchang Barbarians, dwelling on the land of the ancient Yongchang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongchang Barbarians of Yaozhou lived on the old Yongchang commandery lands.

sentences.zh: 咸亨五年叛，高宗以太子右衛副率梁積壽為姚州道行軍總管討平之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianheng they rebelled; Gaozong made Deputy Commander of the Right Guard of the Heir Apparent Liang Jishou Military Commander of the Yaozhou Circuit to campaign and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: They rebelled in Xianheng 5; Gaozong appointed Liang Jishou commander on the Yaozhou route and put the revolt down.

sentences.zh: 武後天授中，遣御史裴懷古招懷。

translations.literal: During Empress Wu's Tian-shou era, dispatched Censor Pei Huaigu to summon and embrace them.
translations.idiomatic: During Empress Wu's Tian-shou reign she sent censor Pei Huaigu to win them over.

sentences.zh: 至長壽時，大首領董期率部落二萬內屬。

translations.literal: By the Changshou era, great chieftain Dong Qi led twenty thousand of the tribes to submit inwardly.
translations.idiomatic: By the Changshou era great chief Dong Qi led twenty thousand tribesmen into submission.

sentences.zh: 其西有撲子蠻，趫悍，以青娑羅為通身褲，善用竹弓，入林射飛鼠無不中。

translations.literal: West of them were the Puzi Man, fierce and swift, using blue sura cloth for whole-body trousers, skilled with bamboo bows—in the forest shooting flying squirrels without missing.
translations.idiomatic: To their west lived the fierce Puzi Man, who wore blue sura trousers, carried bamboo bows, and never missed a flying squirrel in the woods.

sentences.zh: 無食器，以蕉葉藉之。

translations.literal: They had no food vessels; they used banana leaves as plates.
translations.idiomatic: They ate from banana leaves instead of bowls.

sentences.zh: 人多長大，負排持槊而鬥。

translations.literal: The people were mostly tall and large, carrying pike-shields and spears to fight.
translations.idiomatic: They were a tall people who fought with pike-shields and spears.

sentences.zh: 又有望蠻者，用木弓短箭，鏃傅毒藥，中者立死。

translations.literal: Again there were the Wang Man, using wooden bows and short arrows with poison on the tips—a hit meant instant death.
translations.idiomatic: The Wang Man used wooden bows and poisoned short arrows that killed on contact.

sentences.zh: 婦人食乳酪，肥白，跣足；

translations.literal: Women ate dairy, grew plump and fair, and went barefoot;
translations.idiomatic: Women ate dairy, grew plump and fair-skinned, and went barefoot;

sentences.zh: 青布為衫裳，聯貫珂貝珠絡之；

translations.literal: blue cloth for shirts and skirts, strung together with cowrie shells and pearls;
translations.idiomatic: they wore blue shirts and skirts laced with cowries and pearls;

sentences.zh: 髻垂於後，有夫者分兩髻。

translations.literal: topknots hanging behind; married women wore two topknots.
translations.idiomatic: their hair hung in topknots behind, and married women wore two.

sentences.zh: 群蠻群蠻種類，多不可記。

translations.literal: The Group Man—the kinds of Group Man were too many to record.
translations.idiomatic: The Group Man comprised countless varieties.

sentences.zh: 有黑齒、金齒、銀齒三種，見人以漆及鏤金銀飾齒，寢食則去之。

translations.literal: There were Black Teeth, Gold Teeth, and Silver Teeth three kinds—seeing people lacquer and inlay gold and silver on teeth; they removed them for sleeping and eating.
translations.idiomatic: Three groups—the Black, Gold, and Silver Teeth—lacquered or inlaid their teeth like the Chinese but removed the ornaments to eat and sleep.

sentences.zh: 直頂為髻，青布為通褲。

translations.literal: They wore straight topknots and blue whole trousers.
translations.idiomatic: They bound their hair in straight topknots and wore blue trousers.

sentences.zh: 有繡腳種，刻踝至腓為文。

translations.literal: The Embroidered Foot kind carved patterns from ankle to shin.
translations.idiomatic: The Embroidered Foot tattooed their ankles to their shins.

sentences.zh: 有繡面種，生逾月，涅黛於面。

translations.literal: The Embroidered Face kind—past one month of life, indigo dye on the face.
translations.idiomatic: The Embroidered Face stained infants' faces with indigo after the first month.

sentences.zh: 有雕題種，身面涅黛。

translations.literal: The Tattoo Face kind dyed body and face indigo.
translations.idiomatic: The Tattoo Face dyed their entire bodies and faces indigo.

sentences.zh: 有穿鼻種，以金環徑尺貫其鼻，下垂過頤。

translations.literal: The Pierced Nose kind wore a gold ring a foot across through the nose, hanging down past the chin.
translations.idiomatic: The Pierced Nose wore foot-wide gold rings through the nose down to the chin.

sentences.zh: 君長以絲系環，人牽乃行。

translations.literal: The lord tied the ring with silk; a man had to lead him before he could walk.
translations.idiomatic: A chief's nose ring was tied with silk and led like a halter.

sentences.zh: 其次，以二花頭金釘貫鼻下出。

translations.literal: Next in rank, two flower-head gold nails pierced below the nose.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser men wore two flower-shaped gold studs below the nose.

sentences.zh: 又有長鬃種、棟鋒種，皆額前為長髻，下過臍，行以物舉之；

translations.literal: Again there were the Long Mane and Dongfeng kinds—all wore long topknots before the forehead past the navel, walking with an object lifting it;
translations.idiomatic: The Long Mane and Dongfeng wore foretopknots that hung past the navel and had to be carried when they walked;

sentences.zh: 君長則二女在前共舉其髻乃行。

translations.literal: the lord had two women before jointly lifting his topknot then walk.
translations.idiomatic: a chief was preceded by two women who held up his hair.

sentences.zh: 生蠻林睹符部落安南有生蠻林睹符部落，大歷中置德化州，戶一萬。

translations.literal: Raw Man Lindufu tribe—in Annam there was the raw Man Lindufu tribe; in Dali established Dehua prefecture, ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Annam's raw-Man Lindufu tribe was organized as Dehua prefecture in the Dali era, with ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 又以潘歸國部落置龍武州，戶千五百。

translations.literal: Again established Longwu prefecture from the Pan Guiguo tribe, fifteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: The Pan Guiguo tribe was made into Longwu prefecture, with fifteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 詔安南節度使綏定之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Annan military governor to pacify and settle them.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the Annan military governor to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 貞元七年，始以、峰二州為都督府。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenyuan, Ai and Feng two prefectures were first made a governor-general's office.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 7 Ai and Feng prefectures were combined into a governor-general's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 在安南，限重海，與文單、占婆接。

translations.literal: In Annam, bounded by the heavy sea, it adjoined Wendan and Zhanpo.
translations.idiomatic: Annam faced the open sea and bordered Wendan and Champa.

sentences.zh: 峰統羈縻州十八，與蜀爨蠻接。

translations.literal: Feng commanded eighteen jimi prefectures and bordered the Shu Cuan Man.
translations.idiomatic: Feng oversaw eighteen jimi prefectures and adjoined the Cuan Man of Shu.

sentences.zh: 南平獠南平獠，東距智州，南屬渝州，西接南州，北涪州，戶四千餘。

translations.literal: Nanping Liao—east bordering Zhizhou, south subordinate to Yuzhou, west connecting Nan prefecture, north Fuzhou, more than four thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanping Liao lay east of Zhizhou, south under Yuzhou, west of Nan prefecture, and north of Fuzhou, with more than four thousand households.

sentences.zh: 多瘴癘。

translations.literal: There was much miasma and pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: The land was rife with miasma and pestilence.

sentences.zh: 山有毒草、沙虱、蝮虵。

translations.literal: The mountains had poisonous grass, sand fleas, and vipers.
translations.idiomatic: Poisonous plants, sand fleas, and vipers infested the hills.

sentences.zh: 人樓居，梯而上，名為幹欄。

translations.literal: People lived in tower houses, climbing ladders to enter—called ganlan.
translations.idiomatic: They lived in stilted tower houses reached by ladder, called ganlan.

sentences.zh: 婦人橫布二幅，穿中貫其首，號曰通裙。

translations.literal: Women wore two horizontal cloth panels pierced through the head at the center, called pass skirts.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore pass skirts—two cloth panels threaded over the head.

sentences.zh: 美發髻，垂於後。

translations.literal: They wore beautiful topknots hanging behind.
translations.idiomatic: Their hair was dressed in handsome topknots that hung behind.

sentences.zh: 竹筒三寸，斜穿其耳，貴者飾以珠珰。

translations.literal: Bamboo tubes three cun long were slanted through the ears; nobles adorned them with pearl pendants.
translations.idiomatic: They pierced their ears with three-inch bamboo tubes; nobles hung pearls from them.

sentences.zh: 俗女多男少，婦人任役。

translations.literal: Customarily there were many women and few men; women bore the corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Women outnumbered men, and women performed the labor.

sentences.zh: 昏法，女先以貨求男。

translations.literal: By marriage custom the woman first brought goods to seek a man.
translations.idiomatic: In marriage the woman paid bride-price to win a husband.

sentences.zh: 貧者無以嫁，則賣為婢。

translations.literal: Those too poor to marry were sold as maids.
translations.idiomatic: Poor families sold daughters as bondmaids when they could not marry.

sentences.zh: 男子左衽，露發，徒跣。

translations.literal: Men wore left-lapelled robes, bare heads, and went barefoot.
translations.idiomatic: Men left-lapped their robes, went bareheaded, and barefoot.

sentences.zh: 其王姓朱氏，號劍荔王。

translations.literal: Their king was surnamed Zhu and styled Sword Lychee King.
translations.idiomatic: Their king belonged to the Zhu clan and was called the Sword Lychee King.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，遣使內款，以其地隸渝州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan they sent envoys to submit; their land was placed under Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 3 they sent envoys to submit, and their territory was placed under Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 有飛頭獠者，頭欲飛，周項有痕如縷，妻子共守之。

translations.literal: There were Flying Head Liao whose heads seemed about to fly; around the neck was a line like a thread, and wife and children together guarded them.
translations.idiomatic: Some Flying Head Liao bore a threadlike scar around the neck; wives and children had to guard them at night.

sentences.zh: 及夜如病，頭忽亡，比旦還。

translations.literal: At night they seemed ill; the head suddenly vanished, and by dawn it returned.
translations.idiomatic: At night they fell ill, their heads detached and flew away, and returned by dawn.

sentences.zh: 又有烏武獠，地多瘴毒，中者不能飲藥，故自鑿齒。

translations.literal: Again there were Black Teeth Liao; the land had much miasma poison, and those stricken could not take medicine, so they filed their own teeth.
translations.idiomatic: The Black Teeth Liao lived where miasma made medicines useless, so they filed their teeth themselves.

sentences.zh: 有寧氏，世為南平渠帥。

translations.literal: There was the Ning clan, generation after generation channel chieftains of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: The Ning clan had served for generations as Nanping chieftains.

sentences.zh: 陳末，以其帥猛力為寧越太守。

translations.literal: At the end of Chen, their chieftain Mengli was made prefect of Ningyue.
translations.idiomatic: At the fall of Chen their chief Mengli was appointed prefect of Ningyue.

sentences.zh: 陳亡，自以為與陳叔寶同日而生，當代為天子，乃不入朝。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, he believed himself born on the same day as Chen Shubao and destined to replace him as Son of Heaven, and therefore would not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen fell he claimed the same birthday as Chen Shubao and refused court because he believed himself the rightful emperor.

sentences.zh: 隋兵阻瘴，不能進。

translations.literal: Sui troops were blocked by miasma and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Sui armies were halted by miasma and could not push forward.

sentences.zh: 猛力死，子長真襲刺史。

translations.literal: Mengli died; his son Changzhen inherited the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Mengli died his son Changzhen succeeded as prefect.

sentences.zh: 及討林邑，長真出兵攻其後，又率部落數千從征遼東，煬帝召為鴻臚卿，授安撫大使，遣還。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Linyi, Changzhen dispatched troops to attack from the rear; he also led several thousand tribesmen on the Liaodong campaign; Yangdi summoned him as Director of the Court of State Ceremonial, granted him the title of pacification envoy, and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhen sent troops against Linyi's rear and later led thousands of tribesmen to Liaodong; Emperor Yang made him Director of the Court of State Ceremonial and pacification envoy, then sent him home.

sentences.zh: 又以其族人寧宣為合浦太守。

translations.literal: Also made clansman Ning Xuan prefect of Hepu.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Ning Xuan was made prefect of Hepu.

sentences.zh: 隋亂，皆以地附蕭銑。

translations.literal: During the Sui turmoil they all submitted their lands to Xiao Xian.
translations.idiomatic: In the Sui collapse they all submitted their territories to Xiao Xian.

sentences.zh: 長真，部越兵攻丘和於交阯者也，武德初，以寧越、郁林之地降，自是交、愛數州始通。

translations.literal: Changzhen was the man who had led Yue troops against Qiu He at Jiaozhi; at the beginning of Wude he surrendered with the lands of Ningyue and Yulin, and from then Jiao, Ai, and several prefectures were first opened.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhen—the Yue commander who had attacked Qiu He at Jiaozhi—surrendered Ningyue and Yulin in early Wude, opening Jiao, Ai, and neighboring prefectures to the court.

sentences.zh: 高祖授長真欽州都督。

translations.literal: Gaozu appointed Changzhen Area Commander of Qin prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu made Changzhen area commander of Qin prefecture.

sentences.zh: 寧宣亦遣使請降，未報而卒。

translations.literal: Ning Xuan also sent envoys requesting surrender, but died before a reply arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Ning Xuan too sought to surrender but died before the court answered.

sentences.zh: 以其子純為廉州刺史，族人道明為南越州刺史。

translations.literal: Changzhen's son Chun was made prefect of Lian prefecture; clansman Daoming was made prefect of Nanyue prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhen's son Chun became prefect of Lian; kinsman Daoming became prefect of Nanyue.

sentences.zh: 六年，長真獻大珠，昆州刺史沈遜、融州刺史歐陽世普、象州刺史秦元覽亦獻筒布，高祖以道遠勞人，皆不受。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Changzhen presented a great pearl; Kun prefect Shen Xun, Rong prefect Ouyang Shipu, and Xiang prefect Qin Yuanlan also presented tube cloth; Gaozu, because the road was distant and laborious for the people, refused all.
translations.idiomatic: In year six Changzhen sent a great pearl; prefects Shen Xun, Ouyang Shipu, and Qin Yuanlan sent tube cloth as well, but Gaozu refused every gift lest distant tribute burden the people.

sentences.zh: 道明與高州首領馮暄、談殿據南越州反，攻姜州，寧純以兵援之。

translations.literal: Daoming with Gaozhou chieftains Feng Xuan and Tan Dian seized Nanyue prefecture and rebelled, attacking Jiang prefecture; Ning Chun came with troops to aid.
translations.idiomatic: Daoming joined Gaozhou chiefs Feng Xuan and Tan Dian in seizing Nanyue prefecture, attacked Jiang prefecture, and was opposed by Ning Chun's troops.

sentences.zh: 八年，長真陷封山縣，昌州刺史龐孝恭掎擊暄等走之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Changzhen captured Fengshan county; Changzhou prefect Pang Xiaogong struck from the flank and drove Feng Xuan and the others off.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight Changzhen took Fengshan county; Pang Xiaogong of Changzhou flanked Feng Xuan's force and drove them away.

sentences.zh: 明年，道明為州人所殺。

translations.literal: The next year Daoming was killed by the people of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the prefectural people killed Daoming.

sentences.zh: 未幾，長真死，子據襲刺史。

translations.literal: Before long, Changzhen died; his son Ju succeeded to the post of prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Changzhen died, and his son Ju inherited the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 馮暄、談殿阻兵相掠，群臣請擊之，太宗不許，遣員外散騎常侍韋叔諧、員外散騎侍郎李公淹持節宣諭。

translations.literal: Feng Xuan and Tan Dian blocked troops and plundered each other; the ministers requested an attack; Taizong refused, sending Supernumerary Attendant-at-Large Wei Shuxie and Supernumerary Attendant Gentleman Li Gongyan with credentials to proclaim and instruct.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng Xuan and Tan Dian raised armed bands and preyed on one another, the court urged a punitive campaign, but Taizong refused and instead sent Wei Shuxie and Li Gongyan with imperial credentials to announce the throne's will.

sentences.zh: 暄等與溪洞首領皆降，南方遂定。

translations.literal: Xuan and the others together with the stream-cave chieftains all surrendered; the south was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and the stream-cave chiefs all submitted, and the south was pacified.

sentences.zh: 大抵劍南諸獠，武德、貞觀間數寇暴州縣者不一。

translations.literal: Generally speaking, the various Liao of Jiannan during Wude and Zhenguan repeatedly raided and ravaged the prefectures and counties—not just once.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking, the Liao peoples of Jiannan raided and terrorized the prefectures time and again throughout the Wude and Zhenguan reigns.

sentences.zh: 巴州山獠王多馨叛，梁州都督龐玉梟其首，又破餘黨符陽、白石二縣獠。

translations.literal: Wang Duoxin of the Ba prefecture mountain Liao rebelled; Liangzhou Area Commander Pang Yu displayed his head, and again broke the remnant factions—the Liao of Fuyang and Baishi two counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duoxin of the Ba prefecture mountain Liao rose in revolt; the Liangzhou area commander Pang Yu took his head and crushed the holdouts among the Liao of Fuyang and Baishi counties.

sentences.zh: 其後眉州獠反，益州行臺郭行方大破之。

translations.literal: After this the Meizhou Liao rebelled; the Yizhou mobile headquarters Guo Xingfang greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Meizhou Liao rebelled and were routed by Guo Xingfang of the Yizhou field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又破洪、雅二州獠，俘男女五千口。

translations.literal: Before long, again defeated the Liao of Hong and Ya two prefectures, capturing five thousand persons male and female.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he also defeated the Liao of Hong and Ya, taking five thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 是歲，益州獠亦反，都督竇軌請擊之，太宗報曰：「獠依山險，當附以恩信。

translations.literal: That year the Yizhou Liao also rebelled; Area Commander Dou Gui requested to strike them; Taizong replied: "The Liao rely on mountain passes and peril—one should attach them with grace and trust.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the Yizhou Liao also rose; area commander Dou Gui asked leave to attack them, but Taizong answered: "The Liao hold the high mountains—win them with kindness and fidelity.

sentences.zh: 脅之以兵威，豈為人父母意耶？」

translations.literal: To threaten them with military might—is that the intent of one who is father and mother to the people?"
translations.idiomatic: To browbeat them with armies—is that how a ruler should treat his people?"

sentences.zh: 貞觀七年，東、西玉洞獠反，以右屯衛大將軍張士貴為龔州道行軍總管平之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenguan, the eastern and western Yudong Liao rebelled; Right General of the Right Garrison Guard Zhang Shigui was made Military Commander of the Gongzhou Circuit to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 7 the eastern and western Yudong Liao rebelled; Zhang Shigui, grand general of the Right Garrison Guard, was appointed circuit commander on the Gongzhou route and put the revolt down.

sentences.zh: 十二年，巫州獠叛，夔州都督齊善行擊破之，俘男女三千餘口。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Wuzhou Liao rebelled; Kuizhou Area Commander Qi Shanxing struck and broke them, capturing more than three thousand persons male and female.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 12 the Wuzhou Liao rebelled; Kuizhou area commander Qi Shanxing defeated them and took more than three thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 鈞州獠叛，桂州都督張寶德討平之。

translations.literal: Junzhou Liao rebelled; Guizhou Area Commander Zhang Baode suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Junzhou Liao rebelled, Guizhou area commander Zhang Baode quelled them.

sentences.zh: 明州山獠又叛，交州都督李道彥擊走之。

translations.literal: Mingzhou mountain Liao again rebelled; Jiaozhou Area Commander Li Daoyan struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: The Mingzhou mountain Liao rebelled again and were driven off by Jiaozhou area commander Li Daoyan.

sentences.zh: 是歲，巴、洋、集、壁四州山獠叛，攻巴州，遣右武候將軍上官懷仁破之於壁州，虜男女萬餘，明年遂平。

translations.literal: That year the mountain Liao of Ba, Yang, Ji, and Bi four prefectures rebelled, attacking Ba prefecture; Right Warrior Guard General Shangguan Huairen was sent to break them at Bi prefecture, capturing more than ten thousand male and female; the next year they were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: That year the mountain Liao of Ba, Yang, Ji, and Bi rose against Ba prefecture; Shangguan Huairen of the Right Warrior Guard routed them at Bi prefecture, taking more than ten thousand prisoners, and the region was quiet by the following year.

sentences.zh: 十四年，羅、竇諸獠叛，以廣州都督黨仁弘為竇州道行軍總管擊之，虜男女七千餘人。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, the various Liao of Luo and Dou rebelled; Guangzhou Area Commander Dang Renhong was made Military Commander of the Douzhou Circuit to strike them, capturing more than seven thousand male and female.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 14 the Liao of Luo and Dou rebelled; Guangzhou area commander Dang Renhong was put in charge of the Douzhou route and seized more than seven thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 太宗再伐高麗，為舡劍南，諸獠皆半役，雅、邛、眉三州獠不堪其擾，相率叛，詔發隴右、峽兵二萬，以茂州都督張士貴為雅州道行軍總管，與右衛將軍梁建方平之。
