translations.literal: Taizong again attacked Goguryeo, building ships in Jiannan; the various Liao all served at half-corvée; the Liao of Ya, Qiong, and Mei three prefectures could not endure the harassment and rebelled together; an edict ordered twenty thousand troops from Longyou and Xia; Mao prefecture Area Commander Zhang Shigui was made Military Commander of the Yazhou Circuit, together with Right Guard General Liang Jianfang pacifying them.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong launched his second campaign against Goguryeo and requisitioned shipwrights across Jiannan, every Liao community was pressed into half-corvée labor; the Liao of Ya, Qiong, and Mei could bear the burden no longer and rose together. The throne mobilized twenty thousand men from Longyou and the gorges, appointing Zhang Shigui of Maozhou as commander on the Yazhou route along with Right Guard general Liang Jianfang to restore order.

sentences.zh: 高宗初，琰州獠叛，梓州都督謝萬歲、充州刺史謝法興、黔州都督李孟嘗討之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Gaozong's reign, Yanzhou Liao rebelled; Zizhou Area Commander Xie Wansui, Chong prefecture Prefect Xie Faxing, and Qianzhou Area Commander Li Mengchang campaigned against them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Gaozong's reign the Yanzhou Liao rebelled; Xie Wansui of Zizhou, Xie Faxing of Chong prefecture, and Li Mengchang of Qianzhou marched against them.

sentences.zh: 萬歲、法興入洞招慰，遇害。

translations.literal: Wansui and Faxing entered the caves to summon and console; they met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Wansui and Faxing entered the cave settlements to negotiate and were killed.

sentences.zh: 顯慶三年，羅、竇生獠酋領多胡桑率眾內附。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianqing, the Luo and Dou raw Liao chieftain Duohusang led the masses to submit inwardly.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing 3 the raw-Liao chieftain Duohusang of Luo and Dou led his people in submission to the court.

sentences.zh: 上元末，納州獠叛，寇故茂、都掌二縣，殺吏民，焚廨舍，詔黔州都督發兵擊之。

translations.literal: At the end of Shangyuan, Nazhou Liao rebelled, raiding the former Mao and Duzhang two counties, killing officials and people, burning government offices; an edict ordered Qianzhou Area Commander to dispatch troops to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the Shangyuan era the Nazhou Liao rebelled, overrunning Mao and Duzhang counties, killing officials and civilians and burning yamen buildings; the throne ordered the Qianzhou area commander to send troops against them.

sentences.zh: 大歷二年，桂州山獠叛，陷州，刺史李良遁去。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dali, Guizhou mountain Liao rebelled, capturing the prefecture; Prefect Li Liang fled away.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 2 the Guizhou mountain Liao rebelled, seized the prefectural seat, and prefect Li Liang fled.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，嘉州綏山縣婆籠川生獠首領甫枳兄弟誘生蠻為亂，剽居人，西川節度使韋臯斬之，招其首領勇於等出降。

translations.literal: During Zhenyuan, Jia prefecture Suishan county Polongchuan raw Liao chieftains Fuzhi and his brothers enticed raw Man to make disorder, plundering residents; Western Sichuan Military Governor Wei Gao beheaded them, summoning their chieftains Yongyu and others to come out and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenyuan era the raw-Liao brothers Fuzhi of Polong River in Suishan county, Jia prefecture, incited the hill tribes to revolt and prey on settlers; Wei Gao, military governor of western Sichuan, executed them and called out chiefs such as Yongyu to surrender.

sentences.zh: 或請增柵東淩界以守，臯不從，曰：「無戎而城，害所生也。」

translations.literal: Some requested adding stockades at the Dongling frontier to defend; Gao did not follow, saying: "To wall without military necessity harms where people live."
translations.idiomatic: Some urged new palisades on the eastern Ling frontier, but Gao refused: "Building fortifications where there is no war only harms the people who live there."

sentences.zh: 獠亦自是不擾境。

translations.literal: The Liao from this also did not disturb the border.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Liao ceased to trouble the frontier.

sentences.zh: 戎、瀘間有葛獠，居依山谷林菁，逾數百里。

translations.literal: Between Rong and Lu there are Ge Liao, dwelling relying on mountain valleys and forest thickets, extending more than several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Between Rong and Lu lived the Ge Liao, scattered across mountain valleys and deep woods for hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 俗喜叛，州縣撫視不至，必合黨數千人，持排而戰。

translations.literal: Customarily fond of rebellion, when prefecture and county consolation and oversight did not reach them, they necessarily joined factions of several thousand men, holding pikes to battle.
translations.idiomatic: They were restless by nature: when county and prefectural oversight failed to reach them, they would rally thousands and fight with pikes.

sentences.zh: 奉酋帥為王，號曰「婆能」，出入前後植旗。

translations.literal: They enthroned a chieftain as king, styled him "Poneng," and when he went in or out, banners were planted before and behind him.
translations.idiomatic: They enthroned a chieftain as king, styled him "Poneng," and when he went in or out, banners were planted before and behind him.

sentences.zh: 大中末，昌、瀘二州刺史貪沓，以弱繒及羊強獠市，米麥一斛，得直不及半。

translations.literal: At the end of Dazhong, the two prefects of Chang and Lu were greedy and indolent, using inferior silk and sheep to force the Liao to trade; one hu of rice or wheat, the value obtained was not even half.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Dazhong era the prefects of Chang and Lu were grasping; they traded shoddy silk and sheep to the Liao on forced terms, paying less than half the fair price for a bushel of grain.

sentences.zh: 群獠訴曰：「當為賊取死耳！」

translations.literal: The mass of Liao complained, saying: "We ought to become bandits and die fighting!"
translations.idiomatic: The Liao cried out: "We may as well die as brigands!"

sentences.zh: 刺史召二小吏榜之曰：「皆爾屬為之，非吾過。」

translations.literal: The prefect summoned two petty clerks and flogged them, saying: "All your kind did this; it is not my fault."
translations.idiomatic: The prefect had two minor clerks flogged and declared: "Your people did this—not I."

sentences.zh: 獠相視大笑，遂叛。

translations.literal: The Liao looked at each other and laughed greatly, then rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao exchanged glances and burst into laughter—and then rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 立酋長始艾為王，逾梓、潼，所過焚剽。

translations.literal: They established chieftain Shi'ai as king, crossing Zi and Tong, everywhere they passed burning and plundering.
translations.idiomatic: They made chief Shi'ai their king and swept through Zi and Tong, burning and looting as they went.

sentences.zh: 刺史劉成師誘降其黨，斬首領七十餘人。

translations.literal: Prefect Liu Chengshi enticed surrender of their faction, beheading more than seventy chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Liu Chengshi turned part of the rebels and executed more than seventy chiefs.

sentences.zh: 餘眾遁至東川，節度使柳仲郢諭降之。

translations.literal: The remaining masses fled to eastern Chuan; Military Governor Liu Zhongying instructed them to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors fled into eastern Sichuan, where military governor Liu Zhongying persuaded them to submit.

sentences.zh: 始艾稽首請罪，仲郢貰遣之。

translations.literal: Shi'ai kowtowed and requested punishment; Zhongying pardoned and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Shi'ai prostrated himself to beg forgiveness; Zhongying pardoned him and let him go.

sentences.zh: 成都西北二千餘里有附國，蓋漢西南夷也。

translations.literal: More than two thousand li northwest of Chengdu there is Fuguo, broadly the southwestern Yi of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Some two thousand li northwest of Chengdu lay Fuguo, a land of the southwestern Yi known since Han times.

sentences.zh: 其東部有嘉良夷，無姓氏。

translations.literal: Its eastern part has Jialiang Yi, without surnames.
translations.idiomatic: In the east lived the Jialiang Yi, who used no surnames.

sentences.zh: 地縱八百里，橫四千五百里。

translations.literal: The land extends eight hundred li north to south, four thousand five hundred li east to west.
translations.idiomatic: Their territory ran eight hundred li from north to south and four thousand five hundred li from east to west.

sentences.zh: 無城柵，居川谷，疊石為巢，高十餘丈，以高下為差，作狹戶，自內以通上。

translations.literal: No walled stockades; dwelling in river valleys, piling stones as nests, more than ten zhang high, according to high and low as difference, making narrow doors, from within to pass upward.
translations.idiomatic: They built no walled towns but lived in valleys in stone tower-houses more than thirty feet high, graded by elevation, with narrow doors and inner passages leading upward.

sentences.zh: 王酋帥以金飾首，胸垂金花，徑三寸。

translations.literal: Kings and chieftains adorned their heads with gold, chests hanging golden flowers, diameter three cun.
translations.idiomatic: Kings and chiefs wore gold on their heads and golden blossoms three inches across on their chests.

sentences.zh: 地高涼，多風少雨，宜小麥，多白雉。

translations.literal: The land is high and cool, much wind and little rain, suitable for wheat, many white pheasants.
translations.idiomatic: The high, cool country was windy and dry, good for wheat, and rich in silver pheasants.

sentences.zh: 嘉良夷有水廣三十步，附國水廣五十步，皆南流，以韋為舡。

translations.literal: Jialiang Yi has water thirty paces wide; Fuguo water fifty paces wide, all flowing south; using rushes as boats.
translations.idiomatic: A thirty-pace river ran through Jialiang territory and a fifty-pace river through Fuguo; both flowed south, and they made boats of rushes.

sentences.zh: 附國南有薄緣夷，西接女國。

translations.literal: South of Fuguo there is Boyuan Yi; west connects with the Women's State.
translations.idiomatic: South of Fuguo lay the Boyuan Yi, and to the west their land adjoined the Woman Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 三濮者，在雲南僥外千五百里。

translations.literal: The Three Pu, located beyond the frontier of Yunnan one thousand five hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Pu peoples lived fifteen hundred li beyond Yunnan's frontier.

sentences.zh: 有文面濮，俗鏤面，以青涅之。

translations.literal: There is the Tattoo-Face Pu, customarily carving the face, using indigo to dye it.
translations.idiomatic: Among them were the Tattoo-Face Pu, who cut their faces and stained them blue.

sentences.zh: 赤口濮，裸身而折齒，镵其唇使赤。

translations.literal: Red-Mouth Pu, bare body and broken teeth, carving their lips to make them red.
translations.idiomatic: The Red-Mouth Pu went naked, filed their teeth, and cut their lips until they glowed red.

sentences.zh: 黑僰濮，山居如人，以幅布為裙，貫頭而系之。

translations.literal: Black Bo Pu, mountain dwelling like people, using bolt cloth as skirt, piercing the head and tying it.
translations.idiomatic: The Black Bo Pu lived in the hills like ordinary folk, wearing bolt cloth as skirts and tying cloth over their heads.

sentences.zh: 丈夫衣谷皮。

translations.literal: Husbands wore grain-husk bark cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The men dressed in bark cloth.

sentences.zh: 多白蹄牛、虎魄。

translations.literal: Many white-hoof cattle, amber.
translations.idiomatic: They had many white-hoofed cattle and amber.

sentences.zh: 龍朔中，遣使與千支弗、磨臘同朝貢。

translations.literal: During Longshuo, dispatched envoys together with Qianzhifu and Molila to attend court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longshuo era they sent envoys to court together with Qianzhifu and Molila.

sentences.zh: 西原蠻西原蠻，居廣、容之南，邕、桂之西。

translations.literal: Xiyuan Man—Xiyuan Man dwell south of Guang and Rong, west of Yong and Gui.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiyuan Man lived south of Guang and Rong and west of Yong and Gui.

sentences.zh: 有寧氏者，相承為豪。

translations.literal: There is the Ning clan, succeeding one another as magnates.
translations.idiomatic: The Ning clan had long dominated the region.

sentences.zh: 又有黃氏，居黃橙洞，其隸也。

translations.literal: Again there is the Huang clan, dwelling at Huangcheng cave, their subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: The Huang clan, based at Huangcheng Cave, served under them.

sentences.zh: 其地西接南詔。

translations.literal: Their territory west connects with Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands bordered Nanzhao on the west.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，黃氏強，與韋氏、周氏、儂氏相唇齒，為寇害，據十餘州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, the Huang clan was strong, with the Wei clan, Zhou clan, and Nong clan as lips and teeth, making bandit harm, occupying more than ten prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao reign the Huang grew powerful; allied lip-tooth with the Wei, Zhou, and Nong clans, they raided across more than ten prefectures.

sentences.zh: 韋氏、周氏恥不肯附，黃氏攻之，逐於海濱。

translations.literal: The Wei and Zhou clans, shamed, refused to attach; the Huang clan attacked them, driving them to the seashore.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei and Zhou clans, too proud to submit, were attacked by the Huang and driven to the coast.

sentences.zh: 至德初，首領黃乾曜、真崇郁與陸州、武陽、朱蘭洞蠻皆叛，推武承斐、韋敬簡為帥，僭號中越王，廖殿為桂南王，莫淳為拓南王，相支為南越王，梁奉為鎮南王，羅誠為戎成王，莫潯為南海王，合眾二十萬，綿地數千里，署置官吏，攻桂管十八州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhide, chieftains Huang Qianyao and Zhenchong Yu together with Luzhou, Wuyang, and Zhulan Cave Man all rebelled, elevating Wu Chenfei and Wei Jingjian as commanders, usurping titles—Central Yue King, Guinan King, Tuonan King, Nanyue King, Zhennan King, Rongcheng King, and Nanhai King—combined force two hundred thousand, stretching territory several thousand li, appointing officials, attacking eighteen prefectures of Gui Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhide era chieftains Huang Qianyao and Zhenchong Yu, together with the Man of Luzhou, Wuyang, and Zhulan Cave, all rose in revolt. They made Wu Chenfei and Wei Jingjian their warlords and proclaimed a rack of kings—Central Yue, Guinan, Tuonan, Nanyue, Zhennan, Rongcheng, and Nanhai. With two hundred thousand men spread across thousands of li, they set up offices and assaulted all eighteen prefectures under Gui Circuit.

sentences.zh: 所至焚廬舍，掠士女，更四歲不能平。

translations.literal: Wherever they arrived they burned dwellings, seized men and women; four years passed and they could not be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: They burned settlements and carried off men and women wherever they went, and four years passed without their suppression.

sentences.zh: 乾元初，遣中使慰曉諸首領，賜詔書赦其罪，約降。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyuan, dispatched palace envoys to comfort and instruct the various chieftains, bestowing edicts pardoning their crimes, arranging surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianyuan era the court sent palace envoys to reassure the chiefs, issued an amnesty for their crimes, and negotiated their surrender.

sentences.zh: 於是西原、環、古等州首領方子彈、甘令暉、羅承韋、張九解、宋原五百餘人請出兵討承斐等，歲中戰二百，斬黃乾曜、真郁崇、廖殿、莫淳、梁奉、羅誠、莫潯七人。

translations.literal: Thereupon chieftains of Xiyuan, Huan, Gu and other prefectures—Fang Zidan, Gan Linghui, Luo Chengwei, Zhang Jiujie, Song Yuan and more than five hundred others—requested to dispatch troops to campaign against Chenfei and others; within the year they fought two hundred battles, beheading Huang Qianyao, Zhenchong Yu, Liao Dian, Mo Chun, Liang Feng, Luo Cheng, and Mo Xun—seven men.
translations.idiomatic: Then more than five hundred chiefs from Xiyuan, Huan, Gu, and neighboring prefectures—Fang Zidan, Gan Linghui, Luo Chengwei, Zhang Jiujie, Song Yuan, and others—offered troops against Chenfei and his allies. In a single year they fought two hundred engagements and killed Huang Qianyao, Zhenchong Yu, Liao Dian, Mo Chun, Liang Feng, Luo Cheng, and Mo Xun—seven kings in all.

sentences.zh: 承斐等以餘眾面縛詣桂州降，盡釋其縛，差賜布帛縱之。

translations.literal: Chenfei and others with the remaining masses bound themselves and came to Guizhou to surrender; all were released from bonds, given cloth and silk in varying amounts, and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Chenfei and the survivors came to Guizhou with hands bound and were freed, given cloth, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 其種落張侯、夏永與夷獠梁崇牽、覃問及西原酋長吳功曹復合兵內寇，陷道州，據城五十餘日。

translations.literal: Their tribes Zhang Hou and Xia Yong together with Yi Liao Liang Chongqian, Tan Wen, and Xiyuan chieftain Wu Gongcao again combined troops to raid inward, capturing Daozhou, holding the city more than fifty days.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal leaders Zhang Hou and Xia Yong joined the Yi Liao Liang Chongqian and Tan Wen and the Xiyuan chief Wu Gongcao in another invasion, seized Daozhou, and held it for more than fifty days.

sentences.zh: 桂管經略使邢濟擊平之，執吳功曹等。

translations.literal: Gui Circuit Military Commissioner Xing Ji struck and pacified them, capturing Wu Gongcao and others.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Circuit commissioner Xing Ji crushed the revolt and captured Wu Gongcao and his allies.

sentences.zh: 餘眾復圍道州，刺史元結固守不能下，進攻永州，陷邵州，留數日而去。

translations.literal: The remaining masses again besieged Daozhou; Prefect Yuan Ji held firm and could not be taken; advancing to attack Yongzhou, capturing Shaozhou, they stayed several days then departed.
translations.idiomatic: The remnant force besieged Daozhou again, but prefect Yuan Ji held out; they pushed on to Yongzhou, took Shaozhou, lingered a few days, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 湖南團練使辛京杲遣將王國良戍武崗，嫉京杲貪暴，亦叛，有眾千人，侵掠州縣。

translations.literal: Hunan Training Commissioner Xin Jinggao dispatched General Wang Guoliang to garrison Wugang; resenting Jinggao's greed and cruelty, he also rebelled, having a force of one thousand men, invading and plundering prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan training commissioner Xin Jinggao posted general Wang Guoliang at Wugang; Wang, loathing Xin's greed and brutality, rebelled too with a thousand men and raided the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 發使招之，且服且叛，

translations.literal: Envoys were sent to summon them; they submitted and rebelled in turn.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent envoys to win them over, but they submitted one day and rebelled the next.

sentences.zh: 城敘州以斷西原，國良乃降，

translations.literal: They walled Xuzhou to cut off Xiyuan, and Guoliang then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuzhou was fortified to block the Xiyuan route, Guoliang at last surrendered.

sentences.zh: 黃洞首領黃少卿者，攻邕管，圍經略使孫公器。

translations.literal: The Huang Cave chieftain Huang Shaoqing attacked Yong and Guan districts, besieging Military Commissioner Sun Gongqi.
translations.idiomatic: The Huang Cave chieftain Huang Shaoqing attacked the Yong and Guan circuits and besieged commissioner Sun Gongqi.

sentences.zh: 請發嶺南兵窮討之，德宗不許，命中人招諭。

translations.literal: He requested dispatch of Lingnan troops to pursue and exterminate them; Dezong refused, ordering a palace envoy to summon and instruct.
translations.idiomatic: Sun asked for Lingnan troops to hunt the rebels down, but Dezong refused and sent a palace envoy to negotiate.

sentences.zh: 不從，俄陷欽、橫、潯、貴四州。

translations.literal: They did not follow; soon captured Qin, Heng, Xun, and Gui four prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoqing refused; before long he had overrun Qin, Heng, Xun, and Gui.

sentences.zh: 少卿子昌沔趫勇，前後陷十三州，氣益振。

translations.literal: Shaoqing's son Changmian was swift and brave; before and after capturing thirteen prefectures, his spirit grew ever bolder.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoqing's son Changmian was fierce and swift; he took thirteen prefectures in succession, and their confidence soared.

sentences.zh: 乃以唐州刺史陽旻為容管招討經略使，引師掩賊，一日六七戰，皆破之，侵地悉復。

translations.literal: Thereupon Tang prefecture Prefect Yang Min was made Rong Circuit Pacification and Military Commissioner; leading troops to surprise the bandits, six or seven battles in one day, all broken; seized territory entirely recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Yang Min of Tang prefecture pacification commissioner for Rong Circuit; he fell on the rebels in six or seven fights in a single day, routed them all, and recovered every lost district.

sentences.zh: 元和初，邕州擒其別帥黃承慶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe, Yong prefecture captured their deputy commander Huang Chengqing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanhe era Yong prefecture captured their deputy chief Huang Chengqing.

sentences.zh: 明年，少卿等歸款，拜歸順州刺史。

translations.literal: The next year, Shaoqing and others returned in good faith, appointed Prefect of Guishun prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Shaoqing and his followers submitted in good faith and were given the prefecture of Guishun.

sentences.zh: 弟少高為有州刺史。

translations.literal: Younger brother Shaogao was made Prefect of You prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Shaogao was made prefect of You.

sentences.zh: 未幾復叛。

translations.literal: Before long they rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 又有黃少度、黃昌瓘二部，陷賓、蠻二州，據之。

translations.literal: Again there were the two divisions of Huang Shaodu and Huang Changqiong, capturing Bin and Man two prefectures, occupying them.
translations.idiomatic: Two other bands under Huang Shaodu and Huang Changqiong seized and held Bin and Man prefectures.

sentences.zh: 十一年，攻欽、橫二州，邕管經略使韋悅破走之，取賓、巒二州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, attacked Qin and Heng two prefectures; Yong Circuit Military Commissioner Wei Yue broke and drove them off, recovering Bin and Luan two prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year they struck Qin and Heng; Yong Circuit commissioner Wei Yue drove them off and retook Bin and Luan.

sentences.zh: 是歲，復屠巖州，桂管觀察使裴行立輕其軍弱，首請發兵盡誅叛者，僥幸有功，憲宗許之。

translations.literal: That year, again massacred Yan prefecture; Gui Circuit Observation Commissioner Pei Xingli belittled their army as weak, first requesting dispatch of troops to execute all rebels, hoping for merit; Xianzong granted it.
translations.idiomatic: That same year they sacked Yan prefecture; Gui Circuit observer Pei Xingli, thinking their forces weak, was first to ask for troops to exterminate every rebel in hope of glory, and Xianzong agreed.

sentences.zh: 行立兵出擊，彌更二歲，妄奏斬獲二萬，罔天子為解。

translations.literal: Xingli's troops went out to strike; spanning more than two years, falsely reporting beheadings and captures of twenty thousand, deceiving the Son of Heaven as explanation.
translations.idiomatic: Xingli marched out and, over more than two years, falsely claimed twenty thousand kills and captures to mislead the throne.

sentences.zh: 自是邕、容兩道殺傷疾疫死者十八以上。

translations.literal: From this Yong and Rong two circuits—those killed and wounded, plague dead—eighteen tenths and above.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward more than eight-tenths of the people in Yong and Rong circuits died by the sword, wounds, or pestilence.

sentences.zh: 調費鬥亡，繇行立、陽旻二人，當時莫不咎之。

translations.literal: Tax levies and expenses perished in struggle; owing to Xingli and Yang Min the two men, at the time none did not blame them.
translations.idiomatic: Tax revenues collapsed in the fighting, and everyone blamed Xingli and Yang Min.

sentences.zh: 及安南兵亂，殺都護李象古，擢唐州刺史桂仲武為都護，逗留不敢進，貶安州刺史，以行立代之。

translations.literal: When Annan troops mutinied, killing Protector-General Li Xianggu, Tang prefecture Prefect Gui Zhongwu was promoted to Protector-General, lingered and dared not advance, demoted to Annan prefect; Xingli replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Annan garrison mutinied and killed protector-general Li Xianggu, Gui Zhongwu of Tang prefecture was promoted to the post but hung back; he was demoted to Annan prefect and Xingli replaced him.

sentences.zh: 尋召還，卒。

translations.literal: Soon recalled, died.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled and died.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，以容管經略使留後嚴公素為經略使，復上表請討黃氏。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing, Rong Circuit Military Commissioner acting commissioner Yan Gusu was made Military Commissioner, again submitting a memorial requesting campaign against the Huang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Changqing era Yan Gusu, acting Rong Circuit commissioner, was confirmed in office and again petitioned for a campaign against the Huang clan.

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎韓愈建言：「黃賊皆洞獠，無城郭，依山險各治生業，急則屯聚畏死。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War Han Yu offered counsel: "The Huang bandits are all cave Liao, without walled cities; relying on mountain peril each managing livelihood; urgent then they gather fearing death.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of War Han Yu urged: "The Huang rebels are cave-dwelling Liao without walled towns. Each clan lives by the mountains; when pressed they mass together, fearing death.

sentences.zh: 前日邕管經略使德不能綏懷，威不能臨制，侵詐系縛，以致憾恨。

translations.literal: Formerly the Yong Circuit Military Commissioner lacked virtue to soothe and embrace, lacked authority to oversee and restrain; oppression and deceit in binding led to resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier commissioners of Yong Circuit could neither win them with kindness nor govern them with force; fraud and shackling bred hatred.

sentences.zh: 夷性易動而難安，劫州縣復私讎，貪小利不為大患。

translations.literal: Barbarian nature easily stirred yet hard to settle; plundering prefectures to settle private grudges, coveting small profit—not a great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians are quick to rise and slow to rest; they raid counties to settle old scores and chase small gains—they are not a mortal threat.

sentences.zh: 自行立、陽旻建征討，生事詭賞，邕、容兩管，日以雕弊，殺傷疾患，十室九空。

translations.literal: Since Xingli and Yang Min established campaigns, fabricating incidents for false rewards, the two circuits of Yong and Rong daily decayed, casualties and disease—nine of ten households empty.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xingli and Yang Min launched their punitive drives, inventing battles for rewards, Yong and Rong withered day by day; nine houses in ten stood empty from slaughter and sickness.

sentences.zh: 百姓怨嗟，如出一口；

translations.literal: The people groaned in resentment, as with one mouth;
translations.idiomatic: The people groaned as one voice;

sentences.zh: 人神共嫉，二將繼死。

translations.literal: Gods and men alike hated them; the two generals died in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth turned against them, and both generals died in turn.

sentences.zh: 今嚴公素非撫禦之才，復尋往謬，誠恐嶺南未有寧時。

translations.literal: Now Yan Gusu lacks talent for conciliation and control, again pursuing past errors, truly fearing Lingnan will know no peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Gusu is no pacifier, and if he repeats those blunders Lingnan may never know peace.

sentences.zh: 昨合邕、容為一道，邕與賊限一江，若經略使居之，兵鎮所處，物力雄完，則敵人不敢輕犯；

translations.literal: Recently Yong and Rong were merged as one circuit—Yong and the bandits separated by one river; if the Military Commissioner resides there, where troops garrison, resources strong and complete, then enemies dare not lightly violate;
translations.idiomatic: When Yong and Rong were merged, Yong stood one river away from the rebels; if the commissioner stays there where troops and supplies are strong, the enemy will not dare strike lightly;

sentences.zh: 容州則隔阻已甚，以經略使居之，則邕州兵少情見，易啟蠻心。

translations.literal: Rong prefecture is extremely cut off; placing the commissioner there leaves Yong with few troops, intentions exposed, easily stirring barbarian hearts.
translations.idiomatic: but Rong is too remote—stationing the commissioner there leaves Yong undermanned, exposes our hand, and invites fresh raids.

sentences.zh: 請以經略使還邕州，容置刺史，便甚。

translations.literal: Request returning the commissioner to Yong prefecture, placing a prefect at Rong—very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Move the commissioner back to Yong and leave a prefect at Rong—that is the sensible course.

sentences.zh: 又比發南兵，遠鄉羈旅，疾疫殺傷，續添續死，每發倍難。

translations.literal: Again recently dispatching southern troops, far from home as sojourners, plague and casualties, continual reinforcement and continual death, each dispatch doubly difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Sending southern armies from afar means plague and death with every draft; each levy costs twice what it should.

sentences.zh: 若募邕、容千人，以給行營，糧不增而兵便習，守則有威，攻則有利。

translations.literal: If recruiting a thousand from Yong and Rong to supply the field camp, grain not increased yet troops accustomed—defense has authority, attack has advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Recruit a thousand local men from Yong and Rong for the camp: no extra grain, but troops who know the ground—strong in defense, sharp in attack.

sentences.zh: 自南討損傷，嶺南人希，賊之所處，洞壘荒僻。

translations.literal: Since southern campaigns' losses, Lingnan people scarce; where bandits dwell, cave fortresses remote and desolate.
translations.idiomatic: After years of southern war Lingnan is depopulated, and the rebels hide in remote cave fastnesses.

sentences.zh: 假如盡殺其人，得其地，在國計不為有益。

translations.literal: Even if killing all their people and gaining the land, for state reckoning it is not beneficial.
translations.idiomatic: Even exterminating them and taking the land would profit the state nothing.

sentences.zh: 容貸羈縻，比之禽獸，來則捍禦，去則不追，未有虧損朝廷。

translations.literal: Tolerating and keeping them through loose reins, comparing to birds and beasts—when they come then defend, when they go do not pursue—never yet harming the court.
translations.idiomatic: Better to hold them loosely, as one does wild beasts: resist when they come, let them go when they leave—the court has never lost by it.

sentences.zh: 願因改元大慶，普赦其罪，遣郎官、御史以天子意丁寧宣諭，必能喧叫聽命。

translations.literal: May we take the occasion of the Great Celebration era change, universally pardon their crimes, dispatch court officials and censors with the Son of Heaven's intent in earnest proclamation and instruction—they can surely clamor and obey.
translations.idiomatic: I urge a general amnesty at the change of reign to Daqing, with palace officials sent to announce the emperor's will in person—they will listen at once.

sentences.zh: 為選材用威信者，委以經略，處理得方，宜無侵叛事。」

translations.literal: Select men of talent, employment, trust, and authority, entrust to them military governance; handling rightly, there should be no invasion and rebellion matters."
translations.idiomatic: Appoint capable, trusted men to the commission, manage affairs properly, and raids should cease."

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: It was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne did not accept his advice.

sentences.zh: 初，邕管既廢，人不謂宜。

translations.literal: At first, when Yong Circuit was abolished, people did not consider it fitting.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong Circuit was first abolished, opinion held it a mistake.

sentences.zh: 監察御史杜周士使安南，過邕州，刺史李元宗白狀，周士從事五管，積三十年矣，亦知其不便。

translations.literal: Censor Du Zhoushi on mission to Annan, passing Yong prefecture; Prefect Li Yuanzong reported the situation; Zhoushi had served the Five Circuits for thirty years accumulated, also knew its inconvenience.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Du Zhoushi, bound for Annan, stopped at Yong prefecture, where prefect Li Yuanzong laid out the problems; Zhoushi had served in the Five Circuits for thirty years and knew the arrangement was wrong.

sentences.zh: 嚴公素遣人盜其槁，周士憤死。

translations.literal: Yan Gusu sent men to steal his draft; Zhoushi died in anger.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Gusu had men steal his memorial draft, and Zhoushi died of outrage.

sentences.zh: 公素劾元宗擅以羅陽縣還黃少度，元宗懼，引兵一百持印章依少度。

translations.literal: Gusu impeached Yuanzong for on his own authority returning Luoyang county to Huang Shaodu; Yuanzong feared, led one hundred troops holding the seal and went to rely on Shaodu.
translations.idiomatic: Gusu charged Yuanzong with illegally returning Luoyang county to Huang Shaodu; terrified, Yuanzong fled with a hundred men and the seal to join Shaodu.

sentences.zh: 穆宗遣監察御史敬僚按之。

translations.literal: Muzong dispatched censor Jing Liao to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong sent censor Jing Liao to investigate.

sentences.zh: 僚嘗為容州從事，與公素昵，傅致元宗罪，以母老，流州，眾以為不直。

translations.literal: Liao had once been an aide at Rong prefecture, was intimate with Gusu, fabricated Yuanzong's crimes; because his mother was old, he was exiled to a prefecture; all thought it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Liao, once a Rong prefecture aide and Gusu's friend, framed Yuanzong and had him exiled on account of an aged mother—a verdict widely deemed unfair.

sentences.zh: 黃賊更攻邕州，陷左江鎮；

translations.literal: The Huang bandits again attacked Yong prefecture, capturing Zuojiang garrison;
translations.idiomatic: The Huang rebels struck Yong prefecture again and took Zuojiang garrison;

sentences.zh: 攻欽州，陷千金鎮。

translations.literal: attacked Qin prefecture, capturing Qianjin garrison.
translations.idiomatic: they attacked Qin prefecture and seized Qianjin garrison.

sentences.zh: 刺史楊嶼奔石南柵，邕州刺史崔結擊破之。

translations.literal: Prefect Yang Yu fled to Shinan stockade; Yong prefecture Prefect Cui Jie struck and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Qin prefect Yang Yu fled to Shinan stockade, but Yong prefect Cui Jie routed the raiders.

sentences.zh: 明年，又寇欽州，殺將吏。

translations.literal: The next year, again raided Qin prefecture, killing generals and officials.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they raided Qin again and killed officers and officials.

sentences.zh: 是歲，黃昌瓘遣其黨陳少奇二十人歸款請降，敬宗納之。

translations.literal: That year Huang Changqiong sent his follower Chen Shaoqi and twenty others to return in good faith requesting surrender; Jingzong accepted.
translations.idiomatic: That year Huang Changqiong sent Chen Shaoqi and twenty followers to surrender; Emperor Jingzong accepted them.

sentences.zh: 黃氏、儂氏據州十八，經略使至，遣一人詣治所，稍不得意，輒侵掠諸州。

translations.literal: The Huang and Nong clans held eighteen prefectures; when the military commissioner arrived, they sent one person to the administrative seat; slightly displeased, they immediately raided various prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The Huang and Nong clans controlled eighteen prefectures; they sent a single envoy to the commissioner's seat, and at the slightest grievance raided neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 橫州當邕江官道，嶺南節度使常以兵五百戍守，不能制。

translations.literal: Heng prefecture lay on the Yong River official road; the Lingnan military governor often stationed five hundred troops to garrison but could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Heng prefecture stood on the Yong River highway; even five hundred garrison troops from the Lingnan governor could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 大和中，經略使董昌齡遣子蘭討平峒穴，夷其種黨，諸蠻畏服。

translations.literal: In Dahe, Military Commissioner Dong Changling sent his son Lan to campaign and pacify cave settlements, exterminated their tribes; the various Man feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dahe era commissioner Dong Changling sent his son Lan to crush the cave strongholds, wiped out rebel clans, and the tribes submitted in fear.

sentences.zh: 有違命者，必嚴罰之。

translations.literal: Those disobeying orders were strictly punished.
translations.idiomatic: Disobedience brought harsh punishment.

sentences.zh: 十八州歲輸貢賦，道路清平。

translations.literal: Eighteen prefectures paid tribute annually; the roads were clear and peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: All eighteen prefectures paid annual tribute and the roads were safe.

sentences.zh: 其後儂洞最強，結南詔為助。

translations.literal: Afterward the Nong caves were strongest, allying with Nanzhao for aid.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Nong caves grew strongest and allied with Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 懿宗與南詔約和，二洞數構敗之。

translations.literal: Yizong made peace with Nanzhao; the two cave groups repeatedly sabotaged it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yizong made peace with Nanzhao, but the two cave alliances repeatedly wrecked it.

sentences.zh: 邕管節度使辛讜以從事徐雲虔使南詔結和，賫美貨啖二洞首領、太州刺史黃伯蘊、屯洞首領儂金意、員州首領儂金勒等與之通歡。

translations.literal: Yong Circuit Military Governor Xin Dan sent aide Xu Yunqian as envoy to Nanzhao to make peace, carrying fine goods to win over the two cave chieftains—Taizhou prefect Huang Boyun, Tundong chieftain Nong Jinyi, Yuan prefecture chieftain Nong Jinle and others—to exchange goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Circuit governor Xin Dan sent aide Xu Yunqian to Nanzhao with rich gifts to befriend chiefs Huang Boyun of Taizhou, Nong Jinyi of Tundong, Nong Jinle of Yuan prefecture, and others.

sentences.zh: 員州又有首領儂金澄、儂仲武與金勒襲黃洞首領黃伯善，伯善伏兵水，雞鳴，候其半濟，擊殺金澄、仲武，唯金勒遁免。

translations.literal: Yuan prefecture also had chieftains Nong Jincheng and Nong Zhongwu who with Jinle attacked Huang Cave chieftain Huang Boshan; Boshan ambushed at the water, at cockcrow waited until they were half across, struck and killed Jincheng and Zhongwu; only Jinle escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan chiefs Nong Jincheng and Nong Zhongwu joined Jinle in attacking Huang Boshan; Boshan ambushed them at a ford at cockcrow, killed Jincheng and Zhongwu mid-crossing, and only Jinle escaped.

sentences.zh: 後欲興兵報仇，辛讜遣人持牛酒音樂解和，並遺其母衣服。

translations.literal: Later wanting to raise troops for revenge, Xin Dan sent men with oxen, wine, and music to mediate, also giving his mother clothes.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinle sought revenge, Xin Dan sent mediators with cattle, wine, music, and garments for his mother.

sentences.zh: 母，賢者也，讓其子曰：「節度使持物與獠母，非結好也，以汝為吾子。

translations.literal: The mother was a virtuous woman; she reproached her son, saying: "The military governor sending goods to a Liao mother is not making alliance—it means he treats you as my son.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, a wise woman, rebuked him: "When the governor sends gifts to a Liao mother, he is not courting alliance—he treats you as a son to me.

sentences.zh: 前日兵敗水，士卒略盡，不自悔，復欲動眾，兵忿者必敗，吾將囚為官老婢矣。」

translations.literal: The other day the army was defeated at the water and soldiers nearly all gone; not repenting, again wanting to move the masses—resentful soldiers will surely be defeated; I will be imprisoned as an official old maidservant."
translations.idiomatic: You lost your army at the ford and most of your men; instead of repenting you would stir them again—angry soldiers always lose, and I shall become some official's bondwoman."

sentences.zh: 金勒感寤，為罷兵。

translations.literal: Jinle was moved and awakened, and for that reason ceased troops.
translations.idiomatic: Jinle was moved to repentance and stood down his forces.

sentences.zh: 小論贊曰：

translations.literal: Minor Commentary concludes:
translations.idiomatic: The Minor Commentary concludes:

sentences.zh: 唐北禽頡利，西滅高昌、焉耆，東破高麗、百濟，威制夷狄，方策所未有也。

translations.literal: Tang in the north captured Jieli, in the west destroyed Gaochang and Yanqi, in the east broke Goguryeo and Baekje, awe restraining the barbarians—unprecedented in the records.
translations.idiomatic: Tang captured Jieli in the north, destroyed Gaochang and Yanqi in the west, and broke Goguryeo and Baekje in the east—awe over the barbarians unmatched in the annals.

sentences.zh: 交州，漢之故封，其外瀕海諸蠻，無廣土堅城可以居守，故中國兵未嘗至。

translations.literal: Jiaozhou, Han's old enfeoffment—beyond it the coastal various Man had no broad land or strong walls to dwell in and guard, therefore Chinese troops never reached there.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhou was an old Han commandery, but beyond it the coastal tribes held no broad plains or walled towns, so imperial armies seldom went there.

sentences.zh: 及唐稍弱，西原、黃洞繼為邊害，垂百餘年。

translations.literal: When Tang gradually weakened, Xiyuan and Huang Cave successively became border harm, spanning more than a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: As Tang weakened, Xiyuan and Huang Cave plagued the frontier for more than a century.

sentences.zh: 及其亡也，以南詔。

translations.literal: When it perished, it was because of Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty fell, Nanzhao was the cause.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：「惠此中國，以綏四方。」

translations.literal: The Classic of Poetry says, "Show grace to this Central Kingdom, to pacify the four quarters."
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Poetry says, "Show grace to this Central Kingdom, to pacify the four quarters."

sentences.zh: 不以夷狄先諸夏也。

translations.literal: It does not put the barbarians ahead of the civilized domains.
translations.idiomatic: It does not put the barbarians ahead of the civilized domains.
